full_text: Ex-TMC leader Bibhas Adhikari, arrested in Noida for a ‘fake police station’, allegedly ran similar set-up in Kolkata Ex-TMC leader Bibhas Chandra Adhikari, arrested in Noida for “running a fake police station”, has allegedly been found to have operated a similar set-up in Kolkata. Adhikari, a former Trinamool Block President from Nalhati in Birbhum and once under the CBI and ED scanner in the teachers’ recruitment scam, was picked up along with his son and four others for allegedly running the “International Police & Crime Investigation Bureau” in Noida’s Sector 70 on Saturday night. Police said the group allegedly posed as government officials to extort money. Investigations by Kolkata police revealed that in Kolkata’s Beleghata area, Adhikari had allegedly rented two flats on CIT Road where he displayed boards reading “Investigation of Social Justice”, “Interpol” and “Police”. He would allegedly arrive in a car with a blue beacon with four armed guards. Police claimed he owns significant assets, including an Ayurvedic college in Suri, a B.Ed college in Krishnapur, and houses in Kolkata and Delhi. Adhikari was removed from his Trinamool post before the 2021 elections, later forming the “Bhartiya Arya Samaj” party. However, he was seen sharing the stage with TMC leaders in 2024 and was accused of taking money in exchange for job promises in the teachers’ recruitment scam. Sources said he was considered close to jailed former Education Minister Partha Chatterjee. His Krishnapur ashram housed an office using the letterhead of the “National Bureau of Social Investigation and Social Justice.” The CBI questioned him multiple times in 2023 in the recruitment case.

full_text: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver Around 7.30 on January 27, Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad, 56, a resident of Nashik who worked as a rental cab driver, called his wife Aruna on her phone. He had taken a trip from Nashik to Pune around 5 am that day. He told her he would reach home around 7.30 pm. That was the last conversation Aruna had with her husband. Repeated calls made to him were unanswered. Around 10.30 pm that night, Gailkwad’s wife got a call that his phone had been found on the Alephata Santwadi road off the Pune-Nashik highway. The caller had kept the phone at a nearby hotel, from where he had made the call. Around 2.30 am on January 28, the Gaikwad family reached the hotel and searched for him in the area where the phone was found. However, Gaikwad and his car could not be traced. The family registered a missing person case at Alephata police station under the Pune Rural police. At around 9.30 am on January 28, while police were actively searching for Gaikwad, his body was discovered in the Santwadi area. His hands were bound behind his back with a nylon rope and a zip tie, and initial autopsy findings indicated that he had been strangled. The murder investigation was taken up jointly by teams from the Alephata police station and the Pune Rural police’s Local Crime Branch. As part of the investigation, the police reviewed footage from dozens of CCTV cameras on the approach routes to the area. A significant breakthrough came when Gaikwad’s vehicle was spotted on a hotel’s CCTV camera along the Nashik–Pune highway corridor. By piecing together video evidence from multiple locations, investigators traced the car’s movement—first heading toward the area where his body was later discovered, then continuing in the direction of Malshej Ghat. Both the footage and ground inquiries indicated that, at one stage, four people were inside the car along with Gaikwad. Meanwhile, a team which was on the lookout for the car found it abandoned in Kasara Ghat, along the route to Nashik. Continued analysis of CCTV footage helped police identify suspects who were captured travelling in the vehicle. Over the following three days, till January 31, investigators arrested three suspects: Vishal Ananda Chavan, 22; Mayur Vijay Solse, 23; and Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane, 21, all residents of the Gangapur Road area in Nashik. The investigation to arrest the fourth suspect continues even now. Driver resisted carjacking attempt, say police Investigators found out that the suspects had boarded Gaikwad’s car during his return journey to Nashik from Pune. They used the pretext of hitching a ride, but wanted to hijack the vehicle, said the police. The sequence of events, as brought out by the investigation, was that they allegedly strangled him after he resisted their attempt. The group then disposed of his body and fled the scene, said the police. It was soon revealed that the trio are hardened criminals. They allegedly intended to use the hijacked car for an armed robbery in which they wanted to target a shop in Nashik. The police said they, however, decided to abandon it on the way since they thought the vehicle would be flagged in the murder investigation after Gaikwad’s body was found. Solse and Chavan are facing charges of murder registered at Gangapur police station in Nashik in 2022. As the police continued their probe, they found out that these suspects were involved in a case of carjacking at Chakan police station registered in 2024, which had remained unsolved till the time the murder case was cracked. “The chargesheet in the case was filed subsequently. All three accused are currently in prison under judicial custody. A coordinated search for the fourth accused continued. The wanted suspect in the case also has multiple offences registered against him,” said an officer who was part of the probe. The case underscores the dangers faced by drivers who pick up unknown passengers outside their assigned duties. Authorities have reiterated their warning against this practice, noting that similar incidents of passengers turning violent have been reported in the past.

full_text: Gurgaon man masturbates in front of woman waiting for cab, police file FIR The Gurgaon police on August 5 registered a case against a man who was caught on camera allegedly masturbating in front of a young woman near Rajiv Chowk in the city, officers said on Thursday. According to the police, the incident took place on August 2 when the complainant, a model and digital content creator, was waiting for a cab around noon at a busy junction to head home after a journey from Jaipur. Krishan Kumar, Station House Officer, Civil Lines Police Station, said that the police have filed a First Information Report (FIR) under sections 75(2) for sexual harassment and 78 for stalking of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. “The investigation is underway, and the complainant has also joined the probe, and we have recorded her statement. We are scanning CCTV footage in and around the spot and talking to people in the area.” On the same day of the incident, the model narrated her ordeal on social media and posted the video of the alleged act of the perpetrator, while also blaming the police for the delay in registering a complaint. “Something very strange happened to me. A man came around, circling, and he was constantly staring at me. Initially, I just ignored it, like the others do,” she said. She noticed that the man with unzipped pants was allegedly masturbating. The video showed the man wearing a facemask and a backpack that he had slung over his chest to cover the act from being too visible to the public nearby. The woman said it was clear he was ‘very aware’ of what he was doing. The woman in her video also lamented how cab companies were delaying in accepting her ride request, aggravating her ordeal. The complainant stated that although she had initially got a ride booked, the driver was not picking up despite multiple calls, and hence she had to re-book across applications “just to avoid the creep”. Eventually, a cab arrived and she reached home. In the video, she also alleged initial inaction from the police after she had tagged the police and other government authorities while putting the man’s video on X, and later calling the police helpline. “There wasn’t even an automated message,” she said. Regarding the FIR, the model said, the police had asked her to come to the station instead of lodging the complaint online. “It was making me feel very uncomfortable. I felt very, very disgusted. Initially, I froze. I did not record or hit him. People who say I could have shouted at him do not understand what goes through a girl’s mind at that moment. Reactions go viral faster than the real truth, and people judge; they do not help.” The woman stated she wanted to be safe rather than have the moment become viral. “I am not making the video for any kind of attention, just want to be heard,” she said in the video.

full_text: Top 10 Indian states with highest crime rate: Delhi ranks 5th, see which states outranks the national capital Top 10 Indian states with highest crime rate: India, home to over 140 crore people, is the most populous country in the world. With its vast population spread across diverse states, each region faces its own set of challenges. Among the more pressing issues in certain areas is the alarming rate of crime. It threatens public safety, disrupts everyday life, and development. As per the latest data from the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) 2024, crime trends have shifted noticeably across the country. While there have been minor ups and downs in the overall national crime figures, some states have seen a sharp rise in specific categories of crime. Factors such as poverty, unemployment, lack of education, social unrest, and even political instability often play a role in impacting crime rates. Understanding which states have higher crime rates helps people stay aware and allows authorities to better focus their efforts on law enforcement and public safety. In this article, we take a closer look at the top 10 Indian states with the highest crime rates, based on the number of reported crimes per capita. From theft and robbery to violent offenses and crimes against women, the range is wide and deeply concerning. Source: National Crime Records Bureau Uttar Pradesh tops the list with the highest number of reported crimes in the country. A per capita rate of 7.4 reflects the ongoing struggle to maintain order in a densely populated state. Incidents ranging from theft and assault to communal violence continue to pose serious law and order challenges. Despite being one of the least populated states, Arunachal Pradesh reports the second-highest crime rate per capita. Security restrictions like limited night movement in certain areas reveal the underlying safety issues, compounded by remote locations and tough terrain that hinder policing efforts. Jharkhand remains burdened by deep-rooted issues like Naxalite influence, illegal mining operations, and poor infrastructure in rural zones. A per capita crime rate of 5.3 indicates not only high crime levels but also potential underreporting and enforcement gaps. Known for its scenic beauty, Meghalaya struggles with rising crime, particularly in tribal belts. The per capita figures are troubling, especially considering the state’s small population, pointing to a spike in localised law and order concerns. The national capital continues to face a high crime burden, with 5.0 incidents per person reported. Despite being a hub for governance and law enforcement, Delhi sees persistent issues such as gender violence, theft, and street-level crimes that affect residents and visitors alike. Assam’s crime landscape is shaped by its history of political unrest and ethnic conflicts. The crime rate reflects incidents ranging from localized disputes to more serious insurgency-linked violence in sensitive border districts. In Chhattisgarh, the ongoing Maoist insurgency and lack of access to remote tribal regions continue to fuel the crime rate. Long-standing security challenges and slow judicial response have left many vulnerable to both violence and injustice. Haryana and Odisha both report identical crime rates but face different issues. Haryana has seen a surge in urban crimes, including gang activity and violence against women, while Odisha grapples with rural offenses and policing gaps in its interior regions. While Andhra Pradesh boasts relatively strong governance structures, crime remains a concern. The state has recorded an uptick in digital scams, financial fraud, and domestic violence—highlighting the evolving nature of crime in a modernising society.

full_text: Man stabbed to death in East Delhi as he confronts local vendor with whom he had prior tiff, 3 held A 28-year-old man was allegedly stabbed to death during an altercation between two groups in East Delhi’s Ghazipur Wednesday night and the police arrested three men in connection with the murder. The deceased was identified as Vikas Walchera, a resident of Faridabad who was employed as a sales manager at a Noida firm. The police said they received a call at around 11 pm from Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital, informing them about a man who had been brought dead with multiple injuries. Another employee from the same company, Sumit Sharma, a resident of Ghaziabad, was also admitted to the hospital with a fractured leg, said the police. Abhishek Dhania, Deputy Commissioner of Police, East, said, “It was revealed that Walchera and other employees were celebrating a birthday party, and during the gathering, a prior altercation involving a local momo vendor, Salman, was discussed. To verify, the group visited the paper market in Ghazipur at around 10.30 pm in three cars.” “At the wine shop near the CNG pump, they identified Salman, who, upon seeing them, retrieved a rod and called his associates Azad Mishra, Monu Mishra, and others. In the violent scuffle that followed, Vikas Walecha was fatally stabbed, and others, including Sumit Sharma, were injured,” added Dhania. The police filed a case at the Gazipur police station under sections 103 (murder), 109(1) (attempted murder), 191(2) (rioting), and 3(5) (common intent) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). They formed multiple dedicated teams for investigation and arrests. They were assigned tasks such as scanning CCTV and number plate recognition camera footage to establish both forward and backward linkages and to trace the accused, said the police. The police said they arrested Salman Khan, 24, Azad Kumar Mishra, 31, and Monu Mishra, 28, and apprehended one juvenile boy within hours. They also said they recovered the iron rod and knife used in the attack from the crime scene. Further investigation is ongoing to trace more people involved in the crime and to establish a comprehensive motive behind the attack, said the police.

full_text: Within hours, Delhi witnesses 3 murders; police look for motive in 2 cases Delhi witnessed three murders within a span of a few hours early on Saturday morning, all under different jurisdictions, the police said. headline: Truth, blood and broken systems: 5 true-crime books that explore India’s darkest cases
who: Aarushi; Aarushi Talwar; Hemraj; Avirook Sen; Mumtaz; Inayat; Meenal Baghel’s; Maria Susairaj; Jerome Mathew; Baghel

full_text: Truth, blood and broken systems: 5 true-crime books that explore India’s darkest cases In a country where crime stories flood the headlines, once in a while, a case comes along that does more than shock, it unsettles the very idea of justice. From sensational courtroom battles to brutal crimes that shook the nation, India’s true crime genre has evolved into something far more layered than simply mystery solving. Today, true crime is not just about who did it, it is about why it happened and how systems failed to stop it. These stories exposes what lies under sensationalism. Fractured institutions and the psychological complexities of both victims and perpetrators. Here are five meticulously crafted accounts that go beyond the crime to examine the conditions that allowed them to occur. A teenage girl found dead in her own home. A second body discovered on the terrace. And then, a storm of media speculation, botched investigations and courtroom drama that continues to haunt India still. Aarushi is a meticulous and unflinching account of the 2008 Noida double murder of 14 year old Aarushi Talwar and her house helper, Hemraj. From the fumbling local police to the sensationalist media coverage and the Central Bureau of Investigation’s contradictory theories. Avirook Sen exposes the cracks in the investigation, missing evidence, coerced confessions and trial by media, that turned a tragedy into a national spectacle. This is not a whodunit. It’s a look at what happens when institutions designed to deliver justice begin to crumble. The 1925 Bawla murder case. A high society scandal involving princes, prostitutes and political intrigue. This little known but landmark case documents the attempted assassination of a courtesan, Mumtaz, by none other than Prince Inayat of the princely state of Indore. As the bullets missed her and killed her bodyguard instead, the fallout became a media circus in British India. It rattled the foundations of royal immunity. With a meticulous mix of courtroom drama and colonial context, this case raised questions about power, privilege and justice long before independence. In December 2007, a sleepy town in Kerala woke up to the country’s most cinematic bank robbery. Using a fake identity and a rented shop, a gang of thieves drilled a hole from a nearby room into the vault of the South Malabar Gramin Bank, escaping with Rs. 80 million in cash and gold. The Chelembra heist was India’s closest real-life case to Ocean’s Eleven, only without the Hollywood gloss. This book breaks down the precision and planning behind the crime and also reveals how a combination of flawed assumptions and brilliant policing eventually brought the culprits to justice. It’s a pulse pounding account of ambition, deception and the allure of the perfect crime. Meenal Baghel’s investigative reportage on the Neeraj Grover murder case where aspiring actress Maria Susairaj and her boyfriend Emile Jerome Mathew were convicted. It is a chilling portrait of love, jealousy and dismemberment in India. What makes Death in Mumbai unforgettable is how it unpacks the toxic underbelly of aspiration in the entertainment industry. Baghel showed the deep moral ambiguities and societal voyeurism that came with it. The book is a perfect example of how class, media portrayal and sexual politics intersected in a brutal, almost surreal murder that continues to fascinate and repulse even today. India’s roads are treacherous, not just for accidents, but for serial killers. The Highway Murders brings to light a horrifying pattern of killings along Tamil Nadu’s highways, where at least 13 women were raped and murdered over several years. What went unnoticed as isolated crimes was, in fact, a chilling serial pattern, cracked only through forensic breakthroughs and dogged police work. The book paints a disturbing picture of how vulnerable people, especially women become targets in liminal spaces, and how India’s law enforcement often fails to connect the dots. It’s a story of anonymity and the dark spaces between streetlights. (The writer is an intern with indianexpress.com)

headline: Elderly businessman tied and gagged, robbed at gunpoint at his home

full_text: Elderly businessman tied and gagged, robbed at gunpoint at his home A 76-year-old businessman, Chandrabhan Chhoteram Agarwal, was allegedly robbed at gunpoint at his residence in Nigdi Pradhikaran by armed assailants who stormed the house on Saturday night before tying and gagging him. They also locked his domestic help’s family in the outhouse and fled with gold ornaments and valuables worth over Rs 6 lakh. A joint probe by Nigdi police and Pimpri Chinchwad police’s crime branch has been launched. A First Information Report (FIR) in the case has been registered at Nigdi police station by Agarwal. Agarwal lives alone at his residence with the family of his domestic help residing in the outhouse. Around 8.55 pm on Saturday night when he was home watching TV, two suspects stormed into his house while three more stood at the door. The two suspects threatened him at gunpoint and asked him where the safe was. When he replied that there was no safe in his house, the robbers tied his hands and legs and gagged him as they started rummaging the house. The suspects took gold and silver ornaments worth Rs 4.5 lakh, a gold chain worth Rs 1.35 lakh that Agarwal was wearing along with the wrist watches and cash worth Rs 6.15 lakh. Police officials said that one of the neighbours saw the robbers leaving the house and felt that their movements were suspicious and informed the police. A team from the police station arrived at the scene and released the complainant. It also came to light that the suspects had tied and locked the family of the domestic help in the outhouse. The complainant has given a description of the suspects and it is likely that some of the suspects were women, an officer said. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime) Shivaji Pawar said, “We have formed multiple teams for the probe of this case. The team are working on various clues including the footage from the CCTV cameras in the area.”

He said support and counselling was being offered to those living in neighbouring units.A large police presence remained in Adrienne Crescent, Mount Waverley, on Tuesday. (ABC News)Victoria Police has urged anyone who witnessed the incident, has footage or information that may help detectives to contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or www.crimestoppersvic.com.au.Posted 5h ago5 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 7:57pm, updated 2h ago2 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 11:49pmShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMoment the PM gained confidence Australia could recognise a Palestinian stateTopic:Foreign AffairsPhoto shows Albanese and Wong enter the prime minister's courtyard, walking up to two lecterns.Albanese says Netanyahu 'in denial' about conflict's impact on civiliansLIVEPhoto shows Benjamin Netanyahu looking up and to the right of the camera at a press conference.'Israel has succeeded': Final words from journalist killed in GazaTopic:JournalismPhoto shows A young Palestinian man in a press vest and helmet speaks into a microphone featuring the Al Jazeera logo.Reserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chartPilot in fatal chopper crash to take stand in croc wrangler's trialLIVEPhoto shows Matt Wright has brown hair and is wearing a button-up shirt as he walks towards the court.Popular nowReserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chart'Endless' trespassers cost farmers thousands and endanger lifeTopic:Beef Cattle FarmingPhoto shows Geoff Pearson stands in a paddock with cattle behind himYoung Australian hospitalised after ChatGPT useTopic:TechnologyPhoto shows An illustration of a young boy staring at a computer. full_text: Mima McKim-Hill died in 1967. Her suspected killer never faced justice A young woman was murdered in Central Queensland 58 years ago. Her suspected killer never faced justice CBy Ciara JonesTopic:Homicide6h ago6 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 7:50pmMima McKim-Hill's body was found near Biloela in Central Queensland in March 1967. (ABC News: Peter Mullins)abc.net.au/news/mima-mckim-hill-unsolved-murder-rockhampton-1967/105503934Link copiedShareShare articleIt's been well over half a century, but Shirley Eldridge vividly remembers the chilling late-night phone call.It was March 9, 1967, and at the end of the line was the worried mother of her friend and co-worker, Mima McKim-Hill. Mima, 21, hadn't returned home from a work trip in Central Queensland. I knew something had happened, recalls Shirley, then 20.Seventeen days later, her worst fears materialised.On Easter Sunday, Mima's body was found dumped in a small waterhole in bushland at Collard Creek, off the Dawson Highway, near Biloela.Mima McKim-Hill's murder rocked the close-knit community. (Supplied)She'd been abducted, strangled and sexually assaulted. I just collapsed, Shirley says.The brutal crime rocked the close-knit community.A police investigation and an inquest yielded no results. Months gave way to years without any arrests, and the case became Central Queensland's longest-running unsolved murder.As the decades passed, Shirley's frustration became all-consuming. In the 2000s, she launched her own quest for answers, teaming up with retired Vietnam veteran and amateur super sleuth, Trevor Sorenson.Together they dug deeper, analysing hundreds of pages of inquest transcripts, reinterviewing witnesses, revisiting crime scenes and dissecting Mima's final steps.Sister of murdered Brisbane woman chases leads after case runs coldPhoto shows graphic of photos of Deborah and headlines about her murder Deborah Smykalla was brutally murdered on Father's Day, 1981. Her killer has never been found. What they uncovered was a web of lies and a litany of investigative errors that they allege helped her suspected killer slip through the cracks.Their dogged pursuit for justice reignited public interest and police agreed to reopen the investigation in 2008.A breakthrough came in 2009, more than 40 years after Mima's death.Detectives closed in on a suspect. Mr Sorenson says they had enough evidence to nail him .But they were too late.'She never got to play her role'Shirley and Mima worked at the Capricornia Regional Electricity Board (CREB) in Rockhampton, a then-small country town with deep agricultural roots.The women regularly travelled throughout the region, demonstrating new electrical appliances for customers. They quickly grew close.Shirley Eldridge (back right) and Mima McKim-Hill (on her left) at a work conference in Rockhampton in late 1966. (Supplied)In many ways, Shirley says, they were polar opposites . We'd be walking along together and someone on a construction site would wolf-whistle. My thing was, I'd just walk on. Mima turned around and said: 'Oh, drop dead', Shirley laughs. That was Mima. She was confronting, she had spirit, and she was very loyal to her family and friends. The pair joined a local theatre and were both cast in an upcoming production, just weeks before Mima's death. She never got to play her role, Shirley says.Mima was a strong swimmer, pictured diving with her brother, Graham, at the Rockhampton pool. (Supplied)Mima's final hoursThe morning of March 9, 1967 began like any other at the McKim-Hill residence.Around 8:00am, Mima said goodbye to her mother and left for a scheduled work trip to Biloela, a couple of hours' drive south-west from Rockhampton, with her boss, Isobel Hare, 33. They took the company station wagon for the journey.Instead, they ended up heading south to Calliope, near Gladstone, to meet up with Isobel's boyfriend, Arthur Bambrick.Isobel arranged for Mima to pick her up in town in the afternoon and the pair went their separate ways.Afternoon arrived, but Mima didn't show. Isobel waited until dark. Around 7:30pm, she claims she saw the car race past her at high speed.With no ride back to Rockhampton, Bambrick dropped Isobel off and began making his way home to Hervey Bay.En route, he spotted the station wagon on a corrugated dirt detour track, which served as the old Gladstone bypass road, a few kilometres north of the town of Benaraby.The vehicle was unlocked and the keys were still in the ignition. But there was no sign of Mima.Bambrick called Isobel, who phoned Shirley, and in the dead of night the women drove to meet him at the vehicle.While he waited, Bambrick moved the car to the other side of the road and removed a novel from the dash to read.'Mima's out there in trouble'When they arrived around 3:00am, Shirley's gut feeling intensified. There was this log with a dirty white cloth on it — I remember it so clearly, she recalls.Mima McKim-Hill attending a ball in 1964. (Supplied)Her heart pounding, she peered into the mud-splattered car window.Mima's brown handbag was perched on the backseat, with cash and some coins still inside. Her savings book was also intact.The rear vision mirror had been pulled off and the fuse box was dangling. At this point, in my mind, it's like, Mima's out there in trouble, Shirley says.A bright pink fabric-covered button under the front seat caught Shirley's eye. It matched a new outfit Mima was planning to wear at a social club function that night.Believing Mima was with her boyfriend, Shirley says Isobel asked her to drive the car back to Rockhampton to return it to their employer.Mima was listed as a missing person the next day.Read more about Queensland cold cases:Two of Queensland's most brutal unsolved murders may have been committed by the same killerDeborah Smykalla's killer still unknown 43 years after brutal Brisbane murderTwo friends were murdered on Queensland’s 'highway of death'. Some believe their killer can still be foundThe murder of Betty Shanks has haunted Brisbane for decades. After 72 years, it still remains unsolvedWhile being questioned by detectives, Shirley says she offered to take them to the site where the car was abandoned. But they weren't interested.Police investigation a 'shemozzle'More than a fortnight later, on March 26, Alexander Weir was travelling with his family to Biloela when they pulled up at Collard Creek, approximately 80 kilometres from where Mima's car was found.He saw a rag in a running stream and tried to flick it with a stick. A human leg emerged from the water.Mima's father was called to identify the remains. Her body was badly decomposed.A newspaper article from the time of Mima McKim-Hill's murder. (Supplied)Isobel's yellow uniform that had been in the back of their work vehicle was tied around Mima's neck. Her cause of death was ruled as asphyxiation from strangulation. Her arm was broken. There was evidence of sexual assault. Mima was incredibly strong … but police told me she stood no chance, Shirley says.Mr Sorenson believes the initial police investigation was a shemozzle from the outset .Detectives from Brisbane were called in to assist local police and immediately pulled rank, he says, and Rockhampton officers relied on reports in the local newspaper to keep abreast of the situation. They wanted to run the show, they did not want to work with the regional detectives … they were kept at an arm's length, Mr Sorenson says. It wasn't until six weeks after the vehicle was located and four weeks after Mima's body was found that the Brisbane detectives decided to have critical and important locations … photographed by a police photographer such as where the abandoned CREB vehicle was located, he adds.Police examining the waterhole where Mima’s body was found. (Supplied)Witness statements weren't taken until after Mima's body was found. Those statements were taken basically on the run, he says. They were hand-written, scrawled, taken on the bonnet of a car or on the side of the road. The two-tone Ford and mystery menAll leads went nowhere and an inquest into Mima's murder began in earnest in November 1967.It was overseen by five different coroners, none of whom had any of the legal qualifications that they're required to have today , Mr Sorenson says. It was a farce. Shirley gave evidence and was reprimanded for insisting there were signs of a struggle where the vehicle was found, which police denied. The coroner interrupted and threatened to hold me in contempt of court if I continued to contradict, she says.Two key lines of inquiry were pursued.According to witness reports, on the afternoon Mima disappeared, three young men aged between 19 and 23 were seen on the road where her car was found in a blue two-tone 1960 Ford Customline with NSW number plates.The occupants of the Ford Customline with a unique mascot were seen talking to Mima on the day she disappeared. (Supplied)The Customline sported a unique bull mascot with red eyes.One witness reported seeing Mima in her vehicle speaking with one of the men.But despite a nationwide search, it amounted to nothing.A vehicle of interest, seen in the area on the day Mima disappeared, sported a unique bull mascot with red eyes. (Supplied)A new suspect emergesThere were also multiple sightings of a large green prime-mover and tanker trailer on the road where Mima vanished.One witness saw it parked some 300 metres from where her work vehicle was abandoned.Mima McKim-Hill dressed for a job interview in 1964. (Supplied)The driver was identified as 27-year-old Erich Johann Seefuss, originally from Germany but living in Redcliffe, north of Brisbane.He was questioned by police for 17 hours before being released.On that crucial March 9 afternoon, Mr Seefuss admitted to driving his rig in the area. He regularly drove return trips from Rockhampton to Sydney carrying tallow from abbatoirs and knew the region well.He gave evidence at the inquest and vehemently denied any involvement in Mima’s murder, but Mr Sorenson alleges he spun a web of lies . Using an original witness as a guide, he's spent years trying to untangle them. Seefuss deliberately gave false details regarding times, locations and reasons for his movements and non-movements, he says. He lied about where he was parked, he lied about having a thermostat problem with his truck … he claims he went down to Yeppoon to see a nephew but never saw him … the list goes on. Geoff Smith, a retired long-distance truck driver who worked for the same company as Mr Seefuss, came forward in late 2016​ and discounted large parts of his story. This witness knew Seefuss and his truck very well and on that very same day, had come down the Detour Road and saw Seefuss’s truck abandoned on the side of the road … he looked for Seefuss and he couldn’t see him,” Mr Sorensen says. Yet, Seefus says he was asleep, parked much further down the road. Mr Sorenson says Mr Smith, who was also a qualified motor mechanic, crawled under the tanker and concluded it had been stationary for a lengthy amount of time . Smith has [also] been emphatic that Seefuss' claims of having had thermostat problems were false as the truck would not have been able to be driven the lengthy distances which it did cover, Mr Sorensen says.'Wrong place, wrong time'Mr Sorenson believes it was a crime of opportunity.He says Mima likely pulled over onto the side of the bypass road to read her book or sleep to pass time while she waited for Isobel.He alleges Mr Seefuss spotted her by chance, abducted and attacked her, then drove to Collard Creek to dump her body.Mima’s body was found in Collard Creek near Biloela. (Supplied) Mima was unfortunately in the wrong place at the wrong time, Mr Sorenson says. It comes down to one person and one person only. It all points circumstantially at Seefuss. The inquest ruled Mima's death was caused by some person or persons unknown .Mima McKim-Hill graduated in 1964 as an Associate of the London College of Music and Performing Arts. (Supplied)Mr Sorenson says he spoke with Mr Seefuss' daughter, who detailed years of violent and problematic behaviour by her father, tracing back to his youth in Germany.She said she wanted a ringside seat if he was charged with Mima's murder and the case went to trial, according to Mr Sorenson.'There's no such thing as closure'By late 2009, Mr Sorenson says Queensland cold case detectives informed him and Shirley they had enough evidence to question and potentially charge Mr Seefuss, who was living in South Australia. When they got the green light, they rang the South Australian police to check he was still in situ … and they got a phone call back: 'Forget it, he's dead'. He had died six weeks earlier from cancer. I felt as though I'd been slapped hard across the face, Shirley says. It was just heartbreaking. Mima McKim-Hill learning how to ride a scooter at 17. (Supplied)Mr Seefuss was cremated, ruling out the chance of securing DNA evidence.Mima's grieving parents died without knowing what happened to their daughter. Her younger brother, Graham, had a fatal heart attack in his 50s, less than a kilometre away from where Mima's body was found.Mr Sorenson believes the case was bungled at the peak of poor police practices and procedures.Original evidence has been retested using modern forensic techniques.As of 2025, the investigation remains open, with a $250,000 reward for anyone with information that leads to a conviction.Mr Sorenson hopes police will one day publicly name Mima's alleged killer.Shirley Eldridge has written a book where she claims to unmask Mima’s killer. (Supplied)In Shirley's book about the case, which she says she felt duty-bound to write, she alleges Mr Seefus was responsible for her friend's murder.Now in her 70s and living in Western Australia, a long way from her hometown, she says she's found peace . There's no such thing as closure, Shirley says. I'm at peace with it. Queensland Police has been contacted for comment.Shirley Eldridge and Trevor Sorenson teamed up to try and solve Mima’s case. full_text: Trump activates National Guard in Washington, takes over local police Donald Trump announces National Guard deployment to 'rescue' Washington DCBy Brad Ryan and North America correspondent Kamin Gock in Washington DCTopic:World Politics9h ago9 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 4:10pmLoading...In short:US President Donald Trump says he is cracking down on crime in Washington DC through a federal takeover of the local police force.He has also announced plans to deploy at least 800 National Guard members in the US capital.Local authorities are pushing back on the plan, pointing to data that shows a substantial crime decrease since a post-pandemic surge in violence.abc.net.au/news/donald-trump-washington-dc-crime-national-guard-federal-takeover/105640322Link copiedShareShare articleDonald Trump says his administration is seizing control of the Washington DC police department and deploying the National Guard to crack down on local crime and clear the city of homelessness.The US president has been warning the capital of a federal takeover since a former Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) staffer was allegedly assaulted during an attempted carjacking last week.The unusual move represents another push to expand his presidential powers to new areas by utilising emergency powers. Mr Trump said Chicago could be next. Hopefully LA is watching, he added.But Washington represents an easier starting point because, as the national capital, it comes under federal control. Congress has ultimate jurisdiction over the city, but the president can take control of the police department for 30 days if he determines there is an emergency.Speaking at a White House press conference, Mr Trump said at least 800 National Guard troops would be deployed in an effort to rescue our nation's capital from crime, bloodshed, bedlam and squalor . Our capital city has been overtaken by violent gangs and bloodthirsty criminals, he said. We will bring in the military if it's needed, by the way. Local data shows violent crime has decreased in recent years after a crime wave in 2023, which authorities described as a post-pandemic spike. Washington DC imposes curfew in post-pandemic crime surgePhoto shows A street sign says 'NW U ST' under a traffic light. There are high rise apartments with balconies behind it.Washington DC is among major American cities dealing with a post-COVID surge in youth violence, and responding by enforcing a night-time curfew. But will it work?In January this year, the Department of Justice said violent crime was down 35 per cent on the previous year, and had hit a 30-year low. Preliminary police data says it has fallen another 26 per cent this year.But homicide rates remain high. Centers for Disease Control data shows DC had more murders per capita than any of the 50 US states, though city-specific data suggests St Louis, New Orleans and Detroit have higher murder rates.Because the District of Columbia is not a state, the US government — via Congress — has additional authority over Washington DC. The city's residents elect a mayor and local councillors, but the district does not have a governor and Congress retains ultimate control.Mayor Muriel Bowser, a Democrat, argues the city is having significant success managing crime. She has previously taken measures widely seen as designed to fend off federal intervention — including the removal of Washington's Black Lives Matter Plaza in March.Washington attorney-general Brian Schwalb described Mr Trump's move as unprecedented, unnecessary and unlawful. Loading Twitter contentBut Mr Trump pointed to recent incidents such as the shooting death of a 21-year-old intern working for a Republican congressman, and the alleged attack on former DOGE staffer Edward Coristine, better known by the alias Big Balls .The president last week shared a photograph of the 19-year-old, and warned the federal government would take control if DC doesn't get its act together .He said Attorney-General Pam Bondi would oversee the police force.A small group of protesters gathered outside the White House after the announcement.One of them, Jay Ryan, said he felt it was important to stand up to the president's power play . Where were the National Guard troops on January 6 when we had an attack on the Capitol? Trump did nothing for hours, he said. He's becoming an authoritarian and we need to make a stand and stop him now. Jay Ryan and Susan Gamble oppose Donald Trump's move. (ABC News: Cameron Schwarz)Mr Trump's announcement follows his decision to deploy the National Guard in Los Angeles to quell protests over local deportation efforts. full_text: Three shootings in suburban Perth put police on high alert Three shootings and arson in suburban Perth potentially linked to organised crimeCBy Cason HoGBy Grace BurmasTopic:Crime19h ago19 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 6:40amA police officer in front of the Smoke Station shop in Cannington. (ABC News: West Matteeussen)In short:Several shootings at suburban Perth tobacco stores are prompting police to investigate a potential turf war .Businesses were shot at in Cannington and Ballajura, while a store in Huntingdale was the site of suspected arson.Police say the attacks replicate tactics used in the illicit tobacco trade, in an apparent attempt to extort legitimate Perth businesses.abc.net.au/news/arson-extortion-shooting-perth-cannington-ballajura-huntingdale/105636608Link copiedShareShare articleA string of shootings and fires targeted at tobacco stores in Perth's suburbs are part of a potential turf war racket of arson and extortion , detectives say.WA Police detectives are probing three shootings and two fires which occurred over the past three days.Two of the incidents occurred at the same smoke shop on Cecil Avenue in Cannington, south of Perth, in the early hours of Saturday morning.The Cannington store was targeted several times. (ABC News: West Matteeussen)Police say the first shooting occurred about 1:10am, when two shots penetrated the store's metal roller shutter and a glass window.Two off-road motorcycles were observed nearby at the time, which were seen crossing Albany Highway into bushland.Police received reports of the same store being shot at again the following morning, around 4am, by two people in a black sedan.A vehicle parked outside the store, which had a 27-year-old security guard inside, was also shot at.Police say both the building and the car were damaged in the shooting, but the man was unharmed and is assisting with the investigation.Ballajura City Shopping Centre Candy Store was shot at and set alight. (ABC News: Cason Ho)Later on Sunday morning, a pub adjacent to a tobacco store at a shopping complex in Ballajura was targeted in broad daylight about 9am.Could other states adopt WA's gun laws?Photo shows Gun imageWA Police Minister Reece Whitby says officials from two states have reached out to discuss its strict new gun law reforms as firearm control groups call for a national approach.Police say gunshots damaged a window and vehicle.The alleged offenders returned to the same shopping complex on Monday and set fire to another store, just metres away from the pub, according to police.The same store was targeted by arson attacks on two separate occasions earlier this year in January and July.In another incident around 2am on Monday, alleged offenders forced their way into another store on Pipit Close in Huntingdale, south of Perth, and set fire to the premises.Escalation of violenceWA Police Commander Gordon Fairman said he believed all of the incidents were linked. Arson and drive-by shootings are plays straight out of the book of organised crime, he said. Over the last six months there's been an escalation of violence against tobacco businesses in Perth.Commander Gordon Fairman says police are working to ensure the violence doesn't escalate. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto) We've seen the level of violence in other jurisdictions and we are throwing everything we have at this investigation to make sure they do not escalate any further in Perth. 'Turf war' targets businessesCommander Fairman indicated the targeted stores were lawful businesses. It appears that arson and extortion are being used to close legitimate businesses — this appears to be part of a turf war, he said.On Sunday, Acting Superintendent, Eamon Flanagan, said the serious and organised crime division has thrown significant resources at the investigation.He said there was no evidence to suggest the targeted store owner is involved in the illicit tobacco industry. We do have a number of suspects, he said.Police say they have several suspects as they investigate the shooting in Cannington, and incidents elswhere. (ABC News: West Matteeussen)The same Cannington smoke shop was the target of another incident about a month ago when a vehicle attempted to ram-raid the premises.Two people were charged in relation to that incident.Police Commissioner Col Blanch said detectives were investigating whether these attacks were violent intimidation tactics.The Police Commissioner suspects the tactics used in Perth are similar to attacks in the eastern states. ( ABC News: James Carmody ) We have seen over east a number of these incidents occurring where we have seen gunshots fired into premises and arson being committed on stores … we suspect that is a replication of those types of offences, he said. We are taking this extremely seriously. Lucrative marketIn Australia about 70 per cent of the price of cigarettes is tax paid to the government. The illicit tobacco trade sells untaxed cigarettes which can be two to three times cheaper.Authorities have been attempting to tackle the illicit trade, and organised crime related to the trade, across the country — in March the federal government announced additional funding to curb the lucrative market.The black market behind your cheap cigarettes Photo shows Cosco Valencia at Port PhillipCash-only stores, unmarked white vans, and a shipping container with falsified documents. Where does Australia's illegal cigarette trade begin?According to police there were on average two arson attacks a week in Victoria linked to the black market.Commander Fairman said there were a series of similar offences in WA last year. That resulted in offenders being charged in every instance. It's my hope, and it's my promise, that that's what we'll achieve in this instance here, he said. Organised crime are not interested in tobacco. They're interested in money. This is about establishing control of an illicit trade and making millions of dollars. Gun laws reduce risk: PremierPremier Roger Cook said the state government's new gun laws, which are in the process of being implemented, would help reduce the risk posed by firearms in the community. The ongoing risks associated with gun violence, the only way we can get on top of that is the full implementation of our gun laws, he said.For Premier Roger Cook, new gun laws mean a safer community. (ABC News: Jake Sturmer) They're the biggest reform of Western Australia's gun laws in over two decades. full_text: Murder victim set alight in 'act of extreme cruelty', partner tells court Partner of murder victim set alight at Woodville West house tells court of 'permanent' impactEBy Eva BlandisTopic:Homicide19h ago19 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 6:34amAlessandro Cavuoto was found guilty of murdering his housemate Todd Bradmore at a Woodville West house in March 2021. (Supplied: Facebook)In short: A woman has told a court the sounds of her partner's distress as he was murdered by his roommate continues to haunt her. Alessandro Giovanni Cavuoto set Todd Bradmore alight at the home they shared in Adelaide's west in 2021. What's next? Cavuoto, who will be sentenced next week, told the court via his lawyer that he intended to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict.abc.net.au/news/todd-bradmore-family-partner-victim-impact-statements-court/105636496Link copiedShareShare articleA woman has told a court how she watched helplessly as her partner was set on fire and murdered by his housemate in Adelaide's western suburbs more than four years ago.Warning: This story contains content which some readers may find distressing.Alessandro Giovanni Cavuoto, 37, appeared in South Australia's Supreme Court on Monday where he heard victim impact statements from the family and friends of his victim, 31-year-old Todd Bradmore.The court previously found Cavuoto guilty of murdering Mr Bradmore by setting him on fire just after 3.30am on March 17, 2021.Todd Bradmore was murdered by his housemate Alessandro Cavuoto in 2021.He was found not guilty of two aggravated counts of creating likelihood of serious harm to two other people — one of whom was Mr Bradmore's partner Aisha Bistrovic.The court previously heard Mr Bradmore suffered burns to 80 per cent of his body when Cavuoto doused him with two-stroke fuel at their Woodville West home.He was rushed to the Royal Adelaide Hospital where he later succumbed to his injuries two days later on March 19, 2021.In her victim impact statement on Monday, Ms Bistrovic detailed the events of that night. I watched helplessly as he was doused in petrol and set on fire, she said. This image and the sounds of him yelling and moaning in pain haunts me every day. Ms Bistrovic said her partner's murder had left a permanent mark on my life . I want the court to understand that what was done to Todd was an act of extreme cruelty, she said. I and many others have to carry the pain of losing an amazing person, a good friend and a loving partner due to Alex's sick and disturbing act. A police photo of the crime scene inside the Woodville West home. (Supplied: Courts SA)A victim impact statement was also read to the court on behalf of Billie Dawkins, who was also present at the home. The horror didn't end there, for a long time I couldn't sleep, she said in the statement. Every time I closed my eyes, I would see Todd burning, running towards me. I would feel that same terror rushing through my body. Even now, I still have nightmares. In them I can hear Todd's screams - a sound that will haunt me forever. That night, I witnessed a level of evil that changed me. In a victim impact statement read to the court on her behalf, Mr Bradmore's mother, Venette Ramsey, described her son as a caring, loveable, kind-hearted and compassionate person . I still struggle every day because Todd was your friend, and he helped you, she said. I have never understood how anyone could treat someone with such malice to take someone else's life. Cavuoto does not accept guilty verdictProsecutor Taryn Amos told the court there had been a high-level of planning by Mr Cavuoto . He walked into that study, he made the threats that he did … before he threw the two-stroke [fuel] at Mr Bradmore, she said. The act of setting Mr Bradmore alight, in my respectful submission, is a callous and brutal act which saw Mr Bradmore experience significant pain and suffering … no doubt excruciating pain. Alessandro Cavuoto was arrested interstate and extradited back to Adelaide. (ABC News: Claire Campbell)Barrister Scott Henchliffe KC, for Cavuoto, told the court his client did not accept the guilty verdict. I'm instructed he's in the process of arranging … funding for an appeal, he said.Mr Henchliffe said in the lead-up to the incident, Cavuoto was really quite seriously affected by Mr Bradmore's behaviour .He told the court that Cavuoto didn't intend to set Mr Bradmore alight but was instead using the fuel to threaten him, before the argument escalated. Having said all of that, of course it still remains a very serious offence, and it had devastating consequences, he said.However, Ms Amos said the offending had a degree of calculation . He came armed with the necessary weapon to commit this offence, in my respectful submission, this was not a purely opportunistic or reactionary offence, it had a degree of calculation about it and it has some elements of pre-meditation, she said.Cavuoto, who is yet to formally lodge an appeal, will be sentenced next week.Posted 19h ago19 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 6:34amShare optionsCopy full_text: Fresh appeal to find man charged with rape in Fitzroy 50 years ago Fresh appeal to find George Karakis who was charged over a Melbourne rape 50 years agoTopic:CrimeMon 11 AugMonday 11 AugustMon 11 Aug 2025 at 12:38amPolice have issued a fresh appeal for information about George Karakis who allegedly fled after being charged with rape in 1974. (Supplied: Victoria Police)In short:Police have launched a fresh plea for information to locate George Karakis, who was charged with breaking into a woman's Fitzroy home and raping her in 1974.An image of what Mr Karakis may look like now has been released.What's next?Anyone with information is being urged to contact Crime Stoppers.abc.net.au/news/victoria-police-george-karakis-rape-fresh-appeal/105635412Link copiedShareShare articlePolice have renewed an appeal to find a man who they have not been able to locate for more than 50 years after being charged with breaking into a Melbourne home and raping a woman.The woman, who was 30 at the time, told police she was asleep in her Fitzroy home when she was awoken by a stranger and assaulted in the early hours of the morning on July 22,1974.Police arrested George Karakis nine days later.He was charged with rape, burglary and indecent assault and released on bail with a $1,000 surety.Police say he failed to appear in the Fitzroy Magistrates’ Court the following October.A digitally rendered image of what Mr Karakis could look like at the age of 78. (Supplied: Victoria Police)There was no sign of Mr Karakis until 1990 when police officers in New South Wales believed they had found him in Sydney's east, but he allegedly disappeared before they could execute a warrant to arrest him.A public appeal for information in 2015 failed to locate Mr Karakis.Victoria Police has today reissued a photo taken of Mr Karakis upon his arrest in 1974 as well as a digitally generated image of what he could look like at the age of 78 today.Detective Senior Constable Ruby Roberts said the alleged victim was now aged in her eighties. This crime changed her life forever and 50 years is a long time to live without the justice we would so dearly like to give her. At the time of his arrest, Mr Karakis was a 27-year-old living in Gore Street, Fitzroy with his wife, sister and brother-in-law.Police said the Türkiye-born man required a Greek translator during his 1974 interview.He has been described as being about 162cm tall with brown eyes and a two centimetre scar over his left eyebrow. There will absolutely be people out there who … may even know where he is now residing, Senior Constable Roberts said. Given the length of time, there is also the possibility he has passed away. We just want to find answers so we can close this chapter in our victim's life. Anyone with information about Mr Karakis or his whereabouts is urged to contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or www.crimestoppersvic.com.au.Posted Yesterday at 12:38amMon 11 Aug 2025 at 12:38am, updated Yesterday at 12:48amMon 11 Aug 2025 at 12:48amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMoment the PM gained confidence Australia could recognise a Palestinian stateTopic:Foreign AffairsPhoto shows Albanese and Wong enter the prime minister's courtyard, walking up to two lecterns.Albanese says Netanyahu 'in denial' about conflict's impact on civiliansLIVEPhoto shows Benjamin Netanyahu looking up and to the right of the camera at a press conference.'Israel has succeeded': Final words from journalist killed in GazaTopic:JournalismPhoto shows A young Palestinian man in a press vest and helmet speaks into a microphone featuring the Al Jazeera logo.Reserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chartPilot in fatal chopper crash to take stand in croc wrangler's trialLIVEPhoto shows Matt Wright has brown hair and is wearing a button-up shirt as he walks towards the court.Popular nowReserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chart'Endless' trespassers cost farmers thousands and endanger lifeTopic:Beef Cattle FarmingPhoto shows Geoff Pearson stands in a paddock with cattle behind himYoung Australian hospitalised after ChatGPT useTopic:TechnologyPhoto shows An illustration of a young boy staring at a computer. full_text: Car thief who crashed on Hobart bridge still on the run, police say Driver missing after stolen car crashes on Hobart's Bowen BridgeMBy Monty JackaTopic:CrimeSun 10 AugSunday 10 AugustSun 10 Aug 2025 at 11:25pmA police boat searches the water under the Bowen Bridge. (ABC News: Simon Farrell)In short:The search for the driver of a stolen car that collided with a truck on Hobart's Bowen Bridge on Monday morning continues.An aerial and on-water search by police has been called off after the initial investigation found it highly unlikely the missing driver ended up in the River Derwent.What's next?Police say the missing driver is likely to be injured, as the car he was in rolled over.abc.net.au/news/bowen-bridge-crash-stolen-car-aerial-search-hobart/105635680Link copiedShareShare articleA car thief involved in an accident that caused hours of traffic delays in Hobart on Monday morning is on the run and likely injured, according to police.Tasmania police say the dark green Hyundai Excel, stolen from Glenorchy overnight, rolled during the collision with a truck on Bowen Bridge at about 5.50am.A rescue helicopter is also involved in the search. (ABC News: Simon Farrell)Nearby motorists who witnessed the crash went to assist the drivers, but the driver of the car allegedly fled the scene.Tasmania Police Acting Inspector John Rafferty said police officers were on the bridge within two to three minutes of the incident, but were unable to locate the missing driver.He said police boats and a helicopter were called in to assist with the search, after early concerns the driver had jumped into the river.Loading Facebook contentThe marine search, which initially centred on the shoreline and underneath the bridge, has since been called off. From the initial investigation, we consider it highly unlikely that the driver has been thrown from the vehicle or that the driver has in fact jumped from the bridge, Mr Rafferty said.'Likely' driver has been injuredPolice said the crash occurred when the car pulled in front of the truck while both vehicles were travelling east across the bridge.The driver of the truck was uninjured. It's possible and probably likely the driver [of the car] has sustained some sort of injury, Acting Inspector Rafferty said. We strongly encourage that person to seek some sort of medical attention. Debris is swept up from the westbound lane after the crash. (ABC News: Simon Farrell)Police said it was difficult for witnesses to provide details on the whereabouts of the missing driver given the time of day, poor visibility and weather conditions at the time. The weather conditions were cold this morning, also visibility was poor with the fog rolling in and the Bridgewater Jerry as we know it, Mr Rafferty said.Tasmanian Police say it's likely the missing driver was injured in the crash. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)The Bridgewater Jerry is the name of a local fog formation that occasionally blankets the River Derwent, particularly during the cooler months.Police are working with the Department of State Growth to establish what cameras were operating in the area.Crash impacted traffic for hoursThe car involved in the crash had been stolen from a property on Tolosa Street in Glenorchy, police said.The crash and traffic division caused some peak-hour delays for motorists. (ABC News: Simon Farrell)Police had earlier said there were multiple occupants of the Hyundai, but have now confirmed the search involves only looking for a driver.Anyone with information about the theft or who may have seen or captured footage of the Hyundai on dashcam overnight is asked to contact Glenorchy police.Posted Sun 10 Aug 2025 at 11:25pmSunday 10 Aug 2025 at 11:25pmSun 10 Aug 2025 at 11:25pm, updated 2h ago2 hours agoMon 11 Aug 2025 at 11:33pmShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMoment the PM gained confidence Australia could recognise a Palestinian stateTopic:Foreign AffairsPhoto shows Albanese and Wong enter the prime minister's courtyard, walking up to two lecterns.Albanese says Netanyahu 'in denial' about conflict's impact on civiliansLIVEPhoto shows Benjamin Netanyahu looking up and to the right of the camera at a press conference.'Israel has succeeded': Final words from journalist killed in GazaTopic:JournalismPhoto shows A young Palestinian man in a press vest and helmet speaks into a microphone featuring the Al Jazeera logo.Reserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chartPilot in fatal chopper crash to take stand in croc wrangler's trialLIVEPhoto shows Matt Wright has brown hair and is wearing a button-up shirt as he walks towards the court.Popular nowReserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chart'Endless' trespassers cost farmers thousands and endanger lifeTopic:Beef Cattle FarmingPhoto shows Geoff Pearson stands in a paddock with cattle behind himYoung Australian hospitalised after ChatGPT useTopic:TechnologyPhoto shows An illustration of a young boy staring at a computer. full_text: Former CEO agrees to pay back $150k to charity she's accused of defrauding Gabrielle Morrissey accused of misappropriating funds from domestic violence charity she ledCBy Catherine HanrahanTopic:CharitiesSun 10 AugSunday 10 AugustSun 10 Aug 2025 at 7:40pmGabrielle Morrissey reached a confidential settlement with domestic violence charity Women and Children First. (Supplied)In short:Gabrielle Morrissey reached a confidential settlement after she agreed to pay back $150,000 in lieu of funds she had been accused of appropriating for her personal benefit.Dr Morrissey was CEO of domestic violence charity Women and Children First until she resigned in 2024.The settlement terms include the charity agreeing to send a letter to NSW Police saying it was content for a fraud investigation to be terminated.abc.net.au/news/women-and-children-first-dv-shelter-gabrielle-morrissey-funds/105620310Link copiedShareShare articleThe former CEO of a Sydney domestic violence charity has reached a confidential settlement after she agreed to pay back $150,000 in lieu of funds she had been accused of appropriating.Gabrielle Morrissey was CEO of Sydney charity Women and Children First, which supports women experiencing domestic violence, from November 2022 to June 2024.The ABC has seen a document in which Women and Children First accuse Dr Morrissey of defrauding the charity, and alleging the money was paid out for what appeared to be her personal benefit.The charity's board chair Julie Ryan said in a statement that Dr Morrissey resigned from her position on June 15 last year. In June 2024, Women and Children First made a complaint to NSW Police in relation to Dr Morrissey. NSW Police commenced an investigation into the complaint, she said.Dr Morrissey is now the CEO of Women's Resilience Centre, which operates a charity shop called The Resilience Circle. (ABC News: Patrick Thomas) Without any admission of liability, Women and Children First and Dr Morrissey have reached a confidential settlement in relation to the matters subject of the complaint. Women and Children First and Dr Morrissey now regard the matter as resolved from a civil perspective. The confidential settlement includes Dr Morrissey agreeing to pay $150,000 to Women and Children First, in return for being released from civil liability by the charity in relation to the complaint it made to police.The settlement terms also included the charity agreeing to send a letter to NSW Police saying that it was content for the fraud investigation to be terminated.Dr Morrissey told the ABC she had no comment to make on the confidential settlement.Do you know more?If you have any information about a story, contact Amy Greenbank.Morrissey now CEO of another charityWomen and Children First received $2.2 million from governments in 2023-24, according to the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission.Dr Morrissey is now the CEO of Women's Resilience Centre, a Sydney charity that runs online programs to help Australian women recover from domestic violence.Women's Resilience Centre did not respond to the ABC's request for comment. Dr Morrissey's biography on the Harper Collins Australia website states she has been a sexologist since 1990 and has worked in sex therapy, education and research in Australia, Britain and the US.She has published her books including Spicy Sex — 52 Sumptuous and Saucy Sex Recipes for Red-hot Loving Every Week of the Year, and Urge: Hot Secrets for Great Sex.Dr Morrissey received her Masters in Human Sexuality Education from the University of Pennsylvania and her PhD in Human Sexuality/Health Science from Curtin University in Perth, Western Australia, according to her profile on Australian speakers' bureau Celebrity Speakers.Posted Sun 10 Aug 2025 at 7:40pmSunday 10 Aug 2025 at 7:40pmSun 10 Aug 2025 at 7:40pm, updated Yesterday at 12:07amMon 11 Aug 2025 at 12:07amShare optionsCopy full_text: Three wounded after shooting in New York City's Times Square Teenager in custody after three people shot and wounded in New York City's Times SquareTopic:CrimeSat 9 AugSaturday 9 AugustSat 9 Aug 2025 at 11:00amTimes Square is one of New York City's most iconic tourist spots. (Reuters: Hugh Gentry)abc.net.au/news/times-square-shooting-new-york-three-injured-gun-recovered/105632984Link copiedShareShare articleThree people have been wounded in an early morning shooting in Times Square, the New York Police Department says.The people — an 18-year-old woman, a 19-year-old man, and a 65-year-old man — are in a stable condition in hospital, an NYPD spokesperson said.A 17-year-old boy is in custody, the police department added, and officers had recovered a firearm from the scene.The shooting took place at about 1:20am local time, and followed a verbal altercation between the alleged shooter and one of the victims, the NYPD said.It is not yet known whether the shooter or any of the victims knew each other.Mass shootings are relatively common in the United States, where guns are widely available.The incident at one of New York's most iconic tourist spots comes after another high-profile shooting in a Manhattan office tower last month, which left four people dead, including a senior Blackstone executive and an NYPD officer.New York experienced record-low shooting incidents and victims in the first seven months of this year, as well as in July, according to a statement published by the city's police department on August 4.Crime is a key electoral issue for America's largest city, which is set to hold mayoral elections in full_text: Mother guilty of stabbing daughter's boyfriend she thought was home invader Jennifer Mui Len Chin found guilty of stabbing her daughter's boyfriend at her Parkwood homeDBy David WeberTopic:CourtsFri 8 AugFriday 8 AugustFri 8 Aug 2025 at 9:59amJennifer Chin was found guilty of causing bodily harm to her daughter's teenage boyfriend. (ABC News: David Weber)In short:Jennifer Mui Len Chin was found guilty of causing bodily harm to her daughter's 14-year-old boyfriend, whom she stabbed several times after finding him semi-naked in her home.She had claimed she thought he was an intruder and was only trying to protect her family, but the jury rejected her defence.What's next?Chin's bail was renewed, and she will be sentenced next month. abc.net.au/news/jennifer-mui-len-chin-daughters-boyfriend-stabbing-verdict/105630752Link copiedShareShare articleA mother who stabbed her 14-year-old daughter’s secret boyfriend with a kitchen knife because she thought he was an intruder when she found him semi-naked in a bedroom has been found guilty of causing him bodily harm.Jennifer Mui Len Chin had admitted stabbing the 14-year-old in her Parkwood home in 2023 after finding him hiding under a doona in her husband's bedroom, using a knife she'd asked her six-year-old son to fetch from the kitchen.Chin said she did not know the teen had been invited into her house and was only trying to protect her family from someone she feared was a naked armed stranger.But the jury did not agree, finding her guilty of the single charge of causing bodily harm after deliberating for three hours.Secret romanceThe court had heard the woman's daughter, who was also 14, was having a secret romance with the youth and snuck him into the house, where they had sex.The teen had been forbidden by her mother to have a boyfriend because of Chin's strict Christian beliefs, but the court heard she had nonetheless managed to sneak him into the house for secret trysts on multiple occasions before the stabbing.The jury heard Ms Chin;s daughter had snuck the teenager into the house because her mother didn't allow her to have boyfriends. (ABC News: Glyn Jones)On the night in question, Chin had become suspicious when she saw the door to her husband's bedroom was closed, and forced her way in past her daughter to discover the bare chested teen under the covers of the bed.She had told the court she tried to pull the doona off him, thinking he may have been fully naked. A tussle over the bedclothes ensued, as the mother asked the teen who he was. I'm sorry was all the boy said in response, while her daughter claimed he was homeless and said she was trying to help him.Scared, panicking , and convinced the youth was an intruder, Chin said she armed herself to protect my kids , calling on her six-year-old to go get me a knife .As she raised the knife above her head, her daughter warned Ma, you'll be the one who goes to jail for this! I don't care, he's an intruder, she responded.'Chaotic, crazy' sceneThe teenager was near the front door of the home when Chin stabbed him twice in the chest.She had claimed he had turned and taken steps towards her, looking cocky . I just want him to stay away from me and my kids, she told the court.The teenager was near the front door of this Parkwood home when his girlfriend's mother stabbed him repeatedly with a kitchen knife. (ABC News: Glyn Jones)Chin's lawyer Mark Andrews spoke of the “chaotic, crazy few seconds between the bedroom and the front door” and the dread Chin must've felt when she found the bare chested teen in her husband's bedroom. He said she did not know if her daughter was in the bedroom under threat, force or coercion . Mr Andrews told the jury it was lawful to take action to cause a home invader to leave, or to stop them committing an offence.Mother was 'angry'But prosecutor Chadd Graham said the state did not accept the self-defence claim, and there were no grounds for the belief he was a home invader who presented a threat. He ran to the front door and he tried to get out, Mr Graham said, rejecting her claim that he stepped towards her.Jennifer Mui Len Chin admitted stabbing her teenage daughter's boyfriend, but maintained she did so to protect her family. (ABC News: David Weber)He said she was angry , because she did not want her daughter to have a boyfriend, and failed to call 000 after the bleeding youth left the home with her daughter because she knew she had gone too far .The boy suffered wounds to the left and right of his chest, and more superficial cuts on his back near his shoulders. Chin's bail was continued and she will return to court on September 3 for sentencing.Boy 'scarred for life'Judge Belinda Lonsdale said she did not think Chin was at risk of reoffending, but it was a very serious offence and the state may ask for a term of imprisonment.Outside court, the victim's father welcomed the verdict.The man described the events in 2023 as a nightmare for his son, saying he would carry the trauma through his life, along with his physical scars.Jennifer Chin made no comment as she left court after being found guilty of causing her daughter's boyfriend bodily harm. (ABC News: David Weber)Chin had nothing to say to waiting media as she left the court.LoadingPosted Fri 8 Aug 2025 at 9:59amFriday 8 Aug 2025 at 9:59amFri 8 Aug 2025 at 9:59am, updated Fri 8 Aug 2025 at 10:47amFriday 8 Aug 2025 at 10:47amFri 8 Aug 2025 at 10:47amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMoment the PM gained confidence Australia could recognise a Palestinian stateTopic:Foreign AffairsPhoto shows Albanese and Wong enter the prime minister's courtyard, walking up to two lecterns.Albanese says Netanyahu 'in denial' about conflict's impact on civiliansLIVEPhoto shows Benjamin Netanyahu looking up and to the right of the camera at a press conference.'Israel has succeeded': Final words from journalist killed in GazaTopic:JournalismPhoto shows A young Palestinian man in a press vest and helmet speaks into a microphone featuring the Al Jazeera logo.Reserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chartPilot in fatal chopper crash to take stand in croc wrangler's trialLIVEPhoto shows Matt Wright has brown hair and is wearing a button-up shirt as he walks towards the court.Popular nowReserve Bank interest rate cut considered a near-certaintyLIVEPhoto shows Reserve Bank sign overlaid with inflation chart'Endless' trespassers cost farmers thousands and endanger lifeTopic:Beef Cattle FarmingPhoto shows Geoff Pearson stands in a paddock with cattle behind himYoung Australian hospitalised after ChatGPT useTopic:TechnologyPhoto shows An illustration of a young boy staring at a computer.
