full_text: Dobbing in a criminal? Don't do it on social media Crime Stoppers warn of risk of vigilante reaction, other concerns on crimes posted to social mediaBy Crystal McKayTopic:Crime6h ago6 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 7:43pmPosting to social media about local crimes does not help police make arrests, Crime Stoppers says. (ABC News: Rhiannon Shine)In short:Australians who see, hear or suspect criminal or suspicious behaviour are being asked to stop leaving vital information in group chats or social media threads and to instead report it to police through Crime Stoppers.Authorities say posting on social media can sometimes do more harm than good, as sharing unverified information can unintentionally escalate fear, lead to misidentification or incite vigilante behaviour.What's next?Not-for-profit organisation Crime Stoppers has launched a national campaign highlighting the dangers of posting crime on social media.abc.net.au/news/tasmania-police-call-on-community-to-not-post-crime-social-media/105668684Link copiedShareShare articleSocial media is littered with posts about crime.Facebook even has dedicated community-led groups for sharing information to warn others about local criminals.Perhaps you've joined one.But Australians are being urged to not only post about crime on social media, but to report it to authorities.Loading Facebook contentCrime Stoppers Tasmania chair David Daniels said posting to social media provided a false sense of action. Now that we're always online with our phones, it's easy to turn to social media to express our concern or warn others, Mr Daniels said. But typing isn't telling, and if that information never reaches police, they cannot act. So, while the social media may feel immediate and impactful, it does very little to help police track down the offenders or prevent crime or keep communities safe, he said. The real action means sharing the information appropriately [to Crime Stoppers or local police]. Crime Stoppers Tasmania created its online tip line in 2017. (Supplied: crimestopperstas.com.au)Crime Stoppers is a not-for-profit registered charity, separate to police, that relies on donations to operate.High Court finds media outlets are responsible for Facebook commentsPhoto shows A man is silhouetted against a video screen with an Facebook logo as he poses with a smartphoneHigh Court rules on whether media outlets are responsible for comments left on their Facebook pages.It is based on a model that started in New Mexico in the United States in the 1970s when a detective ran out of all leads on a brutal murder case.The detective reportedly arranged for a local television station to show a re-enactment of the murder and invited viewers to call in with information anonymously and offered a cash reward if it led to an arrest.It started an anonymous 'tips line' that became Crime Stoppers and spread around the world.Police unable to act on social postCan you help?Call Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000Report anonymously via the Crime Stoppers websiteOften, alleged offenders are outed by the community naming and shaming them, but if that information is not passed on to authorities through official channels, police are usually unable to investigate. We've had a man seen stealing tools from the rear of a work ute. Other people all post into a group who he is and where he can be found, Tasmania Police Commander Jo Stolp said. But nobody's actually told the police about it and so, we're not able to do anything. Recently, Tasmania Police have also seen social media posts about drug dealing near a park.Secretive nature of Crime Stoppers tip line means reward unclaimedPhoto shows Blue and white police tape in front of traffic accident sceneAn anonymous Tasmanian tipster is eligible for a reward, but they can't be tracked down due to the secretive nature of Crime Stoppers. You've got people on camera from someone's CCTV coming and going, but without a report either to Crime Stoppers or to police, we can't follow that up, Commander Stolp said.There has also been unreported CCTV footage posted to social media showing a person stealing mail from someone's home, and someone claiming to have a picture of the suspect's face. While it's good for people to know there is activity in their area, we like to be sure that it's actual activity, and that somebody is not necessarily being targeted unnecessarily, she said.Posting can lead to 'vigilante' responsePosting information about a crime to social media also carried its own risks, police said.Along with the possibility of spreading misinformation, posts could also incite vigilante responses.'Disgusting' youth disturbance in Big W fuels police probeTasmania Police is investigating a disturbance that broke out at a department store in Hobart's northern suburbs, as a video of the affray emerges.There was a chance the information or footage being shared was not really a crime at all, or could lead to the wrong person being identified as the culprit.Defamation lawyer Rowan Lyndon can attest to the impact of vigilante responses.Mr Lyndon said he was aware of at least one reported case, where a person who was falsely identified online as a paedophile was physically assaulted .There was also the risk of legal action against people who make accusations online that turn out to be false or defamatory, he said.These can range from paying damages — sometimes amounting to hundreds of thousands of dollars — to covering part of the claimant's legal costs, and even imprisonment.The 2024 Bondi Junction stabbings is one of the most recent cases to make national headlines.Within hours of the attack occurring, Benjamin Cohen was falsely named on social media as the assailant who killed six people at the shopping centre.Five women and one man were killed in the attack. (ABC News: Brendan Esposito)Photos of Mr Cohen were taken from his social media accounts and circulated by other users along with his name.The unconfirmed reports were then broadcast by a media outlet.But while the information turned out to be false, by then the damage had been done.Mr Cohen later sued the broadcaster for defamation and received an out-of-court settlement.He also called on the NSW Police to prosecute the social media users who incorrectly identified him.Why reporting officially mattersMr Daniels said in all of these cases, the intent might be right, but the outcome isn't . If the information stops at social media, then police can't act. Offenders stay under the radar and communities remain exposed, he said.To bring greater attention to this issue, Crime Stoppers has launched a nationwide campaign, Don't Just Post It, Report It!The campaign is urging people around Australia who see, hear or suspect criminal or suspicious behaviour to stop leaving vital information in group chats or social media threads, and start reporting it where it truly counts.Crime Stoppers is a not-for-profit registered charity separate to Tasmania Police and relies on donations to operate. (ABC News)People have the option of making an anonymous tip to Crime Stoppers, directly contacting their local police station, or in an emergency, calling triple-0. Crime Stoppers gives people a safe and anonymous way to speak up, Mr Daniels said. You don't have to give your name or make any formal statement or even go to court. All we ask is that you share what you know, so it can be properly assessed and potentially linked to other reports and acted on by police. It's simple and it helps solve and stop crime. David Daniels is the chair of Crimestoppers Tasmania. full_text: Son of Norway crown princess charged with rape, dozens of other offences Marius Borg Høiby, son of Norway crown princess charged with rape, dozens other offencesTopic:Law, Crime and Justice11h ago11 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 2:21pmMarius Borg Høiby is charged with four counts of rape. (AFP: Håkon Mosvold Larsen/NTB)In short:Marius Borg Høiby, the son of Norway's Crown Princess Mette-Marit, has been charged with 32 offences including four counts of rape.The prosecution is pushing for him to be treated equally regardless of his status in the royal family.The four counts of rape for which Mr Høiby is charged allegedly took place in 2018, 2023 and 2024.abc.net.au/news/marius-borg-h%C3%B8iby-son-of-norway-crown-princess-rape-charge/105669472Link copiedShareShare articleA son of Norway's crown princess has been charged with 32 offences including four rapes and several acts of violence and assault, a prosecutor said on Monday.Marius Borg Høiby, who was born from a relationship before Crown Princess Mette-Marit's married Crown Prince Haakon, has been under investigation since his arrest on August 4 last year on suspicion of assaulting a girlfriend.In addition to four counts of rape, the charges include domestic abuse against a former partner and several counts of violence, disturbing the peace, vandalism and violation of restraining orders against another former partner.He is also charged with filming the genitals of a number of women without their knowledge or consent, public prosecutor Sturla Henriksbo told reporters. The maximum penalty for the offences listed in the indictment is imprisonment of up to 10 years, he said. These are very serious acts that can leave lasting scars and destroy lives, Mr Henriksbo said. The fact that Marius Borg Høiby is a member of the royal family should, of course, not mean that he should be treated more lightly or more severely than if similar acts had been committed by others, the prosecutor said.Sturla Henriksbo says the son of Norway's crown princess has been charged with 32 offences. (Reuters: NTB/Jonas Fæste Laksekjon)The four rapes for which Mr Høiby is charged allegedly took place in 2018, 2023 and 2024, the last one after the police investigation began.Mr Høiby has already admitted to assault and vandalism in the August 2024 incident for which he was arrested.In a public statement 10 days after his arrest, he said he had acted under the influence of alcohol and cocaine after an argument , having suffered from mental troubles and struggling for a long time with substance abuse .Mr Høiby was propelled into the spotlight at the age of four when his mother married Norway's crown prince, with whom she went on to have two more children.He was raised by the royal couple alongside his step-siblings Princess Ingrid Alexandra and Prince Sverre Magnus, aged 21 and 19.Unlike them, however, he has no official public role.AFPPosted 11h ago11 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 2:21pmShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesZelenskyy says no 'unacceptable decisions' were made in White House talksLIVEPhoto shows Zelenskyy gestures with hands while speaking into microphones'Go home': Country everyone wants to visit is turning on touristsTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows Tourists taking a selfie.Baby girl found in Perth stormwater drain was dead for two weeksTopic:PolicePhoto shows A police car with a police woman leaning against it. full_text: Boy faces court over car theft that left 76yo tourist in coma Court refuses bail for 14yo charged over Kimberley car theft that left tourist in comaBy Giulia BertoglioABC KimberleyTopic:Courts17h ago17 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 8:20amThe 14-year-old faced the Halls Creek Children's Court on Monday. (ABC Kimberley: Ted O'Connor)In short:A teenager has faced the Halls Creek Children's Court over a car theft which left a 76-year-old South Australian tourist in hospital with life-threatening injuries.The court heard the boy was on bail at the time, accused of stealing a motor vehicle from the same petrol station in a separate incident.What's next?He was remanded in custody and will face court again in September.abc.net.au/news/boy-charged-halls-creek-kimberley-car-theft-tourist-caravan/105667440Link copiedShareShare articleA 14-year-old boy has been refused bail over a car theft in Western Australia's Kimberley, which left an elderly tourist in an induced coma.Police allege the boy, who cannot be identified due to his age, stole a ute which was connected to a caravan parked at the Shell service station in Halls Creek, about 2,800 kilometres north of Perth, on Saturday.It is alleged the 14-year-old drove off while the 76-year-old South Australian man was checking the safety of his caravan.The 76-year-old tourist was checking the safety of his caravan at the service station. (ABC Kimberley: Andrew Seabourne)The man sustained life-threatening injuries and was flown to Royal Darwin Hospital by the Royal Flying Doctor Service on Saturday afternoon.Police arrested and charged the teenager early Sunday morning with one count of stealing a motor vehicle and one count of grievous bodily harm when stealing a motor vehicle.'Dragged for metres'Police prosecutor Darren Clifton told the Halls Creek Children's Court the teenager had been nearby on an electric scooter when he saw the parked vehicle with the door open and the keys left in the ignition. The vehicle's owner, who was on a six-month holiday around Australia with his wife, was conducting a safety check while his partner was inside the petrol station. Sergeant Clifton told the court the man was dragged along the bitumen before the caravan ran over his chest. He said the teenager then drove into bushland, rendering the vehicle undriveable .The 14-year-old was arrested the following morning. Sergeant Clifton told Magistrate Tanya Watt that the teenager had made some admissions to stealing the vehicle and injuring the man, although he did not appreciate the extent of the injuries . The 76-year-old was flown to Royal Darwin Hospital from Halls Creek on Saturday. (ABC Kimberley: Ted O'Connor)Bail refusedSergeant Clifton told the court that at the time of his arrest, the boy was on bail, accused of stealing a motor vehicle from the same petrol station in a separate incident and driving it recklessly. He remains a significant danger to the community, he said.He said the 76-year-old's condition remained very, very grave .The boy's lawyer asked if he would be released to the bail house because of his young age. While Magistrate Watt acknowledged the boy's age, she refused the application. I have significant concerns for reoffending and for community safety, she said. full_text: Police officer details moment he was set upon by teenagers Court hears dramatic testimony from police officer during assault trial of teenager DBy David WeberTopic:Courts19h ago19 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 6:23amThe teenager is on trial in Perth Children's Court. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)In short: A teenage boy is on trial accused of assaulting a public officer after an incident near Perth Stadium last December.About 100 teenagers rode through the CBD on e-rideables, with some reportedly blocking traffic, kicking cars and doing wheelies.Senior Constable Mark Andrew Cooper told the court he had tried to seize an e-motorbike which was being charged when he was surrounded and attacked.abc.net.au/news/teen-trial-assault-police-officer-ebike-ride-out-meeting/105668166Link copiedShareShare articleTeenage boys assaulted a WA police officer when he tried to seize an e-motorbike involved in a 'ride out' in Perth's CBD, causing blood to run down his face, Perth Children's Court has heard.The court was shown CCTV footage of the uniformed traffic officer being punched during a confrontation with dozens of teenagers on bikes, with his back to a wall at Burswood.One of those who allegedly struck the officer, a 16-year-old boy, is on trial accused of assaulting a public officer, causing bodily harm.The incident, on December 28 last year, came after about 100 teenagers rode through the CBD on e-rideables, with some reportedly blocking traffic, kicking cars and doing wheelies.Senior Constable Mark Andrew Cooper told the court he had tried to seize an e-motorbike which was being charged near Perth Stadium when he was surrounded .The incident occurred near Perth Stadium last December. (ABC News: Nicholas Martyr) It was starting to get tense, he told the court. I was surrounded by a large group of young people. I was in a corner near an alcove. I was pretty much on my own at that point. The officer had seen the blue e-motorbike which had been used in the 'ride out' but was unlicensed.The court heard a 16-year-old boy, who the prosecutor described as the principal antagonist , was sitting astride the vehicle, as Senior Constable Cooper explained what he was doing.Footage played in court showed youths on bikes arriving and verbally challenging the officer.WA Police Senior Constable Mark Andrew Cooper was assaulted when he attempted to seize an e-bike near Perth Stadium. (ABC News: David Weber)Senior Constable Cooper said he felt the presence of the 16-year-old, within half a metre of him.He told the court the teen looked up at him and said do you want a kiss? The officer said he was expecting a head butt and put his open right palm out to the youth's chest to arrest him. He started swinging punches, the officer said, and another youth came in over the top and he was hit in the face.Officer's motorbike knocked overThe officer told the court he was hit to the nose and eye area, before getting his helmet visor down to protect his face.Senior Constable Cooper said there was blood running down my face , and he suffered a cut to the right eyebrow, and another between his eyebrows.Perth Children's Court heard the teen on trial was the principal antagonist during a tense confrontation. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)The court heard his own BMW motorcycle was pushed over during the struggle but he didn't know how.The 16-year-old was arrested soon afterwards.Prosecutor James Nicholls had said Senior Constable Cooper was jointly assaulted and whatever he did with his right hand that day was lawful .But the boy's lawyer suggested the officer used excessive force by punching him . I don't believe I punched him, the senior constable said. I had no intention of punching him. The court heard that the 'ride out' gathering was organised via social media and attracted people aged from 11 up to 18, on e-bicycles, e-motorbikes, e-scooters and bicycles.The group gathered at Elizabeth Quay at about 11:30am before riding through the city.Loading...LoadingPosted 19h ago19 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 6:23am, updated 17h ago17 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 8:43amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesZelenskyy says no 'unacceptable decisions' were made in White House talksLIVEPhoto shows Zelenskyy gestures with hands while speaking into microphones'Go home': Country everyone wants to visit is turning on touristsTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows Tourists taking a selfie.Baby girl found in Perth stormwater drain was dead for two weeksTopic:PolicePhoto shows A police car with a police woman leaning against it. full_text: Secret relationship with prison informant set to result in guilty plea Ex-corruption commission employee Louise Carruthers to plead guilty over secret informant relationshipDBy David WeberTopic:Courts22h ago22 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 3:29amLouise Carruthers was charged after allegedly having an inappropriate relationship with a prison informant. (ABC News: Aran Hart)abc.net.au/news/louise-carruthers-to-admit-corruption-informant-relationship/105667316Link copiedShareShare articleA former WA Corruption and Crime Commission employee accused of having an intimate relationship with an informant is set to plead guilty to a charge of corruption.Louise Catherine Carruthers was employed by the commission as a handler of confidential sources and police had alleged she had an inappropriate relationship with a prison informant.Police had said she had developed an inappropriate and intimate relationship with the source over an extended period.When the 42-year-old was charged, police said she had engaged in deceitful conduct to hide the relationship from her employer and to enable clandestine meetings to continue.Ms Carruthers left court on Monday with her lawyer, who told the hearing his client would plead guilty at her next appearance. (ABC News: Aran Hart)Ms Carruthers was charged earlier this year with one count of public officer acts corruptly over the course of November 2018 through to January 2023.She had been employed by the Corruption and Crime Commission from 2005 through to 2023 and held a number of leadership positions.At a hearing in Perth Magistrates Court on Monday morning, Ms Carruthers' lawyer said she would plead guilty at her next court appearance.The facts of the case were not read out and she is due to reappear in court next month.LoadingPosted 22h ago22 hours agoMon 18 Aug 2025 at 3:29amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesZelenskyy says no 'unacceptable decisions' were made in White House talksLIVEPhoto shows Zelenskyy gestures with hands while speaking into microphones'Go home': Country everyone wants to visit is turning on touristsTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows Tourists taking a selfie.Baby girl found in Perth stormwater drain was dead for two weeksTopic:PolicePhoto shows A police car with a police woman leaning against it. full_text: Inside notorious Sydney gangster's resort empire attempt in Belize Sydney crime boss Bassam Hamzy's Belize jungle resort plan among his vast jail business empireABy Anton RoseTopic:CrimeSat 16 AugSaturday 16 AugustSat 16 Aug 2025 at 9:14pmThe ABC tracked down those in Belize who Hamzy enlisted to try and get his scheme off the ground. (ABC: Dylan Goolagong)abc.net.au/news/bassam-hamzy-belize-resort-plans-from-nsw-prison/105646544Link copiedShareShare article We're gunna [sic] probably make tens of millions of dollars. That is how crime lord Bassam Hamzy described ambitious plans for a resort in Belize on a secretly recorded call from his Goulburn Supermax cell.The only problem is, according to anyone in the Central American nation willing to speak about it, the project is a dud.Hamzy, the state's most notorious prisoner who founded the Brothers 4 Life gang while in jail, is planning an outrageous venture for a billion-dollar resort dubbed Boss City to be built in the middle of the jungle.The ABC tracked down those in Belize who Hamzy enlisted to try and get his scheme off the ground, including the country's former prime minister.An artist's impression of the Boss City project, proposed by Sydney crime boss Bassam Hamzy. (Supplied)Grand plan behind Belize propertyWhen news of his project thousands of kilometres away first emerged, it was splashed across the news.Hamzy, who is in jail for murdering a teenager outside a nightclub in the late 1990s, amongst other crimes, was equally excited. I used to write to [Witness A] and I used to tell him about this project that we had going in Belize, Hamzy told his lawyer Martin Churchill in one call from jail.Hamzy has spent the past two decades behind bars. In that time he has been charged over a series of crimes committed on the outside. (Supplied)The phone call with Mr Churchill took place in October 2018 and was tendered in the District Court during a drug supply trial where Hamzy was later found guilty.Witness A is an associate of Hamzy's who cannot be identified for legal reasons. And he used to laugh at me, always telling me … 'Oh you're still trying to get um, develop or sell that property alright?' Hamzy continued. Now that we have this approval, Martin … alright, and it's, we're gunna [sic] probably make tens of millions of dollars. Former Belize prime minister Said Musa's law firm was connected to a development plan by Sydney crime boss Bassam Hamzy. (Supplied)Business records for Boss City Group tie back to a law firm connected to the Belize government, which is run by the former Belize prime minister, Said Musa.No-one from the law firm would respond to the ABC's repeated queries and there is no suggestion Mr Musa is involved in any wrongdoing.In theory, Hamzy's grand plan is a bust, according to the few people in Belize who would publicly comment on the crime boss' ambitious project.'No licence' and 'no development registered'When asked by a local reporter on May 16, Belize's Tourism Minister, Anthony Mahler, scoffed at the idea. Are you aware of it? the reporter asked. Absolutely not, Mr Mahler replied. I know nothing about it so I can't speak for it. If they're going to have that level of investment, we would know, this is the first I'm hearing of it. Mr Mahler promised to investigate the plans with the Belize Tourism Board. And if we find out anything we'll get back to the media, he said.Loading...After several attempts to reach them, another Belize government bureaucrat confirmed the project was a fantasy. There is no development registered with the Belize Tourism Board under that name or by the person associated with that name, Belize Tourism Board registrar of hotels Jacob Leslie said. No licence has been issued to that individual or company. We have made further checks with Beltraide, which is the investment arm in Belize, and have confirmed that they are not aware of any such investment in the country. Hamzy has strong ties to the Central American nation, having fled there seeking refuge with a relative after he shot dead the teenager in 1999.Who that relative is remains a mystery, though his murder trial at the time was told they were wealthy and Hamzy spent time on a farm while on the run there.He was eventually extradited back to Sydney and convicted of murder.Hamzy Inc.Convicted murderer, drug dealer, gangster and property developer — Hamzy is a man who wears many hats.He has evoked equal parts fear and fascination over the years through his criminal exploits.Whether or not his Central American pipedream comes into fruition, Hamzy is still arguably the most prolific businessman behind bars.According to secretly taped conversations from Goulburn's Supermax tendered in the Sydney District Court, Hamzy had his hands in everything from construction to shoes.Hamzy's lawyer described him as having a razor sharp mind . (Supplied: NSW Police)Not to mention South American nightclubs, which he believed would earn him hundreds of thousands of dollars a month . My friend in Peru, I told him to buy 15 per cent into all these nightclubs in Peru, Hamzy said in a call to his lawyer in February 2018. Nightclubs are very cheap. Because there's all these people that, all the travellers that go to Peru and everything you know. I'm gonna choose 10 nightclubs, buy 15 per cent into each nightclub. I reckon that will at least turn us a $100,000 a month. Closer to home, Hamzy's lawyer Mr Churchill, his father Khaled Hamzy and others known to him were busy dealing with a development near Burwood train station in Sydney's inner-west.The ABC was unable to verify the exact housing project, but tendered phone conversations reveal it was 50 metres north of the railway line.Mr Churchill, Hamzy's father Khaled and others known to him were busy dealing with a development near Burwood Station. (ABC News: Jak Rowland) You know with the Burwood property Martin? My dad gave him a copy of the Burwood property. There's 82 units. There's a huge profit margin if he can get his builders, Hamzy said in a February 2018 phone call to his lawyer. That's, of course, over a hundred million dollar project, you know. See how far we can take this you know? This was on top of a plan to sell sneakers, where Hamzy and his associates believed stocking Asics and Adidas shoes would net them $200,000 every single month .'Razor sharp' focus on empire outside of jailAccording to recorded conversations, Hamzy's burgeoning empire was the brainchild of his lawyer, Mr Churchill.Mr Churchill died of natural causes before he could face trial with Hamzy over drug supply charges.It was him who suggested that a business portfolio could lead to his freedom.Lawyer Martin Churchill (left) was allegedly involved in a drug scheme with Hamzy. (Supplied: NSW Police) So you need to be doing things on the outside that are legitimate, Mr Churchill told an associate while waiting for Hamzy to join the call in October 2018.He said if Hamzy were to go before the parole board with a legitimate business plan, it would work in his favour. Now most people would say you know that's a bit far-fetched or whatever, but I said to him, 'Open your mind what connections have you got? What have you got? Let's start something'. Bassam has got this like a razor-sharp mental mind. Together, according to the tendered conversations, they developed a plan so Hamzy could broker a deal to get parole.Hamzy has managed a feat few have dared behind bars; both criminal acts he has been convicted of, and handling legitimate business dealings. (Supplied: NSW Police)Hamzy had earlier attempted to do another deal with authorities where he offered to return 10 stolen army rocket launchers to NSW Police in 2009.It would have ensured a favourable plea deal for his father, but it eventually fell through.Another time they were certain one of the state's most high-risk prisoners was on the cusp of freedom.What exactly was in the deal was never made clear in the conversations captured by police and later tendered to court.Life of crimePhoto shows High-security prisoner Bassam HamzyAustralia's first and only extreme high-risk inmate, Bassam Hamzy, started the Brothers 4 Life gang while in jail after he converted to radical Islam. Whoever can go watch the AG [Attorney-General] sign it, as soon as that signatures on I'm gonna deliver, that I have to deliver, Hamzy said in a prison call from February 2018. You know what that means, Martin? That means I can literally be up for parole tomorrow, Martin. Hamzy was not released on parole. The earliest date he can apply for parole is 2038. I'm not treacherous, I'm not two-faced Martin, you know, especially, and I respect every and the path that I build and the bonds that I build with brothers Martin, he would claim in another phone call a week later.Posted Sat 16 Aug 2025 at 9:14pmSaturday 16 Aug 2025 at 9:14pmSat 16 Aug 2025 at 9:14pmShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesZelenskyy says no 'unacceptable decisions' were made in White House talksLIVEPhoto shows Zelenskyy gestures with hands while speaking into microphones'Go home': Country everyone wants to visit is turning on touristsTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows Tourists taking a selfie.Baby girl found in Perth stormwater drain was dead for two weeksTopic:PolicePhoto shows A police car with a police woman leaning against it. full_text: Victim of 'cowardly' alleged attack granted fresh Australian visa Man who almost lost hand in alleged machete attack gets visa extensionExclusive by Simon Love and Melissa Polimeni7.30Topic:AssaultSat 16 AugSaturday 16 AugustSat 16 Aug 2025 at 8:28pmSaurabh Anand says the decision to extend his visa has rekindled his hope in humanity. (ABC News: Andrew Altree-Williams)abc.net.au/news/machete-attack-victim-gets-visa-extension/105654810Link copiedShareShare articleA man who almost lost his hand in an alleged machete attack has been granted a new visa so his medical treatment can continue in Australia.7.30 can reveal that 33-year-old Indian national Saurabh Anand was granted the visa and is on a pathway to permanent residency after the federal government considered his case on compassionate grounds.Mr Anand survived the incident which allegedly occurred at a shopping centre in Altona Meadows, in Victoria, just under a month ago.Five teenagers have been charged over the alleged attack including a 15-year-old boy arrested last Thursday.The alleged attack happened at Melbourne's Central Square Shopping Centre. (ABC News: Andrew Altree-Williams)Mr Anand was facing deportation as his temporary visa was due to expire on August 25.The new visa will allow him to stay for up to two years, but he is also on a pathway to become a permanent resident of Australia.He says his health has been on rapid decline due to the severity of his injuries and pain. This is a moment where I feel relieved that the government and the community has come together to support me through one of the most horrifying moments in my life, Mr Anand told 7.30.Mr Anand said the decision has rekindled his hope in humanity. There are still good people out there who want to take care of each other, and we are a part of a community that could stand together, he said.'Right thing to do'Mr Anand and his mother Nitin Anand met with his local MP Tim Watts and Assistant Minister for Citizenship Julian Hill to receive the new visa.In a short meeting at the electorate office of Mr Watts, Mr Hill signed documents which granted the extension.Julian Hill met with Mr Anand after he was granted his new visa. (ABC News: Andrew Altree-Williams)The local MP offered Indian sweets to Mr Anand and his mother following the signing. In a poignant moment Ms Anand then took the sweets and offered them back to the two assistant ministers as a gesture of thanks for their decision. If you have some I will have some, Mr Watts said to Ms Anand.Documents granting a two-year renewal to his subclass 485 (Temporary Graduate) visa were signed after Mr Anand was briefly taken temporarily into administrative detention to process the claim.Under law, it is an administrative requirement for the short detention period to take place so that the new visa can be granted.The decision was made under Section 195A of the Migration Act, which allows the minister to grant a detained person a visa if it was in the public interest.Mr Hill told 7.30 he was moved by Mr Anand's case.Assistant Minister for Citizenship Julian Hill says extending Mr Anand's visa was the right thing to do . (ABC News: Elise Worthington) He's been the victim of a horrible, cowardly attack as a human being in our society, Mr Hill said. It's the right thing to do, but also I'd hope as an Australian that if my daughter or any of our sons and daughters were in a foreign land and had been contributing to that country and ended up in a similar circumstance that another country would treat our sons and daughters as well. His recovery and treatment could take up to 12 months. I am taking one day at a time, every day gives me a new hope, and this is a new hope for me, he said. But as of the recovery, both physical and mental, exertion is there. And it's going to be a long journey. I'd like to thank everyone who has been supporting me throughout the community. Skilled workerOn August 7, following the airing of a 7.30 story about Mr Anand's case in which he and his mother pleaded for help from the government, Mr Anand wrote to the minister seeking urgent attention to his case.Loading...In the email, he detailed how he was allegedly assaulted and the local medical care required for his recovery. My injuries were so severe that it took over five hours for surgeons to reconstruct and reattach my left arm and hand, which had been nearly severed, he wrote. Despite their efforts, I have lost approximately 80 per cent sensation in my left arm, hand, and fingers, and currently suffer from excruciating pain, multiple fractures, severed nerves, tendons, and muscles. Mr Anand has worked as a sales representative during his time in Australia and said that before his attack, he intended to move his career into the field of artificial intelligence. I have lived in Australia for over seven years, he wrote in his email to the minister. I have always abided by Australian laws and contributed to the community, I am the only son of my widowed mother in India, and this incident has left me emotionally and financially devastated. I place my hope in your compassion and kindness during this incredibly difficult period. Since the alleged July attack, Mr Anand has received support and visitation from both sides of politics including Victorian State Liberal MP Moira Deeming.Mrs Deeming wrote to Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke on August 7 to plead for Mr Anand to be granted a bridging visa.The federal government will now move to grant Mr Anand permanent residency pending character checks and a full process through the Department of Home Affairs.Mr Hill said Mr Anand's work in Australia were key factors in his decision. He studied a high-quality [degree], a master's at RMIT, and he's worked and contributed to the community, he said. He's already certified as having multiple skills in cybersecurity and IT that our country needs. Saurabh Anand's arm was nearly severed in the alleged machete attack. full_text: Police say investigation into Kumanjayi White's death at 'advanced state' NT police say investigation into Kumanjayi White's death in custody at 'advanced state'GBy Grace AttaTopic:CrimeFri 15 AugFriday 15 AugustFri 15 Aug 2025 at 7:36amHundreds gathered in Alice Springs in June for the town's third vigil after Kumanjayi White's death. (ABC News: Xavier Martin)In short:NT police have provided an update on their investigation into the death in custody of Kumanjayi White, saying it is at an advanced state .The 24-year-old Warlpiri man from Yuendumu, who was living in Alice Springs due to his disabilities, died after being restrained by plain-clothed police on the floor of a Coles supermarket in May. NT Police Acting Deputy Commissioner Travis Wurst says both the criminal and coronial investigations are ongoing, with police are waiting for forensic pathology results from interstate to finalise the autopsy.abc.net.au/news/kumanjayi-white-death-in-custody-nt-police-investigation-update/105659492Link copiedShareShare articleAboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this article contains the name of an Indigenous person who has died, used with the permission of their family.Northern Territory police say their investigation into Kumanjayi White's death in custody is now at an advanced state , nearly three months after his death in Alice Springs.The 24-year-old Warlpiri man died at a Coles supermarket in Alice Springs on May 27 after he was restrained by plain-clothed police officers following an alleged altercation with security guards. The death of Mr White, who was from Yuendumu but was living in Alice Springs at the time due to his disabilities, prompted vigils around the country and an outpouring of grief from Mr White's family and community. During a press conference on Friday, NT Police Acting Deputy Commissioner Travis Wurst confirmed that the criminal investigation into Mr White's death, titled Operation Walcrow, was continuing.Travis Wurst says the investigation into Kumanjayi White's death in custody is at an advanced state . (ABC News: Samantha Dick) Police, however, are still waiting on the forensic pathology report to come from the Northern Territory forensic pathologist, he said. I can confirm that from the original autopsy, a number of samples were sent interstate that required further expert analysis and investigation to support the investigation by the forensic pathologist. Those samples are yet to be obtained and as a consequence NT police are yet to receive that autopsy report. We cannot finalise that investigation until that's been obtained at this stage. Kumanjayi White's death in custody prompted vigils in Alice Springs and around the country. (ABC News: Xavier Martin)Asked why the officers involved had not been stood down during the investigation, Acting Deputy Commissioner Wurst said: Because at this time, the way in which the investigation is being constructed, there isn't a reason to stand them down. At this stage, no charges have been laid, he said.The ABC understands one of the officers involved in the altercation is police prosecutor Steven Haig. Officer involved in Alice Springs death in custody charges man's fatherPhoto shows A woman bends over in mourning next to a pile of flowers laid on the ground.Court documents seen by the ABC show police prosecutor Steven Haig approved charges laid against the father of Kumanjayi White.Earlier this week, the ABC revealed Mr Haig was now leading the prosecution of Mr White's father. Mr White's grandfather and respected Warlpiri elder Ned Jampijinpa Hargraves has previously demanded access to the CCTV footage of the incident and an independent investigation into his grandson's death.He has also called for the officers involved in the incident to be stood down.In response to the family's calls, NT Police Acting Commissioner Martin Dole said in June that the investigation was not something we can just hand to somebody else .Coronial investigation led by policeIn early June, the NT Police Force issued a statement indicating that the coronial investigation into Kumanjayi White's death had been paused while the criminal investigation was underway, before amending that statement, and then retracting it.But on Friday, Acting Deputy Commissioner Wurst said within days of Mr White's death, police had stood up an independent coronial investigation led by an assistant commissioner . That team has been investigating the coronial aspect of this … and that will take a considerable period of time, he said. The coroner is well-involved in that process also. full_text: Police investigating TikTok shooting threats at Perth high school Mt Lawley Senior High School TikTok threats to students being investigated by policeLBy Lucy MartinABy Andrea MayesTopic:Cyber CrimeFri 15 AugFriday 15 AugustFri 15 Aug 2025 at 5:56amA number of police officers were seen outside Mt Lawley Senior High School in the wake of the TikTok threats. (ABC News: Jack Stevenson)abc.net.au/news/mt-lawley-senior-high-school-tiktok-threats-to-students/105659980Link copiedShareShare articleOnline threats posted on social media apparently making reference to school shootings and directed at students at one of Perth's biggest high schools are being investigated by police.Screenshots of the threats seen by the ABC, made in a series of TikTok posts overnight and since deleted, appear to show heavily armed shooters, interspersed with images of Mt Lawley Senior High School students in uniform.In a statement, police said there were no safety concerns or imminent risk to students, teachers or members of the community. Police are actively investigating and are working with the school to resolve the matter, they said in a statement.Police vehicles were seen outside the school on Friday, but authorities said there were no immediate risks to students. (ABC News: Jack Stevenson)The Education Department said it was aware of the incident, which was being handled by police.In an initial email to parents, school principal Lesley Street urged parents to monitor and speak with your child regarding their concerns and social media use , without referencing the threats directly. It is important to be aware of the positive and negative impacts of social media and conversations within the community as misinformation and rumours may be unhelpful, she wrote.Multiple police cars and officers were seen at the school on Friday.Children kept homeThe ABC spoke to one parent, who chose to keep their two children home today in light of the threats.“Yesterday, amongst the school peer group, there were murmurs of a TikTok video, which had today’s date on it, 15 August, and possible innuendo of a shooting at the school,” they said. It's probably a pretty low risk that someone's going to go through with this, but the consequences are high if they do. So we weren't clear what the school's stance was, there was no communication from the school to say there had been an actual threat to the school and that they'd put in extra measures to keep the kids safe. Because there was no real transparency about what was going on, we decided to keep the kids home. The parent described the communication from the school as vague .Mt Lawley Senior High School in Perth was the apparent target of a TikTok threat concerning a school shooting. (ABC News: Jack Stevenson) It was basically a bland letter…it didn't address the actual issue at all, they said.The parent, who did not want to be identified, said they understood many other parents had made the same decision to keep their kids home today.They said one of their children had been particularly concerned by the threats, saying 'I used to feel safe going to school, now I'm not sure'.An email update from the principal on Friday afternoon said: The school is working closely with authorities who are looking into reports linked to the school. I would like to reassure you that police have confirmed that there are no safety concerns or immediate risks to students, staff, or members of the community. full_text: Man accused of Victorian father's cold case murder granted bail Man accused of murdering Victorian father Christopher Jarvis granted bailBy Jean BellABC South West VicTopic:CourtsFri 15 AugFriday 15 AugustFri 15 Aug 2025 at 5:08amChristopher Jarvis has not been seen since his car was found torched in 2006. (Supplied: Australian Missing Persons Register)In short:Steven Federick Johnson has been charged with the murder of Christopher Jarvis, who disappeared in 2006. Police opposed Mr Johnson being released on bail.What's next?Mr Johnson will be released on bail under a $500,000 surety and a number of conditions.abc.net.au/news/steven-federick-johnson-granted-bail-warrnambool-murder-charge/105653030Link copiedShareShare articleA south-west Victorian man charged with the 2006 cold case murder of Christopher Jarvis will be released from custody while he awaits a possible trial. Police arrested 72-year-old Steven Federick Johnson in March and charged him with the murder of Mr Jarvis, who disappeared from his home near Warrnambool in 2006.Justice Rita Incerti approved Mr Johnson's bail application in the Victorian Supreme Court on Friday.Justice Incerti said she was satisfied Mr Johnson's case met the exceptional circumstances required for bail.The circumstances included challenges to his physical and mental health, which needed specialist medical treatment.The court heard Mr Johnson had adhered to all bail conditions when he was released on bail in 2023 after he faced charges in relation to Mr Jarvis's disappearance that were later dropped. Police, Jarvis family oppose bailChristopher Jarvis left his home at Wangoom on the morning of June 13, 2006, and was not seen again. His burnt-out car was later found at Thunder Point, a popular scenic lookout on the coast of Warrnambool. An investigation into his disappearance was at a standstill for almost two decades until Victoria Police's missing persons squad received new information from the public which led to the cold case being re-opened in 2022. The re-ignited investigation led to searches of Framlingham Forest.The court heard Mr Johnson was charged in relation to Mr Jarvis's disappearance in 2022, but the charges were later dropped. He was charged again in March this year.During a bail application hearing in the Supreme Court on Thursday, Detective Senior Constable Alicia Reivers said police opposed the bail application as detectives believed there was an unacceptable risk of him obstructing the course of justice by influencing a witness.The Jarvis family also opposed bail, the court heard.The court also heard police held concerns Mr Johnson could tamper with evidence, namely Mr Jarvis' body, which prosecutors allege is buried in Framlingham Forest near Warrnambool.Mr Jarvis's body has never been found. Public prosecutor Jenaya Ellis said the Crown's case alleged that Mr Johnson knew where the body was located.$500,000 surety for bailMr Johnson's lawyer Patrick Doyle SC told the court Mr Johnson had been released on bail previously in the matter and complied with similar conditions.The current bail application was made with a $500,000 surety, sourced from Mr Johnson's wife's share of a property, along with her commitment to hold him accountable to the bail conditions.His lawyer said Mr Johnson would not breach the conditions, given that contacting a witness would provide incriminating evidence against him, as well as risking the significant surety.Mr Johnson was released on bail on a number of conditions, including that he not contact, or instruct anyone to contact, witnesses.He was also banned from visiting Framlingham Forest.Posted Fri 15 Aug 2025 at 5:08amFriday 15 Aug 2025 at 5:08amFri 15 Aug 2025 at 5:08amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesZelenskyy says no 'unacceptable decisions' were made in White House talksLIVEPhoto shows Zelenskyy gestures with hands while speaking into microphones'Go home': Country everyone wants to visit is turning on touristsTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows Tourists taking a selfie.Baby girl found in Perth stormwater drain was dead for two weeksTopic:PolicePhoto shows A police car with a police woman leaning against it. full_text: Man charged with separate assaults 24 hours after Sydney Airport incident Man on bail over Sydney Airport incident charged with assault at Central train stationABy Anton RoseTopic:PoliceFri 15 AugFriday 15 AugustFri 15 Aug 2025 at 12:35amIt is understood the man charged over alleged assaults at Central Station on Thursday is the same man charged over an incident at Sydney Airport on Wednesday. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)In short:Police allege the man involved in a scuffle with officers at Sydney Airport on Wednesday, where a gun discharged, assaulted train commuters after being released on bail.Nicholas Teplin, 41, has been charged with assault offences after the incident at Central train station on Thursday.What's next?He is due to face court on the new charges on Friday morning. abc.net.au/news/man-on-bail-sydney-airport-incident-charged-with-train-assault/105657696Link copiedShareShare articleA man accused of creating a disturbance at Sydney Airport — where a police firearm was discharged in a struggle with officers — has been charged with more offences 24 hours after being released on bail.Nicholas Teplin, 41, has been charged with allegedly assaulting several people at Central train station after being released from custody on Wednesday.Mr Teplin had been charged with creating a disturbance at an airport and hindering a Commonwealth official.Police were called to Central train station in Sydney's CBD following reports a man had allegedly assaulted two men. (ABC News: Liam Patrick)Police allege on Wednesday Mr Teplin was involved in a struggle with Australian Federal Police officers during his arrest inside the domestic terminal of Sydney Airport, which resulted in a police gun discharging.He fronted court that day and was granted conditional bail.Police allege Mr Teplin on Thursday approached a 45-year-old man on the train station's concourse at about 4.40pm and punched him in the face.The man was left with a bloodied nose and collapsed to the floor, police said.The incident at Sydney airport occurred on Wednesday morning. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)Soon after, police allege, Mr Teplin is accused of approaching two more men and striking them in the head. The man continued towards a fourth 20-year-old man and allegedly attempted to grab his bag from his shoulder, NSW Police said in a statement on Friday morning. As the men continued to struggle over the bag, police from Sydney City Police Area Command attended and arrested the man. Chief Inspector Gary Coffey from the Sydney City Police Area Command said the man had to be physically restrained at the scene and handcuffed .Operation underway after police gun fired at Sydney AirportPhoto shows Woman in AFP uniform around plantsThe Australian Federal Police said officers responded to a request for assistance from an airline at Sudney Airport after the man was acting suspiciously this morning.He was taken to Surry Hills Police Station. Whilst in police custody, the man allegedly assaulted a male constable by pushing him in the chest. Alleged assaults captured on CCTVThe alleged assaults on Thursday were recorded on CCTV at the train station. There's also police body worn footage, Chief Inspector Coffey said.Mr Teplin was charged with hindering police, affray, assaulting police, assaulting occasioning actual bodily harm and common assault.Mr Teplin faced court on Friday.Chief Inspector Coffey said NSW Police was still looking for two of the four men allegedly assaulted on Thursday, asking them to contact authorities to assist with investigations.Gary Coffey addresses the media on Friday. (ABC News)Bail was decided based on risks 'known at that time'When questioned over the decision to grant the man bail on Wednesday, Chief Inspector Coffey said: He was granted conditional bail in relation to two Commonwealth offences. Bail decisions are made every day based on the risks that are known at that time. Police Minister Yasmin Catley said the man's alleged actions were beyond belief and that the decision for bail was made by magistrates . The NSW Police have acted very, very, swiftly, she said, thanking attending officers.Posted Fri 15 Aug 2025 at 12:35amFriday 15 Aug 2025 at 12:35amFri 15 Aug 2025 at 12:35am, updated Fri 15 Aug 2025 at 3:58amFriday 15 Aug 2025 at 3:58amFri 15 Aug 2025 at 3:58amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesZelenskyy says no 'unacceptable decisions' were made in White House talksLIVEPhoto shows Zelenskyy gestures with hands while speaking into microphones'Go home': Country everyone wants to visit is turning on touristsTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows Tourists taking a selfie.Baby girl found in Perth stormwater drain was dead for two weeksTopic:PolicePhoto shows A police car with a police woman leaning against it. full_text: $10m theft of baby formula and other items from Melbourne supermarkets 19 arrested for allegedly stealing $10 million worth of baby formula and other itemsTopic:CourtsThu 14 AugThursday 14 AugustThu 14 Aug 2025 at 9:58pmInfant formula is among $10 million worth of products police say has been stolen by an alleged criminal syndicate in Melbourne. (Getty: dragana991)In short:Police say they've dismantled an alleged major retail theft syndicate that allegedly stole more than $10 million worth of products from Melbourne supermarkets in a five-month period.The items stolen include baby formula, medicine, vitamins and electric toothbrushes.What's next?The investigation is ongoing and further arrests are anticipated.abc.net.au/news/baby-formula-medicine-thefts-criminal-syndicate-melbourne/105657012Link copiedShareShare articlePolice have arrested 19 people for allegedly stealing more than $10 million worth of baby formula, medicines, skincare products and toiletries from supermarkets across Melbourne.The investigation dubbed Operation Supernova targeted an alleged syndicate involving international students which police say are mostly from India on temporary, student or bridging visas.Police said the alleged thieves took baby formula, medicines, vitamins, skincare products, electric toothbrushes and toiletries over the past five months.Officers alleged those who stole items passed them on to receivers who then sold them on to others for profit.Among the arrests are three men, all in their 20s, who police alleged stole more than $100,000 worth of retail items each.They're facing dozens of theft charges and have been remanded to appear in court later this month and next.The investigation was carried out by the Box Hill Divisional Response Unit, which worked with major retailers and the Australian Border Force.Retail theft is one of the fastest-growing crimes in Victoria, with 41,270 offences recorded in the past year — a 38 per cent increase state-wide, police said. (ABC News)In short:Douglas Crabbe is serving five consecutive life sentences for murdering multiple people in an attack at the Inland Hotel near Uluru in 1983.The WA Prisoners Review Board has confirmed his latest bid for parole was rejected in July.Survivor Bernadette Schiller says she believes Crabbe should never be allowed parole.abc.net.au/news/nt-uluru-truck-mass-murderer-douglas-crabbe-makes-parole-bid/105645436Link copiedShareShare articleA convicted mass murderer who killed five people when he ploughed his semi-trailer into a packed pub at Uluru has had his bid for parole rejected in Western Australia.On August 18, 1983, in a fit of rage after being kicked out for intoxication, Douglas Crabbe slammed his truck into the side of the Inland Hotel.It resulted in the deaths of David Seng, 24, Adrian Durnin, 21, Helen Fuller, 22, Patricia Slinn, 45 and Leslie McKay-Ramsay, 35.Many others were seriously wounded in the attack.Five people were killed in Douglas Crabbe's attack at the Inland Hotel. (ABC News)Crabbe is serving five consecutive life sentences for the crime.He has been eligible for parole since 2013, but his bids for freedom have been consistently denied by the government of Western Australia, where he is now incarcerated.The WA Prisoners Review Board confirmed Crabbe's latest bid for parole was rejected in July.WA Attorney-General Tony Buti said in a statement he had decided not to release Douglas Crabbe at this time .In 1983, this man murdered five people at an Uluru motelPhoto shows Old TV footage shows chaotic scenes at the Inland Hotel.Douglas Crabbe was found guilty of one of modern Australia's worst mass murders after he rammed into a Northern Territory motel with his Mack truck, killing five people. I have taken into account the seriousness of the offence, a crime where five people were murdered and a further 16 were injured, some seriously, he said. I also considered the views of the surviving victims and persons affected by Mr Crabbe's actions. A number of those have spoken publicly and written to me personally expressing their opposition to Mr Crabbe's release which was at the forefront of my decision. This horrific crime has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims, their families, and the wider community, she said.Survivor says Crabbe should never be releasedAmong the survivors of the attack is Bernadette Schiller, who said she still suffers anxiety and PTSD from the terror of Crabbe's actions that night in 1983. full_text: WA doctor who paid teens for sex guilty of grooming, child sex offences WA GP Douglas William McCarthy guilty of child sex offencesDBy David WeberTopic:Child Sexual AbuseThu 14 AugThursday 14 AugustThu 14 Aug 2025 at 7:45amDouglas William McCarthy paid underage girls for sex. (ABC News: David Weber)In short: Douglas William McCarthy, 63, was a practising GP in the state's south west, when he engaged in sexual acts with girls aged 14 and 15.Today a District Court jury found him guilty of a range of charges, including persistent sexual conduct or sexual penetration, child exploitation, and encouraging a 17-year-old to engage in prostitution.Prosecutor Sean Stocks told the jury McCarthy had a sexual interest in underage girls and acted on that interest.abc.net.au/news/wa-doctor-douglas-william-mccarthy-guilty-child-sex-offences/105647308Link copiedShareShare articleA WA doctor who paid tens of thousands of dollars to teenage girls for sex and photos, and kept a video library of his offending, has been found guilty of multiple offences.WARNING: This article contains details some readers may find distressing.Douglas William McCarthy, 63, was a practising GP in the state's south west, when he engaged in sexual acts with girls aged 14 and 15.A Perth District Court jury, which had been forced to watch hours of what prosecutor Sean Stocks described as graphic and disturbing footage, today found McCarthy guilty of a range of charges, including persistent sexual conduct and sexual penetration, possessing child pornography, and encouraging a 17-year-old to engage in prostitution.He was also found guilty of attempting to pervert the course of justice.Douglas William McCarthy leaves court during his trial. (ABC News: David Weber)The jury deliberated for more than six hours.McCarthy showed no emotion as the jury foreman delivered guilty verdicts on 14 charges, but when he was finished, he sat with his face in his hands.A sentencing hearing has been scheduled for next week. 'Curated' library of offencesMr Stocks told the jury McCarthy had a sexual interest in underage girls and acted on that interest. They were children, he said, even if they occasionally acted as if they were adults, and had been groomed by an older and apparently more sophisticated person.Mr Stocks said McCarthy had a curated video library of his offences and paid two girls to keep quiet about having sex with them when they were 15.Part-way through the trial, McCarthy had pleaded guilty to charges of sexual penetration regarding two girls aged under 16, but had continued to deny persistent sexual conduct in relation to them.Prosecutor Sean Stocks says footage of McCarthy's offending was graphic and disturbing . (ABC News: David Weber)He had also denied having sexual relations with any other girls aged under 16.McCarthy admitted receiving pictures and videos, and paying for sexual acts, but claimed he believed the girls were older than 16.When he was told one of the girls wasn't really 16, he said he was extremely mad because he thought he could lose his medical registration and go to jail.He told the court he was devastated to then find out another of the girls was younger than 16.Mr Stocks described McCarthy's evidence as nonsense .Douglas William McCarthy paid the girls to keep quiet about his offending. (ABC News: David Weber)He said the accounts of the victims were consistent and inherently plausible , making McCarthy a child sex offender .Assault on massage tableOne victim described how she went with a friend to see McCarthy and they smoked marijuana before engaging in sex acts with him.Later, he told her he had contracted chlamydia and gave her a prescription for treating it.If you or anyone you know needs help:1800 RESPECT national helpline on 1800 737 732Sexual Assault Counselling Australia on 1800 211 028Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors) on 1800 272 831Blue Knot Foundation on 1300 657 380Lifeline (24 hour crisis line) on 131 114Another victim said she was 15 when she went to see him in his home, and was sexually assaulted by McCarthy as she lay on her belly on a massage table.She said he later sent her a message offering to pay her $300 a week.When police started investigating, she messaged McCarthy I'm getting a lot of pressure from my family and the police and said she might need money for a lawyer.McCarthy told her not to flash your wealth around and put more than $500 into her account.LoadingLoadingPosted Thu 14 Aug 2025 at 7:45amThursday 14 Aug 2025 at 7:45amThu 14 Aug 2025 at 7:45am, updated Thu 14 Aug 2025 at 7:50amThursday 14 Aug 2025 at 7:50amThu 14 Aug 2025 at 7:50amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesZelenskyy says no 'unacceptable decisions' were made in White House talksLIVEPhoto shows Zelenskyy gestures with hands while speaking into microphones'Go home': Country everyone wants to visit is turning on touristsTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows Tourists taking a selfie.Baby girl found in Perth stormwater drain was dead for two weeksTopic:PolicePhoto shows A police car with a police woman leaning against it. full_text: Truck driver in deadly Florida turnpike crash booked in California jail Crime Truck driver in deadly Florida turnpike crash booked in California jail By Milena Malaver Updated August 19, 2025 4:50 PM A semi-truck driver caused a fatal crash on the Florida’s Turnpike, killing three South Floridians, FHP said. The driver faces vehicular homicide charges. St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office The semi-truck driver who caused a crash on the Florida Turnpike that killed three South Floridians was jailed in California days after the crash, officials confirmed Tuesday.Harjinder Singh, 28, was booked into the San Joaquin County Jail Saturday afternoon, California jail records show, following last Tuesday’s crash.Singh, who was denied bail, is set to appear in court at 1:30 p.m. Tuesday, California time, at the Stockton Courthouse in San Joaquin County, according to jail records.Typically, law enforcement does not make an arrest at the scene of vehicle crashes. “If there is a fatality associated with a car accident, investigative authorities work to make sure that all evidence is gathered before any arrests are made,” according to the Spatz Law Firm in Miami.Singh and his passenger, Harneet Singh, 25, flew to Sacramento on Aug. 13, the day after the crash, the U.S. Marshals Service said in a press release Tuesday. An arrest warrant for Harjinder was issued on Friday. He was arrested in Stockton, California, without incident on Saturday.“This priority effort was a cross country, multi-state and multi-agency success,” said USMS Director Gadyaces S. Serralta in a statement.The Aug. 12 crash occurred when Singh attempted to make a U-turn in his 18-wheeler at an “official use only” area of the Turnpike, 19 miles north of Fort Pierce in St. Lucie County.Singh was blocking all the northbound lanes as a 2015 black Chrysler Town & Country minivan approached in the middle lane, FHP said. The van slammed into the 18-wheeler, killing its three occupants.READ MORE: Trucking company in fatal Turnpike crash: unsafe trucks, unlicensed drivers, records show ‘On Tuesday, August 14, 2025, a tragic crash unfolded on the Florida Turnpike in Fort Pierce, FL, when a semi-truck attempted an illegal U-turn at an Official Use Only turnout, crossing unexpectedly into the left travel lane.’ pic.twitter.com/n9FHqBC0WN— The Daily Sneed™ (@Tr00peRR) August 15, 2025 On Tuesday, FHP identified the deceased as a 30-year-old Florida City man, who was driving, and two passengers: a 37-year-old Pompano Beach woman and a 54-year-old Miami man.The two passengers were pronounced dead at the scene, while the driver was airlifted to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. He died around 5:15 p.m. later that day, according to FHP.Singh, who has a commercial driver’s license in California, entered the United States illegally in 2018 through the Mexican border, according to FHP. It’s unclear how he obtained a commercial driver’s license, as Californa law requires the license holder to show proof they are in the U.S. legally, among other requirements, according to the California Commercial Driver’s Handbook.Singh lives in Stockton, a city in San Joaquin County.READ MORE: How did truck driver in fatal Turnpike crash get license if not legal resident?“The actions taken by the Defendant while operating a commercial tractor-trailer are both shocking and criminal,” FHP Executive Director Dave Kerner said in a statement Saturday. “Three people lost their lives as a result of his recklessness, and countless friends and family members will experience the pain of their loss forever.“Singh will be deported at the conclusion of his state charges, Kerner added. He is facing three counts of vehicular homicide, the Florida Highway Patrol said. In addition to the criminal charges, he was also issued an immigration detainer by federal agents. False. Harjinder Singh is in the United States illegally and his work authorization was rejected under the Trump Administration on September 14, 2020. full_text: ‘Direct insult’: Victim in Key Biscayne gymnastics coach case demands trial Crime ‘Direct insult’: Victim in Key Biscayne gymnastics coach case demands trial By Clara-Sophia Daly and Ana Claudia Chacin Updated August 18, 2025 6:24 PM Days after a plea agreement was struck in the case of a Key Biscayne coach accused of sexually abusing kids, the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office may reverse course, according to a key witness who said the plea deal was not harsh enough on her abuser.The victim told prosecutors the agreement was a “direct insult,” prompting the state to reconsider the plea, she told the Miami Herald Monday.The State Attorney’s Office did not respond to the Herald’s request for confirmation, but a text message obtained by the newspaper from a prosecutor to a second witness states that it is “pulling the plea.”Ultimately, Alberto Milian, the judge in charge of the case in Miami-Dade circuit court, will decide whether or not to uphold the plea agreement or let the state attorney withdraw it at a hearing scheduled for Thursday.“I am firmly and unequivocally opposed to any plea deal in this case,” the woman, now in her late 20s, wrote in an email shared with the Miami Herald. The email was addressed to Arvind Singh, one of the prosecutors in the state case against Oscar Olea.Olea, 40, has been charged with sexually assaulting girls a decade ago. He was facing six charges of sex crimes against a minor by a person with custodial authority against two of his former students, though two of those charges were dropped by the state attorney’s office last week. His trial had been scheduled to start Monday, but with the plea agreement introduced last week, the trial was canceled.The two former students are now 28 and 31 years old and previously told the Herald and police they started being abused by their then-coach when they were 12 and 16. Miami-Dade Circuit Judge Alberto Milian talks with a corrections officer at the Richard E. Gerstein Justice Building on Thursday, Aug. 14, 2025, in Miami, Fla. Milian will ultimately decide whether or not to ratify the plea deal. Photo by Matias J. Ocner mocner@miamiherald.com The key witness opposed to the plea, who is only identified in court records as “A.E.”, told the Herald that she was sexually abused by Olea from the age of 12 and into her teenage years over a decade ago. He had developed a “brotherly” relationship with her, which turned into a sexual one. Her story was part of Key Biscayne’s Dark Secret, a Herald investigation published last year that revealed her story and those of two other girls who also said they were abused.After the Herald published the story, those same three women went back to the police. Two of the women’s stories resulted in six charges for sexual battery against a minor by a person with custodial authority. Olea was arrested less than a month later.The plea, “reduces the lifelong impact of this crime to a number that lets a predator walk free while I remain sentenced to a lifetime of trauma,” the 28-year-old wrote in the email.Milian said last week in court that he would sign the agreement at a hearing on Thursday if Olea did not change his mind and decide to go to trial.Instead, the state is expected to argue that because the agreement has not yet been ratified, it should be able to withdraw the plea. Ultimately, that decision will be up to Milian.But it is a move that isn’t a great look, attorneys say.“The state is acting in bad faith,” said Mark Eiglarsh, a trial attorney and former prosecutor. “If they extended an offer and the defense agreed to it, then it’s just subject to a judge’s approval.”“The system would shut down if the prosecutor could simply renege on their agreements after extensive negotiations and them being ratified by the defense,” he said.But, Eiglarsh said, he understands why the prosecutors in this case would try to get Milian to allow them to take back the plea. Their responsibility is to the victims, he said. Singh, in response to A.E.’s email, wrote “It is heartbreaking to hear a victim so frustrated and understandably upset.”The plea dealOther prosecutors told the Herald Olea’s plea agreement seemed more or less in line with other cases they have seen and understood why a prosecutor may have favored a plea over taking the case to trial.Maria Schneider, a former prosecutor for Broward County, said 12 years was a “significant sentence,” and there were other factors to consider when taking a case to trial, including the unpredictability of jurors. She said ultimately the state’s job is to protect the public and taking a case to trial would risk Olea walking free. Oscar Olea, right, a former Key Biscayne gymnastics coach who allegedly sexually abused his students, talks with his attorneys Charlton Stoner, center, and Matthew Ladd, left, at the Richard E. Gerstein Justice Building on Thursday, Aug. 14, 2025, in Miami, Fla. Olea was seen at the courthouse after a plea agreement in his case was announced. Photo by Matias J. Ocner mocner@miamiherald.com “Jurors are not always convinced beyond a reasonable doubt,” Schneider said.On plea agreements, Schneider said, a “victim’s wishes are not controlling,” but are “certainly, to all prosecutors, very important.”The victim who spoke to the Herald said she did not feel that her wishes had been considered, and instead felt she had to give “pep talks” to prosecutor Bronwyn Nayci, to get the case to trial.Olea had been charged with the six counts of sexual battery of a minor but two of those were dropped before the plea deal. When asked by a reporter, spokesperson Ed Griffith said that was due to “legal issues” that would be “fully explained once the case is actually closed.”Olea has two separate state cases against him.The two charges that were dropped are related to “E.M.”, who is now in her early thirties. She says Olea began sexually assaulting her when she was 16.In the plea agreement, the charges would be modified: four second-degree felonies for crimes against two victims, two of which involve sex with a minor.Jenny Rossman, a former sex crimes prosecutor who now works for a private firm, said that it did not surprise her that the charges were lowered, as it is often difficult to prove custodial authority in court.Both victims told the Herald and police that Olea would often pick them up from school, take them to practice, take them to his mother’s house where he lived, and off the island of Key Biscayne for practice or to see a movie.This story was originally published August 18, 2025 at 4:46 PM. Gerstein Justice Building on Thursday, Aug. 14, 2025, in Miami, Fla. Olea was surrounded by his attorneys, Charlton Stoner and Matthew Ladd, far-left. Photo by Matias J. Ocner mocner@miamiherald.com More than a decade after he allegedly sexually abused at least three minors, a former Key Biscayne gymnastics coach spotlighted in a Miami Herald investigation last year has reached a deal with state prosecutors to plead guilty to four felony sex charges, including two related to the sexual abuse of a minor.The agreement was revealed Thursday in a Miami-Dade courtroom days before Oscar Olea, 40, was set to go to trial on the sex abuse allegations.He has been incarcerated since his Feb. 28 arrest last year, after Miami-Dade Circuit Judge Alberto Milian judge called him a ‘likely pedophile’ and ordered that he remain in jail until his trial.Olea is scheduled enter his guilty plea and be sentenced next week, at a hearing where victims will testify about the impact of his abuse. Olea would also need to enter a sex offender treatment program, according to a copy of the agreement reviewed by the Herald. The deal needs to be ratified by Milian. Olea’s arrest last year came weeks after the Miami Herald published its Key Biscayne’s Dark Secret investigation, which told for the first time the story of five of the coach’s alleged victims: Four former students who were minors at the time of their alleged abuse and Olea’s colleague at the community center where he worked, who told the Herald he began abusing her when she was a minor.Olea stood in the court room Thursday in an orange jumpsuit and handcuffs, clasping his own hands. His hair was grown out and he appeared to have aged during his time in custody. He flatly said “yes, sir” when Milian asked whether he had read and signed the agreement.Milian told Olea that he has until next week to change his mind about the plea and go to trial.
