full_text: Bulgaria's female 'Andrew Tate' incites anti-women violence SocietyBulgariaBulgaria's female 'Andrew Tate' incites anti-women violenceMina Kirkova in Sofia06/13/2025June 13, 2025Zornitsa Gyutsova is a Bulgarian influencer whose misogynistic online content has sparked outrage in Bulgaria. Why is there a market for her content in the Balkan country and how are some Bulgarians fighting it?https://p.dw.com/p/4vrvKOn her social media profiles, Bulgarian influencer Zornitsa Gyutsova posts misogynistic advice about how men should 'deal with' womenImage: Zgyutsova/TikTokAdvertisement Women love men who can be violent if need be. That's why they like men who hit them, Bulgarian influencer Zornitsa Gyutsova tells her followers. Gyutsova suggests that not only do women prefer men who physically assault them, but that this is also the way men should behave because a woman should respect a man's physical power since she is unable to comprehend his intellectual power. This is the kind of advice that can be found on Gyutsova's social media profiles and in a private group founded by her on Telegram called Upstanding Man. 'Equality is contrary to human nature' Zornitsa Gyutsova offers her followers private chats over video where she teaches them how to deal with women — for a fee, of course. Many influencers, life coaches and other online personalities in Bulgaria and elsewhere offer private sessions or courses. What makes Gyutsova's content stand out from the rest is that its sole purpose is to explain to men that they need to learn to control their partners both psychologically and, if necessary, physically.There have been numerous protests against violence against women in Bulgaria in recent years, such as this one in 2023Image: Alexandar Detev/DW In Gyutsova's view, men in general have been treated badly by women, and women are the ones who exert violence on men, namely by not paying them enough respect. The idea of equality is like a worm in people's brains that insists men and women should be partners […] which is so contrary to human nature that it can never work, Gyutsova declared in a long video about her work that was broadcast on Bulgarian National Television. Although the broadcaster, which is partly financed by taxpayer's money, has since removed the video from its platforms, it has never publicly commented on the case. Huge backlash Gyutsova's profiles on social media have been gaining traction for several years now. Screenshots and videos from her private Telegram group chat recently surfaced on social media, triggering a huge backlash in Bulgaria. Local woman Petya Krasteva was so appalled by Gyutsova's online content that she filed a complaint against Gyutsova with the prosecutor's office. On her social media channels, she not only encourages people to degrade women and use violence against them, she also boasts that she uses the same methods on her child and her cat, she told DW. I thought to myself: This is not only absolutely unacceptable, it's criminal. Gender discrimination not a crime in Bulgaria Many other women did the same as Krasteva, only to find out a couple of weeks later that their efforts had been in vain.Petya Krasteva was appalled by Zornitsa Gyutsova's online content and filed a complaint against her with the prosecutor's officeImage: Nikola Gyulmezov In an official reply, the prosecutor's office stated that nothing could be done because Bulgaria's criminal code does not define gender discrimination as a crime and that the issue was a matter for the Commission against Discrimination. Krasteva promptly lodged a complaint with this commission, but received another negative answer based on the same reasoning. Profiles briefly taken down Although these complaints did not lead to charges being brought against Gyutsova, the backlash did have an impact. The outcry and the fact that Gyutsova's social media accounts were reported by people who found their content abhorrent, meant that the influencer's TikTok and Instagram profiles were deactivated. They were, however, reactivated a short time later. Impunity for abusers Krasteva feels that part of the reason why content like Gyutsova's strikes a chord in Bulgaria is that while patriarchal norms and domestic violence are not accepted in the country, Bulgarian society often turns a blind eye to them. The other huge problem, she says, is that as with many other social issues, there is a complete lack of consequences for the perpetrators. Valentina Dimitrova, a psychologist who works for the Emprove Foundation, a Bulgarian organization that supports women who have suffered domestic violence, holds a similar view.Psychologist Valentina Dimitrova says that content like Gyutsova's is dangerous because 'it can truly cost a human life'Image: Venera Velkovska Sadly it's embedded in the Bulgarian mindset that we often just accept that things are bad and we do nothing about it, says Dimitrova. She believes that this is also why many women stay in violent relationships: They simply have no faith in the authorities because time and time again, men who beat or even kill their partners face no legal consequences. Although some people seem to think that social media content is less problematic than actual abuse in real life, Dimitrova stresses the dangers associated with such content: It can truly cost a human life. A global online problem Misogynistic online content that paints women as lesser human beings and men as oppressed by women is not unique to Bulgaria. Such content has been growing and spreading all over the world in recent years. Influencers like Andrew Tate, who faces charges of rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and more, have created a whole movement around this sort of content. Gyutsova fits neatly into this category of influencer, but what makes her different is that she is a woman. What role does feminism play? Dimitrova thinks one issue here is that feminism is often misunderstood. Feminism does not entail men being suppressed and women controlling them. It means that women can have equal rights and can function as equals to men not only in society but also in their personal relationships, she says. Dimitrova also believes that the patriarchal notion that men should not be allowed to express emotions is highly problematic. This is reflected in Gyutsova's content, which suggests that men are weak and not manly if they dare to express their fears, emotions or feelings.People in Sofia attend a protest against domestic violence and violence against women in Bulgaria in 2023 after a young woman was stabbed by her ex-partner Image: Alexandar Detev/DW It's a vicious circle: Men who are not allowed to express any sort of emotion for fear of being labeled weak don't know what to do when they experience something frustrating in their relationships and so they resort to aggression, says Dimitrova. What can be done? Dimitrova suggests that first and foremost, men should receive support and their concerns should not just be swept under the carpet. She stresses, however, that this support should not validate the inclination to deal with problems by exerting psychological or physical violence on women. Although the Emprove Foundation focuses primarily on women's rights and issues, it does have a project that focuses on men's mental health — something the foundation says is incredibly important in the fight against gender-based violence. Men should be encouraged to connect to a healthy understanding of themselves, so they can build healthy relationships as well, says Dimitrova. Petya Krasteva firmly believes that even though authorities in Bulgaria rarely provide the support needed in cases like this, society should not remain indifferent. We should be as loud as possible when something like this turns up, she says. We should be perfectly clear that it is unacceptable. That way, other people who come across this content will know that this is not something that society approves of, and that could help them realize that they shouldn't have anything to do with it. Dimitrova agrees. We will keep talking about it [this kind of content], calling it out and not tolerating it until the authorities wake up. headline: Pune Crime Files: How cops traced engineering student Bhagyashree Sude’s killers from a ransom message
who: Bhagyashree Sude’s; Devendra Fadnavis; Hafiz Sude; Suryakant Sude; Wagholi; Sagar Ramesh Jadhav; Sagar; Sarjerao Kumbhar; Fadnavis
where: Harangul; Viman Nagar; Pune; Hindi; Mumbai; Nanded; Kamargaon; Ahilyanagar
when: 22-year-old; March 30 last year; fourth-year; around 9 pm; March 30, 2024; April 2; The same day; 21; two years; March 28; 23; the day; March 30; April 7; his school days; 120B
full_text: Pune Crime Files: How cops traced engineering student Bhagyashree Sude’s killers from a ransom message Fulfilling a promise made by Devendra Fadnavis, who was the home minister of Maharashtra at the time, senior lawyer and Rajya Sabha MP Ujjwal Nikam recently appeared before a Pune court for a hearing in the Bhagyashree Sude murder case. The 22-year-old engineering student was allegedly murdered by three youths, including her college friend, on March 30 last year. The state government has appointed Nikam as the Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) in the case. Bhagyashree goes missing A native of Harangul village in Maharashtra’s Latur district, Bhagyashree was a fourth-year student of BE (Computer Science) at GH Raisoni College in Pune’s Wagholi and resided at Sakore Nagar. As per police records, she went to Phoenix Mall in Viman Nagar around 9 pm on March 30, 2024. Bhagyashree had told her mother that she was going to a friend’s birthday party, but went missing soon after, the police said. On failing to contact Bhagyashree, her parents came to Pune and lodged a missing-person report at Viman Nagar police station on April 2. The same day, her mother received a ransom message from Bhagyashree’s mobile phone: “Allah Hafiz Sude family. Stop searching for Bhagyashree. We have kidnapped her. We have sent her to a foreign country.” The message, which was in Hindi, directed Bhagyashree’s parents to transfer Rs 9 lakh to her bank account for her release and threatened to throw pieces of her body in her native village if the police were informed. Investigators later said the message was meant to “divert” their attention and make her family and the police believe that she was still alive. Meanwhile, Bhagyashree’s father Suryakant Sude, a former sarpanch, lodged a First Information Report (FIR) of kidnapping under section 364 (a) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). A technical investigation confirmed that the ransom message to Bhagyashree’s parents was sent from Mumbai’s Jogeshwari area. A police team went to Mumbai, but could not trace the accused. As the probe into Bhagyashree’s mobile phone calls and bank account continued, the police zeroed in on Shivam Madhav Fulawale, 21, a student of BE (IT) at her college. Officers said Bhagyashree knew Fulawale, a native of Nanded, for two years as they were in the same college and belonged to the Marathwada region. They used to talk to each other and she had even met him on March 28, the police said. Based on clues obtained during the investigation, investigators arrested Fulawale from Wagholi for his alleged role in Bhagyashree’s murder. Subsequently, his aides Suresh Shivaji Indure, 23, and Sagar Ramesh Jadhav, 23, were also arrested. A mall visit and a pit dug the day before The probe revealed that Bhagyashree went with Fulawale on March 30 when he came to Phoenix Mall in a rented car along with his friends Suresh and Sagar. The police suspect that Fulawale may have offered to drop her near her room but the three men allegedly choked her to death in the car. Officers said the accused allegedly took her body to a secluded spot at Kamargaon village in Ahilyanagar district. They suspect the men burnt her body with petrol before burying her. The police recovered Bhagyashree’s body from the spot on April 7. Referring to the pit in which Bhagyashree was found buried, an officer said the accused had dug it the day before committing the crime, suggesting that her murder was a premeditated and well-planned act. The accused had hired a car on rent to commit the crime. The police said they went to Mumbai and Nanded after the murder before returning to Pune and giving the car back to the service provider. The vehicle was subsequently seized for investigation. Plan hatched after ‘losses in share market, gaming’ The police said Suresh, who has a diploma in IT and worked in Mumbai, knew Fulawale as both hail from the same district. Fulawale knew Sagar, a Class 10 pass, since his school days. The accused were charged under Indian Penal Code (IPC) sections 302 (murder), 120B (criminal conspiracy), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence), 404 (dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person), and 34 (common intention). As the police began probing the motive behind the murder, it came to light that the suspects had become debt-ridden after losing their money in the share market and to online gaming. So they allegedly hatched a conspiracy to kidnap Bhagyashree and extort money from her family. Officers, however, suspect that she may have been murdered because of her attempts to resist them. Sarjerao Kumbhar, Senior Police Inspector, said, “The accused committed the crime for money. There was no sexual assault on the victim. The accused had no previous criminal record. Technical investigation helped us in solving the case.” After the murder triggered outrage, Fadnavis, who was then the deputy chief minister and home minister of the state at the time, visited Bhagyashree’s family and said he would personally request advocate Ujjwal Nikam to be the SPP in the case. A police officer who was part of the investigation said a chargesheet has been filed against the three accused who are currently in jail. The case is on before a court in Pune.

headline: UK to use AI to predict theft, knife attacks and violent crimes by 2030
who: John; Tom Cruise; Peter Kylethe; Geolitica
where: UK; AI; United Kingdom; England; Wales; Los Angeles; Chicago; Netherlands
how: predict theft, knife attacks and violent
full_text: UK to use AI to predict theft, knife attacks and violent crimes by 2030 Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining the way we do things, but none of it reflects the dystopian worlds we see in movies and TV series. However, that may soon change as the United Kingdom government now wants to use the technology to create interactive crime maps that will help “predict where offences are most likely to occur.” The announcement sounds straight out of the popular dystopian science fiction thriller Minority Report, where John (Tom Cruise) works with the PreCrime police to stop crimes before they occur using three “PreCogs”, who can foresee crimes. In a press release, the UK government said the Technology Secretary Peter Kylethe, the detailed real-time interactive crime map will span across England and Wales and will help “detect, track and predict where devastating knife crime is likely to occur or spot anti-social behaviour early on” to give the police a head start and intel ahead of dangerous situations. Part of the Safer Streets Mission, the AI-powered, real-time interactive crime map is aimed at tackling crime in urban areas. The UK government will be making an initial investment of £4 million for the prototype model, which is expected to come out in April 2026. Under the £500 million R&D Missions Accelerator Programme, the UK government wants a fully functional system by 2030. Designed to focus on crimes that “make people unsafe” in their own neighbourhoods from theft, anti-social behaviour, knife crime and violent crime, the system will help aggregate data shared between police, councils and social services by analysing “previous incident locations and studying the patterns of known offenders.” The map will help the police officers identify areas where the crime rate is high and deploy resources as added to prevent future crimes. The use of AI might sound like science fiction, but similar initiatives in other parts of the world have had mixed results. For example, predictive policing tools used in Los Angeles and Chicago were decommissioned after they were accused of racial bias and had limited success. Another predictive software project named Geolitica (previously called PredPol) was discontinued in 2020, after its effectiveness was cited as uncertain. However, the Crime Anticipation System (CAS), a project in the Netherlands, has seen modest success in terms of burglary rates. The Danish police have also successfully used AI systems to help with fraud investigations.

full_text: Three knifed to death for trying to stop drunk men from ransacking dhaba Three men who tried to stop a group of drunk men from ransacking a dhaba in Chhattisgarh’s Dhamtari district were stabbed to death late Monday night. The incident took place outside Annapurna Dhaba in Bhoyna village, around 78 kilometres from the state capital Raipur. “A group was ransacking the place, throwing tables around in an inebriated condition. The men, Alok Singh Thakur, Nitin Tandi and Suresh Hiyal, and their friends were having food,” said a police official from Arjuni police station. “The men tried to stop the group, but the accused attacked them with a knife. The prime accused, identified as Gopi Diwan (20), was carrying the weapon, and he allegedly stabbed the three men. One of the victims tried to run away but was chased and attacked by Diwan. All three died on the spot. Once police received information, we swung into action and caught all the suspects. We also seized the murder weapon,” the official said. “Eight persons, including three minors, were detained after the incident. The five adults, including Diwan, have been arrested and sent to judicial custody. We are finding out if they have a prior criminal record,” said Superintendent of Police, Dhamtari, Suraj Singh. The three minors have been sent to a correctional home. Police have invoked sections of murder and unlawful assembly of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

full_text: Karnataka woman chopped into 19 pieces; son-in-law among 3 held for murder Four days after the body parts of a woman were found dumped in several locations in Chimpuganahalli in Karnataka’s Tumakuru district, the police on Monday arrested three people, including her son-in-law, a dentist, for the murder. The police identified the deceased as Lakshmi Devi, 42, a resident of Bellavi village, and the accused as Dr Ramachandraiah S, 47, Satish K N, 38, and Kiran K S, 32, all residents of Kallahalli. Ramachandraiah is married to Devi’s daughter, Tejasvi, 26, the police said, adding that this was his second marriage. According to the police, on August 3, Devi left her home to see her daughter. A day later, her husband, Basavaraj, lodged a missing person’s complaint at Bellavi police station. Three days later, on August 7, the police were alerted about 19 body parts being found at various places in Chimpuganahalli. The body parts were found inside bags that were disposed of at no fewer than 19 locations, the police said. The Koratagere police registered a murder case and sent a message to all police stations in the district to check if any missing person complaints had been filed. It was then that the Bellavi police informed Basavaraj, who identified the body as Devi’s. According to the police, CCTV footage showed that a Maruti Suzuki Brezza was used to dump the body parts. The vehicle was allegedly registered in the name of Satish. “We took custody of Satish, and he spilled the beans. Satish and Kiran were taken into custody from Hornad. Ramachandraiah was in Dharmasthala after the murder and was not available for questioning. This also raised our suspicion,” a police officer said. Ramachandraiah allegedly claimed that his wife was listening to her mother’s advice and causing trouble in their marriage, Ashok K V, Superintendent of Police (SP), Tumakuru district, said. “He was unhappy over his mother-in-law’s interference. His first marriage is still in the divorce stage. In 2019, he married Tejasvi,” SP Ashok added. “We are yet to know why the accused cut her body into pieces and threw it at different locations. We have produced them before the court and will take them to police custody for further questioning. The car gave us the major lead to crack the case,” he said. According to the police, Satish was one of Ramachandraiah’s patients and stayed near his house. Kiran was Satish’s cousin, the police added. SP Ashok denied reports that the murder was linked to human sacrifice.

full_text: Ex-TMC leader Bibhas Adhikari, arrested in Noida for a ‘fake police station’, allegedly ran similar set-up in Kolkata Ex-TMC leader Bibhas Chandra Adhikari, arrested in Noida for “running a fake police station”, has allegedly been found to have operated a similar set-up in Kolkata. Adhikari, a former Trinamool Block President from Nalhati in Birbhum and once under the CBI and ED scanner in the teachers’ recruitment scam, was picked up along with his son and four others for allegedly running the “International Police & Crime Investigation Bureau” in Noida’s Sector 70 on Saturday night. Police said the group allegedly posed as government officials to extort money. Investigations by Kolkata police revealed that in Kolkata’s Beleghata area, Adhikari had allegedly rented two flats on CIT Road where he displayed boards reading “Investigation of Social Justice”, “Interpol” and “Police”. He would allegedly arrive in a car with a blue beacon with four armed guards. Police claimed he owns significant assets, including an Ayurvedic college in Suri, a B.Ed college in Krishnapur, and houses in Kolkata and Delhi. Adhikari was removed from his Trinamool post before the 2021 elections, later forming the “Bhartiya Arya Samaj” party. However, he was seen sharing the stage with TMC leaders in 2024 and was accused of taking money in exchange for job promises in the teachers’ recruitment scam. Sources said he was considered close to jailed former Education Minister Partha Chatterjee. His Krishnapur ashram housed an office using the letterhead of the “National Bureau of Social Investigation and Social Justice.” The CBI questioned him multiple times in 2023 in the recruitment case. headline: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver
who: Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad; Aruna; Gailkwad; Gaikwad; Santwadi; Gaikwad’s; Ananda Chavan; Mayur Vijay Solse; Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane
where: Pune Rural; Malshej; Kasara; Gangapur Road; Nashik; Solse; Chavan; Gangapur
when: January 27; 56; around 7.30 pm; Around 10.30 pm that night; Around 2.30 am; January 28; around 9.30 am; three days; January 31; 21; 2022; 2024
full_text: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver Around 7.30 on January 27, Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad, 56, a resident of Nashik who worked as a rental cab driver, called his wife Aruna on her phone. He had taken a trip from Nashik to Pune around 5 am that day. He told her he would reach home around 7.30 pm. That was the last conversation Aruna had with her husband. Repeated calls made to him were unanswered. Around 10.30 pm that night, Gailkwad’s wife got a call that his phone had been found on the Alephata Santwadi road off the Pune-Nashik highway. The caller had kept the phone at a nearby hotel, from where he had made the call. Around 2.30 am on January 28, the Gaikwad family reached the hotel and searched for him in the area where the phone was found. However, Gaikwad and his car could not be traced. The family registered a missing person case at Alephata police station under the Pune Rural police. At around 9.30 am on January 28, while police were actively searching for Gaikwad, his body was discovered in the Santwadi area. His hands were bound behind his back with a nylon rope and a zip tie, and initial autopsy findings indicated that he had been strangled. The murder investigation was taken up jointly by teams from the Alephata police station and the Pune Rural police’s Local Crime Branch. As part of the investigation, the police reviewed footage from dozens of CCTV cameras on the approach routes to the area. A significant breakthrough came when Gaikwad’s vehicle was spotted on a hotel’s CCTV camera along the Nashik–Pune highway corridor. By piecing together video evidence from multiple locations, investigators traced the car’s movement—first heading toward the area where his body was later discovered, then continuing in the direction of Malshej Ghat. Both the footage and ground inquiries indicated that, at one stage, four people were inside the car along with Gaikwad. Meanwhile, a team which was on the lookout for the car found it abandoned in Kasara Ghat, along the route to Nashik. Continued analysis of CCTV footage helped police identify suspects who were captured travelling in the vehicle. Over the following three days, till January 31, investigators arrested three suspects: Vishal Ananda Chavan, 22; Mayur Vijay Solse, 23; and Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane, 21, all residents of the Gangapur Road area in Nashik. The investigation to arrest the fourth suspect continues even now. Driver resisted carjacking attempt, say police Investigators found out that the suspects had boarded Gaikwad’s car during his return journey to Nashik from Pune. They used the pretext of hitching a ride, but wanted to hijack the vehicle, said the police. The sequence of events, as brought out by the investigation, was that they allegedly strangled him after he resisted their attempt. The group then disposed of his body and fled the scene, said the police. It was soon revealed that the trio are hardened criminals. They allegedly intended to use the hijacked car for an armed robbery in which they wanted to target a shop in Nashik. The police said they, however, decided to abandon it on the way since they thought the vehicle would be flagged in the murder investigation after Gaikwad’s body was found. Solse and Chavan are facing charges of murder registered at Gangapur police station in Nashik in 2022. As the police continued their probe, they found out that these suspects were involved in a case of carjacking at Chakan police station registered in 2024, which had remained unsolved till the time the murder case was cracked. “The chargesheet in the case was filed subsequently. All three accused are currently in prison under judicial custody. A coordinated search for the fourth accused continued. The wanted suspect in the case also has multiple offences registered against him,” said an officer who was part of the probe. The case underscores the dangers faced by drivers who pick up unknown passengers outside their assigned duties. Authorities have reiterated their warning against this practice, noting that similar incidents of passengers turning violent have been reported in the past.

headline: Gurgaon man masturbates in front of woman waiting for cab, police file FIR
who: Krishan Kumar
where: Gurgaon; Jaipur

full_text: Gurgaon man masturbates in front of woman waiting for cab, police file FIR The Gurgaon police on August 5 registered a case against a man who was caught on camera allegedly masturbating in front of a young woman near Rajiv Chowk in the city, officers said on Thursday. According to the police, the incident took place on August 2 when the complainant, a model and digital content creator, was waiting for a cab around noon at a busy junction to head home after a journey from Jaipur. Krishan Kumar, Station House Officer, Civil Lines Police Station, said that the police have filed a First Information Report (FIR) under sections 75(2) for sexual harassment and 78 for stalking of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. “The investigation is underway, and the complainant has also joined the probe, and we have recorded her statement. We are scanning CCTV footage in and around the spot and talking to people in the area.” On the same day of the incident, the model narrated her ordeal on social media and posted the video of the alleged act of the perpetrator, while also blaming the police for the delay in registering a complaint. “Something very strange happened to me. A man came around, circling, and he was constantly staring at me. Initially, I just ignored it, like the others do,” she said. She noticed that the man with unzipped pants was allegedly masturbating. The video showed the man wearing a facemask and a backpack that he had slung over his chest to cover the act from being too visible to the public nearby. The woman said it was clear he was ‘very aware’ of what he was doing. The woman in her video also lamented how cab companies were delaying in accepting her ride request, aggravating her ordeal. The complainant stated that although she had initially got a ride booked, the driver was not picking up despite multiple calls, and hence she had to re-book across applications “just to avoid the creep”. Eventually, a cab arrived and she reached home. In the video, she also alleged initial inaction from the police after she had tagged the police and other government authorities while putting the man’s video on X, and later calling the police helpline. “There wasn’t even an automated message,” she said. Regarding the FIR, the model said, the police had asked her to come to the station instead of lodging the complaint online. “It was making me feel very uncomfortable. I felt very, very disgusted. Initially, I froze. I did not record or hit him. People who say I could have shouted at him do not understand what goes through a girl’s mind at that moment. Reactions go viral faster than the real truth, and people judge; they do not help.” The woman stated she wanted to be safe rather than have the moment become viral. “I am not making the video for any kind of attention, just want to be heard,” she said in the video.

full_text: Leader of 'cult-like' UK Christian group guilty of sexually abusing women 'Cult-like' Christian group leader found guilty of sexually abusing multiple women in congregationTopic:Courts1h ago1 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 12:24amChristopher Brain was the leader of the Nine O'Clock Service. (Supplied: South Yorkshire Police)In short: Christopher Brain, 68, was convicted of 17 indecent assault charges relating to nine women. He denied all 36 charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.What's next?Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said it would carefully consider a retrial since the jury could not reach a verdict on four counts of indecent assault and an alleged rape.abc.net.au/news/cult-like-christian-group-leader-found-guilty-of-sexual-abuse/105684554Link copiedShareShare articleA former Church of England priest in the UK has been found guilty of sexually abusing nine women in his congregation.Christopher Brain was the leader of a cult-like Christian group called the Nine O'Clock Service, based in Sheffield, northern England, in the 80s and 90s.The evangelical church movement was famous among young people for its 9pm services on Sundays that featured a live band. At its peak, it attracted hundreds of attendees.But, prosecutors said, Brain, 68, controlled members of the congregation, cutting them off from family and friends, and abused his position to sexually assault a staggering number of women .Brain also had a homebase team of young women dubbed the lycra nuns , prosecutor Tim Clark said. They looked after him, his wife and daughter at their house in Sheffield.He was charged with 36 counts of indecent assault and one count of rape relating to 13 women between 1981 and 1995. He denied the charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.After a trial at the Inner London Crown Court, Brain was convicted on Wednesday, local time, of 17 charges of indecent assault relating to nine women. He was acquitted of a further 15 counts.The jury was unable to reach a verdict on the remaining four counts of indecent assault and the alleged rape, Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said on Thursday, adding it would carefully consider a retrial.'Failing of the church'The Nine O'Clock Service had the blessing of the Church of England. Prosecutors said in 1990 that the Archbishop of Canterbury-elect, George Carey, had met Brain to discuss his methods.Brain's ordination was fast-tracked, and the Nine O'Clock Service spent large sums of money to obtain the outfit worn by actor Robert De Niro for the 1986 film The Mission for the ceremony, prosecutors said.But Brain resigned and left the church days before the broadcast of a 1995 BBC documentary, which accused him of sexually inappropriate behaviour. Mr Carey said he was crushed and let down when the allegations were made public.In his evidence, Brain said he received massages from members of the Nine O'Clock Service, which he said occasionally moved towards sexual activity. He also denied controlling or manipulating members of the congregation. What happened was an appalling abuse of power and leadership that should never have occurred, Bishop of Sheffield Pete Wilcox said in a statement. Where concerns were raised in the past and were not acted upon properly, that was a failing of the Church. For those institutional failures, I offer an unreserved apology. full_text: Police chase 'a bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers', witness says Launceston man refused bail after low-speed chase in stolen truck driven on rimsBy Hayden SmithTopic:Courts6h ago6 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:23pmLoading...In short:A Newnham man has been refused bail after engaging Tasmania police in an hours-long pursuit in a stolen truck on Wednesday, at times while the truck's tyres were blown-out.A bystander has said the noise of metal on the road from the truck being driven on its wheel rims was pretty insane .What's next?Patrick Brown has pleaded guilty to dangerous driving charges and evade police.abc.net.au/news/launceston-man-pleads-guilty-after-stolen-truck-evade/105681218Link copiedShareShare articleA 27-year-old who pleaded guilty to driving a stolen truck on its rims through Launceston has been refused bail.Patrick Brown pleaded guilty to a number of charges in the Launceston Magistrate's Court on Thursday, including two counts of evading police and dangerous driving.The court heard Brown stole a white tipper truck on Tuesday, which he drove on the following night through some of the region's busiest streets, including the East Tamar Highway — at times veering onto the wrong side of the road and ignoring traffic lights.Loading...The court heard he continued for several hours after police spiked the tyres, with Brown then driving the truck on its rims.Numerous police units, including a helicopter, were involved in the truck's pursuit.Police say Brown, from the Launceston suburb of Newnham, was later arrested in Ravenswood without further incident .Sound of 'metal on road': WitnessA Dilston resident who saw part of the pursuit said he was alerted to something happening when he heard a chopper hovering over . I went out to get a better view … and looked down John Lees Drive to see a convoy, he said. You had the truck at the front, police cars flanking and the chopper overhead. The noise was very loud. It was just metal on road [from the wheel rims] — pretty insane really. Dilston is 17 kilometres north-west of Ravenswood, where the driver was arrested.'A bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers'The white, tipper truck was stolen on Tuesday and involved in the chase the following day. (Supplied: Richard Morris)The witness described the scene as a slow-moving police chase with this helicopter and truck in no condition to evade police. He said it was a bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers . Normally it's a pretty quiet place, down there at Dilston. full_text: Officer, elderly woman seriously injured in separate crashes involving police cars WA police officer, 80yo woman injured in separate crashes in Northam, SubiacoBy Kate ChristianTopic:Police17h ago17 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52amA police officer was seriously injured in a crash near Northam, north of Perth. (ABC News)abc.net.au/news/several-injured-after-several-crashes-involving-police-vehicles/105682658Link copiedShareShare articleA police officer has been airlifted to hospital and an elderly woman has been left with serious injuries after two separate crashes involving police vehicles on Thursday.Commander Mike Peters said a marked police car was involved in a collision with a semi-trailer on the Great Eastern Highway near Northam in the Central Wheatbelt just before 11am.A second officer in the car is being treated for minor injuries, while the driver of the semi-trailer was not injured.The police car was involved in a collision with a semi-trailer. (ABC News)Around 20 minutes later at 11.15am, police were responding to reports of a person being armed with a gun when they were involved in a collision with another vehicle on Bagot Road in Subiaco. They were driving under emergency conditions when they collided with an 80-year-old lady turning into a driveway, Commander Peters said. As a result she has been taken to hospital with serious injuries. The officers were not injured. Commander Mike Peters said police did their best to protect the community. full_text: 'Depraved and offensive': WA teacher jailed over multiple child sex offences WA teacher Harry Sing Wan Lagdon jailed after admitting 25 child sex offencesDBy David WeberTopic:Courts19h ago19 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38amHarry Lagdon was sentenced in the District Court of WA on Thursday. (ABC News: Jack Stevenson)In short:Teacher Harry Sing Wan Lagdon groomed a student when she was 15 and had sex with her on school grounds.He also engaged in online offending with three other girls, aged 12 and 13.What's next:Lagdon will be eligible for parole after five years and nine months.abc.net.au/news/wa-teacher-jailed-for-child-sex-offences/105681636Link copiedShareShare articleA WA teacher who groomed and had sex with a teenage student, then sent depraved online messages to even younger girls, has been sentenced to more than seven years in prison.Harry Sing Wan Lagdon, now 29, became sexually involved with the student when she was 15, and their encounters took place on the grounds of the regional high school where he taught and she was enrolled.Lagdon, who was nine years older than the victim, sent hundreds of videos and photos to her over 18 months. Basically, explicit material every other day, District Court Judge Matthew Curwood said.The court heard sexual encounters between them took place in a classroom, a closet and a shed on the school's property, inside his car and at his apartment.Harry Lagdon pleaded guilty to a string of child sex offences. (ABC News)'Breach of trust'It had all started with what the judge described as Lagdon's grooming behaviour , providing gifts to the teenager including a necklace.Support services:Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors): 1800 272 831Lifeline (24-hour Crisis Line): 131 114Victims of Crime Helpline: 1800 819 817Before long, the relief teacher was asking the girl for explicit photos, and sending images and videos of himself to her.The offending also included oral sex and indecent touching in various locations on school grounds, and sexual intercourse without a condom in his car and apartment.While Lagdon's lawyer described it as a consensual relationship , the judge said it represented a significant breach of trust and the victim had nightmares as a result.After he relocated from the regional school to Perth, Lagdon started communicating online with three girls in Queensland, aged 12 to 13, pretending he was a teenager.'Depraved and offensive'Lagdon sent hundreds of messages, some of which the judge described as depraved and offensive .The teacher asked for explicit images from the three girls and two of them complied.Judge Curwood told the court girls aged 12 to 13 were inherently vulnerable to online predators and the psychological impact is likely to be profound and long lasting .Lagdon had pleaded guilty to 25 charges, including sexual penetration of a child over 16 under his authority, exposing a child under 13 to indecent matter, procuring or encouraging a child to engage in sexual behaviour, and possessing child exploitation material.Lagdon also admitted to possessing child exploitation material. (AAP: Mick Tsikas)The judge acknowledged Lagdon's pleas in February had avoided the need for a trial.Lagdon's lawyer Mark Gunning had told the court his client's actions had been devastating for him and his shame was palpable .Mr Gunning said while the school student and Lagdon were infatuated with each other , it was totally inappropriate .He said his client acknowledged his teaching career was finished.Lagdon's total prison sentence of seven years was backdated to June 2024, with eligibility for parole after five years and nine months.The judge ordered that his mobile phone and laptop be destroyed.Loading...LoadingPosted 19h ago19 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38am, updated 18h ago18 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:45amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesAs Israel pushes on with Gaza City invasion, Palestinians trapped there are protestingTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A group of protesters in Gaza holding Palestinian flags and signs in Arabic script.Jason Clare details outcomes of childcare safety meetingLIVEPhoto shows A close up of a man wearing a suit speaking. full_text: Mental health condition considered in sentencing of teen girl shot by police Townsville teen girl shot by police released from detention for mental health treatmentBy Meghan DansieABC North QldTopic:Crime19h ago19 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:01amPolice were called to reports of a female armed with a knife making threats near Townsville's West End Hotel in June. (ABC News: Baz Ruddick)In short:A North Queensland magistrate has criticised Queensland Health in its handling of a teenage girl shot by police.She has been sentenced to 62 days imprisonment, already served.What's next?The now 18-year-old will be released from detention and transferred to hospital for further mental health assessment.abc.net.au/news/teen-girl-shot-by-police-released-for-mental-health-treatment/105680402Link copiedShareShare articleA North Queensland magistrate has criticised Queensland Health over its handling of a teenage girl shot by police.Warning: This story contains mention of suicide and self-harm.The teenager, who self-harmed more than 80 times while being held in youth detention, has been released by the court and sent to hospital for treatment.The now 18-year-old from Townsville was shot by police in June after they were called to reports of a female armed with a large knife making threats near Townsville's West End Hotel.The Ethical Standards Command investigated the Townsville shooting. (ABC News: Chloe Chomicki)Magistrate Viviana Keegan sentenced the woman, who was 17 at the time of the incident, to 62 days imprisonment, already served, for serious assault and obstruction of police.She will be released from Cleveland Youth Detention Centre today and transferred by ambulance to the Townsville University Hospital for further mental health assessment.If you or anyone you know needs help:Suicide Call Back Service on 1300 659 467Lifeline on 13 11 14Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander crisis support line 13YARN on 13 92 76Kids Helpline on 1800 551 800Beyond Blue on 1300 224 636Headspace on 1800 650 890ReachOut at au.reachout.comMensLine Australia on 1300 789 978QLife 1800 184 527The hearing in Townsville's Children's Court was told the teenager had been treated for numerous diagnosed mental health conditions since she was 14.Magistrate Keegan said during her time in custody the teenager was treated for 80 incidents of self-harm and had been admitted for emergency medical treatment 16 times. The criminal justice system can't manage [her], Magistrate Keegan said.She questioned why four suicide attempts, and being shot by police, had not resulted in an involuntary treatment order — which previously resulted in the refusal of a bail application. It's been sought on a number of occasions and on each occasion the clinical team has considered it not necessary, she said. It seems that is what is needed. Magistrate Viviana Keegan sentenced the now 18-year-old to 62 days imprisonment, already served. (ABC North Queensland: Rachael Merritt)Officers were called to the West End Hotel in Townsville at 5:30pm on June 10 after reports a female armed with a large knife was making threats.The court heard the teenager was shot by a police officer after she ignored numerous warnings while she advanced on them brandishing a knife.The Ethical Standards Command investigated the Townsville shooting.Due to the aggravating factor of the knife used in the assaults the magistrate said the teenager was being tried under adult crime, adult time laws passed by the Queensland government last year.She told the now 18-year-old, who appeared via video link from Cleveland Youth Detention Centre, to consider the impact of her actions and seek help moving forward. There are a lot of risks, Magistrate Keegan said. I hope you do as much as you can to engage with the mental health people. full_text: Police charge second man over Melbourne synagogue firebombing Police charge 20-year-old Meadow Heights man over Adass Israel Synagogue arson attackTopic:Crime19h ago19 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 5:55amLoading...In short:A 20-year-old man is facing three charges in relation to an alleged arson attack on a synagogue in Melbourne's south east.He is the second person to be charged over the firebombing.What's next:The man is expected to face court next week. abc.net.au/news/second-man-charged-adass-israel-synagogue-arson-ripponlea/105682132Link copiedShareShare articleCounter-terrorism police have charged a second man over the firebombing of the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne in December last year.The building in Ripponlea in Melbourne's south-east was gutted in a suspicious blaze in the early hours of Friday, December 6, sparking widespread condemnation.Australian Federal Police arrested a 20-year-old Meadow Heights man after carrying out a search warrant last week.A number of items were seized including electronic devices which police said are undergoing forensic examination. He was charged with arson, conduct endangering life and motor vehicle theft today.The Adass Israel Synagogue in Ripponlea was destroyed in the December 2024 attack. (Supplied: Sally Westwood)Australian Federal Police acting assistant commissioner Nick Read said the investigation has been one of the highest priorities for the counter-terrorism unit. I want to reassure the community — especially the Jewish community — that the AFP, together with Victoria Police and ASIO, are working relentlessly to bring this investigation to its conclusion, he said.Victoria Police assistant commissioner Tess Walsh urged the community to come forward with any new information. There is no place for this type of offending in our state, and we will be relentless in pursuing those who are prepared to engage in these acts of violence, she said.Two of three people charged over firebombingPolice allege the 20-year-old man is one of three people who broke into the Ripponlea synagogue and deliberately lit the fire. The Joint Counter Terrorism Team has now charged two of the three alleged offenders accused of directly setting the synagogue on fire, a police spokesperson said. He is due to appear before the Melbourne Magistrates' Court next week.In July, a 21-year-old Werribee man was also charged over his alleged role in breaking into and setting fire to the synagogue. Another man, 20, was charged for allegedly stealing a communal crime car, which police say was used to drive to the synagogue on the day of the attack.It is alleged the same vehicle was used in an arson attack two weeks earlier, on November 21, at LUX nightclub, south-east of Melbourne. Another man has also been charged over the nightclub fire. full_text: ATM supplier pulls machines amid money laundering concerns International ATM giant NCR Atleos begins removing machines from tobacco stores after ABC investigationBy Liam WalshABy Amy GreenbankBy Rory CallinanTopic:Crime22h ago22 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 3:15amNCR Atleos has begun removing its Cashzone ATMs from stores. (ABC News: Liz Pickering)In short:One of the world's largest ATM suppliers will begin removing machines from tobacco stores across Australia.NCR Atleos's move follows an ABC investigation which revealed how private ATM suppliers were fuelling illegal tobacco and vape sales.Other large companies have also begun removing their machines from suspected illegal stores.abc.net.au/news/ncr-atleos-removing-machines-suspected-illegal-tobacco-stores/105680294Link copiedShareShare articleGiant international ATM supplier NCR Atleos will remove more than 50 machines from tobacco stores across Australia after an ABC investigation revealed how ATM companies were fuelling illegal tobacco and vape sales.The New York Stock Exchange-listed company, which boasts of having the world's largest ATM network, has reviewed its fleet following the revelations, including how private ATM companies had cut deals with local tobacco criminals.Some tobacco stores have relied on ATMs for cash sales of illicit products, and NCR's move means, in total, more than 100 machines from multiple suppliers are now being extracted.NCR's specifically includes machines that tobacco store owners can load with cash themselves — a feature that experts say raises potential money laundering fears due to a regulatory blind spot.NCR's Cashzone ATMs were found in stores selling illegal tobacco. (Supplied)Third company to make the moveThe $4 billion company's decision follows fellow ATM suppliers – Melbourne-based Next Payments, backed by prestigious investment bank Macquarie Group, and Queensland-based atm2go — which also began pulling their machines from stores linked to illicit tobacco sales.The fraudster, illicit smokes and an ATM giantPhoto shows Cash zone receipt with money in backgroundA New York Stock Exchange listed company is the latest to be found to have links to the illicit tobacco trade after an ABC investigation into how private ATM suppliers are oiling the industry.The ABC had found how those companies' machines and NCR's green Cashzone ATMs were in stores selling illicit tobacco and vapes in locations including Brisbane, Darwin and Sydney.One such store with a Cashzone ATM in Sydney was owned by a man already convicted on 15 counts of illicit tobacco sales; another illegal tobacco outlet in Brisbane was owned by a man once jailed for fraud.NCR declined to answer questions about due diligence conducted before placing its Cashzone machines in stores.Do you know more about this story? Email Callinan.Rory@abc.net.au or Walsh.Liam@abc.net.auBut a company spokesman told the ABC that following a review, we have chosen to remove a number of ATMs and will be removing self-filled ATMs in tobacco stores, which account for 1 per cent of our fleet . Additionally, we will continue to review this issue and will remove any ATMs from stores that we believe are linked to illegal tobacco trade. NCR has over 5,300 ATMs across Australia and complied with all applicable legislation , he said.Loading...Doron Goldbarsht, director of the Financial Integrity Hub at Macquarie University, said NCR's move to withdraw self-loading ATMs from tobacconists suggests recognition of the risks associated with the machines, particularly around traceability of funds . Because cash is filled directly by store owners rather than through a regulated provider, such ATMs may present heightened vulnerabilities to misuse, including for money laundering or to facilitate proceeds of crime, Dr Goldbarsht told the ABC.He said that NCR's move was positive and appeared a voluntary one. This should signal to both government and industry that current oversight may be insufficient, and that stronger regulatory settings or supervisory mechanisms could be needed to mitigate financial crime risks in the ATM sector, he said.Supplier Next Payments had already begun removing its machines from some stores. (ABC News: Liam Walsh)Money laundering concernsThe ABC has found examples of a man ultimately convicted of proceeds of crime and tobacco offences being able to load cash into Next Payments ATMs.Macquarie Group company's private ATM's fuelling illegal tobacco tradePhoto shows Next ATM in a closed tobacconist in BurpengaryAn ABC investigation finds that among investments raking in the dollars for the Australian-founded Macquarie Group is the nation's billion-dollar illegal tobacco trade.Court records also show a large Darwin cannabis supplier told an underling to load ATMs from atm2go with money from drug sales.Some parts of the private ATM industry, including Next Payments, have disputed whether money laundering could occur.But a concern is that private ATMs themselves are not captured by anti-money laundering laws, and that dirty money could be loaded into the machines.If an innocent person unwittingly withdraws that dirty money, that person's bank account ultimately credits the same amount cleanly into the private ATM cash-loader's bank account.The original source of the cash does not come under the same level of scrutiny that occurs if criminals try depositing certain amounts of cash in various ways directly into a bank.The ABC has found more than 20 stores selling illegal cigarettes with private ATMs inside, and at least five cases of ATM companies cutting deals with businesses tied to men either charged or convicted of offences including illicit tobacco sales.This Riverwood store was selling illegal cigarettes in Sydney this week. (Supplied)Sydney store selling $10 packs of cigarettesAnother example this week was a south-western Sydney store, the Riverwood News Agency and Tobacconist, selling illicit $10 packs of Double Happiness cigarettes.The store is registered to a company owned by Rui Chen, who did not answer requests for comment.Chen had been convicted and made headlines in 2020 for 15 tobacco sales breaches at the store.An example of the illegal cigarettes being sold for $10. (Supplied)He was hit with $4,250 in fines, and reports described authorities having seized 241 cartons and 386 packets of illegal cigarettes, and almost six kilograms of loose leaf chop-chop tobacco — the local area's largest-ever seizure at the time.NCR's Australian subsidiary had signed a deal with Chen's company for an ATM in the same store 10 months after he was convicted, mortgage records show.Unlike many other stores selling illicit tobacco, the Riverwood outlet this week was selling the cigarettes for the same cash price as an electronic payment.The ABC is not suggesting Chen was involved in money laundering.Posted 22h ago22 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 3:15am, updated 20h ago20 hours agoThu 21 Aug 2025 at 5:34amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesAs Israel pushes on with Gaza City invasion, Palestinians trapped there are protestingTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A group of protesters in Gaza holding Palestinian flags and signs in Arabic script.Jason Clare details outcomes of childcare safety meetingLIVEPhoto shows A close up of a man wearing a suit speaking. full_text: Sunshine Coast childcare centre intruder on parole at time of death Sunshine Coast childcare centre intruder on parole at time of deathBy Madeline GraceABC Sunshine CoastTopic:PoliceWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:36amStaff acted quickly to hide six children as a man forced his way in. (ABC News: Madeline Grace)In short:Reubhan Mickeal Gary Ralph forced his way into a Sunshine Coast childcare centre, sending five staff and six children into lockdown, then died as a result of self-harm.He had faced Queensland courts multiple times for drug dealing, stalking and weapons offences.What's next?Police are investigating whether Ralph was in a drug psychosis at the time of his death.abc.net.au/news/sunshine-coast-childcare-intruder-lengthy-criminal-history/105677456Link copiedShareShare articleThe 28-year-old intruder at the centre of a Queensland childcare centre emergency had a lengthy criminal history, including charges for stalking, weapon offences and drug dealing.Reubhan Mickeal Gary Ralph was on parole when he died on Monday after smashing his way into the Habitat Early Learning childcare centre at Peregian Springs on the Sunshine Coast. It is understood he was armed, and police tasered him multiple times.Ralph was not known to any staff or families at the centre.Police are investigating whether he was in a drug psychosis at the time of his death.Police were called to Habitat Childcare Centre at Peregian Springs about 6pm on Monday. (Supplied)Attack at closing timeThe centre had five staff and six children inside and was winding down at 6pm, about 30 minutes before it was due to close.The staff heard Ralph's efforts to break in and swiftly moved to hide the children.The time it took him to smash through the centre's front glass doors was enough for them to alert police, who arrived to confront Ralph soon after.The offender was not known to any staff or families of the centre. (ABC News: Madeline Grace)They attempted to subdue Ralph, who was self-harming.Ralph died in the custody of police.History of drugs, crime, stalkingCourt documents chronicled Ralph's criminal history, starting in 2021, which included multiple drug offences.Since then, he faced court multiple times and was convicted for drug driving, speeding, drug trafficking, breaching bail, stalking, and carrying a knife in public.He spent five months in custody for the stalking offences.According to court documents, he was part of a syndicate which sold narcotics on the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast.The money he made was used to pay off his drug debts.Emergency services responded quickly after staff raised the alarm. (Supplied)Most recently, in May last year, Ralph pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane to possessing and selling drugs.He was convicted but had his three-and-a-half-year prison sentence wholly suspended and was put on probation for two-and-a-half years.Ralph was released on parole in June after breaching his bail conditions.Police acted 'extremely well'Queensland Police Union president Shane Prior said every officer at the scene acted bravely during the harrowing incident . One young constable used initiative and resourcefulness to enter the rear of the premises without the offender being aware and guided the children and carers to safety, he said. He has saved these kids from a potential lifetime of trauma. Every officer there stood between a violent intruder and innocent children. It's a selfless act police are prepared to do to keep the community safe. Dan Purdie says he has spoken with the responding officers. (ABC News: Lucas Hill)Police and Emergency Services Minister Daniel Purdie said he spoke with officers after the attack. They handled it extremely well and did whatever they could to protect the children and carers, Mr Purdie said. It really was a horrific incident for this tight-knit community. full_text: Man charged with assaulting police officer after arrest turns violent WA man charged with assaulting police officer after attempted arrest in MullewaBy Brianna MelvilleABC Midwest & WheatbeltTopic:PoliceWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amGeraldton detectives charged the 29-year-old man in relation to the incident. (ABC News: Sissy Reyes)In short:Two officers from Mullewa Police have been injured after an arrest turned violent.Police say Ronald James Gregory Merry repeatedly attacked the officers when they tried to arrest him over an alleged domestic assault.What's next?Mr Merry was remanded in custody and will face court again in October.abc.net.au/news/police-officers-assaulted-mullewa-wa-arrest/105676826Link copiedShareShare articleA police officer in WA's Midwest has been flown to Perth with serious facial fractures, and another officer injured, after the arrest of an alleged domestic abuser turned violent.Police said the officers were responding to a reported domestic violence incident in Mullewa, 450 kilometres north of Perth, on Tuesday afternoon when they were allegedly attacked by 29-year-old Ronald James Gregory Merry.Mr Merry, who faced Geraldton Magistrates Court on Wednesday, allegedly punched a 47-year-old woman, who reported the incident to police.In police body-worn camera footage played to the court, Mr Merry appeared agitated as the two officers questioned him about the alleged earlier assault. He could be heard telling officers, I'll grab your handcuffs and take you to jail, repeatedly calling them c*nts and telling them to go . Go now before I knock you out, he was heard saying in the footage. One police officer was taken from Mullewa to Geraldton for treatment at the hospital. (ABC Midwest and Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis)Violence caught on videoThe footage showed two officers tell Mr Merry he was under arrest, and attempt to pull him up by his arms. It showed Mr Merry then repeatedly punch the male officer in the face and head, knocking him to the ground and continuing to hit him.The footage then captured the officer's female colleague attempting to pepper spray Mr Merry, who began throwing punches at her.The 29-year-old then turned his attention back to the male officer, punching him several times in the head while the police officer remained on the ground.Ronald Merry faced the Geraldton Magistrates Court on Wednesday. (ABC News)The female officer then attempted to taser Mr Merry, who fled the scene and ran out of the house.Police located him several hours after the incident, charging him with a string of offences, including aggravated assault, escaping lawful custody and assaulting a public officer.The female officer was treated at the Mullewa Nursing Post, and the male officer was flown to Sir Charles Gairdner Hospital in Perth.Man allegedly drinking, using methamphetamineMagistrate Matthew Walton noted the male officer's injuries showed bruising and an apparently closed-over eye. Police alleged Mr Merry had been drinking and using methamphetamine the previous night.Defence counsel Matt Reen requested Mr Merry be released on bail, although he noted the prosecution's case was strong.Magistrate Walton denied bail, remarking the body-worn footage was clear and stark in supporting the alleged facts of the matter. He noted Mr Merry's history of breaching court orders, and the inevitability of an immediate term of imprisonment following a conviction. Mr Merry was remanded in custody and will return to court in October.ABC Midwest & Wheatbelt — local news in your inboxGet our local newsletter, delivered free each ThursdayEmail addressSubscribeYour information is being handled in accordance with the ABC Privacy Collection Statement.Posted Wed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amWednesday 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amWed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesAs Israel pushes on with Gaza City invasion, Palestinians trapped there are protestingTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A group of protesters in Gaza holding Palestinian flags and signs in Arabic script.Jason Clare details outcomes of childcare safety meetingLIVEPhoto shows A close up of a man wearing a suit speaking. full_text: Woman assisting police after baby's body found in Perth drain Police say woman assisting them with inquiries after baby's body found in Alexander Heights stormwater drainCBy Cason HoTopic:CrimeWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 5:48amFlowers and stuffed animals were placed next to the stormwater drain in Alexander Heights where the baby's body was found. (ABC News: Keana Naughton)abc.net.au/news/new-leads-in-baby-body-n-stormwater-drain-case/105677546Link copiedShareShare articlePolice say a woman aged in her 30s is assisting them with inquiries into the death of a newborn baby whose body was found in a storm drain in suburban Perth.In a short statement on Wednesday evening, police said the woman is receiving appropriate care and support . The Western Australia Police Force would like to thank the community for their concern, support and assistance, the statement said.Maintenance workers who were clearing drains and conducting checks on La Salle Road in Alexander Heights discovered the baby boy's body on Monday afternoon.Police say the baby was put in the drain in recent days and were urgently chasing the identity and location of the mother.Police say they have uncovered a number of potential leads in the case. (ABC News: Blake Kagi)The circumstances surrounding the baby's death were still being investigated.Commissioner Blanch said detectives had been chasing clues since the grim discovery, ranging from eye-witness accounts to forensic evidence. We've got some leads. And as always with Crime Stoppers and people ringing up, there is lots of things that people have seen, he said. The job now is to sift through which ones may be relevant and which ones may not. They will follow everything down. Public appeal ongoingThe commissioner urged the public to alert authorities to any information they have, even if it does not seem relevant. If you're in the area, just ring up Crime Stoppers and tell us what you saw, he said.Forensic evidence has been gathered from the stormwater drain where the baby was discovered. (ABC News: Keana Naughton)Police say forensic tests of evidence from the scene have been completed but analysis was still ongoing.The incident has been described by WA Premier Roger Cook as a horrifying scenario , and police have previously said it was a distressing scene for both the workers who found the body, and for first responders at the scene.Residents in the area have voiced their shock, with some leaving flowers at the scene as a tribute to the baby boy.Tributes were left at the stormwater drain in Alexander Heights. (ABC News: Keana Naughton) Even though it was so heartbreakingly sad of how the baby left this earth, while it was here it was still a human, resident Sarah said on Tuesday. It's not just a baby in a drain. full_text: Ferrari, 40 kilograms of meth seized in WA organised crime crackdown WA Police seize $18 million worth of drugs, cash and a Ferrari in Perth organised crime crackdownTopic:Drug OffencesWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 5:28amAuthorities have seized a large amount of drugs, cash and firearms in WA. (ABC: Kate Hill)In short:WA Police have seized 40 kilograms of methamphetamine, a large amount of cash, firearms and a Ferrari in an organised crime bust in Perth.Nine people have been charged following the operation.It comes as methamphetamine use in regional WA and Perth continues to rise, with drug crime experts saying demand has exceeded pre-COVID levels.abc.net.au/news/huge-perth-meth-firearms-cash-seizure-by-police/105677136Link copiedShareShare articleMore than $18 million dollars in drugs has been taken off the streets of Western Australia, as methamphetamine use skyrockets across the state.In operations during June and July, WA Police officers seized almost 40 kilograms of methamphetamine, more than $800,000 in cash, three firearms and a Ferrari.The vehicle will be sold, the expected $500,000 in proceeds to go back into the community.The haul removed hundreds of thousands of drug hits from the streets, with nine people charged.One of two men arrested in the Perth suburb of Joondanna in relation to a large seizure of meth, cash and firearms. (Supplied: WA Police)The drug haul comes amid skyrocketing meth use across regional WA, with levels in Perth at an almost 10-year high.Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission principal drug specialist Shane Neilsen said an increasing demand for illicit stimulants in WA pointed to a demand that was resistant to treatment .This 2018 silver Ferrari was seized by police from a house in North Fremantle as part of a coordinated series of raids targeting organised crime. (Supplied: WA Police) That's the thing we constantly advocate [for] is treatment for and also education to stop people taking the drug in the first place, around the dangers that it poses, he said.Mr Neilsen said demand had grown since WA's borders re-opened after COVID, and now exceeded pre-COVID levels. What we're seeing at the moment is a significant market correction getting back to where it was before COVID, he said.'Awash with cocaine'He said it appeared cartels from South America and Mexico were supplying large quantities of cocaine globally. They're certainly supplying large quantities of the drug into Australia, but they're also doing this into Europe and the United States, he said. The world is just awash with cocaine at the moment. Australia is no different. The crackdown on organised crime in WA comes as police continue to investigate whether a number of fatal shootings in Sydney this week were gang-related.WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch said the state's tough organised crime laws made it difficult for those involved to live on the west coast. As soon as they buy that Ferrari, as soon as they buy that house, as soon as they start flashing the cash, we're onto them, he said.Police seized a number of firearms during a series of raids on Perth properties that netted more than 17 kilograms of methylamphetamine and cash. (Supplied: WA Police) Most organised crime [participants] do not reside at the higher levels in WA. They reside over east or they reside offshore. We've had two fatal shootings in New South Wales just in the last two days that is suspected to be gang related. So we can see some of the origins of this serious crime is coming from the east coast of Australia and our job is to prevent it from coming to the community of WA. Commissioner Blanch said the amount of drugs seized in Australia exceeded the consumption of the drug itself.WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch said the amount of drugs seized in Australia exceeded the consumption of the drugs. (ABC News: Andrew O'Connor) There's no doubt that West Australians prefer meth as a drug, but when we look at it in totality with cocaine and heroin, which are two other drugs that are used consistently across the country, we're well down the chains, he said.He said a multi-agency approach was needed to support users and slash demand for illicit substances. full_text: Aspiring astrophysicist pleads not guilty over triple fatal Perth crash Zack Thomas Heylen pleads not guilty to killing three people, injuring two others in Rivervale crashDBy David WeberTopic:CourtsWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 3:40amZack Thomas Heylen (centre) has denied manslaughter and dangerous driving causing bodily harm. (ABC News: David Weber)In short:Zack Thomas Heylen was driving a utility carrying five passengers when it crashed into a tree on Orrong Road in Perth last October, leaving three of his friends dead.The 23-year-old has pleaded not guilty to three counts of manslaughter and two counts of dangerous driving causing grievous bodily harm.What's next?Mr Heylen will stand trial and is due to appear in the Supreme Court in October.abc.net.au/news/zack-thomas-heylen-pleads-not-guilty-over-rivervale-crash/105676284Link copiedShareShare articleAn aspiring astrophysicist who was behind the wheel of a car that crashed and left three of his friends dead in suburban Perth is due to stand trial after he pleaded not guilty to manslaughter.Zack Thomas Heylen, 23, was behind the wheel of a utility carrying five passengers when it veered off Orrong Road in Rivervale last October, crashing through a brick fence and into a house.Two 22-year-old men and a 34-year-old man who were in the back of the ute died at the scene.Three people died at the scene of the crash in Rivervale. (ABC News: Briana Shepherd)Another two of Mr Heylen's friends, a 19-year-old and a 23-year-old, were injured and taken to Royal Perth Hospital.The busy road has a speed limit of 70 kilometres per hour, but police allege Mr Heylen was travelling at 114 kph before the crash.Police said the driver was the only person wearing a seatbelt in the car, which was designed to carry five people in total.Police allege Mr Heylen was travelling at 114 kilometres per hour before the crash. (ABC News)Appearing in Stirling Gardens Magistrate court on Wednesday, Mr Heylen pleaded not guilty to three counts of manslaughter and two counts of dangerous driving causing bodily harm.The court previously heard Mr Heylen was out drinking with friends before the crash, and recorded an initial alcohol reading of 0.095.The utility veered off Orrong Road and crashed through a fence and into a house. (ABC News: Macey Turner)He was taken to hospital after the crash and required surgery for his injuries.The court was told he lived with his family in Roleystone and had been working with his father while he studied physics with the dream of being an astrophysicist.It also heard he was dux of his graduating class and was a talented sportsman.His bail was continued in court on Wednesday, and he is due to appear in the Supreme Court in October.LoadingPosted Wed 20 Aug 2025 at 3:40amWednesday 20 Aug 2025 at 3:40amWed 20 Aug 2025 at 3:40am, updated Wed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:12amWednesday 20 Aug 2025 at 7:12amWed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:12amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesAs Israel pushes on with Gaza City invasion, Palestinians trapped there are protestingTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A group of protesters in Gaza holding Palestinian flags and signs in Arabic script.Jason Clare details outcomes of childcare safety meetingLIVEPhoto shows A close up of a man wearing a suit speaking. full_text: Man charged over 'random' attack of 83yo man in Newcastle car park Man dies in 'random attack' near Newcastle shopping strip in alleged stabbing assaultBy Alex Turner-Cohen, Nakita Jager and Ben CliffordABC NewcastleTopic:CrimeWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 2:12amPolice established a crime scene at the car park in Charlestown. (ABC News: Bridget Murphy)In short: A 53-year-old man has been charged with murder and assault over the death of an elderly man in a Newcastle car park.Emergency services were called to Charlestown on Wednesday morning, where they found the victim unresponsive.What's next?The 53-year old will appear before Bail Division Court 2 on Thursday.abc.net.au/news/man-dies-at-charlestown-shopping-centre-car-park/105675840Link copiedShareShare articlePolice say the fatal stabbing of an 83-year old man in a Newcastle car park was a random attack. Emergency services were called to the scene near a Charlestown shopping strip around 9:50am on Wednesday and found the man unresponsive.Police said the elderly man appeared to have suffered multiple stab wounds. He died before emergency service crews arrived.A 53-year-old man has been arrested and charged over the incident.He was reportedly seen running along the Pacific Highway in Charlestown shortly after the incident, and turned himself into Newcastle Police Station three hours later. The 53-year-old was charged with murder and assault with intent to rob, and armed offensive weapon wound/grievous bodily harm. There are no indicators that the men are known to one another, said Detective Chief Inspector Scott Parker. The investigation is very much in its infancy, with multiple lines of inquiry being considered. Detective Chief Inspector Scott Parker says the attack was random and senseless. (ABC Newcastle: Nakita Jager)'Senseless attack', police sayInspector Parker described the incident as a tragic situation. The deceased man is a man of very good character, he said. It seems a very random and senseless attack. Inspector Parker said members of the public attempted to save the man before paramedics arrived. The man lost his life, despite the best efforts of a number of witnesses who performed resuscitation attempts, he said.Police said a knife was recovered from the scene. Several schools were in lockdown throughout the day while a manhunt was underway. No one else was injured.
