full_text: Karnataka woman chopped into 19 pieces; son-in-law among 3 held for murder Four days after the body parts of a woman were found dumped in several locations in Chimpuganahalli in Karnataka’s Tumakuru district, the police on Monday arrested three people, including her son-in-law, a dentist, for the murder. The police identified the deceased as Lakshmi Devi, 42, a resident of Bellavi village, and the accused as Dr Ramachandraiah S, 47, Satish K N, 38, and Kiran K S, 32, all residents of Kallahalli. Ramachandraiah is married to Devi’s daughter, Tejasvi, 26, the police said, adding that this was his second marriage. According to the police, on August 3, Devi left her home to see her daughter. A day later, her husband, Basavaraj, lodged a missing person’s complaint at Bellavi police station. Three days later, on August 7, the police were alerted about 19 body parts being found at various places in Chimpuganahalli. The body parts were found inside bags that were disposed of at no fewer than 19 locations, the police said. The Koratagere police registered a murder case and sent a message to all police stations in the district to check if any missing person complaints had been filed. It was then that the Bellavi police informed Basavaraj, who identified the body as Devi’s. According to the police, CCTV footage showed that a Maruti Suzuki Brezza was used to dump the body parts. The vehicle was allegedly registered in the name of Satish. “We took custody of Satish, and he spilled the beans. Satish and Kiran were taken into custody from Hornad. Ramachandraiah was in Dharmasthala after the murder and was not available for questioning. This also raised our suspicion,” a police officer said. Ramachandraiah allegedly claimed that his wife was listening to her mother’s advice and causing trouble in their marriage, Ashok K V, Superintendent of Police (SP), Tumakuru district, said. “He was unhappy over his mother-in-law’s interference. His first marriage is still in the divorce stage. In 2019, he married Tejasvi,” SP Ashok added. “We are yet to know why the accused cut her body into pieces and threw it at different locations. We have produced them before the court and will take them to police custody for further questioning. The car gave us the major lead to crack the case,” he said. According to the police, Satish was one of Ramachandraiah’s patients and stayed near his house. Kiran was Satish’s cousin, the police added. SP Ashok denied reports that the murder was linked to human sacrifice.

headline: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver
who: Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad; Aruna; Gailkwad; Gaikwad; Santwadi; Gaikwad’s; Ananda Chavan; Mayur Vijay Solse; Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane
where: Pune Rural; Malshej; Kasara; Gangapur Road; Nashik; Solse; Chavan; Gangapur

full_text: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver Around 7.30 on January 27, Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad, 56, a resident of Nashik who worked as a rental cab driver, called his wife Aruna on her phone. He had taken a trip from Nashik to Pune around 5 am that day. He told her he would reach home around 7.30 pm. That was the last conversation Aruna had with her husband. Repeated calls made to him were unanswered. Around 10.30 pm that night, Gailkwad’s wife got a call that his phone had been found on the Alephata Santwadi road off the Pune-Nashik highway. The caller had kept the phone at a nearby hotel, from where he had made the call. Around 2.30 am on January 28, the Gaikwad family reached the hotel and searched for him in the area where the phone was found. However, Gaikwad and his car could not be traced. The family registered a missing person case at Alephata police station under the Pune Rural police. At around 9.30 am on January 28, while police were actively searching for Gaikwad, his body was discovered in the Santwadi area. His hands were bound behind his back with a nylon rope and a zip tie, and initial autopsy findings indicated that he had been strangled. The murder investigation was taken up jointly by teams from the Alephata police station and the Pune Rural police’s Local Crime Branch. As part of the investigation, the police reviewed footage from dozens of CCTV cameras on the approach routes to the area. A significant breakthrough came when Gaikwad’s vehicle was spotted on a hotel’s CCTV camera along the Nashik–Pune highway corridor. By piecing together video evidence from multiple locations, investigators traced the car’s movement—first heading toward the area where his body was later discovered, then continuing in the direction of Malshej Ghat. Both the footage and ground inquiries indicated that, at one stage, four people were inside the car along with Gaikwad. Meanwhile, a team which was on the lookout for the car found it abandoned in Kasara Ghat, along the route to Nashik. Continued analysis of CCTV footage helped police identify suspects who were captured travelling in the vehicle. Over the following three days, till January 31, investigators arrested three suspects: Vishal Ananda Chavan, 22; Mayur Vijay Solse, 23; and Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane, 21, all residents of the Gangapur Road area in Nashik. The investigation to arrest the fourth suspect continues even now. Driver resisted carjacking attempt, say police Investigators found out that the suspects had boarded Gaikwad’s car during his return journey to Nashik from Pune. They used the pretext of hitching a ride, but wanted to hijack the vehicle, said the police. The sequence of events, as brought out by the investigation, was that they allegedly strangled him after he resisted their attempt. The group then disposed of his body and fled the scene, said the police. It was soon revealed that the trio are hardened criminals. They allegedly intended to use the hijacked car for an armed robbery in which they wanted to target a shop in Nashik. The police said they, however, decided to abandon it on the way since they thought the vehicle would be flagged in the murder investigation after Gaikwad’s body was found. Solse and Chavan are facing charges of murder registered at Gangapur police station in Nashik in 2022. As the police continued their probe, they found out that these suspects were involved in a case of carjacking at Chakan police station registered in 2024, which had remained unsolved till the time the murder case was cracked. “The chargesheet in the case was filed subsequently. All three accused are currently in prison under judicial custody. A coordinated search for the fourth accused continued. The wanted suspect in the case also has multiple offences registered against him,” said an officer who was part of the probe. The case underscores the dangers faced by drivers who pick up unknown passengers outside their assigned duties. Authorities have reiterated their warning against this practice, noting that similar incidents of passengers turning violent have been reported in the past.

full_text: Gurgaon man masturbates in front of woman waiting for cab, police file FIR The Gurgaon police on August 5 registered a case against a man who was caught on camera allegedly masturbating in front of a young woman near Rajiv Chowk in the city, officers said on Thursday. According to the police, the incident took place on August 2 when the complainant, a model and digital content creator, was waiting for a cab around noon at a busy junction to head home after a journey from Jaipur. Krishan Kumar, Station House Officer, Civil Lines Police Station, said that the police have filed a First Information Report (FIR) under sections 75(2) for sexual harassment and 78 for stalking of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. “The investigation is underway, and the complainant has also joined the probe, and we have recorded her statement. We are scanning CCTV footage in and around the spot and talking to people in the area.” On the same day of the incident, the model narrated her ordeal on social media and posted the video of the alleged act of the perpetrator, while also blaming the police for the delay in registering a complaint. “Something very strange happened to me. A man came around, circling, and he was constantly staring at me. Initially, I just ignored it, like the others do,” she said. She noticed that the man with unzipped pants was allegedly masturbating. The video showed the man wearing a facemask and a backpack that he had slung over his chest to cover the act from being too visible to the public nearby. The woman said it was clear he was ‘very aware’ of what he was doing. The woman in her video also lamented how cab companies were delaying in accepting her ride request, aggravating her ordeal. The complainant stated that although she had initially got a ride booked, the driver was not picking up despite multiple calls, and hence she had to re-book across applications “just to avoid the creep”. Eventually, a cab arrived and she reached home. In the video, she also alleged initial inaction from the police after she had tagged the police and other government authorities while putting the man’s video on X, and later calling the police helpline. “There wasn’t even an automated message,” she said. Regarding the FIR, the model said, the police had asked her to come to the station instead of lodging the complaint online. “It was making me feel very uncomfortable. I felt very, very disgusted. Initially, I froze. I did not record or hit him. People who say I could have shouted at him do not understand what goes through a girl’s mind at that moment. Reactions go viral faster than the real truth, and people judge; they do not help.” The woman stated she wanted to be safe rather than have the moment become viral. “I am not making the video for any kind of attention, just want to be heard,” she said in the video.

full_text: 'Sophisticated fraudster' behind cancelled Victorian bushfire charity event Victorian charity CEO with new identity previously charged with deceptionBy Mikaela Ortolan and ABC News VerifyStatelineTopic:Crime4h ago4 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pmFounder of Disaster Recovery Army Inc, Jay Brady, served time in prison for fraud-related offences under another name. (ABC News: Shane Willner-Browne)In short:A man who presided over a controversial fundraiser for bushfire-affected communities previously went by another name, under which he was convicted of multiple crimes of deception.The bushfire recovery event was cancelled earlier this year when community members raised concerns about the legitimacy of the charity behind the event.Charity founder Jay Brady did not deny the past convictions but declined to answer specific questions. He maintains the charity is legitimate.abc.net.au/news/jay-brady-jason-palankay-deception-charges-bushfire-recovery/105610002Link copiedShareShare articleA Victorian man who attempted to organise a charity event for bushfire-affected communities has a history of committing crimes of deception under a different name dating back decades, the ABC can reveal.Earlier this year, a charity event to support bushfire-affected communities in Victoria's west was called off amid community concern over the way it had been organised. Jay Brady founded and headed up the registered charity, Disaster Recovery Army Inc, which was behind the Recover Grampians event.The event was due to take place in March — after a summer of devastating fires in the Grampians National Park — but its site was taken down and a GoFundMe page that had raised almost $16,000 was closed when local businesses started questioning the event and its legitimacy. The webpage for the Recover Grampians event, which was taken down after the local community raised concerns. (Supplied)An ABC investigation has found Mr Brady previously went by the name Jason Palankay, under which he had been convicted of numerous deception-related offences and served time in prison, according to court documents.In 2011, while facing court over several charges of obtaining property by deception, he was described by a judge as an artful, skilful and sophisticated fraudster .While considering his sentence, the judge said Palankay was a persistent offender who has not been deterred by previous sentences . When contacted by the ABC, Mr Brady did not deny the past convictions but said he would not divulge personal details and could not answer specific questions because of legal proceedings. He said he changed his surname from Palankay a long time ago for personal family reasons .A psychological report submitted to the courts during the 2011 matter said Palankay met the criteria for Narcissistic Personality Disorder and displayed a grandiose sense of self-importance .A number of residential properties were destroyed in the Grampians bushfires. (Supplied: David Grimble )Businesses suffer almost $180,000 in lossesCourt documents show Palankay was convicted of deception offences at the Melbourne Magistrates' Court as early as 1998 after writing cheques that could not be honoured. He was convicted for similar offences the following year and then again in 2002, according to the same material.He was again convicted over a matter involving bouncing cheques in 2005, the documents show.The same documents also reference another charge in South Australia. They suggest Palankay served time in prison in that state, but the ABC was unable to obtain further details.The ABC compared a still from a TV interview with Jay Brady (left) and an image from a 2016 newspaper article that identified Jason Palankay (right). (WIN News/Leader Newspapers: Stuart Milligan)In 2007, Palankay turned to fraudulently obtaining vehicles and profiting from their sale, costing impacted businesses nearly $180,000, a court heard. During this time, he worked as an independent contractor for LeaseMasters — a salary packaging specialist offering novated leasing, which is a way to pay for a car and its running costs directly through a person's salary.Do you know more about this story?Contact Mikaela Ortolan at ortolan.mikaela@abc.net.au. If you're sharing sensitive information, read our tips on how to contact us confidentially.Court documents say Palankay requested a quote for a vehicle and gave falsified purchase orders to the car retailer on a number of occasions, despite not being authorised to do so.Palankay obtained the vehicles by falsely representing that finances had been approved . According to court documents, he would then use the vehicles as security to obtain loans.Court documents say Palankay would then sell the vehicle, using some of the money to pay off the loans and pocketing any profit. After his engagement with LeaseMasters was terminated, court documents say he continued contacting car dealers and obtaining vehicles while falsely representing that [he was] operating a genuine business known as Fleet Development .He purchased several cars in this way over a nine-month period, the documents say.Palankay sentenced to prisonPalankay was convicted of one count of using a false document and five counts of obtaining property by deception in relation to the vehicles in 2011.It was submitted to the court that Palankay undertook this fraudulent activity to pay back debts to the Australian Tax Office of more than $110,000 at the time of offending.However, in sentencing, County Court judge Mark Taft said none of the proceeds from the cars you sold made their way to the ATO and I find the account you proffer as utterly implausible . In the course of committing the frauds on car dealers you displayed a high level of cunning, the judge said. Your level of intelligence increases the risk you represent to the public. Palankay had initially pleaded guilty to the charges, but weeks before his sentencing, he sought to change his plea after claiming he had been improperly induced to plead guilty by statements from the judge. The change of plea application was dismissed by the County Court Chief Judge. Mr Brady was photographed leaving a court in Bendigo over a separate matter, in which he was the complainant, earlier this year. (ABC News: Emile Pavlich)During his sentencing remarks, Judge Taft said Palankay's guilty pleas were not accompanied by any remorse whatsoever and you do not have a skerrick of insight into your wrongdoing . He was sentenced to three years and 10 months in prison with a non-parole period of two-and-a-half years.He was also sentenced to nine months in prison in 2019 after pleading guilty to unrelated charges of obtaining property by deception. In that case, he was ordered to undertake a 12 month community correction order upon his release. A psychological report tendered to court during a hearing for the car-related crimes, authored by Aaron Cunningham and dated November 2011, stated Palankay said he had previously been diagnosed with delusions of grandeur .In the report, Dr Cunningham expressed the opinion that Palankay met the criteria for Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD). Mr Palankay's NPD is evident by his grandiose sense of self-importance, preoccupation with fantasies of unlimited success, belief that he [is] special and unique, need for excessive admiration, sense of entitlement, interpersonally exploitative and lack of empathy, Dr Cunningham said in his report submitted to the court. When asked about this Mr Brady said, I certainly do not have a diagnosis of delusions of grandeur or NPD .Bushfire event won't go aheadIn 2008, Palankay filed for bankruptcy.At some stage he began using the name Jay Brady. The ABC is not aware of any criminal convictions since his name change.Mr Brady registered the charity Disaster Recovery Army Inc in March 2024 and after devastating bushfires in the Grampians over two summers, he began advertising charity work and calling on volunteers.The event's website once advertised tickets but Mr Brady previously told the ABC none were sold.He also previously said the sum raised through GoFundMe was used for equipment hire, vehicles, rent and other charity operational expenses.Mr Brady previously told the ABC no tickets to the event were sold. (ABC News)Community members who held concerns about the fundraising event said businesses had not been consulted despite its website at one point claiming it had 100-plus local business supporters.Earlier this year, the Northern Grampians Shire Council said Mr Brady had expressed interest in registering the event but had not completed the registration process. The ABC has also confirmed at least one image on the charity's website — purporting to show a volunteer — appears on other social media profiles and blog posts unrelated to the charity, where the person photographed has a different name. A photo of a woman on the charity's website (left) appears on other websites unrelated to Mr Brady's charity (right). (ABC News)The ABC put a series of detailed questions to Mr Brady about his past offending, his name change and the bushfire recovery event. In a written response earlier this month, he said he could not answer questions about his past offending because of legal proceedings underway . In relation to the name change, he said for personal family reasons, my surname was changed to Brady a long time ago as I do not have a relationship with my birth father .He maintains the charity is legitimate but said there is no intention to hold a Recover Grampians event at a later date , despite earlier suggesting it would be rescheduled. My term with the charity concludes shortly, so it will be up to any future board and management to canvass that, Mr Brady said. [Any] insinuation also that I have deceived or utilised funds associated with the charity are also false. Clearly, anecdotes have been taken out of context and/or used to create a narrative that doesn’t accurately reflect the charity’s, or my own, intentions to serve the communities we do. The ABC previously spoke with an employee at Disaster Recovery Army Inc who said volunteers had carried out work including trimming and removing dead bushes, fixing containment fences and removing burnt fences. The employee said they were legally doing work with the intention of helping people in disaster-affected communities.Victoria Police said no complainants had come forward and no offences had been identified in relation to the charity event.How the ABC uncovered a second identity:A search of the Disaster Recovery Army Inc's listed phone number led the ABC to a defunct website Jay Brady used to campaign for local councillor. The ABN linked to that website was different to the ABN the charity was registered under.A subsequent search of the campaign website ABN identified Jason Palankay as an entity name alongside Jay Brady and one other name. The ABC carried out a number of other searches as part of its investigation. One search found company records for both Jason Palankay and Jay Brady that listed the same home address.An article published in the Herald Sun in 2016 contained a photograph of Jason Palankay after he participated in an interview, and that image was compared against a still from a TV interview with Jay Brady.The ABC attended a court hearing in Bendigo in June where Jay Brady appeared as the complainant, and was able to confirm a visual match with a photograph of Jason Palankey in a Leader Newspapers article.Posted 4h ago4 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pm, updated 3h ago3 hours agoFri full_text: Convicted bucks party gang rapists argue guilty verdicts 'unsafe' Sydney men jailed over bucks party gang rape in Newcastle argue guilty verdicts 'unsafe'GBy Giselle WakatamaABC NewcastleTopic:Crime17h ago17 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amComposite Andrew David and Maurice Hawell outside court after their lengthy gang rape trial in 2024. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)In short: Three men jailed over gang rapes in Newcastle are appealing, arguing guilty verdicts were unsafe.Their barristers have argued witnesses were unreliable and have questions directions given to the jury by the presiding judge.What's next?The appellant judges have reserved their decision. abc.net.au/news/convicted-gang-rapists-argue-guilty-verdicts-unsafe-on-appeal/105687344Link copiedShareShare articleLegal teams for a group of men jailed for gang raping three women in Newcastle have argued their guilty verdicts were an unsafe and unsatisfactory verdict , and witnesses were unreliable.Last year brothers Maurice Hawell, 31, and Marius Hawell, 24, and friend Andrew David, 31, were convicted of multiple counts of aggravated sexual assault and aggravated sexual touching in company.The trio's lawyers have spent the past two days challenging the men's convictions and sentences in the Court of Criminal Appeal.An argument around an unsafe verdict alleges the jury's guilty verdict was unsatisfactory and should be overturned.The offences occurred during a bucks weekend in February 2022.The men had travelled to Newcastle and stayed in an Airbnb for the weekend.Two of the women were 18 at the time and the third was 19.'Callous and degrading'In sentencing, Justice Gina O'Rourke said the men engaged in a pack mentality and treated the women in a cold, callous, degrading and criminal way .Maurice Hawell was sentenced to 14 years in prison with a non-parole period of eight years and six months.Maurice Hawell is one of the men appealing his conviction and sentence. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)Andrew David was sentenced to 13 years in prison with a non-parole period of seven years and nine months.Marius Hawell was sentenced to nine years in prison with a non-parole period of five years and five months.The appealThe three men appealed on the grounds the verdicts were unsafe and victims unreliable.The men's barristers also claimed the jury could have been led to misinterpret their state of mind during the bucks weekend.The appellant judges are Justices Stephen Free, Peter Hamill and Belinda Rigg.Crown Prosecutor Bret Hatfield SC today elaborated on the claim about state of mind . The crown says state of mind exists over a 24-hour period and the men were looking for women in nightclubs, Mr Hatfield said.Mr Hatfield added there was a clear a break when the men went and had breakfast and went sightseeing in Newcastle.The court heard it was Andrew David's bucks party. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)The men's barristers also took aim at the credibility of witnesses on the Friday night and their understanding of consent.Mr Hatfield today told the judges there should not be expectations about how complainants in sexual assault matters should behave .'Inconsistencies'He said inconsistencies in their evidence largely relates to the number of people walking back to the apartment [where they were staying] and how many men were outside the room when they were being sexually assaulted. They have visceral and graphic detail that is hard to make up and embellish, Mr Hatfield said.He said that inconsistencies were relevant of course, but they were not significant .The presiding trial judge ruled against separate trials due to the context of the evidence.The men met two of the women at Newcastle's Cambridge Hotel. (Supplied: Vision Collective)Barristers for all three men rejected claims of a joint criminal enterprise raising concerns the jury was not given adequate directions about the concept.A joint criminal enterprise exists where two or more persons commit criminal activity and each is held to be criminally responsible for the acts of another.Justices Free, Hamill and Rigg reserved their decision.ABC full_text: Magistrate convicts police officer who punched teen during arrest Magistrate finds police officer assaulted teen during arrest in Batemans BayBy Christien de GarisABC South East NSWTopic:Courts17h ago17 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amBrett David Lindsay outside Batemans Bay Local Court. (ABC South East NSW: Christien De Garis)In short:A Senior Constable has been found guilty of using unreasonable force during the arrest of two teenage boys in Batemans Bay.Brett David Lindsay punched a 17-year-old boy during the arrest, with the magistrate finding the officer had no intention of de-escalating the situation .What's next?He was sentenced to two-year community correction order.abc.net.au/news/police-officer-assaulted-teen-batemans-bay-arrest-court-finds/105684886Link copiedShareShare articleA New South Wales police officer has been found guilty of assault and using an unreasonable amount of force during the arrest of two teenage boys in Batemans Bay.The case centred on the way Senior Constable Brett David Lindsay forced the then 14 and 17-year-old boys to the ground during the arrest in October 2023.Lindsay described using a distraction strike when he punched the older boy's collarbone.In Batemans Bay Local Court on Friday, Magistrate Doug Dick said he was satisfied the use of force was unnecessary. It was a use of force no reasonable officer would have used in the circumstances, he said.Investigating home invasionThe court heard Senior Constable Lindsay and his partner were investigating claims of a potential home invasion in Batemans Bay, which led them to a block of units where several teenagers were.Senior Constable Lindsay told the court they suspected the teenagers were involved in the alleged home invasion and arrested them.Over the two-day hearing, prosecutors pointed to body-worn camera footage which captured Senior Constable Lindsay grabbing the younger boy by his shoulders and throwing him onto a concrete floor.Brett David Lindsay's hearing took place in the Batemans Bay Local Court. (ABC News: James Tugwell)It also showed when a scuffle broke out between Senior Constable Lindsay and the 17-year-old, where the officer ended up on top of the teenager.Senior Constable Lindsay told the court the teenager tensed up, and he feared the boy was in reach of his gun and handcuffs, so he struck him on his collarbone area. I used what I would call a distraction strike … hopefully change [the teenager's] demeanour and direction it was heading, he said.The older teenager then repeatedly called the officer a white gronk and a f***ing dog .Giving evidence, the 17-year-old said: I didn't think a copper would hit me at that age. The court was told in another interaction, the police officer forced the 17-year-old to the ground, with his knee coming into contact with the teenager's stomach.Senior Constable Lindsay testified the teenager then clenched his fist.The Batemans Bay Senior Constable pleaded not guilty to six charges. (ABC News: James Tugwell)On the body-worn camera footage, the police officer can be heard saying to the teen: Do you want a f***ing punch mate, you'll get one. Magistrate rejects evidenceIn delivering his verdict, Magistrate Dick said it was clear [the 17-year-old] held ill feeling towards all police … [he] was deliberately confrontational and hostile .However, he went on to say he did not believe Senior Constable Lindsay's evidence that the officer genuinely believed he used necessary force. [Senior Constable Lindsay] had no intention of de-escalating the situation … [he] downplayed the seriousness of his conduct, Magistrate Dick said.Brett David Lindsay was given a community correction order. (ABC South East NSW: Christien De Garis)In sentencing, Senior Constable Lindsay's defence lawyer Ahmad Moutasallem revealed his client was suffering post-traumatic stress disorder and was on medical leave, as well as being suspended from the police force. He will not be working as a police officer anymore, Mr Moutasallem said.Magistrate Dick recorded a criminal conviction against the three assault charges and ordered Senior Constable Lindsay to serve a two-year community correction order.A NSW Police spokesperson confirmed Senior Constable Lindsay remained suspended with pay and a review would now be conducted.ABC South East NSW — local news in your full_text: Men charged over alleged plot to import 185 kg of methamphetamine into WA Perth men charged over alleged plot to import 185 kg of methamphetamine, attempt to steal $300kBy Nicolas PerpitchTopic:Crime17h ago17 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:05amAuthorities discovered 185 kilograms of meth hidden in bags of rice. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)In short:Police have charged a Perth man with trying to import 185 kilograms of methamphetamine into WA.The drugs were seized in bags of rice sent by sea from Pakistan.He and another Perth man have been charged over an alleged conspiracy to steal $300,000 in cash from two Victorians accused of trying to smuggle the money out of WA.abc.net.au/news/wa-perth-drug-cash-haul-/105686958Link copiedShareShare articleIt's a rare insight into Perth's violent organised criminal underworld.Authorities have lifted the lid on an operation that stopped 185 kilograms of methamphetamine hitting the streets and foiled a suspected plot by the alleged drug traffickers to also steal $300,000 in illicit cash off a Victorian man and woman in an armed highway heist.Police allege the Victorians were trying to smuggle the crime money out of Western Australia.In dramatic footage, officers can be seen pulling over a white van with suspects inside in the outer Perth suburb of Wooroloo on August 5. Show me your hands, put your hands out of the window now! One officer yells to the occupants as he approaches the car. Passenger, open the window! Hands out! Do not move! Do not move for anything, do you understand me? Loading...Police handcuff a man and pull him out of the van and onto the grass next to the road.An officer removes a loaded handgun from the front of the man's tracksuit pants.He takes the magazine out of the gun and puts it in an evidence bag.The video then shows officers searching the boot of a car and pulling out two vacuum sealed clear plastic bags from a hidden compartment, full of crisp $50 notes.Police allege the men involved had clear links to organised crime networks with international connections and outlaw motorcycle gangs.Operation Estevan was conducted by the WA Joint Organised Crime taskforce, involving the Australian Federal Police, WA Police, Australian Border Force, Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission and AUSTRAC.Information from the investigation yesterday led police to a home in the northern Perth suburb of Nollamara, where they arrested a man after finding a point-22 handgun, a sawn-off shotgun, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, knuckledusters, banned knives, methamphetamine, cannabis and other drugs.Significant discoveryThe operation started in December 2024, when authorities discovered 185 kilograms of meth hidden in bags of rice in a consignment sent by sea from Pakistan.That's the equivalent of 1.8 million street deals and would have been worth about $171 million to the criminal group.But AFP Assistant Commissioner Pryce Scanlan said the drug seizure has hurt the syndicate and left them potentially vulnerable. They obviously owe a lot of money potentially offshore. But this puts a big dent into organised crime, he said.A package containing methamphetamine which authorities will allege was found in a bag of rice. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)A 35-year-old man from the Perth suburb of Doubleview has subsequently been charged with importing a commercial quantity of methamphetamine, a charge that carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment.He's due in the Perth Magistrates court next week.Police then received intelligence tipping them off to what they call a threat to life .'Highway robbery'Police allege the Doubleview man and a 35-year-old man from the Perth suburb of Gwelup hatched a plan to execute what we can only refer to as a highway robbery .WA Police assistant commissioner Tony Longhorn said their target was the Victorian man and woman allegedly trying to smuggle $300,000 in cash gained through crime out of the state in a car.The two Perth men had allegedly placed tracking devices on the Victorians' vehicle and knew exactly where they would be. It is alleged that the drug traffickers planned to stop the couriers on the highway at gunpoint and steal the cash, assistant commissioner Longhorn said. It wasn't going to take place in a dark back street. This was going to be open air. Midday. With the community at risk. And we all know how this could have gone if it had gone wrong. Police say the meth haul had a value of about $171 million. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)Police allege one of the men had a loaded handgun when he was arrested.The two Perth men have been charged with one count each of conspiracy to commit an indictable offence, unlawful possession of a firearm, and one count of possessing money from the proceeds of crime.The two Victorians were charged with the same offence.WA 'hostile' to organised crimeAFP assistant commissioner Scanlan said it showed the links between illicit drugs and violent crime. These people are the ones who are preying on our children, your friends, your neighbours, trying to get them hooked onto these insidious drugs and turn them into people you do not recognise, he said. People who will rob, lie, steal and cheat. We're making WA as hostile as possible, and make sure drugs aren't coming through our borders. The 41-year-old man was arrested in bushland in Perth. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)In other recent operations, earlier this month a 41-year-old Coffin Cheaters Outlaw motorcycle gang member and a 34-year-old associate were charged after they were caught allegedly collecting 30 kilograms of methamphetamine in tea packaging from Perth bushland.Police say they were arrested after a lengthy foot chase, and they seized a hessian bag from one man allegedly containing a shovel, night vision goggles and a dedicated encrypted communications device.The 34 year old man was arrested after a lengthy police pursuit. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)Police also seized 15 kilograms of methamphetamine hidden in wooden furniture that arrived in Fremantle from South Africa earlier this year, with a street value close to $14 million.A Sydney man, who had flown to Perth the day before, has been charged with one count of importing a commercial quantity of border-controlled drugs.LoadingPosted 17h ago17 hours full_text: 'Sorry and sordid tale': WA GP jailed for child sex offences WA GP Douglas William McCarthy jailed for child sex offencesDBy David WeberTopic:Courts18h ago18 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03amDouglas McCarthy was sentenced for a range of sexual offences against teenage girls. (ABC News: Dave Weber)In short: Douglas William McCarthy, 63, who was a practising GP when he paid underage girls for sex has been sentenced to 20 years in jail. Judge Wendy Gillan rejected his evidence that he did not know the ages of most of the girls and said he should have known better given his age, intelligence and education.What's next? He'll be eligible for parole after 18 years.abc.net.au/news/wa-gp-douglas-william-mccarthy-sentenced-for-child-sex-/105686986Link copiedShareShare articleA West Australian doctor who paid tens of thousands of dollars to teenage girls for sex and photos, and kept a video library of his offending, has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.WARNING: This article contains details some readers may find distressing.Douglas William McCarthy, 63, was a practising GP in the state's south west, when he engaged in sexual acts with girls aged 14 and 15.McCarthy was found guilty by a WA District Court jury last week of a range of offences, including persistent sexual conduct and sexual penetration, possessing child pornography, and encouraging a 17-year-old to engage in prostitution.He was also found guilty of attempting to pervert the course of justice after paying some of his victims to keep quiet , including depositing $800 into one of the girls' bank accounts.If you or anyone you know needs help:1800 RESPECT national helpline on 1800 737 732Sexual Assault Counselling Australia on 1800 211 028Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors) on 1800 272 831Blue Knot Foundation on 1300 657 380Lifeline (24 hour crisis line) on 131 114'Sordid and sorry tale'In a scathing sentencing hearing, District Judge Wendy Gillan said McCarthy was only interested in his own selfish desires and described his offending over more than two years as a sorry and sordid tale .Judge Gillan said McCarthy, whose sexual involvement with the girls started when he was aged in his late fifties, engaged in a high level of corruption and should have known better given his age, intelligence and education.Douglas McCarthy has been jailed for 20 years. (ABC News: David Weber)She rejected his evidence that he didn't know the ages of most of the girls. Their true age was not an impediment to you, she said, pointing out that they were intoxicated during the sexual acts.One girl was 14 when she first posed for photos and sent them to McCarthy after being told by a friend that he would pay for them.This led to her going to see him and being paid for sexual acts, in what was a familiar pattern for other victims.In other incidents, he recorded videos of the offending, many of which the judge said were degrading .Judge Gillan said he'd allowed teenage girls to drink alcohol, take MDMA and smoke marijuana in his presence, including at his home. Your house was a party house where young people were able to use drugs with impunity. Victim impact statementsThe court heard that five of the teenagers had provided victim impact statements, with one saying McCarthy had stolen her innocence and she had been made to feel like a cheap prostitute .Another said she now found it difficult to trust older men and to speak with doctors.McCarthy's lawyer Wayne Burg referred to a letter his client had provided for the judge, saying he now believed the girls are blameless and he takes responsibility for his actions .But prosecutor Sean Stocks said last week those girls weren't blameless , telling the court that there was no remorse, just manipulation .Prosecutor Sean Stocks said McCarthy was not remorseful. (ABC News: David Weber)Mr Stocks said he had groomed vulnerable children and took advantage of them using his apparent wealth , and kept an extensive video library for his own interests. They've all clearly suffered , Mr Stocks told the court. The person he was to his family and friends was not the person he was. The judge said she couldn't accept he was remorseful.McCarthy was found guilty of 14 charges including child sex offences and attempting to pervert the course of justice, after a jury trial.The jury was forced to watch hours of graphic and disturbing footage filmed by McCarthy of him sexually abusing the teenagers, with the court hearing he had kept an extensive video library of his offending.During his trial, he'd pleaded guilty to four charges of sexual penetration.He'll be eligible for parole after 18 years.LoadingPosted 18h ago18 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03am, updated full_text: Podcaster faces murder charge over death of 30yo Perth woman Tobias Marcus Nuttall faces Perth court charged with murder of woman in BassendeanKBy Kenith PngTopic:Courts18h ago18 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:00amTobias Nuttall has been charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Bassendean. (YouTube)In short:A Perth conspiracy podcaster, Tobias Marcus Nuttall, has been charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Bassendean.He appeared briefly in Midland Magistrates Court, speaking only to confirm his name, and will remain in custody until a September court date.Police say the woman was found critically injured at a Reid Street home on Wednesday, later dying in hospital as homicide detectives continue investigating.abc.net.au/news/tobias-marcus-nuttall-faces-court-charged-with-bassendean-murder/105684606Link copiedShareShare articleA conspiracy theorist podcaster has appeared in court charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Perth's eastern suburbs.Tobias Marcus Nuttall, 32, appeared in the Midland Magistrates court today in custody, wearing a blue jumpsuit, with a beard and long hair.Mr Nuttall is accused of killing the woman, who is believed to be known to him, in Bassendean on Wednesday.The scene was cordoned off by police as they investigated the woman's death. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)In court, Mr Nuttall did not speak, other than to confirm his name.No further information was given by prosecutors, and Mr Nuttall will remain in custody ahead of his next court appearance in September.The WA Police Homicide Squad are investigating the woman's death, after emergency crews rushed to a house on Reid Street just after midday, finding a woman who had sustained critical injuries.Police were called to the house on Reid Street on Wednesday afternoon. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)She was rushed to Royal Perth Hospital where she died.Deep dive podcastMr Nuttall co-hosts an online podcast which is branded as a deep dive into the realms of conspiracy, the occult, magic, spirituality, and everything clandestine. As two inquisitive minds on a quest for truth, they pull back the curtains of the mundane to reveal a world bubbling with mysteries, hidden agendas, and esoteric knowledge, the podcast description says.Tobias Nuttall appearing on a podcast. (YouTube)On an episode posted on Wednesday night, after the alleged murder took place, Mr Nuttall's co-host excused his absence. There's nothing wrong with Toby, his co-host said.The 32-year-old was a co-host of a podcast that had last posted an episode on the day of the alleged murder. (YouTube) Toby had an appointment he had to come over to Sydney for and he was flying back from Sydney to Perth today. This is just to tell everybody we won't be doing one with Toby tonight, we'll have to do that tomorrow. Mr Nuttall was charged with murder the following evening.The charges were referenced by the co-host in a later episode.“Toby has been charged …. with a very very serious offence over in Perth, something that happened on Wednesday, the co-host said.Supporters of Tobias Marcus Nuttall outside the Midland Magistrates Court on Friday. (ABC News: Kenith Png)Members of Mr Nuttall's family were in court for the hearing.He will reappear in the Stirling Gardens Magistates Court on September 17.LoadingPosted 18h ago18 hours agoFri 22 Aug full_text: Illicit tobacco, money laundering funding Victorian burglaries, arsons Seizure of $7.2 million worth of illicit tobacco is linked to an alleged Iraqi crime syndicateTopic:Crime19h ago19 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amPolice intercepted a truck in Laverton North allegedly carrying $5 million of illicit tobacco. (Supplied: Victoria Police)abc.net.au/news/two-men-arrested-seven-million-dollars-illicit-tobacco/105686114Link copiedShareShare articleVictorian police say the seizure of $7.2 million worth of illicit tobacco is linked to an alleged Iraqi crime syndicate that is laundering money and using it to fund serious offending like aggravated burglaries.Police said they became aware an organised crime syndicate was conducting cash drops and collections at a small takeaway shop in Somerton, in Melbourne's north, in January. They also said further transactions were taking place at a factory in Epping. On Thursday Victoria Police, along with the Australian Border Force, executed warrants at two homes in Dallas and a business in Epping, where they seized $1.9 million worth of illicit tobacco, $80,000 in cash and six high-end watches. A 40-year-old Dallas man was arrested and is expected to be charged with possession of a commercial quantity of illicit tobacco and knowingly dealing with the proceeds of crime.Police believe over $83 million of cash has been laundered since May 2021.Victoria Police said as part of a separate investigation they intercepted a truck carrying $5 million of illegal cigarettes in Laverton North.The alleged driver, a 34-year-old Cambellfield man, was arrested at his home on Thursday, where detectives seized $100,000 in cash.Police said they believed the man attended the same Somerton shop linked to the money laundering investigation, and has alleged links to the organised crime syndicate involved. 'Vast number of crimes' can be committed with millions of dollarsDetective Inspector Graham Banks from Victoria Police said the seizures were significant. This group is connected to Iraqi organised crime entities, and they're funnelling money offshore to people who are directing very serious crimes in Victoria and the rest of Australia, he said.Detective Inspector Banks said to put the money into context, $1 million could buy a criminal syndicate 400 stolen cars. A million dollars will pay for 100 arsonists, a million dollars will buy you about 40 semi-automatic pistols with rounds, or if you prefer 20 assault rifles, he said. A million dollars will probably pay for two underworld hits of mid-level underworld characters, sometimes it goes up to $1 million. So there's $4 million, and there's a vast number of crimes that can committed with that money. But it doesn't speak to the money behind the crime, or the houses that have been broken into and the hundreds of people who have been victims of aggravated home invasions, or the large number of businesses that have had their businesses destroyed who aren't even related to the illicit tobacco trade. Syndicates using apps to hire criminalsDetective Inspector Banks said the crimes were organised on encrypted apps like Signal and WhatsApp. And people take up contracts, sometimes very small in monetary value, to do very serious offending, he said.Detective Inspector Graham Banks says criminals are being hired using encrypted apps. (ABC News)He said the amount of money that had been generated by the illicit tobacco trade was really staggering , and it was equal to, or more than, the drug trade.Detective Inspector Banks said there were one or two syndicates driving it. They will be the focus [of police]. They are the people who are killing people, they are the people organising arsons and they people who are organising aggravated burglaries which are impacting all members of the community, he said.Posted 19h ago19 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'Sophisticated fraudster': Documents reveal criminal history of charity full_text: 'Blind drunk' driver jailed for 14 years over hit and run death of 43yo mum Drunk driver Brett Eddy imprisoned for 14 years over manslaughter of Fraser Coast woman Natasha RavenBy Talissa SigantoTopic:Crime19h ago19 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51amNatasha Raven died after being struck by the vehicle Brett Eddy was driving. (Supplied)In short:Drunk driver Brett Eddy has been sentenced to 14 years' jail for the hit and run death of 43-year-old Natasha Raven last year.Ms Raven's family and friends told the Supreme Court in Brisbane of the pain they have been living with since her death.What's next?Eddy will be eligible for parole in 2033.abc.net.au/news/brett-eddy-imprisoned-for-manslaughter-drink-driver/105686842Link copiedShareShare articleA driver who was blind drunk and travelling at extreme speed when he killed a pedestrian in a hit and run on Queensland's Fraser Coast has been sentenced to 14 years in jail.Brett Eddy, 42, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane on Friday to several charges, including the manslaughter of Natasha Raven.The 43-year-old was struck by a car being driven by Eddy and left for dead on a Urangan street late at night in May last year. Eddy pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane on Friday. (Supplied)During a sentencing hearing, the court heard the day in question had been Eddy's birthday, and he had been drinking heavily throughout the day.The court heard at around 10pm, after being removed from a licensed venue, he drove to a friend's home who described him as being loud and obnoxious and blind drunk .He continued drinking, and around two hours later, the court heard he drove to a convenience store with a child, where staff said he was f*****g hammered .Court hears child filmed 'drunken joyride'Crown prosecutor Stephen Muir told the court Eddy then went on a drunken joyride , reaching speeds of up to 180 kilometres an hour through suburban streets. He should have been nowhere near behind the wheel of a car, he said.Mr Muir told the court Eddy reprehensibly then had the child film his dangerous driving, which was played to the court. That recording captures the defendant's obvious enjoyment in the moments before the killing, he said.The court heard at similar extreme speed he entered the shoulder of the road where Ms Raven was walking, just metres from her home, before he hit her and fled the scene.Ms Raven died at the scene of the crash. (ABC News)'Your actions are unforgivable'Ms Raven's brother Josh Raven submitted a victim impact statement to the court which was read by the prosecution.In his statement he said Eddy was a nightmare that lives in my head . The pain you've caused me is beyond anything I've already experienced, he said. Your actions are unforgivable. Mr Raven told the court the images, thoughts and smells from the crash scene will haunt me for the rest of my life . I hope this lives in your head for as long as you may live, he said to Eddy.Ms Raven's best friend Lauren Richards read her victim impact statement to the court.She said her death had left me with a pain I will carry for the rest of my life . Since she's been gone, I have been so alone, she said.Ms Richards told the court the death had taken the hardest toll on Ms Raven's son who is broken by grief and headed down the wrong path. Every day I watch him struggle and it tears me apart, she said. He feels lost without his Mum and he doesn't see much for his life ahead. Eddy appeared in court via video link on Friday. (ABC News: Curtis Rodda)Driver tells court 'I will never forgive myself'Appearing in court via video link from prison Eddy apologised to the Raven family and through tears said: I'll never forgive myself . I'm so sorry for this, I shouldn't have been on the road and it's my fault that this has happened, he said. I don't wish for anyone to forgive me, but I just want everyone to know that I am so sorry. The court heard Eddy had a lengthy criminal record across three states which spanned decades, and that he had a highly relevant traffic history of repeated unlicensed and drink driving offending.Justice Peter Davis took into consideration Eddy had entered into timely pleas and accepted other mitigating factors such as a PTSD diagnosis.However, when determining his sentence, he said Eddy exhibited “a high level of criminality” which caused Ms Raven, who was “innocent in all this” to lose her life in “violent circumstances”.“The nature of your driving was outrageously reckless,” he said.Eddy will be eligible for parole in 2033.Posted 19h ago19 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51am, updated 19h ago19 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:02amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly full_text: Postal worker charged over alleged $1.4m fraud from stolen bank cards Postal worker charged over alleged $1.4m fraud from stolen bank cards in Sydney's eastBy Danuta KozakiTopic:Police20h ago20 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amLuxury items including watches, handbags and jewellery were seized by police. (Supplied: NSW Police)In short: A 56-year-old postal worker is accused of stealing bank cards and other items from mail in Sydney's east.Police allege he supplied the stolen cards to two separate criminal syndicates, resulting in $1.4 million worth of fraud.Two other men were charged in connection and all three men are due before court next month.abc.net.au/news/nsw-sydney-postal-worker-charged-over-alleged-bank-fraud/105685680Link copiedShareShare articleA Sydney postman has been charged with the alleged mail theft of bank cards and other items in Sydney's east, resulting in $1.4 million worth of fraud.Police from the Financial Crimes Squad allege the 56-year-old postman supplied the stolen bank cards to two separate criminal syndicates.The postman allegedly stole items from 70 letters or packages in Edgecliff, Woollahra and Double Bay in the city's east, with police and Australia Post last November launching a joint investigation.Strike Force Detectives on Wednesday with help from NSW Police's organised crime squad Raptor executed five search warrants in Rockdale in Sydney's south and Roselands in the city's south west. During the warrants, police allegedly located and seized more than $14,000 in cash, a Dedicated Encrypted Criminal Communication Device, electronics, stolen bank cards, a taser, and luxury items including watches, handbags and jewellery, NSW Police said in a statement.56-year-old postman Mauro Coluzzi was then arrested in his home in Rockdale, along with two other men at separate locations.He was charged by police with 143 counts of dishonestly obtaining financial advantage by deception, stealing items from 70 pieces of mail, and participating in a criminal group.Police seized more than $14,000 in cash after executing five search warrants. (Supplied: NSW Police)The postman appeared before Sutherland Local Court on Thursday where he was granted conditional bail, including surrendering his passport.The other two men charged in connection with the alleged theft and fraud — 35-year-old Ashish Tamrakar from Rockdale and 27-year-old Ibrahim Abbas from Roselands — have also been granted bail.All three men are due before court next month.Alleged thefts reported by concerned banksNSW Financial Crimes Squad Commander, Detective Acting Superintendent Con Galea, said two of the three men were known to police previously. They were known to each other; they had an association from the time we were investigating them. Two of them — including the postman — were known to police. He said the alleged thefts were initially reported by the banks. The reporting happened in mid last year [2024] and several hundred customers have been affected. Acting Superintendent Galea said the criminal syndicates were allegedly involved in fraud. Basically, the criminal syndicates are focusing on fraud and deception related offences, obtaining those cards and perpetrating other frauds using those cards. Australia Post confirmed it has been supporting NSW Police in their investigation. (ABC South East NSW: Fatima Olumee)Police said the amount of money allegedly defrauded is expected to increase, as police investigate further cases from the alleged theft of the bank cards.In a statement, a spokesperson for Australia Post said more than 2.3 billion items are delivered through its network each year. Australia Post is proud of the role it plays in delivering for the community. This is a very serious matter and Australia Post has been supporting NSW Police in their investigation — and will continue to do so. Given the matter is before the Courts, it is not appropriate for us to comment further, Australia Post said.The ABC understands the postman has been suspended from his duties pending the investigation.Posted 20h ago20 hours agoFri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'Sophisticated fraudster': Documents reveal criminal history of charity full_text: Leader of 'cult-like' UK Christian group guilty of sexually abusing women 'Cult-like' Christian group leader found guilty of sexually abusing multiple women in congregationTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 12:24amChristopher Brain was the leader of the Nine O'Clock Service. (Supplied: South Yorkshire Police)In short: Christopher Brain, 68, was convicted of 17 indecent assault charges relating to nine women. He denied all 36 charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.What's next?Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said it would carefully consider a retrial since the jury could not reach a verdict on four counts of indecent assault and an alleged rape.abc.net.au/news/cult-like-christian-group-leader-found-guilty-of-sexual-abuse/105684554Link copiedShareShare articleA former Church of England priest in the UK has been found guilty of sexually abusing nine women in his congregation.Christopher Brain was the leader of a cult-like Christian group called the Nine O'Clock Service, based in Sheffield, northern England, in the 80s and 90s.The evangelical church movement was famous among young people for its 9pm services on Sundays that featured a live band. At its peak, it attracted hundreds of attendees.But, prosecutors said, Brain, 68, controlled members of the congregation, cutting them off from family and friends, and abused his position to sexually assault a staggering number of women .Brain also had a homebase team of young women dubbed the lycra nuns , prosecutor Tim Clark said. They looked after him, his wife and daughter at their house in Sheffield.He was charged with 36 counts of indecent assault and one count of rape relating to 13 women between 1981 and 1995. He denied the charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.After a trial at the Inner London Crown Court, Brain was convicted on Wednesday, local time, of 17 charges of indecent assault relating to nine women. He was acquitted of a further 15 counts.The jury was unable to reach a verdict on the remaining four counts of indecent assault and the alleged rape, Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said on Thursday, adding it would carefully consider a retrial.'Failing of the church'The Nine O'Clock Service had the blessing of the Church of England. Prosecutors said in 1990 that the Archbishop of Canterbury-elect, George Carey, had met Brain to discuss his methods.Brain's ordination was fast-tracked, and the Nine O'Clock Service spent large sums of money to obtain the outfit worn by actor Robert De Niro for the 1986 film The Mission for the ceremony, prosecutors said.But Brain resigned and left the church days before the broadcast of a 1995 BBC documentary, which accused him of sexually inappropriate behaviour. Mr Carey said he was crushed and let down when the allegations were made public.In his evidence, Brain said he received massages from members of the Nine O'Clock Service, which he said occasionally moved towards sexual activity. He also denied controlling or manipulating members of the congregation. What happened was an appalling abuse of power and leadership that should never have occurred, Bishop of Sheffield Pete Wilcox said in a statement. Where concerns were raised in the past and were not acted upon properly, that was a failing of the Church. For those institutional failures, I offer an unreserved apology. full_text: Man dead after stabbing on central Queensland coast Man dead after stabbing on central Queensland coastBy Jasmine Hines and Katrina BeavanABC CapricorniaTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 11:26pmPolice were called to Maida Street, Lammermoor, just after 7am. (ABC News: Niccola Way)In short:A man has died in Yeppoon this morning after being stabbed in the chest.Police have arrested a man and a woman, hours after the alleged offenders left the scene in a white utility.What's next?Forensic investigators are on site and police have launched a homicide investigation.abc.net.au/news/stabbing-death-central-queensland-coast-yeppoon/105684354Link copiedShareShare articlePolice have arrested a man and a woman after a 27-year-old man was fatally stabbed in Yeppoon, central Queensland, this morning.Authorities were called to Lammermoor just after 7am to reports of a man being wounded.He was treated for stab wounds to the chest, but died at the scene. It is alleged there was an altercation between the 27-year-old and another man at the address, and that they were known to each other. Detective Superintendent Darrin Shadlow alleged a man, aged 36, visited an address on Ganter Street in Yeppoon on Thursday night and assaulted two people. Police attended the residence at that time. However, no complaints were made, Detective Shadlow said.He said the man returned to the address this morning. An altercation has occurred, and he has chased the 27-year-old deceased from the residence through a backyard of a neighbouring property, to where, unfortunately, he received his fatal injuries, Detective Shadlow alleged.Neighbours say the street is typically quiet. (ABC News: Katrina Beavan)Police said the alleged offender left the scene in a white utility with a woman, before crashing it at Hamilton Creek near Mount Morgan, more than 80 kilometres away, around 10:45am. It is alleged the pair then abandoned the crashed ute before threatening another woman and taking her car.Police intercepted that car along Benaraby Road near Gladstone, south of Rockhampton, before taking the man, aged 36, and the woman, 20, into custody. The most dangerous aspect for the public was the manner of driving of this person, Detective Shadlow said.Detective Superintendent Darrin Shadlow addresses media in Rockhampton. (ABC Capricornia: Aaron Kelly)Neighbours tried to helpLocal woman Sue, who asked that her surname be withheld as she was yet to speak to police, said she found the victim on her front lawn and tried to save him with the help of other neighbours. We tried to resuscitate him until the ambulance arrived … we applied a lot of pressure and then we had to proceed with CPR, she said. It's pretty shocking and a bit surreal. It's very tragic. She described the street as quiet and close-knit. We have Christmas parties together, we enjoy each other's company, we look out for each other, she said. It's a really lovely neighbourhood, so this is really shocking and surprising. Police have arrested a 36-year-old man and a 20-year-old woman after a fatal stabbing in Yeppoon. full_text: Police chase 'a bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers', witness says Launceston man refused bail after low-speed chase in stolen truck driven on rimsBy Hayden SmithTopic:CourtsThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:23pmLoading...In short:A Newnham man has been refused bail after engaging Tasmania police in an hours-long pursuit in a stolen truck on Wednesday, at times while the truck's tyres were blown-out.A bystander has said the noise of metal on the road from the truck being driven on its wheel rims was pretty insane .What's next?Patrick Brown has pleaded guilty to dangerous driving charges and evade police.abc.net.au/news/launceston-man-pleads-guilty-after-stolen-truck-evade/105681218Link copiedShareShare articleA 27-year-old who pleaded guilty to driving a stolen truck on its rims through Launceston has been refused bail.Patrick Brown pleaded guilty to a number of charges in the Launceston Magistrate's Court on Thursday, including two counts of evading police and dangerous driving.The court heard Brown stole a white tipper truck on Tuesday, which he drove on the following night through some of the region's busiest streets, including the East Tamar Highway — at times veering onto the wrong side of the road and ignoring traffic lights.Loading...The court heard he continued for several hours after police spiked the tyres, with Brown then driving the truck on its rims.Numerous police units, including a helicopter, were involved in the truck's pursuit.Police say Brown, from the Launceston suburb of Newnham, was later arrested in Ravenswood without further incident .The driver led police on a chase despite driving on rims.Sound of 'metal on road': WitnessA Dilston resident who saw part of the pursuit said he was alerted to something happening when he heard a chopper hovering over . I went out to get a better view … and looked down John Lees Drive to see a convoy, he said. You had the truck at the front, police cars flanking and the chopper overhead. The noise was very loud. It was just metal on road [from the wheel rims] — pretty insane really. Dilston is 17 kilometres north-west of Ravenswood, where the driver was arrested.'A bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers'The white, tipper truck was stolen on Tuesday and involved in the chase the following day. (Supplied: Richard Morris)The witness described the scene as a slow-moving police chase with this helicopter and truck in no condition to evade police. He said it was a bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers . Normally it's a pretty quiet place, down there at Dilston. Appearing without legal representation on Thursday, Brown's bail application was denied by Magistrate Simon Brown.Brown also pleaded guilty to charges dating back more than 12 months, including multiple stealing offences and breaching bail.The dangerous driving charges were committed to the Supreme Court for sentencing on September 5.Posted Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:23pmThursday 21 Aug 2025 at full_text: Officer, elderly woman seriously injured in separate crashes involving police cars WA police officer, 80yo woman injured in separate crashes in Northam, SubiacoBy Kate ChristianTopic:PoliceThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52amA police officer was seriously injured in a crash near Northam, east of Perth. (ABC News)abc.net.au/news/several-injured-after-several-crashes-involving-police-vehicles/105682658Link copiedShareShare articleA police officer has been airlifted to hospital and an elderly woman has been left with serious injuries after two separate crashes involving police vehicles on Thursday.Commander Mike Peters said a marked police car was involved in a collision with a semi-trailer on the Great Eastern Highway near Northam in the Central Wheatbelt just before 11am.A second officer in the car is being treated for minor injuries, while the driver of the semi-trailer was not injured.The police car was involved in a collision with a semi-trailer. (ABC News)Around 20 minutes later at 11.15am, police were responding to reports of a person being armed with a gun when they were involved in a collision with another vehicle on Bagot Road in Subiaco. They were driving under emergency conditions when they collided with an 80-year-old lady turning into a driveway, Commander Peters said. As a result she has been taken to hospital with serious injuries. The officers were not injured. Commander Mike Peters said police did their best to protect the community. (ABC News) It is always confronting for us when we see one of our own officers injured, Commander Peters said. The police go out every day to do their absolute best to protect the community and it is unfortunate that these events happen and our hearts and minds go out to all people affected by this. Commander Peters said there was no further risk to the community as a result of the Subiaco incident, while a 23-year-old woman is assisting police with their inquiries.He said it was a stark reminder to the community about the inherent dangers of policing.LoadingPosted Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52am, updated Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 8:08amThursday 21 Aug full_text: 'Depraved and offensive': WA teacher jailed over multiple child sex offences WA teacher Harry Sing Wan Lagdon jailed after admitting 25 child sex offencesDBy David WeberTopic:CourtsThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38amHarry Lagdon was sentenced in the District Court of WA on Thursday. (ABC News: Jack Stevenson)In short:Teacher Harry Sing Wan Lagdon groomed a student when she was 15 and had sex with her on school grounds.He also engaged in online offending with three other girls, aged 12 and 13.What's next:Lagdon will be eligible for parole after five years and nine months.abc.net.au/news/wa-teacher-jailed-for-child-sex-offences/105681636Link copiedShareShare articleA WA teacher who groomed and had sex with a teenage student, then sent depraved online messages to even younger girls, has been sentenced to more than seven years in prison.Harry Sing Wan Lagdon, now 29, became sexually involved with the student when she was 15, and their encounters took place on the grounds of the regional high school where he taught and she was enrolled.Lagdon, who was nine years older than the victim, sent hundreds of videos and photos to her over 18 months. Basically, explicit material every other day, District Court Judge Matthew Curwood said.The court heard sexual encounters between them took place in a classroom, a closet and a shed on the school's property, inside his car and at his apartment.Harry Lagdon pleaded guilty to a string of child sex offences. (ABC News)'Breach of trust'It had all started with what the judge described as Lagdon's grooming behaviour , providing gifts to the teenager including a necklace.Support services:Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors): 1800 272 831Lifeline (24-hour Crisis Line): 131 114Victims of Crime Helpline: 1800 819 817Before long, the relief teacher was asking the girl for explicit photos, and sending images and videos of himself to her.The offending also included oral sex and indecent touching in various locations on school grounds, and sexual intercourse without a condom in his car and apartment.While Lagdon's lawyer described it as a consensual relationship , the judge said it represented a significant breach of trust and the victim had nightmares as a result.After he relocated from the regional school to Perth, Lagdon started communicating online with three girls in Queensland, aged 12 to 13, pretending he was a teenager.'Depraved and offensive'Lagdon sent hundreds of messages, some of which the judge described as depraved and offensive .The teacher asked for explicit images from the three girls and two of them complied.Judge Curwood told the court girls aged 12 to 13 were inherently vulnerable to online predators and the psychological impact is likely to be profound and long lasting .Lagdon had pleaded guilty to 25 charges, including sexual penetration of a child over 16 under his authority, exposing a child under 13 to indecent matter, procuring or encouraging a child to engage in sexual behaviour, and possessing child exploitation material.Lagdon also admitted to possessing child exploitation material. (AAP: Mick Tsikas)The judge acknowledged Lagdon's pleas in February had avoided the need for a trial.Lagdon's lawyer Mark Gunning had told the court his client's actions had been devastating for him and his shame was palpable .Mr Gunning said while the school student and Lagdon were infatuated with each other , it was totally inappropriate .He said his client acknowledged his teaching career was finished.Lagdon's total prison sentence of seven years was backdated to June 2024, with eligibility for parole after five years and nine months.The judge ordered that his mobile phone and laptop be destroyed.Loading...LoadingPosted Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38am, updated Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:45amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 7:45amThu 21 Aug 2025 at full_text: Mental health condition considered in sentencing of teen girl shot by police Townsville teen girl shot by police released from detention for mental health treatmentBy Meghan DansieABC North QldTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:01amPolice were called to reports of a female armed with a knife making threats near Townsville's West End Hotel in June. (ABC News: Baz Ruddick)In short:A North Queensland magistrate has criticised Queensland Health in its handling of a teenage girl shot by police.She has been sentenced to 62 days imprisonment, already served.What's next?The now 18-year-old will be released from detention and transferred to hospital for further mental health assessment.abc.net.au/news/teen-girl-shot-by-police-released-for-mental-health-treatment/105680402Link copiedShareShare articleA North Queensland magistrate has criticised Queensland Health over its handling of a teenage girl shot by police.Warning: This story contains mention of suicide and self-harm.The teenager, who self-harmed more than 80 times while being held in youth detention, has been released by the court and sent to hospital for treatment.The now 18-year-old from Townsville was shot by police in June after they were called to reports of a female armed with a large knife making threats near Townsville's West End Hotel.The Ethical Standards Command investigated the Townsville shooting. (ABC News: Chloe Chomicki)Magistrate Viviana Keegan sentenced the woman, who was 17 at the time of the incident, to 62 days imprisonment, already served, for serious assault and obstruction of police.She will be released from Cleveland Youth Detention Centre today and transferred by ambulance to the Townsville University Hospital for further mental health assessment.If you or anyone you know needs help:Suicide Call Back Service on 1300 659 467Lifeline on 13 11 14Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander crisis support line 13YARN on 13 92 76Kids Helpline on 1800 551 800Beyond Blue on 1300 224 636Headspace on 1800 650 890ReachOut at au.reachout.comMensLine Australia on 1300 789 978QLife 1800 184 527The hearing in Townsville's Children's Court was told the teenager had been treated for numerous diagnosed mental health conditions since she was 14.Magistrate Keegan said during her time in custody the teenager was treated for 80 incidents of self-harm and had been admitted for emergency medical treatment 16 times. The criminal justice system can't manage [her], Magistrate Keegan said.She questioned why four suicide attempts, and being shot by police, had not resulted in an involuntary treatment order — which previously resulted in the refusal of a bail application. It's been sought on a number of occasions and on each occasion the clinical team has considered it not necessary, she said. It seems that is what is needed. Magistrate Viviana Keegan sentenced the now 18-year-old to 62 days imprisonment, already served. (ABC North Queensland: Rachael Merritt)Officers were called to the West End Hotel in Townsville at 5:30pm on June 10 after reports a female armed with a large knife was making threats.The court heard the teenager was shot by a police officer after she ignored numerous warnings while she advanced on them brandishing a knife.The Ethical Standards Command investigated the Townsville shooting.Due to the aggravating factor of the knife used in the assaults the magistrate said the teenager was being tried under adult crime, adult time laws passed by the Queensland government last year.She told the now 18-year-old, who appeared via video link from Cleveland Youth Detention Centre, to consider the impact of her actions and seek help moving forward. There are a lot of risks, Magistrate Keegan said. I hope you do as much as you can to engage with the mental health people. full_text: Police charge second man over Melbourne synagogue firebombing Police charge 20-year-old Meadow Heights man over Adass Israel Synagogue arson attackTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 5:55amLoading...In short:A 20-year-old man is facing three charges in relation to an alleged arson attack on a synagogue in Melbourne's south east.He is the second person to be charged over the firebombing.What's next:The man is expected to face court next week. abc.net.au/news/second-man-charged-adass-israel-synagogue-arson-ripponlea/105682132Link copiedShareShare articleCounter-terrorism police have charged a second man over the firebombing of the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne in December last year.The building in Ripponlea in Melbourne's south-east was gutted in a suspicious blaze in the early hours of Friday, December 6, sparking widespread condemnation.Australian Federal Police arrested a 20-year-old Meadow Heights man after carrying out a search warrant last week.A number of items were seized including electronic devices which police said are undergoing forensic examination. He was charged with arson, conduct endangering life and motor vehicle theft today.The Adass Israel Synagogue in Ripponlea was destroyed in the December 2024 attack. (Supplied: Sally Westwood)Australian Federal Police acting assistant commissioner Nick Read said the investigation has been one of the highest priorities for the counter-terrorism unit. I want to reassure the community — especially the Jewish community — that the AFP, together with Victoria Police and ASIO, are working relentlessly to bring this investigation to its conclusion, he said.Victoria Police assistant commissioner Tess Walsh urged the community to come forward with any new information. There is no place for this type of offending in our state, and we will be relentless in pursuing those who are prepared to engage in these acts of violence, she said.Two of three people charged over firebombingPolice allege the 20-year-old man is one of three people who broke into the Ripponlea synagogue and deliberately lit the fire. The Joint Counter Terrorism Team has now charged two of the three alleged offenders accused of directly setting the synagogue on fire, a police spokesperson said. He is due to appear before the Melbourne Magistrates' Court next week.In July, a 21-year-old Werribee man was also charged over his alleged role in breaking into and setting fire to the synagogue. Another man, 20, was charged for allegedly stealing a communal crime car, which police say was used to drive to the synagogue on the day of the attack.It is alleged the same vehicle was used in an arson attack two weeks earlier, on November 21, at LUX nightclub, south-east of Melbourne. Another man has also been charged over the nightclub fire.
