headline: Pune Crime Files: How cops traced engineering student Bhagyashree Sude’s killers from a ransom message
who: Bhagyashree Sude’s; Devendra Fadnavis; Hafiz Sude; Suryakant Sude; Wagholi; Sagar Ramesh Jadhav; Sagar; Sarjerao Kumbhar; Fadnavis
where: Harangul; Viman Nagar; Pune; Hindi; Mumbai; Nanded; Kamargaon; Ahilyanagar
when: 22-year-old; March 30 last year; fourth-year; around 9 pm; March 30, 2024; April 2; The same day; 21; two years; March 28; 23; the day; March 30; April 7; his school days; 120B
full_text: Pune Crime Files: How cops traced engineering student Bhagyashree Sude’s killers from a ransom message Fulfilling a promise made by Devendra Fadnavis, who was the home minister of Maharashtra at the time, senior lawyer and Rajya Sabha MP Ujjwal Nikam recently appeared before a Pune court for a hearing in the Bhagyashree Sude murder case. The 22-year-old engineering student was allegedly murdered by three youths, including her college friend, on March 30 last year. The state government has appointed Nikam as the Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) in the case. Bhagyashree goes missing A native of Harangul village in Maharashtra’s Latur district, Bhagyashree was a fourth-year student of BE (Computer Science) at GH Raisoni College in Pune’s Wagholi and resided at Sakore Nagar. As per police records, she went to Phoenix Mall in Viman Nagar around 9 pm on March 30, 2024. Bhagyashree had told her mother that she was going to a friend’s birthday party, but went missing soon after, the police said. On failing to contact Bhagyashree, her parents came to Pune and lodged a missing-person report at Viman Nagar police station on April 2. The same day, her mother received a ransom message from Bhagyashree’s mobile phone: “Allah Hafiz Sude family. Stop searching for Bhagyashree. We have kidnapped her. We have sent her to a foreign country.” The message, which was in Hindi, directed Bhagyashree’s parents to transfer Rs 9 lakh to her bank account for her release and threatened to throw pieces of her body in her native village if the police were informed. Investigators later said the message was meant to “divert” their attention and make her family and the police believe that she was still alive. Meanwhile, Bhagyashree’s father Suryakant Sude, a former sarpanch, lodged a First Information Report (FIR) of kidnapping under section 364 (a) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). A technical investigation confirmed that the ransom message to Bhagyashree’s parents was sent from Mumbai’s Jogeshwari area. A police team went to Mumbai, but could not trace the accused. As the probe into Bhagyashree’s mobile phone calls and bank account continued, the police zeroed in on Shivam Madhav Fulawale, 21, a student of BE (IT) at her college. Officers said Bhagyashree knew Fulawale, a native of Nanded, for two years as they were in the same college and belonged to the Marathwada region. They used to talk to each other and she had even met him on March 28, the police said. Based on clues obtained during the investigation, investigators arrested Fulawale from Wagholi for his alleged role in Bhagyashree’s murder. Subsequently, his aides Suresh Shivaji Indure, 23, and Sagar Ramesh Jadhav, 23, were also arrested. A mall visit and a pit dug the day before The probe revealed that Bhagyashree went with Fulawale on March 30 when he came to Phoenix Mall in a rented car along with his friends Suresh and Sagar. The police suspect that Fulawale may have offered to drop her near her room but the three men allegedly choked her to death in the car. Officers said the accused allegedly took her body to a secluded spot at Kamargaon village in Ahilyanagar district. They suspect the men burnt her body with petrol before burying her. The police recovered Bhagyashree’s body from the spot on April 7. Referring to the pit in which Bhagyashree was found buried, an officer said the accused had dug it the day before committing the crime, suggesting that her murder was a premeditated and well-planned act. The accused had hired a car on rent to commit the crime. The police said they went to Mumbai and Nanded after the murder before returning to Pune and giving the car back to the service provider. The vehicle was subsequently seized for investigation. Plan hatched after ‘losses in share market, gaming’ The police said Suresh, who has a diploma in IT and worked in Mumbai, knew Fulawale as both hail from the same district. Fulawale knew Sagar, a Class 10 pass, since his school days. The accused were charged under Indian Penal Code (IPC) sections 302 (murder), 120B (criminal conspiracy), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence), 404 (dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person), and 34 (common intention). As the police began probing the motive behind the murder, it came to light that the suspects had become debt-ridden after losing their money in the share market and to online gaming. So they allegedly hatched a conspiracy to kidnap Bhagyashree and extort money from her family. Officers, however, suspect that she may have been murdered because of her attempts to resist them. Sarjerao Kumbhar, Senior Police Inspector, said, “The accused committed the crime for money. There was no sexual assault on the victim. The accused had no previous criminal record. Technical investigation helped us in solving the case.” After the murder triggered outrage, Fadnavis, who was then the deputy chief minister and home minister of the state at the time, visited Bhagyashree’s family and said he would personally request advocate Ujjwal Nikam to be the SPP in the case. A police officer who was part of the investigation said a chargesheet has been filed against the three accused who are currently in jail. The case is on before a court in Pune.

full_text: UK to use AI to predict theft, knife attacks and violent crimes by 2030 Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining the way we do things, but none of it reflects the dystopian worlds we see in movies and TV series. However, that may soon change as the United Kingdom government now wants to use the technology to create interactive crime maps that will help “predict where offences are most likely to occur.” The announcement sounds straight out of the popular dystopian science fiction thriller Minority Report, where John (Tom Cruise) works with the PreCrime police to stop crimes before they occur using three “PreCogs”, who can foresee crimes. In a press release, the UK government said the Technology Secretary Peter Kylethe, the detailed real-time interactive crime map will span across England and Wales and will help “detect, track and predict where devastating knife crime is likely to occur or spot anti-social behaviour early on” to give the police a head start and intel ahead of dangerous situations. Part of the Safer Streets Mission, the AI-powered, real-time interactive crime map is aimed at tackling crime in urban areas. The UK government will be making an initial investment of £4 million for the prototype model, which is expected to come out in April 2026. Under the £500 million R&D Missions Accelerator Programme, the UK government wants a fully functional system by 2030. Designed to focus on crimes that “make people unsafe” in their own neighbourhoods from theft, anti-social behaviour, knife crime and violent crime, the system will help aggregate data shared between police, councils and social services by analysing “previous incident locations and studying the patterns of known offenders.” The map will help the police officers identify areas where the crime rate is high and deploy resources as added to prevent future crimes. The use of AI might sound like science fiction, but similar initiatives in other parts of the world have had mixed results. For example, predictive policing tools used in Los Angeles and Chicago were decommissioned after they were accused of racial bias and had limited success. Another predictive software project named Geolitica (previously called PredPol) was discontinued in 2020, after its effectiveness was cited as uncertain. However, the Crime Anticipation System (CAS), a project in the Netherlands, has seen modest success in terms of burglary rates. The Danish police have also successfully used AI systems to help with fraud investigations.

full_text: Three knifed to death for trying to stop drunk men from ransacking dhaba Three men who tried to stop a group of drunk men from ransacking a dhaba in Chhattisgarh’s Dhamtari district were stabbed to death late Monday night. The incident took place outside Annapurna Dhaba in Bhoyna village, around 78 kilometres from the state capital Raipur. “A group was ransacking the place, throwing tables around in an inebriated condition. The men, Alok Singh Thakur, Nitin Tandi and Suresh Hiyal, and their friends were having food,” said a police official from Arjuni police station. “The men tried to stop the group, but the accused attacked them with a knife. The prime accused, identified as Gopi Diwan (20), was carrying the weapon, and he allegedly stabbed the three men. One of the victims tried to run away but was chased and attacked by Diwan. All three died on the spot. Once police received information, we swung into action and caught all the suspects. We also seized the murder weapon,” the official said. “Eight persons, including three minors, were detained after the incident. The five adults, including Diwan, have been arrested and sent to judicial custody. We are finding out if they have a prior criminal record,” said Superintendent of Police, Dhamtari, Suraj Singh. The three minors have been sent to a correctional home. Police have invoked sections of murder and unlawful assembly of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

full_text: Karnataka woman chopped into 19 pieces; son-in-law among 3 held for murder Four days after the body parts of a woman were found dumped in several locations in Chimpuganahalli in Karnataka’s Tumakuru district, the police on Monday arrested three people, including her son-in-law, a dentist, for the murder. The police identified the deceased as Lakshmi Devi, 42, a resident of Bellavi village, and the accused as Dr Ramachandraiah S, 47, Satish K N, 38, and Kiran K S, 32, all residents of Kallahalli. Ramachandraiah is married to Devi’s daughter, Tejasvi, 26, the police said, adding that this was his second marriage. According to the police, on August 3, Devi left her home to see her daughter. A day later, her husband, Basavaraj, lodged a missing person’s complaint at Bellavi police station. Three days later, on August 7, the police were alerted about 19 body parts being found at various places in Chimpuganahalli. The body parts were found inside bags that were disposed of at no fewer than 19 locations, the police said. The Koratagere police registered a murder case and sent a message to all police stations in the district to check if any missing person complaints had been filed. It was then that the Bellavi police informed Basavaraj, who identified the body as Devi’s. According to the police, CCTV footage showed that a Maruti Suzuki Brezza was used to dump the body parts. The vehicle was allegedly registered in the name of Satish. “We took custody of Satish, and he spilled the beans. Satish and Kiran were taken into custody from Hornad. Ramachandraiah was in Dharmasthala after the murder and was not available for questioning. This also raised our suspicion,” a police officer said. Ramachandraiah allegedly claimed that his wife was listening to her mother’s advice and causing trouble in their marriage, Ashok K V, Superintendent of Police (SP), Tumakuru district, said. “He was unhappy over his mother-in-law’s interference. His first marriage is still in the divorce stage. In 2019, he married Tejasvi,” SP Ashok added. “We are yet to know why the accused cut her body into pieces and threw it at different locations. We have produced them before the court and will take them to police custody for further questioning. The car gave us the major lead to crack the case,” he said. According to the police, Satish was one of Ramachandraiah’s patients and stayed near his house. Kiran was Satish’s cousin, the police added. SP Ashok denied reports that the murder was linked to human sacrifice.

full_text: Ex-TMC leader Bibhas Adhikari, arrested in Noida for a ‘fake police station’, allegedly ran similar set-up in Kolkata Ex-TMC leader Bibhas Chandra Adhikari, arrested in Noida for “running a fake police station”, has allegedly been found to have operated a similar set-up in Kolkata. Adhikari, a former Trinamool Block President from Nalhati in Birbhum and once under the CBI and ED scanner in the teachers’ recruitment scam, was picked up along with his son and four others for allegedly running the “International Police & Crime Investigation Bureau” in Noida’s Sector 70 on Saturday night. Police said the group allegedly posed as government officials to extort money. Investigations by Kolkata police revealed that in Kolkata’s Beleghata area, Adhikari had allegedly rented two flats on CIT Road where he displayed boards reading “Investigation of Social Justice”, “Interpol” and “Police”. He would allegedly arrive in a car with a blue beacon with four armed guards. Police claimed he owns significant assets, including an Ayurvedic college in Suri, a B.Ed college in Krishnapur, and houses in Kolkata and Delhi. Adhikari was removed from his Trinamool post before the 2021 elections, later forming the “Bhartiya Arya Samaj” party. However, he was seen sharing the stage with TMC leaders in 2024 and was accused of taking money in exchange for job promises in the teachers’ recruitment scam. Sources said he was considered close to jailed former Education Minister Partha Chatterjee. His Krishnapur ashram housed an office using the letterhead of the “National Bureau of Social Investigation and Social Justice.” The CBI questioned him multiple times in 2023 in the recruitment case. headline: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver
who: Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad; Aruna; Gailkwad; Gaikwad; Santwadi; Gaikwad’s; Ananda Chavan; Mayur Vijay Solse; Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane
where: Pune Rural; Malshej; Kasara; Gangapur Road; Nashik; Solse; Chavan; Gangapur

full_text: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver Around 7.30 on January 27, Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad, 56, a resident of Nashik who worked as a rental cab driver, called his wife Aruna on her phone. He had taken a trip from Nashik to Pune around 5 am that day. He told her he would reach home around 7.30 pm. That was the last conversation Aruna had with her husband. Repeated calls made to him were unanswered. Around 10.30 pm that night, Gailkwad’s wife got a call that his phone had been found on the Alephata Santwadi road off the Pune-Nashik highway. The caller had kept the phone at a nearby hotel, from where he had made the call. Around 2.30 am on January 28, the Gaikwad family reached the hotel and searched for him in the area where the phone was found. However, Gaikwad and his car could not be traced. The family registered a missing person case at Alephata police station under the Pune Rural police. At around 9.30 am on January 28, while police were actively searching for Gaikwad, his body was discovered in the Santwadi area. His hands were bound behind his back with a nylon rope and a zip tie, and initial autopsy findings indicated that he had been strangled. The murder investigation was taken up jointly by teams from the Alephata police station and the Pune Rural police’s Local Crime Branch. As part of the investigation, the police reviewed footage from dozens of CCTV cameras on the approach routes to the area. A significant breakthrough came when Gaikwad’s vehicle was spotted on a hotel’s CCTV camera along the Nashik–Pune highway corridor. By piecing together video evidence from multiple locations, investigators traced the car’s movement—first heading toward the area where his body was later discovered, then continuing in the direction of Malshej Ghat. Both the footage and ground inquiries indicated that, at one stage, four people were inside the car along with Gaikwad. Meanwhile, a team which was on the lookout for the car found it abandoned in Kasara Ghat, along the route to Nashik. Continued analysis of CCTV footage helped police identify suspects who were captured travelling in the vehicle. Over the following three days, till January 31, investigators arrested three suspects: Vishal Ananda Chavan, 22; Mayur Vijay Solse, 23; and Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane, 21, all residents of the Gangapur Road area in Nashik. The investigation to arrest the fourth suspect continues even now. Driver resisted carjacking attempt, say police Investigators found out that the suspects had boarded Gaikwad’s car during his return journey to Nashik from Pune. They used the pretext of hitching a ride, but wanted to hijack the vehicle, said the police. The sequence of events, as brought out by the investigation, was that they allegedly strangled him after he resisted their attempt. The group then disposed of his body and fled the scene, said the police. It was soon revealed that the trio are hardened criminals. They allegedly intended to use the hijacked car for an armed robbery in which they wanted to target a shop in Nashik. The police said they, however, decided to abandon it on the way since they thought the vehicle would be flagged in the murder investigation after Gaikwad’s body was found. Solse and Chavan are facing charges of murder registered at Gangapur police station in Nashik in 2022. As the police continued their probe, they found out that these suspects were involved in a case of carjacking at Chakan police station registered in 2024, which had remained unsolved till the time the murder case was cracked. “The chargesheet in the case was filed subsequently. All three accused are currently in prison under judicial custody. A coordinated search for the fourth accused continued. The wanted suspect in the case also has multiple offences registered against him,” said an officer who was part of the probe. The case underscores the dangers faced by drivers who pick up unknown passengers outside their assigned duties. Authorities have reiterated their warning against this practice, noting that similar incidents of passengers turning violent have been reported in the past.

full_text: Gurgaon man masturbates in front of woman waiting for cab, police file FIR The Gurgaon police on August 5 registered a case against a man who was caught on camera allegedly masturbating in front of a young woman near Rajiv Chowk in the city, officers said on Thursday. According to the police, the incident took place on August 2 when the complainant, a model and digital content creator, was waiting for a cab around noon at a busy junction to head home after a journey from Jaipur. Krishan Kumar, Station House Officer, Civil Lines Police Station, said that the police have filed a First Information Report (FIR) under sections 75(2) for sexual harassment and 78 for stalking of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. “The investigation is underway, and the complainant has also joined the probe, and we have recorded her statement. We are scanning CCTV footage in and around the spot and talking to people in the area.” On the same day of the incident, the model narrated her ordeal on social media and posted the video of the alleged act of the perpetrator, while also blaming the police for the delay in registering a complaint. “Something very strange happened to me. A man came around, circling, and he was constantly staring at me. Initially, I just ignored it, like the others do,” she said. She noticed that the man with unzipped pants was allegedly masturbating. The video showed the man wearing a facemask and a backpack that he had slung over his chest to cover the act from being too visible to the public nearby. The woman said it was clear he was ‘very aware’ of what he was doing. The woman in her video also lamented how cab companies were delaying in accepting her ride request, aggravating her ordeal. The complainant stated that although she had initially got a ride booked, the driver was not picking up despite multiple calls, and hence she had to re-book across applications “just to avoid the creep”. Eventually, a cab arrived and she reached home. In the video, she also alleged initial inaction from the police after she had tagged the police and other government authorities while putting the man’s video on X, and later calling the police helpline. “There wasn’t even an automated message,” she said. Regarding the FIR, the model said, the police had asked her to come to the station instead of lodging the complaint online. “It was making me feel very uncomfortable. I felt very, very disgusted. Initially, I froze. I did not record or hit him. People who say I could have shouted at him do not understand what goes through a girl’s mind at that moment. Reactions go viral faster than the real truth, and people judge; they do not help.” The woman stated she wanted to be safe rather than have the moment become viral. “I am not making the video for any kind of attention, just want to be heard,” she said in the video.

full_text: 'Sophisticated fraudster' behind cancelled Victorian bushfire charity event Victorian charity CEO with new identity previously charged with deceptionBy Mikaela Ortolan and ABC News VerifyStatelineTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pmFounder of Disaster Recovery Army Inc, Jay Brady, served time in prison for fraud-related offences under another name. (ABC News: Shane Willner-Browne)In short:A man who presided over a controversial fundraiser for bushfire-affected communities previously went by another name, under which he was convicted of multiple crimes of deception.The bushfire recovery event was cancelled earlier this year when community members raised concerns about the legitimacy of the charity behind the event.Charity founder Jay Brady did not deny the past convictions but declined to answer specific questions. He maintains the charity is legitimate.abc.net.au/news/jay-brady-jason-palankay-deception-charges-bushfire-recovery/105610002Link copiedShareShare articleA Victorian man who attempted to organise a charity event for bushfire-affected communities has a history of committing crimes of deception under a different name dating back decades, the ABC can reveal.Earlier this year, a charity event to support bushfire-affected communities in Victoria's west was called off amid community concern over the way it had been organised. Jay Brady founded and headed up the registered charity, Disaster Recovery Army Inc, which was behind the Recover Grampians event.The event was due to take place in March — after a summer of devastating fires in the Grampians National Park — but its site was taken down and a GoFundMe page that had raised almost $16,000 was closed when local businesses started questioning the event and its legitimacy. The webpage for the Recover Grampians event, which was taken down after the local community raised concerns. (Supplied)An ABC investigation has found Mr Brady previously went by the name Jason Palankay, under which he had been convicted of numerous deception-related offences and served time in prison, according to court documents.In 2011, while facing court over several charges of obtaining property by deception, he was described by a judge as an artful, skilful and sophisticated fraudster .While considering his sentence, the judge said Palankay was a persistent offender who has not been deterred by previous sentences . When contacted by the ABC, Mr Brady did not deny the past convictions but said he would not divulge personal details and could not answer specific questions because of legal proceedings. He said he changed his surname from Palankay a long time ago for personal family reasons .A psychological report submitted to the courts during the 2011 matter said Palankay met the criteria for Narcissistic Personality Disorder and displayed a grandiose sense of self-importance .A number of residential properties were destroyed in the Grampians bushfires. (Supplied: David Grimble )Businesses suffer almost $180,000 in lossesCourt documents show Palankay was convicted of deception offences at the Melbourne Magistrates' Court as early as 1998 after writing cheques that could not be honoured. He was convicted for similar offences the following year and then again in 2002, according to the same material.He was again convicted over a matter involving bouncing cheques in 2005, the documents show.The same documents also reference another charge in South Australia. They suggest Palankay served time in prison in that state, but the ABC was unable to obtain further details.The ABC compared a still from a TV interview with Jay Brady (left) and an image from a 2016 newspaper article that identified Jason Palankay (right). (WIN News/Leader Newspapers: Stuart Milligan)In 2007, Palankay turned to fraudulently obtaining vehicles and profiting from their sale, costing impacted businesses nearly $180,000, a court heard. During this time, he worked as an independent contractor for LeaseMasters — a salary packaging specialist offering novated leasing, which is a way to pay for a car and its running costs directly through a person's salary.Do you know more about this story?Contact Mikaela Ortolan at ortolan.mikaela@abc.net.au. If you're sharing sensitive information, read our tips on how to contact us confidentially.Court documents say Palankay requested a quote for a vehicle and gave falsified purchase orders to the car retailer on a number of occasions, despite not being authorised to do so.Palankay obtained the vehicles by falsely representing that finances had been approved . According to court documents, he would then use the vehicles as security to obtain loans.Court documents say Palankay would then sell the vehicle, using some of the money to pay off the loans and pocketing any profit. After his engagement with LeaseMasters was terminated, court documents say he continued contacting car dealers and obtaining vehicles while falsely representing that [he was] operating a genuine business known as Fleet Development .He purchased several cars in this way over a nine-month period, the documents say.Palankay sentenced to prisonPalankay was convicted of one count of using a false document and five counts of obtaining property by deception in relation to the vehicles in 2011.It was submitted to the court that Palankay undertook this fraudulent activity to pay back debts to the Australian Tax Office of more than $110,000 at the time of offending.However, in sentencing, County Court judge Mark Taft said none of the proceeds from the cars you sold made their way to the ATO and I find the account you proffer as utterly implausible . In the course of committing the frauds on car dealers you displayed a high level of cunning, the judge said. Your level of intelligence increases the risk you represent to the public. Palankay had initially pleaded guilty to the charges, but weeks before his sentencing, he sought to change his plea after claiming he had been improperly induced to plead guilty by statements from the judge. The change of plea application was dismissed by the County Court Chief Judge. Mr Brady was photographed leaving a court in Bendigo over a separate matter, in which he was the complainant, earlier this year. (ABC News: Emile Pavlich)During his sentencing remarks, Judge Taft said Palankay's guilty pleas were not accompanied by any remorse whatsoever and you do not have a skerrick of insight into your wrongdoing . He was sentenced to three years and 10 months in prison with a non-parole period of two-and-a-half years.He was also sentenced to nine months in prison in 2019 after pleading guilty to unrelated charges of obtaining property by deception. In that case, he was ordered to undertake a 12 month community correction order upon his release. A psychological report tendered to court during a hearing for the car-related crimes, authored by Aaron Cunningham and dated November 2011, stated Palankay said he had previously been diagnosed with delusions of grandeur .In the report, Dr Cunningham expressed the opinion that Palankay met the criteria for Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD). Mr Palankay's NPD is evident by his grandiose sense of self-importance, preoccupation with fantasies of unlimited success, belief that he [is] special and unique, need for excessive admiration, sense of entitlement, interpersonally exploitative and lack of empathy, Dr Cunningham said in his report submitted to the court. When asked about this Mr Brady said, I certainly do not have a diagnosis of delusions of grandeur or NPD .Bushfire event won't go aheadIn 2008, Palankay filed for bankruptcy.At some stage he began using the name Jay Brady. The ABC is not aware of any criminal convictions since his name change.Mr Brady registered the charity Disaster Recovery Army Inc in March 2024 and after devastating bushfires in the Grampians over two summers, he began advertising charity work and calling on volunteers.The event's website once advertised tickets but Mr Brady previously told the ABC none were sold.He also previously said the sum raised through GoFundMe was used for equipment hire, vehicles, rent and other charity operational expenses.Mr Brady previously told the ABC no tickets to the event were sold. (ABC News)Community members who held concerns about the fundraising event said businesses had not been consulted despite its website at one point claiming it had 100-plus local business supporters.Earlier this year, the Northern Grampians Shire Council said Mr Brady had expressed interest in registering the event but had not completed the registration process. The ABC has also confirmed at least one image on the charity's website — purporting to show a volunteer — appears on other social media profiles and blog posts unrelated to the charity, where the person photographed has a different name. A photo of a woman on the charity's website (left) appears on other websites unrelated to Mr Brady's charity (right). (ABC News)The ABC put a series of detailed questions to Mr Brady about his past offending, his name change and the bushfire recovery event. In a written response earlier this month, he said he could not answer questions about his past offending because of legal proceedings underway . In relation to the name change, he said for personal family reasons, my surname was changed to Brady a long time ago as I do not have a relationship with my birth father .He maintains the charity is legitimate but said there is no intention to hold a Recover Grampians event at a later date , despite earlier suggesting it would be rescheduled. My term with the charity concludes shortly, so it will be up to any future board and management to canvass that, Mr Brady said. [Any] insinuation also that I have deceived or utilised funds associated with the charity are also false. Clearly, anecdotes have been taken out of context and/or used to create a narrative that doesn’t accurately reflect the charity’s, or my own, intentions to serve the communities we do. The ABC previously spoke with an employee at Disaster Recovery Army Inc who said volunteers had carried out work including trimming and removing dead bushes, fixing containment fences and removing burnt fences. The employee said they were legally doing work with the intention of helping people in disaster-affected communities.Victoria Police said no complainants had come forward and no offences had been identified in relation to the charity event.How the ABC uncovered a second identity:A search of the Disaster Recovery Army Inc's listed phone number led the ABC to a defunct website Jay Brady used to campaign for local councillor. The ABN linked to that website was different to the ABN the charity was registered under.A subsequent search of the campaign website ABN identified Jason Palankay as an entity name alongside Jay Brady and one other name. The ABC carried out a number of other searches as part of its investigation. One search found company records for both Jason Palankay and Jay Brady that listed the same home address.An article published in the Herald Sun in 2016 contained a photograph of Jason Palankay after he participated in an interview, and that image was compared against a still from a TV interview with Jay Brady.The ABC attended a court hearing in Bendigo in June where Jay Brady appeared as the complainant, and was able to confirm a visual match with a photograph of Jason Palankey in a Leader Newspapers article.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pmFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pmFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pm, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:45pmFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 9:45pmFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:45pmShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: Convicted bucks party gang rapists argue guilty verdicts 'unsafe' Sydney men jailed over bucks party gang rape in Newcastle argue guilty verdicts 'unsafe'GBy Giselle WakatamaABC NewcastleTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amComposite Andrew David and Maurice Hawell outside court after their lengthy gang rape trial in 2024. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)In short: Three men jailed over gang rapes in Newcastle are appealing, arguing guilty verdicts were unsafe.Their barristers have argued witnesses were unreliable and have questions directions given to the jury by the presiding judge.What's next?The appellant judges have reserved their decision. abc.net.au/news/convicted-gang-rapists-argue-guilty-verdicts-unsafe-on-appeal/105687344Link copiedShareShare articleLegal teams for a group of men jailed for gang raping three women in Newcastle have argued their guilty verdicts were an unsafe and unsatisfactory verdict , and witnesses were unreliable.Last year brothers Maurice Hawell, 31, and Marius Hawell, 24, and friend Andrew David, 31, were convicted of multiple counts of aggravated sexual assault and aggravated sexual touching in company.The trio's lawyers have spent the past two days challenging the men's convictions and sentences in the Court of Criminal Appeal.An argument around an unsafe verdict alleges the jury's guilty verdict was unsatisfactory and should be overturned.The offences occurred during a bucks weekend in February 2022.The men had travelled to Newcastle and stayed in an Airbnb for the weekend.Two of the women were 18 at the time and the third was 19.'Callous and degrading'In sentencing, Justice Gina O'Rourke said the men engaged in a pack mentality and treated the women in a cold, callous, degrading and criminal way .Maurice Hawell was sentenced to 14 years in prison with a non-parole period of eight years and six months.Maurice Hawell is one of the men appealing his conviction and sentence. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)Andrew David was sentenced to 13 years in prison with a non-parole period of seven years and nine months.Marius Hawell was sentenced to nine years in prison with a non-parole period of five years and five months.The appealThe three men appealed on the grounds the verdicts were unsafe and victims unreliable.The men's barristers also claimed the jury could have been led to misinterpret their state of mind during the bucks weekend.The appellant judges are Justices Stephen Free, Peter Hamill and Belinda Rigg.Crown Prosecutor Bret Hatfield SC today elaborated on the claim about state of mind . The crown says state of mind exists over a 24-hour period and the men were looking for women in nightclubs, Mr Hatfield said.Mr Hatfield added there was a clear a break when the men went and had breakfast and went sightseeing in Newcastle.The court heard it was Andrew David's bucks party. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)The men's barristers also took aim at the credibility of witnesses on the Friday night and their understanding of consent.Mr Hatfield today told the judges there should not be expectations about how complainants in sexual assault matters should behave .'Inconsistencies'He said inconsistencies in their evidence largely relates to the number of people walking back to the apartment [where they were staying] and how many men were outside the room when they were being sexually assaulted. They have visceral and graphic detail that is hard to make up and embellish, Mr Hatfield said.He said that inconsistencies were relevant of course, but they were not significant .The presiding trial judge ruled against separate trials due to the context of the evidence.The men met two of the women at Newcastle's Cambridge Hotel. (Supplied: Vision Collective)Barristers for all three men rejected claims of a joint criminal enterprise raising concerns the jury was not given adequate directions about the concept.A joint criminal enterprise exists where two or more persons commit criminal activity and each is held to be criminally responsible for the acts of another.Justices Free, Hamill and Rigg reserved their decision.ABC Newcastle — local news in your inboxGet our local newsletter, delivered free each WednesdayEmail addressSubscribeYour information is being handled in accordance with the ABC Privacy Collection Statement.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: Magistrate convicts police officer who punched teen during arrest Magistrate finds police officer assaulted teen during arrest in Batemans BayBy Christien de GarisABC South East NSWTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amBrett David Lindsay outside Batemans Bay Local Court. (ABC South East NSW: Christien De Garis)In short:A Senior Constable has been found guilty of using unreasonable force during the arrest of two teenage boys in Batemans Bay.Brett David Lindsay punched a 17-year-old boy during the arrest, with the magistrate finding the officer had no intention of de-escalating the situation .What's next?He was sentenced to two-year community correction order.abc.net.au/news/police-officer-assaulted-teen-batemans-bay-arrest-court-finds/105684886Link copiedShareShare articleA New South Wales police officer has been found guilty of assault and using an unreasonable amount of force during the arrest of two teenage boys in Batemans Bay.The case centred on the way Senior Constable Brett David Lindsay forced the then 14 and 17-year-old boys to the ground during the arrest in October 2023.Lindsay described using a distraction strike when he punched the older boy's collarbone.In Batemans Bay Local Court on Friday, Magistrate Doug Dick said he was satisfied the use of force was unnecessary. It was a use of force no reasonable officer would have used in the circumstances, he said.Investigating home invasionThe court heard Senior Constable Lindsay and his partner were investigating claims of a potential home invasion in Batemans Bay, which led them to a block of units where several teenagers were.Senior Constable Lindsay told the court they suspected the teenagers were involved in the alleged home invasion and arrested them.Over the two-day hearing, prosecutors pointed to body-worn camera footage which captured Senior Constable Lindsay grabbing the younger boy by his shoulders and throwing him onto a concrete floor.Brett David Lindsay's hearing took place in the Batemans Bay Local Court. (ABC News: James Tugwell)It also showed when a scuffle broke out between Senior Constable Lindsay and the 17-year-old, where the officer ended up on top of the teenager.Senior Constable Lindsay told the court the teenager tensed up, and he feared the boy was in reach of his gun and handcuffs, so he struck him on his collarbone area. I used what I would call a distraction strike … hopefully change [the teenager's] demeanour and direction it was heading, he said.The older teenager then repeatedly called the officer a white gronk and a f***ing dog .Giving evidence, the 17-year-old said: I didn't think a copper would hit me at that age. The court was told in another interaction, the police officer forced the 17-year-old to the ground, with his knee coming into contact with the teenager's stomach.Senior Constable Lindsay testified the teenager then clenched his fist.The Batemans Bay Senior Constable pleaded not guilty to six charges. (ABC News: James Tugwell)On the body-worn camera footage, the police officer can be heard saying to the teen: Do you want a f***ing punch mate, you'll get one. Magistrate rejects evidenceIn delivering his verdict, Magistrate Dick said it was clear [the 17-year-old] held ill feeling towards all police … [he] was deliberately confrontational and hostile .However, he went on to say he did not believe Senior Constable Lindsay's evidence that the officer genuinely believed he used necessary force. [Senior Constable Lindsay] had no intention of de-escalating the situation … [he] downplayed the seriousness of his conduct, Magistrate Dick said.Brett David Lindsay was given a community correction order. (ABC South East NSW: Christien De Garis)In sentencing, Senior Constable Lindsay's defence lawyer Ahmad Moutasallem revealed his client was suffering post-traumatic stress disorder and was on medical leave, as well as being suspended from the police force. He will not be working as a police officer anymore, Mr Moutasallem said.Magistrate Dick recorded a criminal conviction against the three assault charges and ordered Senior Constable Lindsay to serve a two-year community correction order.A NSW Police spokesperson confirmed Senior Constable Lindsay remained suspended with pay and a review would now be conducted.ABC South East NSW — local news in your inboxGet our local newsletter, delivered free each ThursdayEmail addressSubscribeYour information is being handled in accordance with the ABC Privacy Collection Statement.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: Men charged over alleged plot to import 185 kg of methamphetamine into WA Perth men charged over alleged plot to import 185 kg of methamphetamine, attempt to steal $300kBy Nicolas PerpitchTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:05amAuthorities discovered 185 kilograms of meth hidden in bags of rice. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)In short:Police have charged a Perth man with trying to import 185 kilograms of methamphetamine into WA.The drugs were seized in bags of rice sent by sea from Pakistan.He and another Perth man have been charged over an alleged conspiracy to steal $300,000 in cash from two Victorians accused of trying to smuggle the money out of WA.abc.net.au/news/wa-perth-drug-cash-haul-/105686958Link copiedShareShare articleIt's a rare insight into Perth's violent organised criminal underworld.Authorities have lifted the lid on an operation that stopped 185 kilograms of methamphetamine hitting the streets and foiled a suspected plot by the alleged drug traffickers to also steal $300,000 in illicit cash off a Victorian man and woman in an armed highway heist.Police allege the Victorians were trying to smuggle the crime money out of Western Australia.In dramatic footage, officers can be seen pulling over a white van with suspects inside in the outer Perth suburb of Wooroloo on August 5. Show me your hands, put your hands out of the window now! One officer yells to the occupants as he approaches the car. Passenger, open the window! Hands out! Do not move! Do not move for anything, do you understand me? Loading...Police handcuff a man and pull him out of the van and onto the grass next to the road.An officer removes a loaded handgun from the front of the man's tracksuit pants.He takes the magazine out of the gun and puts it in an evidence bag.The video then shows officers searching the boot of a car and pulling out two vacuum sealed clear plastic bags from a hidden compartment, full of crisp $50 notes.Police allege the men involved had clear links to organised crime networks with international connections and outlaw motorcycle gangs.Operation Estevan was conducted by the WA Joint Organised Crime taskforce, involving the Australian Federal Police, WA Police, Australian Border Force, Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission and AUSTRAC.Information from the investigation yesterday led police to a home in the northern Perth suburb of Nollamara, where they arrested a man after finding a point-22 handgun, a sawn-off shotgun, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, knuckledusters, banned knives, methamphetamine, cannabis and other drugs.Significant discoveryThe operation started in December 2024, when authorities discovered 185 kilograms of meth hidden in bags of rice in a consignment sent by sea from Pakistan.That's the equivalent of 1.8 million street deals and would have been worth about $171 million to the criminal group.But AFP Assistant Commissioner Pryce Scanlan said the drug seizure has hurt the syndicate and left them potentially vulnerable. They obviously owe a lot of money potentially offshore. But this puts a big dent into organised crime, he said.A package containing methamphetamine which authorities will allege was found in a bag of rice. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)A 35-year-old man from the Perth suburb of Doubleview has subsequently been charged with importing a commercial quantity of methamphetamine, a charge that carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment.He's due in the Perth Magistrates court next week.Police then received intelligence tipping them off to what they call a threat to life .'Highway robbery'Police allege the Doubleview man and a 35-year-old man from the Perth suburb of Gwelup hatched a plan to execute what we can only refer to as a highway robbery .WA Police assistant commissioner Tony Longhorn said their target was the Victorian man and woman allegedly trying to smuggle $300,000 in cash gained through crime out of the state in a car.The two Perth men had allegedly placed tracking devices on the Victorians' vehicle and knew exactly where they would be. It is alleged that the drug traffickers planned to stop the couriers on the highway at gunpoint and steal the cash, assistant commissioner Longhorn said. It wasn't going to take place in a dark back street. This was going to be open air. Midday. With the community at risk. And we all know how this could have gone if it had gone wrong. Police say the meth haul had a value of about $171 million. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)Police allege one of the men had a loaded handgun when he was arrested.The two Perth men have been charged with one count each of conspiracy to commit an indictable offence, unlawful possession of a firearm, and one count of possessing money from the proceeds of crime.The two Victorians were charged with the same offence.WA 'hostile' to organised crimeAFP assistant commissioner Scanlan said it showed the links between illicit drugs and violent crime. These people are the ones who are preying on our children, your friends, your neighbours, trying to get them hooked onto these insidious drugs and turn them into people you do not recognise, he said. full_text: 'Sorry and sordid tale': WA GP jailed for child sex offences WA GP Douglas William McCarthy jailed for child sex offencesDBy David WeberTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03amDouglas McCarthy was sentenced for a range of sexual offences against teenage girls. (ABC News: Dave Weber)In short: Douglas William McCarthy, 63, who was a practising GP when he paid underage girls for sex has been sentenced to 20 years in jail. Judge Wendy Gillan rejected his evidence that he did not know the ages of most of the girls and said he should have known better given his age, intelligence and education.What's next? He'll be eligible for parole after 18 years.abc.net.au/news/wa-gp-douglas-william-mccarthy-sentenced-for-child-sex-/105686986Link copiedShareShare articleA West Australian doctor who paid tens of thousands of dollars to teenage girls for sex and photos, and kept a video library of his offending, has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.WARNING: This article contains details some readers may find distressing.Douglas William McCarthy, 63, was a practising GP in the state's south west, when he engaged in sexual acts with girls aged 14 and 15.McCarthy was found guilty by a WA District Court jury last week of a range of offences, including persistent sexual conduct and sexual penetration, possessing child pornography, and encouraging a 17-year-old to engage in prostitution.He was also found guilty of attempting to pervert the course of justice after paying some of his victims to keep quiet , including depositing $800 into one of the girls' bank accounts.If you or anyone you know needs help:1800 RESPECT national helpline on 1800 737 732Sexual Assault Counselling Australia on 1800 211 028Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors) on 1800 272 831Blue Knot Foundation on 1300 657 380Lifeline (24 hour crisis line) on 131 114'Sordid and sorry tale'In a scathing sentencing hearing, District Judge Wendy Gillan said McCarthy was only interested in his own selfish desires and described his offending over more than two years as a sorry and sordid tale .Judge Gillan said McCarthy, whose sexual involvement with the girls started when he was aged in his late fifties, engaged in a high level of corruption and should have known better given his age, intelligence and education.Douglas McCarthy has been jailed for 20 years. (ABC News: David Weber)She rejected his evidence that he didn't know the ages of most of the girls. Their true age was not an impediment to you, she said, pointing out that they were intoxicated during the sexual acts.One girl was 14 when she first posed for photos and sent them to McCarthy after being told by a friend that he would pay for them.This led to her going to see him and being paid for sexual acts, in what was a familiar pattern for other victims.In other incidents, he recorded videos of the offending, many of which the judge said were degrading .Judge Gillan said he'd allowed teenage girls to drink alcohol, take MDMA and smoke marijuana in his presence, including at his home. Your house was a party house where young people were able to use drugs with impunity. Victim impact statementsThe court heard that five of the teenagers had provided victim impact statements, with one saying McCarthy had stolen her innocence and she had been made to feel like a cheap prostitute .Another said she now found it difficult to trust older men and to speak with doctors.McCarthy's lawyer Wayne Burg referred to a letter his client had provided for the judge, saying he now believed the girls are blameless and he takes responsibility for his actions .But prosecutor Sean Stocks said last week those girls weren't blameless , telling the court that there was no remorse, just manipulation .Prosecutor Sean Stocks said McCarthy was not remorseful. (ABC News: David Weber)Mr Stocks said he had groomed vulnerable children and took advantage of them using his apparent wealth , and kept an extensive video library for his own interests. They've all clearly suffered , Mr Stocks told the court. The person he was to his family and friends was not the person he was. The judge said she couldn't accept he was remorseful.McCarthy was found guilty of 14 charges including child sex offences and attempting to pervert the course of justice, after a jury trial.The jury was forced to watch hours of graphic and disturbing footage filmed by McCarthy of him sexually abusing the teenagers, with the court hearing he had kept an extensive video library of his offending.During his trial, he'd pleaded guilty to four charges of sexual penetration.He'll be eligible for parole after 18 years.LoadingPosted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03am, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:16amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 7:16amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:16amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: Podcaster faces murder charge over death of 30yo Perth woman Tobias Marcus Nuttall faces Perth court charged with murder of woman in BassendeanKBy Kenith PngTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:00amTobias Nuttall has been charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Bassendean. (YouTube)In short:A Perth conspiracy podcaster, Tobias Marcus Nuttall, has been charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Bassendean.He appeared briefly in Midland Magistrates Court, speaking only to confirm his name, and will remain in custody until a September court date.Police say the woman was found critically injured at a Reid Street home on Wednesday, later dying in hospital as homicide detectives continue investigating.abc.net.au/news/tobias-marcus-nuttall-faces-court-charged-with-bassendean-murder/105684606Link copiedShareShare articleA conspiracy theorist podcaster has appeared in court charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Perth's eastern suburbs.Tobias Marcus Nuttall, 32, appeared in the Midland Magistrates court today in custody, wearing a blue jumpsuit, with a beard and long hair.Mr Nuttall is accused of killing the woman, who is believed to be known to him, in Bassendean on Wednesday.The scene was cordoned off by police as they investigated the woman's death. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)In court, Mr Nuttall did not speak, other than to confirm his name.No further information was given by prosecutors, and Mr Nuttall will remain in custody ahead of his next court appearance in September.The WA Police Homicide Squad are investigating the woman's death, after emergency crews rushed to a house on Reid Street just after midday, finding a woman who had sustained critical injuries.Police were called to the house on Reid Street on Wednesday afternoon. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)She was rushed to Royal Perth Hospital where she died.Deep dive podcastMr Nuttall co-hosts an online podcast which is branded as a deep dive into the realms of conspiracy, the occult, magic, spirituality, and everything clandestine. As two inquisitive minds on a quest for truth, they pull back the curtains of the mundane to reveal a world bubbling with mysteries, hidden agendas, and esoteric knowledge, the podcast description says.Tobias Nuttall appearing on a podcast. (YouTube)On an episode posted on Wednesday night, after the alleged murder took place, Mr Nuttall's co-host excused his absence. There's nothing wrong with Toby, his co-host said.The 32-year-old was a co-host of a podcast that had last posted an episode on the day of the alleged murder. (YouTube) Toby had an appointment he had to come over to Sydney for and he was flying back from Sydney to Perth today. This is just to tell everybody we won't be doing one with Toby tonight, we'll have to do that tomorrow. Mr Nuttall was charged with murder the following evening.The charges were referenced by the co-host in a later episode.“Toby has been charged …. with a very very serious offence over in Perth, something that happened on Wednesday, the co-host said.Supporters of Tobias Marcus Nuttall outside the Midland Magistrates Court on Friday. (ABC News: Kenith Png)Members of Mr Nuttall's family were in court for the hearing.He will reappear in the Stirling Gardens Magistates Court on September 17.LoadingPosted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:00amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 7:00amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:00am, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 11:26amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 11:26amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 11:26amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: Illicit tobacco, money laundering funding Victorian burglaries, arsons Seizure of $7.2 million worth of illicit tobacco is linked to an alleged Iraqi crime syndicateTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amPolice intercepted a truck in Laverton North allegedly carrying $5 million of illicit tobacco. (Supplied: Victoria Police)abc.net.au/news/two-men-arrested-seven-million-dollars-illicit-tobacco/105686114Link copiedShareShare articleVictorian police say the seizure of $7.2 million worth of illicit tobacco is linked to an alleged Iraqi crime syndicate that is laundering money and using it to fund serious offending like aggravated burglaries.Police said they became aware an organised crime syndicate was conducting cash drops and collections at a small takeaway shop in Somerton, in Melbourne's north, in January. They also said further transactions were taking place at a factory in Epping. On Thursday Victoria Police, along with the Australian Border Force, executed warrants at two homes in Dallas and a business in Epping, where they seized $1.9 million worth of illicit tobacco, $80,000 in cash and six high-end watches. A 40-year-old Dallas man was arrested and is expected to be charged with possession of a commercial quantity of illicit tobacco and knowingly dealing with the proceeds of crime.Police believe over $83 million of cash has been laundered since May 2021.Victoria Police said as part of a separate investigation they intercepted a truck carrying $5 million of illegal cigarettes in Laverton North.The alleged driver, a 34-year-old Cambellfield man, was arrested at his home on Thursday, where detectives seized $100,000 in cash.Police said they believed the man attended the same Somerton shop linked to the money laundering investigation, and has alleged links to the organised crime syndicate involved. 'Vast number of crimes' can be committed with millions of dollarsDetective Inspector Graham Banks from Victoria Police said the seizures were significant. This group is connected to Iraqi organised crime entities, and they're funnelling money offshore to people who are directing very serious crimes in Victoria and the rest of Australia, he said.Detective Inspector Banks said to put the money into context, $1 million could buy a criminal syndicate 400 stolen cars. A million dollars will pay for 100 arsonists, a million dollars will buy you about 40 semi-automatic pistols with rounds, or if you prefer 20 assault rifles, he said. A million dollars will probably pay for two underworld hits of mid-level underworld characters, sometimes it goes up to $1 million. So there's $4 million, and there's a vast number of crimes that can committed with that money. But it doesn't speak to the money behind the crime, or the houses that have been broken into and the hundreds of people who have been victims of aggravated home invasions, or the large number of businesses that have had their businesses destroyed who aren't even related to the illicit tobacco trade. Syndicates using apps to hire criminalsDetective Inspector Banks said the crimes were organised on encrypted apps like Signal and WhatsApp. And people take up contracts, sometimes very small in monetary value, to do very serious offending, he said.Detective Inspector Graham Banks says criminals are being hired using encrypted apps. (ABC News)He said the amount of money that had been generated by the illicit tobacco trade was really staggering , and it was equal to, or more than, the drug trade.Detective Inspector Banks said there were one or two syndicates driving it. They will be the focus [of police]. They are the people who are killing people, they are the people organising arsons and they people who are organising aggravated burglaries which are impacting all members of the community, he said.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: 'Blind drunk' driver jailed for 14 years over hit and run death of 43yo mum Drunk driver Brett Eddy imprisoned for 14 years over manslaughter of Fraser Coast woman Natasha RavenBy Talissa SigantoTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51amNatasha Raven died after being struck by the vehicle Brett Eddy was driving. (Supplied)In short:Drunk driver Brett Eddy has been sentenced to 14 years' jail for the hit and run death of 43-year-old Natasha Raven last year.Ms Raven's family and friends told the Supreme Court in Brisbane of the pain they have been living with since her death.What's next?Eddy will be eligible for parole in 2033.abc.net.au/news/brett-eddy-imprisoned-for-manslaughter-drink-driver/105686842Link copiedShareShare articleA driver who was blind drunk and travelling at extreme speed when he killed a pedestrian in a hit and run on Queensland's Fraser Coast has been sentenced to 14 years in jail.Brett Eddy, 42, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane on Friday to several charges, including the manslaughter of Natasha Raven.The 43-year-old was struck by a car being driven by Eddy and left for dead on a Urangan street late at night in May last year. Eddy pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane on Friday. (Supplied)During a sentencing hearing, the court heard the day in question had been Eddy's birthday, and he had been drinking heavily throughout the day.The court heard at around 10pm, after being removed from a licensed venue, he drove to a friend's home who described him as being loud and obnoxious and blind drunk .He continued drinking, and around two hours later, the court heard he drove to a convenience store with a child, where staff said he was f*****g hammered .Court hears child filmed 'drunken joyride'Crown prosecutor Stephen Muir told the court Eddy then went on a drunken joyride , reaching speeds of up to 180 kilometres an hour through suburban streets. He should have been nowhere near behind the wheel of a car, he said.Mr Muir told the court Eddy reprehensibly then had the child film his dangerous driving, which was played to the court. That recording captures the defendant's obvious enjoyment in the moments before the killing, he said.The court heard at similar extreme speed he entered the shoulder of the road where Ms Raven was walking, just metres from her home, before he hit her and fled the scene.Ms Raven died at the scene of the crash. (ABC News)'Your actions are unforgivable'Ms Raven's brother Josh Raven submitted a victim impact statement to the court which was read by the prosecution.In his statement he said Eddy was a nightmare that lives in my head . The pain you've caused me is beyond anything I've already experienced, he said. Your actions are unforgivable. Mr Raven told the court the images, thoughts and smells from the crash scene will haunt me for the rest of my life . I hope this lives in your head for as long as you may live, he said to Eddy.Ms Raven's best friend Lauren Richards read her victim impact statement to the court.She said her death had left me with a pain I will carry for the rest of my life . Since she's been gone, I have been so alone, she said.Ms Richards told the court the death had taken the hardest toll on Ms Raven's son who is broken by grief and headed down the wrong path. Every day I watch him struggle and it tears me apart, she said. He feels lost without his Mum and he doesn't see much for his life ahead. Eddy appeared in court via video link on Friday. (ABC News: Curtis Rodda)Driver tells court 'I will never forgive myself'Appearing in court via video link from prison Eddy apologised to the Raven family and through tears said: I'll never forgive myself . I'm so sorry for this, I shouldn't have been on the road and it's my fault that this has happened, he said. I don't wish for anyone to forgive me, but I just want everyone to know that I am so sorry. The court heard Eddy had a lengthy criminal record across three states which spanned decades, and that he had a highly relevant traffic history of repeated unlicensed and drink driving offending.Justice Peter Davis took into consideration Eddy had entered into timely pleas and accepted other mitigating factors such as a PTSD diagnosis.However, when determining his sentence, he said Eddy exhibited “a high level of criminality” which caused Ms Raven, who was “innocent in all this” to lose her life in “violent circumstances”.“The nature of your driving was outrageously reckless,” he said.Eddy will be eligible for parole in 2033.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51am, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:02amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 6:02amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:02amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: Postal worker charged over alleged $1.4m fraud from stolen bank cards Postal worker charged over alleged $1.4m fraud from stolen bank cards in Sydney's eastBy Danuta KozakiTopic:PoliceFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amLuxury items including watches, handbags and jewellery were seized by police. (Supplied: NSW Police)In short: A 56-year-old postal worker is accused of stealing bank cards and other items from mail in Sydney's east.Police allege he supplied the stolen cards to two separate criminal syndicates, resulting in $1.4 million worth of fraud.Two other men were charged in connection and all three men are due before court next month.abc.net.au/news/nsw-sydney-postal-worker-charged-over-alleged-bank-fraud/105685680Link copiedShareShare articleA Sydney postman has been charged with the alleged mail theft of bank cards and other items in Sydney's east, resulting in $1.4 million worth of fraud.Police from the Financial Crimes Squad allege the 56-year-old postman supplied the stolen bank cards to two separate criminal syndicates.The postman allegedly stole items from 70 letters or packages in Edgecliff, Woollahra and Double Bay in the city's east, with police and Australia Post last November launching a joint investigation.Strike Force Detectives on Wednesday with help from NSW Police's organised crime squad Raptor executed five search warrants in Rockdale in Sydney's south and Roselands in the city's south west. During the warrants, police allegedly located and seized more than $14,000 in cash, a Dedicated Encrypted Criminal Communication Device, electronics, stolen bank cards, a taser, and luxury items including watches, handbags and jewellery, NSW Police said in a statement.56-year-old postman Mauro Coluzzi was then arrested in his home in Rockdale, along with two other men at separate locations.He was charged by police with 143 counts of dishonestly obtaining financial advantage by deception, stealing items from 70 pieces of mail, and participating in a criminal group.Police seized more than $14,000 in cash after executing five search warrants. (Supplied: NSW Police)The postman appeared before Sutherland Local Court on Thursday where he was granted conditional bail, including surrendering his passport.The other two men charged in connection with the alleged theft and fraud — 35-year-old Ashish Tamrakar from Rockdale and 27-year-old Ibrahim Abbas from Roselands — have also been granted bail.All three men are due before court next month.Alleged thefts reported by concerned banksNSW Financial Crimes Squad Commander, Detective Acting Superintendent Con Galea, said two of the three men were known to police previously. They were known to each other; they had an association from the time we were investigating them. Two of them — including the postman — were known to police. He said the alleged thefts were initially reported by the banks. The reporting happened in mid last year [2024] and several hundred customers have been affected. Acting Superintendent Galea said the criminal syndicates were allegedly involved in fraud. Basically, the criminal syndicates are focusing on fraud and deception related offences, obtaining those cards and perpetrating other frauds using those cards. Australia Post confirmed it has been supporting NSW Police in their investigation. (ABC South East NSW: Fatima Olumee)Police said the amount of money allegedly defrauded is expected to increase, as police investigate further cases from the alleged theft of the bank cards.In a statement, a spokesperson for Australia Post said more than 2.3 billion items are delivered through its network each year. Australia Post is proud of the role it plays in delivering for the community. This is a very serious matter and Australia Post has been supporting NSW Police in their investigation — and will continue to do so. Given the matter is before the Courts, it is not appropriate for us to comment further, Australia Post said.The ABC understands the postman has been suspended from his duties pending the investigation.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top Stories'What have we done?': Gazan boys allege sexual abuse and torture in Israeli custodyTopic:Unrest, Conflict and WarPhoto shows A boy's back with tents in front of himStates threatened to get on board with NDIS changes or risk hospital funding dealTopic:Federal GovernmentPhoto shows Jim ChalmersPlans to surrender idyllic UK town to the seaTopic:Climate ChangePhoto shows A small coastal village, seen from the air, on a fine day.New Zealand town popular with Australians at 'cusp' of overtourismTopic:Travel and TourismPhoto shows A lit up no vacancy sign. full_text: Leader of 'cult-like' UK Christian group guilty of sexually abusing women 'Cult-like' Christian group leader found guilty of sexually abusing multiple women in congregationTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 12:24amChristopher Brain was the leader of the Nine O'Clock Service. (Supplied: South Yorkshire Police)In short: Christopher Brain, 68, was convicted of 17 indecent assault charges relating to nine women. He denied all 36 charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.What's next?Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said it would carefully consider a retrial since the jury could not reach a verdict on four counts of indecent assault and an alleged rape.abc.net.au/news/cult-like-christian-group-leader-found-guilty-of-sexual-abuse/105684554Link copiedShareShare articleA former Church of England priest in the UK has been found guilty of sexually abusing nine women in his congregation.Christopher Brain was the leader of a cult-like Christian group called the Nine O'Clock Service, based in Sheffield, northern England, in the 80s and 90s.The evangelical church movement was famous among young people for its 9pm services on Sundays that featured a live band. At its peak, it attracted hundreds of attendees.But, prosecutors said, Brain, 68, controlled members of the congregation, cutting them off from family and friends, and abused his position to sexually assault a staggering number of women .Brain also had a homebase team of young women dubbed the lycra nuns , prosecutor Tim Clark said. They looked after him, his wife and daughter at their house in Sheffield.He was charged with 36 counts of indecent assault and one count of rape relating to 13 women between 1981 and 1995. He denied the charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.After a trial at the Inner London Crown Court, Brain was convicted on Wednesday, local time, of 17 charges of indecent assault relating to nine women. He was acquitted of a further 15 counts.The jury was unable to reach a verdict on the remaining four counts of indecent assault and the alleged rape, Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said on Thursday, adding it would carefully consider a retrial.'Failing of the church'The Nine O'Clock Service had the blessing of the Church of England. Prosecutors said in 1990 that the Archbishop of Canterbury-elect, George Carey, had met Brain to discuss his methods.Brain's ordination was fast-tracked, and the Nine O'Clock Service spent large sums of money to obtain the outfit worn by actor Robert De Niro for the 1986 film The Mission for the ceremony, prosecutors said.But Brain resigned and left the church days before the broadcast of a 1995 BBC documentary, which accused him of sexually inappropriate behaviour. Mr Carey said he was crushed and let down when the allegations were made public.In his evidence, Brain said he received massages from members of the Nine O'Clock Service, which he said occasionally moved towards sexual activity. He also denied controlling or manipulating members of the congregation. What happened was an appalling abuse of power and leadership that should never have occurred, Bishop of Sheffield Pete Wilcox said in a statement. Where concerns were raised in the past and were not acted upon properly, that was a failing of the Church. For those institutional failures, I offer an unreserved apology. full_text: Man dead after stabbing on central Queensland coast Man dead after stabbing on central Queensland coastBy Jasmine Hines and Katrina BeavanABC CapricorniaTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 11:26pmPolice were called to Maida Street, Lammermoor, just after 7am. (ABC News: Niccola Way)In short:A man has died in Yeppoon this morning after being stabbed in the chest.Police have arrested a man and a woman, hours after the alleged offenders left the scene in a white utility.What's next?Forensic investigators are on site and police have launched a homicide investigation.abc.net.au/news/stabbing-death-central-queensland-coast-yeppoon/105684354Link copiedShareShare articlePolice have arrested a man and a woman after a 27-year-old man was fatally stabbed in Yeppoon, central Queensland, this morning.Authorities were called to Lammermoor just after 7am to reports of a man being wounded.He was treated for stab wounds to the chest, but died at the scene. It is alleged there was an altercation between the 27-year-old and another man at the address, and that they were known to each other. Detective Superintendent Darrin Shadlow alleged a man, aged 36, visited an address on Ganter Street in Yeppoon on Thursday night and assaulted two people. Police attended the residence at that time. However, no complaints were made, Detective Shadlow said.He said the man returned to the address this morning. An altercation has occurred, and he has chased the 27-year-old deceased from the residence through a backyard of a neighbouring property, to where, unfortunately, he received his fatal injuries, Detective Shadlow alleged.Neighbours say the street is typically quiet. (ABC News: Katrina Beavan)Police said the alleged offender left the scene in a white utility with a woman, before crashing it at Hamilton Creek near Mount Morgan, more than 80 kilometres away, around 10:45am. It is alleged the pair then abandoned the crashed ute before threatening another woman and taking her car.Police intercepted that car along Benaraby Road near Gladstone, south of Rockhampton, before taking the man, aged 36, and the woman, 20, into custody. The most dangerous aspect for the public was the manner of driving of this person, Detective Shadlow said.Detective Superintendent Darrin Shadlow addresses media in Rockhampton. (ABC Capricornia: Aaron Kelly)Neighbours tried to helpLocal woman Sue, who asked that her surname be withheld as she was yet to speak to police, said she found the victim on her front lawn and tried to save him with the help of other neighbours. We tried to resuscitate him until the ambulance arrived … we applied a lot of pressure and then we had to proceed with CPR, she said. It's pretty shocking and a bit surreal. It's very tragic. She described the street as quiet and close-knit. We have Christmas parties together, we enjoy each other's company, we look out for each other, she said.
