full_text: Starvation is a war crime, but will justice ever be done? ConflictsPalestinian TerritoriesStarvation is a war crime, but will justice ever be done?Cathrin Schaer08/15/2025August 15, 2025Experts say that food is increasingly being used as a weapon in conflicts in places like Sudan, Syria and Gaza. But there's never been a war crimes case about it in an international court. That may soon change.https://p.dw.com/p/4z3Y1Aid agencies and human rights organizations say Israel is deliberately starving civilians in Gaza, a charge Israel deniesImage: Ahmed Jihad Ibrahim Al-arini/Anadolu/picture allianceAdvertisementCalls to prosecute the war crime of starvation are becoming louder and more frequent. [Famine] is a weapon of war being wielded across the globe at the moment. But this has to stop, it's against international humanitarian law, Shayna Lewis, senior adviser on Sudan for the US-based group PAEMA (Preventing and Ending Mass Atrocities) told DW recently. She was talking about the Sudanese city of El Fasher, which has been under siege for a year now and where food is running out for around 30,000 people trapped there. It is a crime internationally and it needs to be prosecuted as such, Lewis argued. Human rights groups, including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, have said similar about Israel's blockade of aid and food into the Gaza Strip. Israel is starving Gaza. It's genocide. It's a crime against humanity. It's a war crime, Michael Fakhri, the United Nations' special rapporteur on the right to food, told UK newspaper the Guardian last week. The western Sudanese city of El Fasher has been under siege for almost a year. Around 300,000 inhabitants are at risk of famine.Image: UNICEF/Xinhua/picture alliance Food as a weapon of war Experts say that part of the reason there are now more calls to prosecute starvation of civilians as a war crime, is that there is more famine being caused by conflict. Over the first decade of this century, there was very little famine, researchers at the World Peace Foundation, or WPF, wrote in a 2022 collection of essays, Accountability for Starvation. But more recently that has changed. This is an ancient phenomenon, warring parties have been using it for centuries, Rebecca Bakos Blumenthal, a legal adviser with the Starvation Accountability project run by Netherlands-based law foundation, Global Rights Compliance, or GRC, says. After 2015, this kind of tactic has re-emerged, she noted. Syria's ousted dictator Bashar Assad's strategy of 'Besiege, starve, force to surrender' saw Yarmouk, Damascus, sealed off in 2013 with 18,000 civilians trapped thereImage: UNRWA via AP/picture alliance Over the past decade, there have been conflict-related famines in Nigeria, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria and Yemen. Food security experts suggest Russian attacks on Ukraine's agricultural sector could also be seen as criminal attempts to weaponize food. Basically there's just more of this war crime happening again, they argue. Even while global food security is improving, the incidence of famines is increasing, Alex de Waal, a professor at Tufts University in the US and head of the WPF's research into mass starvation, wrote last week. This tells us that the global food security is more volatile and unequal. That's consistent with hunger being used as a weapon. The deliberate withholding of food or other essentials needed for civilians' survival is categorized as a war crime by many nations as well as in various iterations of international law, including the Geneva Conventions and the Rome Statute (which is applied by the International Criminal Court, or ICC). But so far, those who wield that weapon have never been brought to trial: The war crime of starvation has never been prosecuted in an international court on its own, only as a part of around 20 other war crimes cases. And just because civilians are going hungry in a conflict, doesn't mean a crime was committed. One of the issues in law is the question of intent, de Waal told DW. The war crime of starvation requires that the perpetrator is acting with intent. Starvation was not always classified as a war crime: Nazi Germany's siege of Leningrad, which resulted in hundreds of thousands dying from starvation between 1941 and 1942, was considered a legal tacticImage: akg-images/picture alliance Starvation happens over the longer term, de Waal points out, and some legal scholars have argued it must be proven that a perpetrator intended to starve people from the very beginning of, for example, a siege or blockade. But most legal experts believe there could also be indirect intent, de Waal explains. That is, it's clear that starvation will occur in the normal course of events, and the perpetrator knows that, they've had opportunities to prevent it, but didn't do so. Another issue for any legal case involving starvation is the lack of precedent, and which international or national courts have jurisdiction over the alleged war criminals. Changing views on starvation as war crime Up until a couple of years ago, starvation was often seen as a developmental or humanitarian issue, GRC's Blumenthal explains. But now there is more attention being paid to its criminal aspects. I've worked on this issue for quite a few years now and these things do move slowly, concedes Blumenthal, who's been looking at the topic since 2020. But I do think the needle is moving and there have been some consequential steps taken over the past 10 years. Starvation as a war crime has occasionally been in national courts: In Croatia in 1997, officers of the former Yugoslav People’s Army were tried in absentia for the siege of the city of ZadarImage: Gepa/AP Photo/picture alliance In 2018, the UN Security Council unanimously passed Resolution 2417, condemning the starving of civilians as a method of warfare. In 2019, changes were made to the Rome Statute, making starvation a war crime in non-international armed conflicts too, rather than just international. There have also been UN commissions of inquiry on conflicts in South Sudan and Ethiopia-Tigray specifically focusing on the topic of starvation as a war crime, Blumenthal points out. We're seeing a lot more international and local organizations, together with accountability mechanisms, calling this out and certain striking examples, like the case of Gaza today, have really amplified awareness around the crime as well, she notes. In fact, the ICC warrants issued against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Israeli defense minister Yoav Gallant in November 2024, which specifically mention the war crime of starvation, are a historic milestone, Blumenthal notes. It's the first time that international warrants have been issued for starvation as a stand-alone crime. The ICC also has an open investigation into Sudan going, she adds. The issue has undoubtedly gained more attention over the last 10 years, de Waal confirms. The legal frameworks are all in place. What's lacking is the political will to act. In Gaza, desperation grows as food supplies dwindleTo view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Will perpetrators of starvation ever end up in court? There are still jurisdictional challenges, de Waal told DW. But I am confident that there are many cases for which conviction is possible. It just requires getting the accused in court. Blumenthal agrees. There are misconceptions around this and so many people think [starvation] is an inevitable part of war, she says. But during our in-depth investigations, it's surprising how quickly it becomes clear that actually these patterns are very stark and in many situations, you can discern a deliberate strategy. Blumenthal is cautiously optimistic that one day soon those who deliberately starve civilians will face justice. That is certainly the hope, she concludes. That's what we are all working towards. full_text: What you need to know about Kenyan protester's shooting PoliticsKenyaWhat you need to know about Kenyan protester's shootingMartina Schwikowski06/18/2025June 18, 2025The shooting in one of Nairobi's busiest streets outraged many Kenyans who have long witnessed officers abusing protesters and bystanders. Human rights groups are concerned about the rising lawlessness in Kenya.https://p.dw.com/p/4w8BuYoung Kenyans have borne the brunt of brutality by police forces in large cities like NairobiImage: Brian Inganga/AP/picture allianceAdvertisementWhat happened? In Nairobi's business district, small groups of protesters gathered on Tuesday, initially peacefully, to call for an end to police brutality. But according to media reports, they were quickly attacked by hundreds of men on motorbikes armed with makeshift weapons, known in Kenya as goons. Nairobi: Police, protesters clash in second week of unrestTo view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Police vehicles and officers appeared as vendors hastily packed up their stalls. One of the officers pointed his gun in the direction of protesters, then ran with a colleague to a vendor named Jonah Kariuki. The officers pushed the man. As he is shoved and is moving away, Kariuki glances back. The officer raises his weapon and shoots 22-year-old Kariuki at close range in the head — who crumples to the sidewalk. After the shooting, the officer and his colleague walk away. Police's reaction to the shooting Police did not directly deny any cooperation with the armed goons, releasing a statement saying it does not condone such unlawful groupings. Police also said the officer who shot Kariuki in the head using an anti-riot shotgun had been arrested. Activists called for the officer to be charged. The judiciary in a statement on Wednesday said it was committed to uphold justice in all cases, including those involving alleged police brutality. Nairobi: Pro-government counter-protesters clash with a protester during a protest over the death of Kenyan blogger Albert Ojwang in police custodyImage: Thomas Mukoya/REUTERS A wave of protests Tensions were already high in the East African country as it marks a year since massive Gen Z-led protests over the economy. Kenyan government's latest finance bill avoided the tax hikes that sparked weeks of protests in mid-2024. Rights groups say over 60 people were killed and dozens more were illegally detained by security forces in the aftermath. The protests peaked when thousands stormed parliament on June 25, 2024 when lawmakers debated the unpopular finance bill. The bill is now expected to take effect on July 1, 2025. But demonstrations picked up again over the death of 31-year-old teacher and blogger Albert Ojwang, who died in police custody earlier this month. Protesters want a senior officer they blame for the death to resign. A protester scuffles with police during the recent protests in downtown NairobiImage: Andrew Kasuku/AP Photo/picture alliance History of state violence Kenya has a history of politicians using armed mobs. Earlier this year, President William Ruto was accused of paying goons to follow his cavalcade around a tour of Nairobi to prevent protests. Ruto adamantly denied paying any mobs after the tour was cut short amid widespread violence and robberies against bystanders. Rights groups concerned We are turning into a lawless country, Ndungi Githuku, of civil rights group Kongamano La Mapinduzi, told AFP at Tuesday's protest. We see hundreds of paid goons, with whips and weapons, crude weapons, coming to brutalize our people. Despite reforms to improve the relationship between police and citizens, human rights activists say police have not managed to transform their image from an authoritarian force to one that serves Kenyan citizens within a democracy.The wave of protestes of young Kenyans in Nairobi's streets against police brutality continues Image: Simon Maina/AFP/Getty Images Edited by: Cai Nebe Martina Schwikowski Author for the Africa deskSend us your feedbackYour feedbackAdvertisement

full_text: Bulgaria's female 'Andrew Tate' incites anti-women violence SocietyBulgariaBulgaria's female 'Andrew Tate' incites anti-women violenceMina Kirkova in Sofia06/13/2025June 13, 2025Zornitsa Gyutsova is a Bulgarian influencer whose misogynistic online content has sparked outrage in Bulgaria. Why is there a market for her content in the Balkan country and how are some Bulgarians fighting it?https://p.dw.com/p/4vrvKOn her social media profiles, Bulgarian influencer Zornitsa Gyutsova posts misogynistic advice about how men should 'deal with' womenImage: Zgyutsova/TikTokAdvertisement Women love men who can be violent if need be. That's why they like men who hit them, Bulgarian influencer Zornitsa Gyutsova tells her followers. Gyutsova suggests that not only do women prefer men who physically assault them, but that this is also the way men should behave because a woman should respect a man's physical power since she is unable to comprehend his intellectual power. This is the kind of advice that can be found on Gyutsova's social media profiles and in a private group founded by her on Telegram called Upstanding Man. 'Equality is contrary to human nature' Zornitsa Gyutsova offers her followers private chats over video where she teaches them how to deal with women — for a fee, of course. Many influencers, life coaches and other online personalities in Bulgaria and elsewhere offer private sessions or courses. What makes Gyutsova's content stand out from the rest is that its sole purpose is to explain to men that they need to learn to control their partners both psychologically and, if necessary, physically.There have been numerous protests against violence against women in Bulgaria in recent years, such as this one in 2023Image: Alexandar Detev/DW In Gyutsova's view, men in general have been treated badly by women, and women are the ones who exert violence on men, namely by not paying them enough respect. The idea of equality is like a worm in people's brains that insists men and women should be partners […] which is so contrary to human nature that it can never work, Gyutsova declared in a long video about her work that was broadcast on Bulgarian National Television. Although the broadcaster, which is partly financed by taxpayer's money, has since removed the video from its platforms, it has never publicly commented on the case. Huge backlash Gyutsova's profiles on social media have been gaining traction for several years now. Screenshots and videos from her private Telegram group chat recently surfaced on social media, triggering a huge backlash in Bulgaria. Local woman Petya Krasteva was so appalled by Gyutsova's online content that she filed a complaint against Gyutsova with the prosecutor's office. On her social media channels, she not only encourages people to degrade women and use violence against them, she also boasts that she uses the same methods on her child and her cat, she told DW. I thought to myself: This is not only absolutely unacceptable, it's criminal. Gender discrimination not a crime in Bulgaria Many other women did the same as Krasteva, only to find out a couple of weeks later that their efforts had been in vain.Petya Krasteva was appalled by Zornitsa Gyutsova's online content and filed a complaint against her with the prosecutor's officeImage: Nikola Gyulmezov In an official reply, the prosecutor's office stated that nothing could be done because Bulgaria's criminal code does not define gender discrimination as a crime and that the issue was a matter for the Commission against Discrimination. Krasteva promptly lodged a complaint with this commission, but received another negative answer based on the same reasoning. Profiles briefly taken down Although these complaints did not lead to charges being brought against Gyutsova, the backlash did have an impact. The outcry and the fact that Gyutsova's social media accounts were reported by people who found their content abhorrent, meant that the influencer's TikTok and Instagram profiles were deactivated. They were, however, reactivated a short time later. Impunity for abusers Krasteva feels that part of the reason why content like Gyutsova's strikes a chord in Bulgaria is that while patriarchal norms and domestic violence are not accepted in the country, Bulgarian society often turns a blind eye to them. The other huge problem, she says, is that as with many other social issues, there is a complete lack of consequences for the perpetrators. Valentina Dimitrova, a psychologist who works for the Emprove Foundation, a Bulgarian organization that supports women who have suffered domestic violence, holds a similar view.Psychologist Valentina Dimitrova says that content like Gyutsova's is dangerous because 'it can truly cost a human life'Image: Venera Velkovska Sadly it's embedded in the Bulgarian mindset that we often just accept that things are bad and we do nothing about it, says Dimitrova. She believes that this is also why many women stay in violent relationships: They simply have no faith in the authorities because time and time again, men who beat or even kill their partners face no legal consequences. Although some people seem to think that social media content is less problematic than actual abuse in real life, Dimitrova stresses the dangers associated with such content: It can truly cost a human life. A global online problem Misogynistic online content that paints women as lesser human beings and men as oppressed by women is not unique to Bulgaria. Such content has been growing and spreading all over the world in recent years. Influencers like Andrew Tate, who faces charges of rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and more, have created a whole movement around this sort of content. Gyutsova fits neatly into this category of influencer, but what makes her different is that she is a woman. What role does feminism play? Dimitrova thinks one issue here is that feminism is often misunderstood. Feminism does not entail men being suppressed and women controlling them. It means that women can have equal rights and can function as equals to men not only in society but also in their personal relationships, she says. Dimitrova also believes that the patriarchal notion that men should not be allowed to express emotions is highly problematic. This is reflected in Gyutsova's content, which suggests that men are weak and not manly if they dare to express their fears, emotions or feelings.People in Sofia attend a protest against domestic violence and violence against women in Bulgaria in 2023 after a young woman was stabbed by her ex-partner Image: Alexandar Detev/DW It's a vicious circle: Men who are not allowed to express any sort of emotion for fear of being labeled weak don't know what to do when they experience something frustrating in their relationships and so they resort to aggression, says Dimitrova. What can be done? Dimitrova suggests that first and foremost, men should receive support and their concerns should not just be swept under the carpet. She stresses, however, that this support should not validate the inclination to deal with problems by exerting psychological or physical violence on women. Although the Emprove Foundation focuses primarily on women's rights and issues, it does have a project that focuses on men's mental health — something the foundation says is incredibly important in the fight against gender-based violence. Men should be encouraged to connect to a healthy understanding of themselves, so they can build healthy relationships as well, says Dimitrova. Petya Krasteva firmly believes that even though authorities in Bulgaria rarely provide the support needed in cases like this, society should not remain indifferent. We should be as loud as possible when something like this turns up, she says. We should be perfectly clear that it is unacceptable. That way, other people who come across this content will know that this is not something that society approves of, and that could help them realize that they shouldn't have anything to do with it. Dimitrova agrees. We will keep talking about it [this kind of content], calling it out and not tolerating it until the authorities wake up. headline: Pune Crime Files: How cops traced engineering student Bhagyashree Sude’s killers from a ransom message

where: Harangul; Viman Nagar; Pune; Hindi; Mumbai; Nanded; Kamargaon; Ahilyanagar
when: 22-year-old; March 30 last year; fourth-year; around 9 pm; March 30, 2024; April 2; The same day; 21; two years; March 28; 23; the day; March 30; April 7; his school days; 120B
full_text: Pune Crime Files: How cops traced engineering student Bhagyashree Sude’s killers from a ransom message Fulfilling a promise made by Devendra Fadnavis, who was the home minister of Maharashtra at the time, senior lawyer and Rajya Sabha MP Ujjwal Nikam recently appeared before a Pune court for a hearing in the Bhagyashree Sude murder case. The 22-year-old engineering student was allegedly murdered by three youths, including her college friend, on March 30 last year. The state government has appointed Nikam as the Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) in the case. Bhagyashree goes missing A native of Harangul village in Maharashtra’s Latur district, Bhagyashree was a fourth-year student of BE (Computer Science) at GH Raisoni College in Pune’s Wagholi and resided at Sakore Nagar. As per police records, she went to Phoenix Mall in Viman Nagar around 9 pm on March 30, 2024. Bhagyashree had told her mother that she was going to a friend’s birthday party, but went missing soon after, the police said. On failing to contact Bhagyashree, her parents came to Pune and lodged a missing-person report at Viman Nagar police station on April 2. The same day, her mother received a ransom message from Bhagyashree’s mobile phone: “Allah Hafiz Sude family. Stop searching for Bhagyashree. We have kidnapped her. We have sent her to a foreign country.” The message, which was in Hindi, directed Bhagyashree’s parents to transfer Rs 9 lakh to her bank account for her release and threatened to throw pieces of her body in her native village if the police were informed. Investigators later said the message was meant to “divert” their attention and make her family and the police believe that she was still alive. Meanwhile, Bhagyashree’s father Suryakant Sude, a former sarpanch, lodged a First Information Report (FIR) of kidnapping under section 364 (a) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). A technical investigation confirmed that the ransom message to Bhagyashree’s parents was sent from Mumbai’s Jogeshwari area. A police team went to Mumbai, but could not trace the accused. As the probe into Bhagyashree’s mobile phone calls and bank account continued, the police zeroed in on Shivam Madhav Fulawale, 21, a student of BE (IT) at her college. Officers said Bhagyashree knew Fulawale, a native of Nanded, for two years as they were in the same college and belonged to the Marathwada region. They used to talk to each other and she had even met him on March 28, the police said. Based on clues obtained during the investigation, investigators arrested Fulawale from Wagholi for his alleged role in Bhagyashree’s murder. Subsequently, his aides Suresh Shivaji Indure, 23, and Sagar Ramesh Jadhav, 23, were also arrested. A mall visit and a pit dug the day before The probe revealed that Bhagyashree went with Fulawale on March 30 when he came to Phoenix Mall in a rented car along with his friends Suresh and Sagar. The police suspect that Fulawale may have offered to drop her near her room but the three men allegedly choked her to death in the car. Officers said the accused allegedly took her body to a secluded spot at Kamargaon village in Ahilyanagar district. They suspect the men burnt her body with petrol before burying her. The police recovered Bhagyashree’s body from the spot on April 7. Referring to the pit in which Bhagyashree was found buried, an officer said the accused had dug it the day before committing the crime, suggesting that her murder was a premeditated and well-planned act. The accused had hired a car on rent to commit the crime. The police said they went to Mumbai and Nanded after the murder before returning to Pune and giving the car back to the service provider. The vehicle was subsequently seized for investigation. Plan hatched after ‘losses in share market, gaming’ The police said Suresh, who has a diploma in IT and worked in Mumbai, knew Fulawale as both hail from the same district. Fulawale knew Sagar, a Class 10 pass, since his school days. The accused were charged under Indian Penal Code (IPC) sections 302 (murder), 120B (criminal conspiracy), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence), 404 (dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person), and 34 (common intention). As the police began probing the motive behind the murder, it came to light that the suspects had become debt-ridden after losing their money in the share market and to online gaming. So they allegedly hatched a conspiracy to kidnap Bhagyashree and extort money from her family. Officers, however, suspect that she may have been murdered because of her attempts to resist them. Sarjerao Kumbhar, Senior Police Inspector, said, “The accused committed the crime for money. There was no sexual assault on the victim. The accused had no previous criminal record. Technical investigation helped us in solving the case.” After the murder triggered outrage, Fadnavis, who was then the deputy chief minister and home minister of the state at the time, visited Bhagyashree’s family and said he would personally request advocate Ujjwal Nikam to be the SPP in the case. A police officer who was part of the investigation said a chargesheet has been filed against the three accused who are currently in jail. The case is on before a court in Pune.

headline: UK to use AI to predict theft, knife attacks and violent crimes by 2030
who: John; Tom Cruise; Peter Kylethe; Geolitica
where: UK; AI; United Kingdom; England; Wales; Los Angeles; Chicago; Netherlands
how: predict theft, knife attacks and violent
full_text: UK to use AI to predict theft, knife attacks and violent crimes by 2030 Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining the way we do things, but none of it reflects the dystopian worlds we see in movies and TV series. However, that may soon change as the United Kingdom government now wants to use the technology to create interactive crime maps that will help “predict where offences are most likely to occur.” The announcement sounds straight out of the popular dystopian science fiction thriller Minority Report, where John (Tom Cruise) works with the PreCrime police to stop crimes before they occur using three “PreCogs”, who can foresee crimes. In a press release, the UK government said the Technology Secretary Peter Kylethe, the detailed real-time interactive crime map will span across England and Wales and will help “detect, track and predict where devastating knife crime is likely to occur or spot anti-social behaviour early on” to give the police a head start and intel ahead of dangerous situations. Part of the Safer Streets Mission, the AI-powered, real-time interactive crime map is aimed at tackling crime in urban areas. The UK government will be making an initial investment of £4 million for the prototype model, which is expected to come out in April 2026. Under the £500 million R&D Missions Accelerator Programme, the UK government wants a fully functional system by 2030. Designed to focus on crimes that “make people unsafe” in their own neighbourhoods from theft, anti-social behaviour, knife crime and violent crime, the system will help aggregate data shared between police, councils and social services by analysing “previous incident locations and studying the patterns of known offenders.” The map will help the police officers identify areas where the crime rate is high and deploy resources as added to prevent future crimes. The use of AI might sound like science fiction, but similar initiatives in other parts of the world have had mixed results. For example, predictive policing tools used in Los Angeles and Chicago were decommissioned after they were accused of racial bias and had limited success. Another predictive software project named Geolitica (previously called PredPol) was discontinued in 2020, after its effectiveness was cited as uncertain. However, the Crime Anticipation System (CAS), a project in the Netherlands, has seen modest success in terms of burglary rates. The Danish police have also successfully used AI systems to help with fraud investigations.

full_text: Three knifed to death for trying to stop drunk men from ransacking dhaba Three men who tried to stop a group of drunk men from ransacking a dhaba in Chhattisgarh’s Dhamtari district were stabbed to death late Monday night. The incident took place outside Annapurna Dhaba in Bhoyna village, around 78 kilometres from the state capital Raipur. “A group was ransacking the place, throwing tables around in an inebriated condition. The men, Alok Singh Thakur, Nitin Tandi and Suresh Hiyal, and their friends were having food,” said a police official from Arjuni police station. “The men tried to stop the group, but the accused attacked them with a knife. The prime accused, identified as Gopi Diwan (20), was carrying the weapon, and he allegedly stabbed the three men. One of the victims tried to run away but was chased and attacked by Diwan. All three died on the spot. Once police received information, we swung into action and caught all the suspects. We also seized the murder weapon,” the official said. “Eight persons, including three minors, were detained after the incident. The five adults, including Diwan, have been arrested and sent to judicial custody. We are finding out if they have a prior criminal record,” said Superintendent of Police, Dhamtari, Suraj Singh. The three minors have been sent to a correctional home. Police have invoked sections of murder and unlawful assembly of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

full_text: Karnataka woman chopped into 19 pieces; son-in-law among 3 held for murder Four days after the body parts of a woman were found dumped in several locations in Chimpuganahalli in Karnataka’s Tumakuru district, the police on Monday arrested three people, including her son-in-law, a dentist, for the murder. The police identified the deceased as Lakshmi Devi, 42, a resident of Bellavi village, and the accused as Dr Ramachandraiah S, 47, Satish K N, 38, and Kiran K S, 32, all residents of Kallahalli. Ramachandraiah is married to Devi’s daughter, Tejasvi, 26, the police said, adding that this was his second marriage. According to the police, on August 3, Devi left her home to see her daughter. A day later, her husband, Basavaraj, lodged a missing person’s complaint at Bellavi police station. Three days later, on August 7, the police were alerted about 19 body parts being found at various places in Chimpuganahalli. The body parts were found inside bags that were disposed of at no fewer than 19 locations, the police said. The Koratagere police registered a murder case and sent a message to all police stations in the district to check if any missing person complaints had been filed. It was then that the Bellavi police informed Basavaraj, who identified the body as Devi’s. According to the police, CCTV footage showed that a Maruti Suzuki Brezza was used to dump the body parts. The vehicle was allegedly registered in the name of Satish. “We took custody of Satish, and he spilled the beans. Satish and Kiran were taken into custody from Hornad. Ramachandraiah was in Dharmasthala after the murder and was not available for questioning. This also raised our suspicion,” a police officer said. Ramachandraiah allegedly claimed that his wife was listening to her mother’s advice and causing trouble in their marriage, Ashok K V, Superintendent of Police (SP), Tumakuru district, said. “He was unhappy over his mother-in-law’s interference. His first marriage is still in the divorce stage. In 2019, he married Tejasvi,” SP Ashok added. “We are yet to know why the accused cut her body into pieces and threw it at different locations. We have produced them before the court and will take them to police custody for further questioning. The car gave us the major lead to crack the case,” he said. According to the police, Satish was one of Ramachandraiah’s patients and stayed near his house. Kiran was Satish’s cousin, the police added. SP Ashok denied reports that the murder was linked to human sacrifice.

Adhikari, a former Trinamool Block President from Nalhati in Birbhum and once under the CBI and ED scanner in the teachers’ recruitment scam, was picked up along with his son and four others for allegedly running the “International Police & Crime Investigation Bureau” in Noida’s Sector 70 on Saturday night. Police said the group allegedly posed as government officials to extort money. Investigations by Kolkata police revealed that in Kolkata’s Beleghata area, Adhikari had allegedly rented two flats on CIT Road where he displayed boards reading “Investigation of Social Justice”, “Interpol” and “Police”. He would allegedly arrive in a car with a blue beacon with four armed guards. Police claimed he owns significant assets, including an Ayurvedic college in Suri, a B.Ed college in Krishnapur, and houses in Kolkata and Delhi. Adhikari was removed from his Trinamool post before the 2021 elections, later forming the “Bhartiya Arya Samaj” party. However, he was seen sharing the stage with TMC leaders in 2024 and was accused of taking money in exchange for job promises in the teachers’ recruitment scam. Sources said he was considered close to jailed former Education Minister Partha Chatterjee. His Krishnapur ashram housed an office using the letterhead of the “National Bureau of Social Investigation and Social Justice.” The CBI questioned him multiple times in 2023 in the recruitment case. headline: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver

full_text: Pune Crime Files: How offering a ride to 4 strangers turned fatal for Nashik cab driver Around 7.30 on January 27, Rajesh Baburao Gaikwad, 56, a resident of Nashik who worked as a rental cab driver, called his wife Aruna on her phone. He had taken a trip from Nashik to Pune around 5 am that day. He told her he would reach home around 7.30 pm. That was the last conversation Aruna had with her husband. Repeated calls made to him were unanswered. Around 10.30 pm that night, Gailkwad’s wife got a call that his phone had been found on the Alephata Santwadi road off the Pune-Nashik highway. The caller had kept the phone at a nearby hotel, from where he had made the call. Around 2.30 am on January 28, the Gaikwad family reached the hotel and searched for him in the area where the phone was found. However, Gaikwad and his car could not be traced. The family registered a missing person case at Alephata police station under the Pune Rural police. At around 9.30 am on January 28, while police were actively searching for Gaikwad, his body was discovered in the Santwadi area. His hands were bound behind his back with a nylon rope and a zip tie, and initial autopsy findings indicated that he had been strangled. The murder investigation was taken up jointly by teams from the Alephata police station and the Pune Rural police’s Local Crime Branch. As part of the investigation, the police reviewed footage from dozens of CCTV cameras on the approach routes to the area. A significant breakthrough came when Gaikwad’s vehicle was spotted on a hotel’s CCTV camera along the Nashik–Pune highway corridor. By piecing together video evidence from multiple locations, investigators traced the car’s movement—first heading toward the area where his body was later discovered, then continuing in the direction of Malshej Ghat. Both the footage and ground inquiries indicated that, at one stage, four people were inside the car along with Gaikwad. Meanwhile, a team which was on the lookout for the car found it abandoned in Kasara Ghat, along the route to Nashik. Continued analysis of CCTV footage helped police identify suspects who were captured travelling in the vehicle. Over the following three days, till January 31, investigators arrested three suspects: Vishal Ananda Chavan, 22; Mayur Vijay Solse, 23; and Ruturaj Vijay Sonavane, 21, all residents of the Gangapur Road area in Nashik. The investigation to arrest the fourth suspect continues even now. Driver resisted carjacking attempt, say police Investigators found out that the suspects had boarded Gaikwad’s car during his return journey to Nashik from Pune. They used the pretext of hitching a ride, but wanted to hijack the vehicle, said the police. The sequence of events, as brought out by the investigation, was that they allegedly strangled him after he resisted their attempt. The group then disposed of his body and fled the scene, said the police. It was soon revealed that the trio are hardened criminals. They allegedly intended to use the hijacked car for an armed robbery in which they wanted to target a shop in Nashik. The police said they, however, decided to abandon it on the way since they thought the vehicle would be flagged in the murder investigation after Gaikwad’s body was found. Solse and Chavan are facing charges of murder registered at Gangapur police station in Nashik in 2022. As the police continued their probe, they found out that these suspects were involved in a case of carjacking at Chakan police station registered in 2024, which had remained unsolved till the time the murder case was cracked. “The chargesheet in the case was filed subsequently. All three accused are currently in prison under judicial custody. A coordinated search for the fourth accused continued. The wanted suspect in the case also has multiple offences registered against him,” said an officer who was part of the probe. The case underscores the dangers faced by drivers who pick up unknown passengers outside their assigned duties. Authorities have reiterated their warning against this practice, noting that similar incidents of passengers turning violent have been reported in the past. headline: Gurgaon man masturbates in front of woman waiting for cab, police file FIR
who: Krishan Kumar
where: Gurgaon; Jaipur

full_text: Gurgaon man masturbates in front of woman waiting for cab, police file FIR The Gurgaon police on August 5 registered a case against a man who was caught on camera allegedly masturbating in front of a young woman near Rajiv Chowk in the city, officers said on Thursday. According to the police, the incident took place on August 2 when the complainant, a model and digital content creator, was waiting for a cab around noon at a busy junction to head home after a journey from Jaipur. Krishan Kumar, Station House Officer, Civil Lines Police Station, said that the police have filed a First Information Report (FIR) under sections 75(2) for sexual harassment and 78 for stalking of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. “The investigation is underway, and the complainant has also joined the probe, and we have recorded her statement. We are scanning CCTV footage in and around the spot and talking to people in the area.” On the same day of the incident, the model narrated her ordeal on social media and posted the video of the alleged act of the perpetrator, while also blaming the police for the delay in registering a complaint. “Something very strange happened to me. A man came around, circling, and he was constantly staring at me. Initially, I just ignored it, like the others do,” she said. She noticed that the man with unzipped pants was allegedly masturbating. The video showed the man wearing a facemask and a backpack that he had slung over his chest to cover the act from being too visible to the public nearby. The woman said it was clear he was ‘very aware’ of what he was doing. The woman in her video also lamented how cab companies were delaying in accepting her ride request, aggravating her ordeal. The complainant stated that although she had initially got a ride booked, the driver was not picking up despite multiple calls, and hence she had to re-book across applications “just to avoid the creep”. Eventually, a cab arrived and she reached home. In the video, she also alleged initial inaction from the police after she had tagged the police and other government authorities while putting the man’s video on X, and later calling the police helpline. “There wasn’t even an automated message,” she said. Regarding the FIR, the model said, the police had asked her to come to the station instead of lodging the complaint online. “It was making me feel very uncomfortable. I felt very, very disgusted. Initially, I froze. I did not record or hit him. People who say I could have shouted at him do not understand what goes through a girl’s mind at that moment. Reactions go viral faster than the real truth, and people judge; they do not help.” The woman stated she wanted to be safe rather than have the moment become viral. “I am not making the video for any kind of attention, just want to be heard,” she said in the video.

full_text: 'Sophisticated fraudster' behind cancelled Victorian bushfire charity event Victorian charity CEO with new identity previously charged with deceptionBy Mikaela Ortolan and ABC News VerifyStatelineTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pmFounder of Disaster Recovery Army Inc, Jay Brady, served time in prison for fraud-related offences under another name. (ABC News: Shane Willner-Browne)In short:A man who presided over a controversial fundraiser for bushfire-affected communities previously went by another name, under which he was convicted of multiple crimes of deception.The bushfire recovery event was cancelled earlier this year when community members raised concerns about the legitimacy of the charity behind the event.Charity founder Jay Brady did not deny the past convictions but declined to answer specific questions. He maintains the charity is legitimate.abc.net.au/news/jay-brady-jason-palankay-deception-charges-bushfire-recovery/105610002Link copiedShareShare articleA Victorian man who attempted to organise a charity event for bushfire-affected communities has a history of committing crimes of deception under a different name dating back decades, the ABC can reveal.Earlier this year, a charity event to support bushfire-affected communities in Victoria's west was called off amid community concern over the way it had been organised. Jay Brady founded and headed up the registered charity, Disaster Recovery Army Inc, which was behind the Recover Grampians event.The event was due to take place in March — after a summer of devastating fires in the Grampians National Park — but its site was taken down and a GoFundMe page that had raised almost $16,000 was closed when local businesses started questioning the event and its legitimacy. The webpage for the Recover Grampians event, which was taken down after the local community raised concerns. (Supplied)An ABC investigation has found Mr Brady previously went by the name Jason Palankay, under which he had been convicted of numerous deception-related offences and served time in prison, according to court documents.In 2011, while facing court over several charges of obtaining property by deception, he was described by a judge as an artful, skilful and sophisticated fraudster .While considering his sentence, the judge said Palankay was a persistent offender who has not been deterred by previous sentences . When contacted by the ABC, Mr Brady did not deny the past convictions but said he would not divulge personal details and could not answer specific questions because of legal proceedings. He said he changed his surname from Palankay a long time ago for personal family reasons .A psychological report submitted to the courts during the 2011 matter said Palankay met the criteria for Narcissistic Personality Disorder and displayed a grandiose sense of self-importance .A number of residential properties were destroyed in the Grampians bushfires. (Supplied: David Grimble )Businesses suffer almost $180,000 in lossesCourt documents show Palankay was convicted of deception offences at the Melbourne Magistrates' Court as early as 1998 after writing cheques that could not be honoured. He was convicted for similar offences the following year and then again in 2002, according to the same material.He was again convicted over a matter involving bouncing cheques in 2005, the documents show.The same documents also reference another charge in South Australia. They suggest Palankay served time in prison in that state, but the ABC was unable to obtain further details.The ABC compared a still from a TV interview with Jay Brady (left) and an image from a 2016 newspaper article that identified Jason Palankay (right). (WIN News/Leader Newspapers: Stuart Milligan)In 2007, Palankay turned to fraudulently obtaining vehicles and profiting from their sale, costing impacted businesses nearly $180,000, a court heard. During this time, he worked as an independent contractor for LeaseMasters — a salary packaging specialist offering novated leasing, which is a way to pay for a car and its running costs directly through a person's salary.Do you know more about this story?Contact Mikaela Ortolan at ortolan.mikaela@abc.net.au. If you're sharing sensitive information, read our tips on how to contact us confidentially.Court documents say Palankay requested a quote for a vehicle and gave falsified purchase orders to the car retailer on a number of occasions, despite not being authorised to do so.Palankay obtained the vehicles by falsely representing that finances had been approved . According to court documents, he would then use the vehicles as security to obtain loans.Court documents say Palankay would then sell the vehicle, using some of the money to pay off the loans and pocketing any profit. After his engagement with LeaseMasters was terminated, court documents say he continued contacting car dealers and obtaining vehicles while falsely representing that [he was] operating a genuine business known as Fleet Development .He purchased several cars in this way over a nine-month period, the documents say.Palankay sentenced to prisonPalankay was convicted of one count of using a false document and five counts of obtaining property by deception in relation to the vehicles in 2011.It was submitted to the court that Palankay undertook this fraudulent activity to pay back debts to the Australian Tax Office of more than $110,000 at the time of offending.However, in sentencing, County Court judge Mark Taft said none of the proceeds from the cars you sold made their way to the ATO and I find the account you proffer as utterly implausible . In the course of committing the frauds on car dealers you displayed a high level of cunning, the judge said. Your level of intelligence increases the risk you represent to the public. Palankay had initially pleaded guilty to the charges, but weeks before his sentencing, he sought to change his plea after claiming he had been improperly induced to plead guilty by statements from the judge. The change of plea application was dismissed by the County Court Chief Judge. Mr Brady was photographed leaving a court in Bendigo over a separate matter, in which he was the complainant, earlier this year. (ABC News: Emile Pavlich)During his sentencing remarks, Judge Taft said Palankay's guilty pleas were not accompanied by any remorse whatsoever and you do not have a skerrick of insight into your wrongdoing . He was sentenced to three years and 10 months in prison with a non-parole period of two-and-a-half years.He was also sentenced to nine months in prison in 2019 after pleading guilty to unrelated charges of obtaining property by deception. In that case, he was ordered to undertake a 12 month community correction order upon his release. A psychological report tendered to court during a hearing for the car-related crimes, authored by Aaron Cunningham and dated November 2011, stated Palankay said he had previously been diagnosed with delusions of grandeur .In the report, Dr Cunningham expressed the opinion that Palankay met the criteria for Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD). Mr Palankay's NPD is evident by his grandiose sense of self-importance, preoccupation with fantasies of unlimited success, belief that he [is] special and unique, need for excessive admiration, sense of entitlement, interpersonally exploitative and lack of empathy, Dr Cunningham said in his report submitted to the court. When asked about this Mr Brady said, I certainly do not have a diagnosis of delusions of grandeur or NPD .Bushfire event won't go aheadIn 2008, Palankay filed for bankruptcy.At some stage he began using the name Jay Brady. The ABC is not aware of any criminal convictions since his name change.Mr Brady registered the charity Disaster Recovery Army Inc in March 2024 and after devastating bushfires in the Grampians over two summers, he began advertising charity work and calling on volunteers.The event's website once advertised tickets but Mr Brady previously told the ABC none were sold.He also previously said the sum raised through GoFundMe was used for equipment hire, vehicles, rent and other charity operational expenses.Mr Brady previously told the ABC no tickets to the event were sold. (ABC News)Community members who held concerns about the fundraising event said businesses had not been consulted despite its website at one point claiming it had 100-plus local business supporters.Earlier this year, the Northern Grampians Shire Council said Mr Brady had expressed interest in registering the event but had not completed the registration process. The ABC has also confirmed at least one image on the charity's website — purporting to show a volunteer — appears on other social media profiles and blog posts unrelated to the charity, where the person photographed has a different name. A photo of a woman on the charity's website (left) appears on other websites unrelated to Mr Brady's charity (right). (ABC News)The ABC put a series of detailed questions to Mr Brady about his past offending, his name change and the bushfire recovery event. In a written response earlier this month, he said he could not answer questions about his past offending because of legal proceedings underway . In relation to the name change, he said for personal family reasons, my surname was changed to Brady a long time ago as I do not have a relationship with my birth father .He maintains the charity is legitimate but said there is no intention to hold a Recover Grampians event at a later date , despite earlier suggesting it would be rescheduled. My term with the charity concludes shortly, so it will be up to any future board and management to canvass that, Mr Brady said. [Any] insinuation also that I have deceived or utilised funds associated with the charity are also false. Clearly, anecdotes have been taken out of context and/or used to create a narrative that doesn’t accurately reflect the charity’s, or my own, intentions to serve the communities we do. The ABC previously spoke with an employee at Disaster Recovery Army Inc who said volunteers had carried out work including trimming and removing dead bushes, fixing containment fences and removing burnt fences. The employee said they were legally doing work with the intention of helping people in disaster-affected communities.Victoria Police said no complainants had come forward and no offences had been identified in relation to the charity event.How the ABC uncovered a second identity:A search of the Disaster Recovery Army Inc's listed phone number led the ABC to a defunct website Jay Brady used to campaign for local councillor. The ABN linked to that website was different to the ABN the charity was registered under.A subsequent search of the campaign website ABN identified Jason Palankay as an entity name alongside Jay Brady and one other name. The ABC carried out a number of other searches as part of its investigation. One search found company records for both Jason Palankay and Jay Brady that listed the same home address.An article published in the Herald Sun in 2016 contained a photograph of Jason Palankay after he participated in an interview, and that image was compared against a still from a TV interview with Jay Brady.The ABC attended a court hearing in Bendigo in June where Jay Brady appeared as the complainant, and was able to confirm a visual match with a photograph of Jason Palankey in a Leader Newspapers article.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pmFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pmFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:08pm, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:45pmFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 9:45pmFri 22 Aug 2025 at 9:45pmShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Convicted bucks party gang rapists argue guilty verdicts 'unsafe' Sydney men jailed over bucks party gang rape in Newcastle argue guilty verdicts 'unsafe'GBy Giselle WakatamaABC NewcastleTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amComposite Andrew David and Maurice Hawell outside court after their lengthy gang rape trial in 2024. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)In short: Three men jailed over gang rapes in Newcastle are appealing, arguing guilty verdicts were unsafe.Their barristers have argued witnesses were unreliable and have questions directions given to the jury by the presiding judge.What's next?The appellant judges have reserved their decision. abc.net.au/news/convicted-gang-rapists-argue-guilty-verdicts-unsafe-on-appeal/105687344Link copiedShareShare articleLegal teams for a group of men jailed for gang raping three women in Newcastle have argued their guilty verdicts were an unsafe and unsatisfactory verdict , and witnesses were unreliable.Last year brothers Maurice Hawell, 31, and Marius Hawell, 24, and friend Andrew David, 31, were convicted of multiple counts of aggravated sexual assault and aggravated sexual touching in company.The trio's lawyers have spent the past two days challenging the men's convictions and sentences in the Court of Criminal Appeal.An argument around an unsafe verdict alleges the jury's guilty verdict was unsatisfactory and should be overturned.The offences occurred during a bucks weekend in February 2022.The men had travelled to Newcastle and stayed in an Airbnb for the weekend.Two of the women were 18 at the time and the third was 19.'Callous and degrading'In sentencing, Justice Gina O'Rourke said the men engaged in a pack mentality and treated the women in a cold, callous, degrading and criminal way .Maurice Hawell was sentenced to 14 years in prison with a non-parole period of eight years and six months.Maurice Hawell is one of the men appealing his conviction and sentence. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)Andrew David was sentenced to 13 years in prison with a non-parole period of seven years and nine months.Marius Hawell was sentenced to nine years in prison with a non-parole period of five years and five months.The appealThe three men appealed on the grounds the verdicts were unsafe and victims unreliable.The men's barristers also claimed the jury could have been led to misinterpret their state of mind during the bucks weekend.The appellant judges are Justices Stephen Free, Peter Hamill and Belinda Rigg.Crown Prosecutor Bret Hatfield SC today elaborated on the claim about state of mind . The crown says state of mind exists over a 24-hour period and the men were looking for women in nightclubs, Mr Hatfield said.Mr Hatfield added there was a clear a break when the men went and had breakfast and went sightseeing in Newcastle.The court heard it was Andrew David's bucks party. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)The men's barristers also took aim at the credibility of witnesses on the Friday night and their understanding of consent.Mr Hatfield today told the judges there should not be expectations about how complainants in sexual assault matters should behave .'Inconsistencies'He said inconsistencies in their evidence largely relates to the number of people walking back to the apartment [where they were staying] and how many men were outside the room when they were being sexually assaulted. They have visceral and graphic detail that is hard to make up and embellish, Mr Hatfield said.He said that inconsistencies were relevant of course, but they were not significant .The presiding trial judge ruled against separate trials due to the context of the evidence.The men met two of the women at Newcastle's Cambridge Hotel. (Supplied: Vision Collective)Barristers for all three men rejected claims of a joint criminal enterprise raising concerns the jury was not given adequate directions about the concept.A joint criminal enterprise exists where two or more persons commit criminal activity and each is held to be criminally responsible for the acts of another.Justices Free, Hamill and Rigg reserved their decision.ABC Newcastle — local news in your inboxGet our local newsletter, delivered free each WednesdayEmail addressSubscribeYour information is being handled in accordance with the ABC Privacy Collection Statement.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:21amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Magistrate convicts police officer who punched teen during arrest Magistrate finds police officer assaulted teen during arrest in Batemans BayBy Christien de GarisABC South East NSWTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amBrett David Lindsay outside Batemans Bay Local Court. (ABC South East NSW: Christien De Garis)In short:A Senior Constable has been found guilty of using unreasonable force during the arrest of two teenage boys in Batemans Bay.Brett David Lindsay punched a 17-year-old boy during the arrest, with the magistrate finding the officer had no intention of de-escalating the situation .What's next?He was sentenced to two-year community correction order.abc.net.au/news/police-officer-assaulted-teen-batemans-bay-arrest-court-finds/105684886Link copiedShareShare articleA New South Wales police officer has been found guilty of assault and using an unreasonable amount of force during the arrest of two teenage boys in Batemans Bay.The case centred on the way Senior Constable Brett David Lindsay forced the then 14 and 17-year-old boys to the ground during the arrest in October 2023.Lindsay described using a distraction strike when he punched the older boy's collarbone.In Batemans Bay Local Court on Friday, Magistrate Doug Dick said he was satisfied the use of force was unnecessary. It was a use of force no reasonable officer would have used in the circumstances, he said.Investigating home invasionThe court heard Senior Constable Lindsay and his partner were investigating claims of a potential home invasion in Batemans Bay, which led them to a block of units where several teenagers were.Senior Constable Lindsay told the court they suspected the teenagers were involved in the alleged home invasion and arrested them.Over the two-day hearing, prosecutors pointed to body-worn camera footage which captured Senior Constable Lindsay grabbing the younger boy by his shoulders and throwing him onto a concrete floor.Brett David Lindsay's hearing took place in the Batemans Bay Local Court. (ABC News: James Tugwell)It also showed when a scuffle broke out between Senior Constable Lindsay and the 17-year-old, where the officer ended up on top of the teenager.Senior Constable Lindsay told the court the teenager tensed up, and he feared the boy was in reach of his gun and handcuffs, so he struck him on his collarbone area. I used what I would call a distraction strike … hopefully change [the teenager's] demeanour and direction it was heading, he said.The older teenager then repeatedly called the officer a white gronk and a f***ing dog .Giving evidence, the 17-year-old said: I didn't think a copper would hit me at that age. The court was told in another interaction, the police officer forced the 17-year-old to the ground, with his knee coming into contact with the teenager's stomach.Senior Constable Lindsay testified the teenager then clenched his fist.The Batemans Bay Senior Constable pleaded not guilty to six charges. (ABC News: James Tugwell)On the body-worn camera footage, the police officer can be heard saying to the teen: Do you want a f***ing punch mate, you'll get one. Magistrate rejects evidenceIn delivering his verdict, Magistrate Dick said it was clear [the 17-year-old] held ill feeling towards all police … [he] was deliberately confrontational and hostile .However, he went on to say he did not believe Senior Constable Lindsay's evidence that the officer genuinely believed he used necessary force. [Senior Constable Lindsay] had no intention of de-escalating the situation … [he] downplayed the seriousness of his conduct, Magistrate Dick said.Brett David Lindsay was given a community correction order. (ABC South East NSW: Christien De Garis)In sentencing, Senior Constable Lindsay's defence lawyer Ahmad Moutasallem revealed his client was suffering post-traumatic stress disorder and was on medical leave, as well as being suspended from the police force. He will not be working as a police officer anymore, Mr Moutasallem said.Magistrate Dick recorded a criminal conviction against the three assault charges and ordered Senior Constable Lindsay to serve a two-year community correction order.A NSW Police spokesperson confirmed Senior Constable Lindsay remained suspended with pay and a review would now be conducted.ABC South East NSW — local news in your inboxGet our local newsletter, delivered free each ThursdayEmail addressSubscribeYour information is being handled in accordance with the ABC Privacy Collection Statement.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:11amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Men charged over alleged plot to import 185 kg of methamphetamine into WA Perth men charged over alleged plot to import 185 kg of methamphetamine, attempt to steal $300kBy Nicolas PerpitchTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:05amAuthorities discovered 185 kilograms of meth hidden in bags of rice. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)In short:Police have charged a Perth man with trying to import 185 kilograms of methamphetamine into WA.The drugs were seized in bags of rice sent by sea from Pakistan.He and another Perth man have been charged over an alleged conspiracy to steal $300,000 in cash from two Victorians accused of trying to smuggle the money out of WA.abc.net.au/news/wa-perth-drug-cash-haul-/105686958Link copiedShareShare articleIt's a rare insight into Perth's violent organised criminal underworld.Authorities have lifted the lid on an operation that stopped 185 kilograms of methamphetamine hitting the streets and foiled a suspected plot by the alleged drug traffickers to also steal $300,000 in illicit cash off a Victorian man and woman in an armed highway heist.Police allege the Victorians were trying to smuggle the crime money out of Western Australia.In dramatic footage, officers can be seen pulling over a white van with suspects inside in the outer Perth suburb of Wooroloo on August 5. Show me your hands, put your hands out of the window now! One officer yells to the occupants as he approaches the car. Passenger, open the window! Hands out! Do not move! Do not move for anything, do you understand me? Loading...Police handcuff a man and pull him out of the van and onto the grass next to the road.An officer removes a loaded handgun from the front of the man's tracksuit pants.He takes the magazine out of the gun and puts it in an evidence bag.The video then shows officers searching the boot of a car and pulling out two vacuum sealed clear plastic bags from a hidden compartment, full of crisp $50 notes.Police allege the men involved had clear links to organised crime networks with international connections and outlaw motorcycle gangs.Operation Estevan was conducted by the WA Joint Organised Crime taskforce, involving the Australian Federal Police, WA Police, Australian Border Force, Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission and AUSTRAC.Information from the investigation yesterday led police to a home in the northern Perth suburb of Nollamara, where they arrested a man after finding a point-22 handgun, a sawn-off shotgun, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, knuckledusters, banned knives, methamphetamine, cannabis and other drugs.Significant discoveryThe operation started in December 2024, when authorities discovered 185 kilograms of meth hidden in bags of rice in a consignment sent by sea from Pakistan.That's the equivalent of 1.8 million street deals and would have been worth about $171 million to the criminal group.But AFP Assistant Commissioner Pryce Scanlan said the drug seizure has hurt the syndicate and left them potentially vulnerable. They obviously owe a lot of money potentially offshore. But this puts a big dent into organised crime, he said.A package containing methamphetamine which authorities will allege was found in a bag of rice. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)A 35-year-old man from the Perth suburb of Doubleview has subsequently been charged with importing a commercial quantity of methamphetamine, a charge that carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment.He's due in the Perth Magistrates court next week.Police then received intelligence tipping them off to what they call a threat to life .'Highway robbery'Police allege the Doubleview man and a 35-year-old man from the Perth suburb of Gwelup hatched a plan to execute what we can only refer to as a highway robbery .WA Police assistant commissioner Tony Longhorn said their target was the Victorian man and woman allegedly trying to smuggle $300,000 in cash gained through crime out of the state in a car.The two Perth men had allegedly placed tracking devices on the Victorians' vehicle and knew exactly where they would be. It is alleged that the drug traffickers planned to stop the couriers on the highway at gunpoint and steal the cash, assistant commissioner Longhorn said. It wasn't going to take place in a dark back street. This was going to be open air. Midday. With the community at risk. And we all know how this could have gone if it had gone wrong. Police say the meth haul had a value of about $171 million. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)Police allege one of the men had a loaded handgun when he was arrested.The two Perth men have been charged with one count each of conspiracy to commit an indictable offence, unlawful possession of a firearm, and one count of possessing money from the proceeds of crime.The two Victorians were charged with the same offence.WA 'hostile' to organised crimeAFP assistant commissioner Scanlan said it showed the links between illicit drugs and violent crime. These people are the ones who are preying on our children, your friends, your neighbours, trying to get them hooked onto these insidious drugs and turn them into people you do not recognise, he said. People who will rob, lie, steal and cheat. We're making WA as hostile as possible, and make sure drugs aren't coming through our borders. The 41-year-old man was arrested in bushland in Perth. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)In other recent operations, earlier this month a 41-year-old Coffin Cheaters Outlaw motorcycle gang member and a 34-year-old associate were charged after they were caught allegedly collecting 30 kilograms of methamphetamine in tea packaging from Perth bushland.Police say they were arrested after a lengthy foot chase, and they seized a hessian bag from one man allegedly containing a shovel, night vision goggles and a dedicated encrypted communications device.The 34 year old man was arrested after a lengthy police pursuit. (Supplied: Australian Federal Police)Police also seized 15 kilograms of methamphetamine hidden in wooden furniture that arrived in Fremantle from South Africa earlier this year, with a street value close to $14 million.A Sydney man, who had flown to Perth the day before, has been charged with one count of importing a commercial quantity of border-controlled drugs.LoadingPosted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:05amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 8:05amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 8:05amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: 'Sorry and sordid tale': WA GP jailed for child sex offences WA GP Douglas William McCarthy jailed for child sex offencesDBy David WeberTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03amDouglas McCarthy was sentenced for a range of sexual offences against teenage girls. (ABC News: Dave Weber)In short: Douglas William McCarthy, 63, who was a practising GP when he paid underage girls for sex has been sentenced to 20 years in jail. Judge Wendy Gillan rejected his evidence that he did not know the ages of most of the girls and said he should have known better given his age, intelligence and education.What's next? He'll be eligible for parole after 18 years.abc.net.au/news/wa-gp-douglas-william-mccarthy-sentenced-for-child-sex-/105686986Link copiedShareShare articleA West Australian doctor who paid tens of thousands of dollars to teenage girls for sex and photos, and kept a video library of his offending, has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.WARNING: This article contains details some readers may find distressing.Douglas William McCarthy, 63, was a practising GP in the state's south west, when he engaged in sexual acts with girls aged 14 and 15.McCarthy was found guilty by a WA District Court jury last week of a range of offences, including persistent sexual conduct and sexual penetration, possessing child pornography, and encouraging a 17-year-old to engage in prostitution.He was also found guilty of attempting to pervert the course of justice after paying some of his victims to keep quiet , including depositing $800 into one of the girls' bank accounts.If you or anyone you know needs help:1800 RESPECT national helpline on 1800 737 732Sexual Assault Counselling Australia on 1800 211 028Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors) on 1800 272 831Blue Knot Foundation on 1300 657 380Lifeline (24 hour crisis line) on 131 114'Sordid and sorry tale'In a scathing sentencing hearing, District Judge Wendy Gillan said McCarthy was only interested in his own selfish desires and described his offending over more than two years as a sorry and sordid tale .Judge Gillan said McCarthy, whose sexual involvement with the girls started when he was aged in his late fifties, engaged in a high level of corruption and should have known better given his age, intelligence and education.Douglas McCarthy has been jailed for 20 years. (ABC News: David Weber)She rejected his evidence that he didn't know the ages of most of the girls. Their true age was not an impediment to you, she said, pointing out that they were intoxicated during the sexual acts.One girl was 14 when she first posed for photos and sent them to McCarthy after being told by a friend that he would pay for them.This led to her going to see him and being paid for sexual acts, in what was a familiar pattern for other victims.In other incidents, he recorded videos of the offending, many of which the judge said were degrading .Judge Gillan said he'd allowed teenage girls to drink alcohol, take MDMA and smoke marijuana in his presence, including at his home. Your house was a party house where young people were able to use drugs with impunity. Victim impact statementsThe court heard that five of the teenagers had provided victim impact statements, with one saying McCarthy had stolen her innocence and she had been made to feel like a cheap prostitute .Another said she now found it difficult to trust older men and to speak with doctors.McCarthy's lawyer Wayne Burg referred to a letter his client had provided for the judge, saying he now believed the girls are blameless and he takes responsibility for his actions .But prosecutor Sean Stocks said last week those girls weren't blameless , telling the court that there was no remorse, just manipulation .Prosecutor Sean Stocks said McCarthy was not remorseful. (ABC News: David Weber)Mr Stocks said he had groomed vulnerable children and took advantage of them using his apparent wealth , and kept an extensive video library for his own interests. They've all clearly suffered , Mr Stocks told the court. The person he was to his family and friends was not the person he was. The judge said she couldn't accept he was remorseful.McCarthy was found guilty of 14 charges including child sex offences and attempting to pervert the course of justice, after a jury trial.The jury was forced to watch hours of graphic and disturbing footage filmed by McCarthy of him sexually abusing the teenagers, with the court hearing he had kept an extensive video library of his offending.During his trial, he'd pleaded guilty to four charges of sexual penetration.He'll be eligible for parole after 18 years.LoadingPosted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:03am, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:16amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 7:16amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:16amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Podcaster faces murder charge over death of 30yo Perth woman Tobias Marcus Nuttall faces Perth court charged with murder of woman in BassendeanKBy Kenith PngTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 7:00amTobias Nuttall has been charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Bassendean. (YouTube)In short:A Perth conspiracy podcaster, Tobias Marcus Nuttall, has been charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Bassendean.He appeared briefly in Midland Magistrates Court, speaking only to confirm his name, and will remain in custody until a September court date.Police say the woman was found critically injured at a Reid Street home on Wednesday, later dying in hospital as homicide detectives continue investigating.abc.net.au/news/tobias-marcus-nuttall-faces-court-charged-with-bassendean-murder/105684606Link copiedShareShare articleA conspiracy theorist podcaster has appeared in court charged with murder over the death of a 30-year-old woman in Perth's eastern suburbs.Tobias Marcus Nuttall, 32, appeared in the Midland Magistrates court today in custody, wearing a blue jumpsuit, with a beard and long hair.Mr Nuttall is accused of killing the woman, who is believed to be known to him, in Bassendean on Wednesday.The scene was cordoned off by police as they investigated the woman's death. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)In court, Mr Nuttall did not speak, other than to confirm his name.No further information was given by prosecutors, and Mr Nuttall will remain in custody ahead of his next court appearance in September.The WA Police Homicide Squad are investigating the woman's death, after emergency crews rushed to a house on Reid Street just after midday, finding a woman who had sustained critical injuries.Police were called to the house on Reid Street on Wednesday afternoon. (ABC News: Lily Kristanto)She was rushed to Royal Perth Hospital where she died.Deep dive podcastMr Nuttall co-hosts an online podcast which is branded as a deep dive into the realms of conspiracy, the occult, magic, spirituality, and everything clandestine. As two inquisitive minds on a quest for truth, they pull back the curtains of the mundane to reveal a world bubbling with mysteries, hidden agendas, and esoteric knowledge, the podcast description says.Tobias Nuttall appearing on a podcast. (YouTube)On an episode posted on Wednesday night, after the alleged murder took place, Mr Nuttall's co-host excused his absence. There's nothing wrong with Toby, his co-host said.The 32-year-old was a co-host of a podcast that had last posted an episode on the day of the alleged murder. (YouTube) Toby had an appointment he had to come over to Sydney for and he was flying back from Sydney to Perth today. This is just to tell everybody we won't be doing one with Toby tonight, we'll have to do that tomorrow. Mr Nuttall was charged with murder the following evening.The charges were referenced by the co-host in a later episode.“Toby has been charged …. with a very very serious offence over in Perth, something that happened on Wednesday, the co-host said.Supporters of Tobias Marcus Nuttall outside the Midland Magistrates Court on Friday.
