full_text: Illicit tobacco, money laundering funding Victorian burglaries, arsons Seizure of $7.2 million worth of illicit tobacco is linked to an alleged Iraqi crime syndicateTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amPolice intercepted a truck in Laverton North allegedly carrying $5 million of illicit tobacco. (Supplied: Victoria Police)abc.net.au/news/two-men-arrested-seven-million-dollars-illicit-tobacco/105686114Link copiedShareShare articleVictorian police say the seizure of $7.2 million worth of illicit tobacco is linked to an alleged Iraqi crime syndicate that is laundering money and using it to fund serious offending like aggravated burglaries.Police said they became aware an organised crime syndicate was conducting cash drops and collections at a small takeaway shop in Somerton, in Melbourne's north, in January. They also said further transactions were taking place at a factory in Epping. On Thursday Victoria Police, along with the Australian Border Force, executed warrants at two homes in Dallas and a business in Epping, where they seized $1.9 million worth of illicit tobacco, $80,000 in cash and six high-end watches. A 40-year-old Dallas man was arrested and is expected to be charged with possession of a commercial quantity of illicit tobacco and knowingly dealing with the proceeds of crime.Police believe over $83 million of cash has been laundered since May 2021.Victoria Police said as part of a separate investigation they intercepted a truck carrying $5 million of illegal cigarettes in Laverton North.The alleged driver, a 34-year-old Cambellfield man, was arrested at his home on Thursday, where detectives seized $100,000 in cash.Police said they believed the man attended the same Somerton shop linked to the money laundering investigation, and has alleged links to the organised crime syndicate involved. 'Vast number of crimes' can be committed with millions of dollarsDetective Inspector Graham Banks from Victoria Police said the seizures were significant. This group is connected to Iraqi organised crime entities, and they're funnelling money offshore to people who are directing very serious crimes in Victoria and the rest of Australia, he said.Detective Inspector Banks said to put the money into context, $1 million could buy a criminal syndicate 400 stolen cars. A million dollars will pay for 100 arsonists, a million dollars will buy you about 40 semi-automatic pistols with rounds, or if you prefer 20 assault rifles, he said. A million dollars will probably pay for two underworld hits of mid-level underworld characters, sometimes it goes up to $1 million. So there's $4 million, and there's a vast number of crimes that can committed with that money. But it doesn't speak to the money behind the crime, or the houses that have been broken into and the hundreds of people who have been victims of aggravated home invasions, or the large number of businesses that have had their businesses destroyed who aren't even related to the illicit tobacco trade. Syndicates using apps to hire criminalsDetective Inspector Banks said the crimes were organised on encrypted apps like Signal and WhatsApp. And people take up contracts, sometimes very small in monetary value, to do very serious offending, he said.Detective Inspector Graham Banks says criminals are being hired using encrypted apps. (ABC News)He said the amount of money that had been generated by the illicit tobacco trade was really staggering , and it was equal to, or more than, the drug trade.Detective Inspector Banks said there were one or two syndicates driving it. They will be the focus [of police]. They are the people who are killing people, they are the people organising arsons and they people who are organising aggravated burglaries which are impacting all members of the community, he said.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:00amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: 'Blind drunk' driver jailed for 14 years over hit and run death of 43yo mum Drunk driver Brett Eddy imprisoned for 14 years over manslaughter of Fraser Coast woman Natasha RavenBy Talissa SigantoTopic:CrimeFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51amNatasha Raven died after being struck by the vehicle Brett Eddy was driving. (Supplied)In short:Drunk driver Brett Eddy has been sentenced to 14 years' jail for the hit and run death of 43-year-old Natasha Raven last year.Ms Raven's family and friends told the Supreme Court in Brisbane of the pain they have been living with since her death.What's next?Eddy will be eligible for parole in 2033.abc.net.au/news/brett-eddy-imprisoned-for-manslaughter-drink-driver/105686842Link copiedShareShare articleA driver who was blind drunk and travelling at extreme speed when he killed a pedestrian in a hit and run on Queensland's Fraser Coast has been sentenced to 14 years in jail.Brett Eddy, 42, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane on Friday to several charges, including the manslaughter of Natasha Raven.The 43-year-old was struck by a car being driven by Eddy and left for dead on a Urangan street late at night in May last year. Eddy pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane on Friday. (Supplied)During a sentencing hearing, the court heard the day in question had been Eddy's birthday, and he had been drinking heavily throughout the day.The court heard at around 10pm, after being removed from a licensed venue, he drove to a friend's home who described him as being loud and obnoxious and blind drunk .He continued drinking, and around two hours later, the court heard he drove to a convenience store with a child, where staff said he was f*****g hammered .Court hears child filmed 'drunken joyride'Crown prosecutor Stephen Muir told the court Eddy then went on a drunken joyride , reaching speeds of up to 180 kilometres an hour through suburban streets. He should have been nowhere near behind the wheel of a car, he said.Mr Muir told the court Eddy reprehensibly then had the child film his dangerous driving, which was played to the court. That recording captures the defendant's obvious enjoyment in the moments before the killing, he said.The court heard at similar extreme speed he entered the shoulder of the road where Ms Raven was walking, just metres from her home, before he hit her and fled the scene.Ms Raven died at the scene of the crash. (ABC News)'Your actions are unforgivable'Ms Raven's brother Josh Raven submitted a victim impact statement to the court which was read by the prosecution.In his statement he said Eddy was a nightmare that lives in my head . The pain you've caused me is beyond anything I've already experienced, he said. Your actions are unforgivable. Mr Raven told the court the images, thoughts and smells from the crash scene will haunt me for the rest of my life . I hope this lives in your head for as long as you may live, he said to Eddy.Ms Raven's best friend Lauren Richards read her victim impact statement to the court.She said her death had left me with a pain I will carry for the rest of my life . Since she's been gone, I have been so alone, she said.Ms Richards told the court the death had taken the hardest toll on Ms Raven's son who is broken by grief and headed down the wrong path. Every day I watch him struggle and it tears me apart, she said. He feels lost without his Mum and he doesn't see much for his life ahead. Eddy appeared in court via video link on Friday. (ABC News: Curtis Rodda)Driver tells court 'I will never forgive myself'Appearing in court via video link from prison Eddy apologised to the Raven family and through tears said: I'll never forgive myself . I'm so sorry for this, I shouldn't have been on the road and it's my fault that this has happened, he said. I don't wish for anyone to forgive me, but I just want everyone to know that I am so sorry. The court heard Eddy had a lengthy criminal record across three states which spanned decades, and that he had a highly relevant traffic history of repeated unlicensed and drink driving offending.Justice Peter Davis took into consideration Eddy had entered into timely pleas and accepted other mitigating factors such as a PTSD diagnosis.However, when determining his sentence, he said Eddy exhibited “a high level of criminality” which caused Ms Raven, who was “innocent in all this” to lose her life in “violent circumstances”.“The nature of your driving was outrageously reckless,” he said.Eddy will be eligible for parole in 2033.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 5:51am, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:02amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 6:02amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 6:02amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Postal worker charged over alleged $1.4m fraud from stolen bank cards Postal worker charged over alleged $1.4m fraud from stolen bank cards in Sydney's eastBy Danuta KozakiTopic:PoliceFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amLuxury items including watches, handbags and jewellery were seized by police. (Supplied: NSW Police)In short: A 56-year-old postal worker is accused of stealing bank cards and other items from mail in Sydney's east.Police allege he supplied the stolen cards to two separate criminal syndicates, resulting in $1.4 million worth of fraud.Two other men were charged in connection and all three men are due before court next month.abc.net.au/news/nsw-sydney-postal-worker-charged-over-alleged-bank-fraud/105685680Link copiedShareShare articleA Sydney postman has been charged with the alleged mail theft of bank cards and other items in Sydney's east, resulting in $1.4 million worth of fraud.Police from the Financial Crimes Squad allege the 56-year-old postman supplied the stolen bank cards to two separate criminal syndicates.The postman allegedly stole items from 70 letters or packages in Edgecliff, Woollahra and Double Bay in the city's east, with police and Australia Post last November launching a joint investigation.Strike Force Detectives on Wednesday with help from NSW Police's organised crime squad Raptor executed five search warrants in Rockdale in Sydney's south and Roselands in the city's south west. During the warrants, police allegedly located and seized more than $14,000 in cash, a Dedicated Encrypted Criminal Communication Device, electronics, stolen bank cards, a taser, and luxury items including watches, handbags and jewellery, NSW Police said in a statement.56-year-old postman Mauro Coluzzi was then arrested in his home in Rockdale, along with two other men at separate locations.He was charged by police with 143 counts of dishonestly obtaining financial advantage by deception, stealing items from 70 pieces of mail, and participating in a criminal group.Police seized more than $14,000 in cash after executing five search warrants. (Supplied: NSW Police)The postman appeared before Sutherland Local Court on Thursday where he was granted conditional bail, including surrendering his passport.The other two men charged in connection with the alleged theft and fraud — 35-year-old Ashish Tamrakar from Rockdale and 27-year-old Ibrahim Abbas from Roselands — have also been granted bail.All three men are due before court next month.Alleged thefts reported by concerned banksNSW Financial Crimes Squad Commander, Detective Acting Superintendent Con Galea, said two of the three men were known to police previously. They were known to each other; they had an association from the time we were investigating them. Two of them — including the postman — were known to police. He said the alleged thefts were initially reported by the banks. The reporting happened in mid last year [2024] and several hundred customers have been affected. Acting Superintendent Galea said the criminal syndicates were allegedly involved in fraud. Basically, the criminal syndicates are focusing on fraud and deception related offences, obtaining those cards and perpetrating other frauds using those cards. Australia Post confirmed it has been supporting NSW Police in their investigation. (ABC South East NSW: Fatima Olumee)Police said the amount of money allegedly defrauded is expected to increase, as police investigate further cases from the alleged theft of the bank cards.In a statement, a spokesperson for Australia Post said more than 2.3 billion items are delivered through its network each year. Australia Post is proud of the role it plays in delivering for the community. This is a very serious matter and Australia Post has been supporting NSW Police in their investigation — and will continue to do so. Given the matter is before the Courts, it is not appropriate for us to comment further, Australia Post said.The ABC understands the postman has been suspended from his duties pending the investigation.Posted Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 4:56amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Leader of 'cult-like' UK Christian group guilty of sexually abusing women 'Cult-like' Christian group leader found guilty of sexually abusing multiple women in congregationTopic:CourtsFri 22 AugFriday 22 AugustFri 22 Aug 2025 at 12:24amChristopher Brain was the leader of the Nine O'Clock Service. (Supplied: South Yorkshire Police)In short: Christopher Brain, 68, was convicted of 17 indecent assault charges relating to nine women. He denied all 36 charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.What's next?Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said it would carefully consider a retrial since the jury could not reach a verdict on four counts of indecent assault and an alleged rape.abc.net.au/news/cult-like-christian-group-leader-found-guilty-of-sexual-abuse/105684554Link copiedShareShare articleA former Church of England priest in the UK has been found guilty of sexually abusing nine women in his congregation.Christopher Brain was the leader of a cult-like Christian group called the Nine O'Clock Service, based in Sheffield, northern England, in the 80s and 90s.The evangelical church movement was famous among young people for its 9pm services on Sundays that featured a live band. At its peak, it attracted hundreds of attendees.But, prosecutors said, Brain, 68, controlled members of the congregation, cutting them off from family and friends, and abused his position to sexually assault a staggering number of women .Brain also had a homebase team of young women dubbed the lycra nuns , prosecutor Tim Clark said. They looked after him, his wife and daughter at their house in Sheffield.He was charged with 36 counts of indecent assault and one count of rape relating to 13 women between 1981 and 1995. He denied the charges and said any sexual contact was consensual.After a trial at the Inner London Crown Court, Brain was convicted on Wednesday, local time, of 17 charges of indecent assault relating to nine women. He was acquitted of a further 15 counts.The jury was unable to reach a verdict on the remaining four counts of indecent assault and the alleged rape, Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said on Thursday, adding it would carefully consider a retrial.'Failing of the church'The Nine O'Clock Service had the blessing of the Church of England. Prosecutors said in 1990 that the Archbishop of Canterbury-elect, George Carey, had met Brain to discuss his methods.Brain's ordination was fast-tracked, and the Nine O'Clock Service spent large sums of money to obtain the outfit worn by actor Robert De Niro for the 1986 film The Mission for the ceremony, prosecutors said.But Brain resigned and left the church days before the broadcast of a 1995 BBC documentary, which accused him of sexually inappropriate behaviour. Mr Carey said he was crushed and let down when the allegations were made public.In his evidence, Brain said he received massages from members of the Nine O'Clock Service, which he said occasionally moved towards sexual activity. He also denied controlling or manipulating members of the congregation. What happened was an appalling abuse of power and leadership that should never have occurred, Bishop of Sheffield Pete Wilcox said in a statement. Where concerns were raised in the past and were not acted upon properly, that was a failing of the Church. For those institutional failures, I offer an unreserved apology. full_text: Man dead after stabbing on central Queensland coast Man dead after stabbing on central Queensland coastBy Jasmine Hines and Katrina BeavanABC CapricorniaTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 11:26pmPolice were called to Maida Street, Lammermoor, just after 7am. (ABC News: Niccola Way)In short:A man has died in Yeppoon this morning after being stabbed in the chest.Police have arrested a man and a woman, hours after the alleged offenders left the scene in a white utility.What's next?Forensic investigators are on site and police have launched a homicide investigation.abc.net.au/news/stabbing-death-central-queensland-coast-yeppoon/105684354Link copiedShareShare articlePolice have arrested a man and a woman after a 27-year-old man was fatally stabbed in Yeppoon, central Queensland, this morning.Authorities were called to Lammermoor just after 7am to reports of a man being wounded.He was treated for stab wounds to the chest, but died at the scene. It is alleged there was an altercation between the 27-year-old and another man at the address, and that they were known to each other. Detective Superintendent Darrin Shadlow alleged a man, aged 36, visited an address on Ganter Street in Yeppoon on Thursday night and assaulted two people. Police attended the residence at that time. However, no complaints were made, Detective Shadlow said.He said the man returned to the address this morning. An altercation has occurred, and he has chased the 27-year-old deceased from the residence through a backyard of a neighbouring property, to where, unfortunately, he received his fatal injuries, Detective Shadlow alleged.Neighbours say the street is typically quiet. (ABC News: Katrina Beavan)Police said the alleged offender left the scene in a white utility with a woman, before crashing it at Hamilton Creek near Mount Morgan, more than 80 kilometres away, around 10:45am. It is alleged the pair then abandoned the crashed ute before threatening another woman and taking her car.Police intercepted that car along Benaraby Road near Gladstone, south of Rockhampton, before taking the man, aged 36, and the woman, 20, into custody. The most dangerous aspect for the public was the manner of driving of this person, Detective Shadlow said.Detective Superintendent Darrin Shadlow addresses media in Rockhampton. (ABC Capricornia: Aaron Kelly)Neighbours tried to helpLocal woman Sue, who asked that her surname be withheld as she was yet to speak to police, said she found the victim on her front lawn and tried to save him with the help of other neighbours. We tried to resuscitate him until the ambulance arrived … we applied a lot of pressure and then we had to proceed with CPR, she said. It's pretty shocking and a bit surreal. It's very tragic. She described the street as quiet and close-knit. We have Christmas parties together, we enjoy each other's company, we look out for each other, she said. It's a really lovely neighbourhood, so this is really shocking and surprising. Police have arrested a 36-year-old man and a 20-year-old woman after a fatal stabbing in Yeppoon. full_text: Police chase 'a bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers', witness says Launceston man refused bail after low-speed chase in stolen truck driven on rimsBy Hayden SmithTopic:CourtsThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:23pmLoading...In short:A Newnham man has been refused bail after engaging Tasmania police in an hours-long pursuit in a stolen truck on Wednesday, at times while the truck's tyres were blown-out.A bystander has said the noise of metal on the road from the truck being driven on its wheel rims was pretty insane .What's next?Patrick Brown has pleaded guilty to dangerous driving charges and evade police.abc.net.au/news/launceston-man-pleads-guilty-after-stolen-truck-evade/105681218Link copiedShareShare articleA 27-year-old who pleaded guilty to driving a stolen truck on its rims through Launceston has been refused bail.Patrick Brown pleaded guilty to a number of charges in the Launceston Magistrate's Court on Thursday, including two counts of evading police and dangerous driving.The court heard Brown stole a white tipper truck on Tuesday, which he drove on the following night through some of the region's busiest streets, including the East Tamar Highway — at times veering onto the wrong side of the road and ignoring traffic lights.Loading...The court heard he continued for several hours after police spiked the tyres, with Brown then driving the truck on its rims.Numerous police units, including a helicopter, were involved in the truck's pursuit.Police say Brown, from the Launceston suburb of Newnham, was later arrested in Ravenswood without further incident .The driver led police on a chase despite driving on rims.Sound of 'metal on road': WitnessA Dilston resident who saw part of the pursuit said he was alerted to something happening when he heard a chopper hovering over . I went out to get a better view … and looked down John Lees Drive to see a convoy, he said. You had the truck at the front, police cars flanking and the chopper overhead. The noise was very loud. It was just metal on road [from the wheel rims] — pretty insane really. Dilston is 17 kilometres north-west of Ravenswood, where the driver was arrested.'A bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers'The white, tipper truck was stolen on Tuesday and involved in the chase the following day. (Supplied: Richard Morris)The witness described the scene as a slow-moving police chase with this helicopter and truck in no condition to evade police. He said it was a bit Fred Flintstone, a bit Blues Brothers . Normally it's a pretty quiet place, down there at Dilston. Appearing without legal representation on Thursday, Brown's bail application was denied by Magistrate Simon Brown.Brown also pleaded guilty to charges dating back more than 12 months, including multiple stealing offences and breaching bail.The dangerous driving charges were committed to the Supreme Court for sentencing on September 5.Posted Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:23pmThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 7:23pmThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:23pm, updated Fri 22 Aug 2025 at 2:56amFriday 22 Aug 2025 at 2:56amFri 22 Aug 2025 at 2:56amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Officer, elderly woman seriously injured in separate crashes involving police cars WA police officer, 80yo woman injured in separate crashes in Northam, SubiacoBy Kate ChristianTopic:PoliceThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52amA police officer was seriously injured in a crash near Northam, east of Perth. (ABC News)abc.net.au/news/several-injured-after-several-crashes-involving-police-vehicles/105682658Link copiedShareShare articleA police officer has been airlifted to hospital and an elderly woman has been left with serious injuries after two separate crashes involving police vehicles on Thursday.Commander Mike Peters said a marked police car was involved in a collision with a semi-trailer on the Great Eastern Highway near Northam in the Central Wheatbelt just before 11am.A second officer in the car is being treated for minor injuries, while the driver of the semi-trailer was not injured.The police car was involved in a collision with a semi-trailer. (ABC News)Around 20 minutes later at 11.15am, police were responding to reports of a person being armed with a gun when they were involved in a collision with another vehicle on Bagot Road in Subiaco. They were driving under emergency conditions when they collided with an 80-year-old lady turning into a driveway, Commander Peters said. As a result she has been taken to hospital with serious injuries. The officers were not injured. Commander Mike Peters said police did their best to protect the community. (ABC News) It is always confronting for us when we see one of our own officers injured, Commander Peters said. The police go out every day to do their absolute best to protect the community and it is unfortunate that these events happen and our hearts and minds go out to all people affected by this. Commander Peters said there was no further risk to the community as a result of the Subiaco incident, while a 23-year-old woman is assisting police with their inquiries.He said it was a stark reminder to the community about the inherent dangers of policing.LoadingPosted Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:52am, updated Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 8:08amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 8:08amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 8:08amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: 'Depraved and offensive': WA teacher jailed over multiple child sex offences WA teacher Harry Sing Wan Lagdon jailed after admitting 25 child sex offencesDBy David WeberTopic:CourtsThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38amHarry Lagdon was sentenced in the District Court of WA on Thursday. (ABC News: Jack Stevenson)In short:Teacher Harry Sing Wan Lagdon groomed a student when she was 15 and had sex with her on school grounds.He also engaged in online offending with three other girls, aged 12 and 13.What's next:Lagdon will be eligible for parole after five years and nine months.abc.net.au/news/wa-teacher-jailed-for-child-sex-offences/105681636Link copiedShareShare articleA WA teacher who groomed and had sex with a teenage student, then sent depraved online messages to even younger girls, has been sentenced to more than seven years in prison.Harry Sing Wan Lagdon, now 29, became sexually involved with the student when she was 15, and their encounters took place on the grounds of the regional high school where he taught and she was enrolled.Lagdon, who was nine years older than the victim, sent hundreds of videos and photos to her over 18 months. Basically, explicit material every other day, District Court Judge Matthew Curwood said.The court heard sexual encounters between them took place in a classroom, a closet and a shed on the school's property, inside his car and at his apartment.Harry Lagdon pleaded guilty to a string of child sex offences. (ABC News)'Breach of trust'It had all started with what the judge described as Lagdon's grooming behaviour , providing gifts to the teenager including a necklace.Support services:Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors): 1800 272 831Lifeline (24-hour Crisis Line): 131 114Victims of Crime Helpline: 1800 819 817Before long, the relief teacher was asking the girl for explicit photos, and sending images and videos of himself to her.The offending also included oral sex and indecent touching in various locations on school grounds, and sexual intercourse without a condom in his car and apartment.While Lagdon's lawyer described it as a consensual relationship , the judge said it represented a significant breach of trust and the victim had nightmares as a result.After he relocated from the regional school to Perth, Lagdon started communicating online with three girls in Queensland, aged 12 to 13, pretending he was a teenager.'Depraved and offensive'Lagdon sent hundreds of messages, some of which the judge described as depraved and offensive .The teacher asked for explicit images from the three girls and two of them complied.Judge Curwood told the court girls aged 12 to 13 were inherently vulnerable to online predators and the psychological impact is likely to be profound and long lasting .Lagdon had pleaded guilty to 25 charges, including sexual penetration of a child over 16 under his authority, exposing a child under 13 to indecent matter, procuring or encouraging a child to engage in sexual behaviour, and possessing child exploitation material.Lagdon also admitted to possessing child exploitation material. (AAP: Mick Tsikas)The judge acknowledged Lagdon's pleas in February had avoided the need for a trial.Lagdon's lawyer Mark Gunning had told the court his client's actions had been devastating for him and his shame was palpable .Mr Gunning said while the school student and Lagdon were infatuated with each other , it was totally inappropriate .He said his client acknowledged his teaching career was finished.Lagdon's total prison sentence of seven years was backdated to June 2024, with eligibility for parole after five years and nine months.The judge ordered that his mobile phone and laptop be destroyed.Loading...LoadingPosted Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:38am, updated Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:45amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 7:45amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 7:45amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Mental health condition considered in sentencing of teen girl shot by police Townsville teen girl shot by police released from detention for mental health treatmentBy Meghan DansieABC North QldTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 6:01amPolice were called to reports of a female armed with a knife making threats near Townsville's West End Hotel in June. (ABC News: Baz Ruddick)In short:A North Queensland magistrate has criticised Queensland Health in its handling of a teenage girl shot by police.She has been sentenced to 62 days imprisonment, already served.What's next?The now 18-year-old will be released from detention and transferred to hospital for further mental health assessment.abc.net.au/news/teen-girl-shot-by-police-released-for-mental-health-treatment/105680402Link copiedShareShare articleA North Queensland magistrate has criticised Queensland Health over its handling of a teenage girl shot by police.Warning: This story contains mention of suicide and self-harm.The teenager, who self-harmed more than 80 times while being held in youth detention, has been released by the court and sent to hospital for treatment.The now 18-year-old from Townsville was shot by police in June after they were called to reports of a female armed with a large knife making threats near Townsville's West End Hotel.The Ethical Standards Command investigated the Townsville shooting. (ABC News: Chloe Chomicki)Magistrate Viviana Keegan sentenced the woman, who was 17 at the time of the incident, to 62 days imprisonment, already served, for serious assault and obstruction of police.She will be released from Cleveland Youth Detention Centre today and transferred by ambulance to the Townsville University Hospital for further mental health assessment.If you or anyone you know needs help:Suicide Call Back Service on 1300 659 467Lifeline on 13 11 14Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander crisis support line 13YARN on 13 92 76Kids Helpline on 1800 551 800Beyond Blue on 1300 224 636Headspace on 1800 650 890ReachOut at au.reachout.comMensLine Australia on 1300 789 978QLife 1800 184 527The hearing in Townsville's Children's Court was told the teenager had been treated for numerous diagnosed mental health conditions since she was 14.Magistrate Keegan said during her time in custody the teenager was treated for 80 incidents of self-harm and had been admitted for emergency medical treatment 16 times. The criminal justice system can't manage [her], Magistrate Keegan said.She questioned why four suicide attempts, and being shot by police, had not resulted in an involuntary treatment order — which previously resulted in the refusal of a bail application. It's been sought on a number of occasions and on each occasion the clinical team has considered it not necessary, she said. It seems that is what is needed. Magistrate Viviana Keegan sentenced the now 18-year-old to 62 days imprisonment, already served. (ABC North Queensland: Rachael Merritt)Officers were called to the West End Hotel in Townsville at 5:30pm on June 10 after reports a female armed with a large knife was making threats.The court heard the teenager was shot by a police officer after she ignored numerous warnings while she advanced on them brandishing a knife.The Ethical Standards Command investigated the Townsville shooting.Due to the aggravating factor of the knife used in the assaults the magistrate said the teenager was being tried under adult crime, adult time laws passed by the Queensland government last year.She told the now 18-year-old, who appeared via video link from Cleveland Youth Detention Centre, to consider the impact of her actions and seek help moving forward. There are a lot of risks, Magistrate Keegan said. I hope you do as much as you can to engage with the mental health people. full_text: Police charge second man over Melbourne synagogue firebombing Police charge 20-year-old Meadow Heights man over Adass Israel Synagogue arson attackTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 5:55amLoading...In short:A 20-year-old man is facing three charges in relation to an alleged arson attack on a synagogue in Melbourne's south east.He is the second person to be charged over the firebombing.What's next:The man is expected to face court next week. abc.net.au/news/second-man-charged-adass-israel-synagogue-arson-ripponlea/105682132Link copiedShareShare articleCounter-terrorism police have charged a second man over the firebombing of the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne in December last year.The building in Ripponlea in Melbourne's south-east was gutted in a suspicious blaze in the early hours of Friday, December 6, sparking widespread condemnation.Australian Federal Police arrested a 20-year-old Meadow Heights man after carrying out a search warrant last week.A number of items were seized including electronic devices which police said are undergoing forensic examination. He was charged with arson, conduct endangering life and motor vehicle theft today.The Adass Israel Synagogue in Ripponlea was destroyed in the December 2024 attack. (Supplied: Sally Westwood)Australian Federal Police acting assistant commissioner Nick Read said the investigation has been one of the highest priorities for the counter-terrorism unit. I want to reassure the community — especially the Jewish community — that the AFP, together with Victoria Police and ASIO, are working relentlessly to bring this investigation to its conclusion, he said.Victoria Police assistant commissioner Tess Walsh urged the community to come forward with any new information. There is no place for this type of offending in our state, and we will be relentless in pursuing those who are prepared to engage in these acts of violence, she said.Two of three people charged over firebombingPolice allege the 20-year-old man is one of three people who broke into the Ripponlea synagogue and deliberately lit the fire. The Joint Counter Terrorism Team has now charged two of the three alleged offenders accused of directly setting the synagogue on fire, a police spokesperson said. He is due to appear before the Melbourne Magistrates' Court next week.In July, a 21-year-old Werribee man was also charged over his alleged role in breaking into and setting fire to the synagogue. Another man, 20, was charged for allegedly stealing a communal crime car, which police say was used to drive to the synagogue on the day of the attack.It is alleged the same vehicle was used in an arson attack two weeks earlier, on November 21, at LUX nightclub, south-east of Melbourne. Another man has also been charged over the nightclub fire. full_text: ATM supplier pulls machines amid money laundering concerns International ATM giant NCR Atleos begins removing machines from tobacco stores after ABC investigationBy Liam WalshABy Amy GreenbankBy Rory CallinanTopic:CrimeThu 21 AugThursday 21 AugustThu 21 Aug 2025 at 3:15amNCR Atleos has begun removing its Cashzone ATMs from stores. (ABC News: Liz Pickering)In short:One of the world's largest ATM suppliers will begin removing machines from tobacco stores across Australia.NCR Atleos's move follows an ABC investigation which revealed how private ATM suppliers were fuelling illegal tobacco and vape sales.Other large companies have also begun removing their machines from suspected illegal stores.abc.net.au/news/ncr-atleos-removing-machines-suspected-illegal-tobacco-stores/105680294Link copiedShareShare articleGiant international ATM supplier NCR Atleos will remove more than 50 machines from tobacco stores across Australia after an ABC investigation revealed how ATM companies were fuelling illegal tobacco and vape sales.The New York Stock Exchange-listed company, which boasts of having the world's largest ATM network, has reviewed its fleet following the revelations, including how private ATM companies had cut deals with local tobacco criminals.Some tobacco stores have relied on ATMs for cash sales of illicit products, and NCR's move means, in total, more than 100 machines from multiple suppliers are now being extracted.NCR's specifically includes machines that tobacco store owners can load with cash themselves — a feature that experts say raises potential money laundering fears due to a regulatory blind spot.NCR's Cashzone ATMs were found in stores selling illegal tobacco. (Supplied)Third company to make the moveThe $4 billion company's decision follows fellow ATM suppliers – Melbourne-based Next Payments, backed by prestigious investment bank Macquarie Group, and Queensland-based atm2go — which also began pulling their machines from stores linked to illicit tobacco sales.The fraudster, illicit smokes and an ATM giantPhoto shows Cash zone receipt with money in backgroundA New York Stock Exchange listed company is the latest to be found to have links to the illicit tobacco trade after an ABC investigation into how private ATM suppliers are oiling the industry.The ABC had found how those companies' machines and NCR's green Cashzone ATMs were in stores selling illicit tobacco and vapes in locations including Brisbane, Darwin and Sydney.One such store with a Cashzone ATM in Sydney was owned by a man already convicted on 15 counts of illicit tobacco sales; another illegal tobacco outlet in Brisbane was owned by a man once jailed for fraud.NCR declined to answer questions about due diligence conducted before placing its Cashzone machines in stores.Do you know more about this story? Email Callinan.Rory@abc.net.au or Walsh.Liam@abc.net.auBut a company spokesman told the ABC that following a review, we have chosen to remove a number of ATMs and will be removing self-filled ATMs in tobacco stores, which account for 1 per cent of our fleet . Additionally, we will continue to review this issue and will remove any ATMs from stores that we believe are linked to illegal tobacco trade. NCR has over 5,300 ATMs across Australia and complied with all applicable legislation , he said.Loading...Doron Goldbarsht, director of the Financial Integrity Hub at Macquarie University, said NCR's move to withdraw self-loading ATMs from tobacconists suggests recognition of the risks associated with the machines, particularly around traceability of funds . Because cash is filled directly by store owners rather than through a regulated provider, such ATMs may present heightened vulnerabilities to misuse, including for money laundering or to facilitate proceeds of crime, Dr Goldbarsht told the ABC.He said that NCR's move was positive and appeared a voluntary one. This should signal to both government and industry that current oversight may be insufficient, and that stronger regulatory settings or supervisory mechanisms could be needed to mitigate financial crime risks in the ATM sector, he said.Supplier Next Payments had already begun removing its machines from some stores. (ABC News: Liam Walsh)Money laundering concernsThe ABC has found examples of a man ultimately convicted of proceeds of crime and tobacco offences being able to load cash into Next Payments ATMs.Macquarie Group company's private ATM's fuelling illegal tobacco tradePhoto shows Next ATM in a closed tobacconist in BurpengaryAn ABC investigation finds that among investments raking in the dollars for the Australian-founded Macquarie Group is the nation's billion-dollar illegal tobacco trade.Court records also show a large Darwin cannabis supplier told an underling to load ATMs from atm2go with money from drug sales.Some parts of the private ATM industry, including Next Payments, have disputed whether money laundering could occur.But a concern is that private ATMs themselves are not captured by anti-money laundering laws, and that dirty money could be loaded into the machines.If an innocent person unwittingly withdraws that dirty money, that person's bank account ultimately credits the same amount cleanly into the private ATM cash-loader's bank account.The original source of the cash does not come under the same level of scrutiny that occurs if criminals try depositing certain amounts of cash in various ways directly into a bank.The ABC has found more than 20 stores selling illegal cigarettes with private ATMs inside, and at least five cases of ATM companies cutting deals with businesses tied to men either charged or convicted of offences including illicit tobacco sales.This Riverwood store was selling illegal cigarettes in Sydney this week. (Supplied)Sydney store selling $10 packs of cigarettesAnother example this week was a south-western Sydney store, the Riverwood News Agency and Tobacconist, selling illicit $10 packs of Double Happiness cigarettes.The store is registered to a company owned by Rui Chen, who did not answer requests for comment.Chen had been convicted and made headlines in 2020 for 15 tobacco sales breaches at the store.An example of the illegal cigarettes being sold for $10. (Supplied)He was hit with $4,250 in fines, and reports described authorities having seized 241 cartons and 386 packets of illegal cigarettes, and almost six kilograms of loose leaf chop-chop tobacco — the local area's largest-ever seizure at the time.NCR's Australian subsidiary had signed a deal with Chen's company for an ATM in the same store 10 months after he was convicted, mortgage records show.Unlike many other stores selling illicit tobacco, the Riverwood outlet this week was selling the cigarettes for the same cash price as an electronic payment.The ABC is not suggesting Chen was involved in money laundering.Posted Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 3:15amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 3:15amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 3:15am, updated Thu 21 Aug 2025 at 5:34amThursday 21 Aug 2025 at 5:34amThu 21 Aug 2025 at 5:34amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. full_text: Sunshine Coast childcare centre intruder on parole at time of death Sunshine Coast childcare centre intruder on parole at time of deathBy Madeline GraceABC Sunshine CoastTopic:PoliceWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:36amStaff acted quickly to hide six children as a man forced his way in. (ABC News: Madeline Grace)In short:Reubhan Mickeal Gary Ralph forced his way into a Sunshine Coast childcare centre, sending five staff and six children into lockdown, then died as a result of self-harm.He had faced Queensland courts multiple times for drug dealing, stalking and weapons offences.What's next?Police are investigating whether Ralph was in a drug psychosis at the time of his death.abc.net.au/news/sunshine-coast-childcare-intruder-lengthy-criminal-history/105677456Link copiedShareShare articleThe 28-year-old intruder at the centre of a Queensland childcare centre emergency had a lengthy criminal history, including charges for stalking, weapon offences and drug dealing.Reubhan Mickeal Gary Ralph was on parole when he died on Monday after smashing his way into the Habitat Early Learning childcare centre at Peregian Springs on the Sunshine Coast. It is understood he was armed, and police tasered him multiple times.Ralph was not known to any staff or families at the centre.Police are investigating whether he was in a drug psychosis at the time of his death.Police were called to Habitat Childcare Centre at Peregian Springs about 6pm on Monday. (Supplied)Attack at closing timeThe centre had five staff and six children inside and was winding down at 6pm, about 30 minutes before it was due to close.The staff heard Ralph's efforts to break in and swiftly moved to hide the children.The time it took him to smash through the centre's front glass doors was enough for them to alert police, who arrived to confront Ralph soon after.The offender was not known to any staff or families of the centre. (ABC News: Madeline Grace)They attempted to subdue Ralph, who was self-harming.Ralph died in the custody of police.History of drugs, crime, stalkingCourt documents chronicled Ralph's criminal history, starting in 2021, which included multiple drug offences.Since then, he faced court multiple times and was convicted for drug driving, speeding, drug trafficking, breaching bail, stalking, and carrying a knife in public.He spent five months in custody for the stalking offences.According to court documents, he was part of a syndicate which sold narcotics on the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast.The money he made was used to pay off his drug debts.Emergency services responded quickly after staff raised the alarm. (Supplied)Most recently, in May last year, Ralph pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court in Brisbane to possessing and selling drugs.He was convicted but had his three-and-a-half-year prison sentence wholly suspended and was put on probation for two-and-a-half years.Ralph was released on parole in June after breaching his bail conditions.Police acted 'extremely well'Queensland Police Union president Shane Prior said every officer at the scene acted bravely during the harrowing incident . One young constable used initiative and resourcefulness to enter the rear of the premises without the offender being aware and guided the children and carers to safety, he said. He has saved these kids from a potential lifetime of trauma. Every officer there stood between a violent intruder and innocent children. It's a selfless act police are prepared to do to keep the community safe. Dan Purdie says he has spoken with the responding officers. (ABC News: Lucas Hill)Police and Emergency Services Minister Daniel Purdie said he spoke with officers after the attack. They handled it extremely well and did whatever they could to protect the children and carers, Mr Purdie said. It really was a horrific incident for this tight-knit community. full_text: Man charged with assaulting police officer after arrest turns violent WA man charged with assaulting police officer after attempted arrest in MullewaBy Brianna MelvilleABC Midwest & WheatbeltTopic:PoliceWed 20 AugWednesday 20 AugustWed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amGeraldton detectives charged the 29-year-old man in relation to the incident. (ABC News: Sissy Reyes)In short:Two officers from Mullewa Police have been injured after an arrest turned violent.Police say Ronald James Gregory Merry repeatedly attacked the officers when they tried to arrest him over an alleged domestic assault.What's next?Mr Merry was remanded in custody and will face court again in October.abc.net.au/news/police-officers-assaulted-mullewa-wa-arrest/105676826Link copiedShareShare articleA police officer in WA's Midwest has been flown to Perth with serious facial fractures, and another officer injured, after the arrest of an alleged domestic abuser turned violent.Police said the officers were responding to a reported domestic violence incident in Mullewa, 450 kilometres north of Perth, on Tuesday afternoon when they were allegedly attacked by 29-year-old Ronald James Gregory Merry.Mr Merry, who faced Geraldton Magistrates Court on Wednesday, allegedly punched a 47-year-old woman, who reported the incident to police.In police body-worn camera footage played to the court, Mr Merry appeared agitated as the two officers questioned him about the alleged earlier assault. He could be heard telling officers, I'll grab your handcuffs and take you to jail, repeatedly calling them c*nts and telling them to go . Go now before I knock you out, he was heard saying in the footage. One police officer was taken from Mullewa to Geraldton for treatment at the hospital. (ABC Midwest and Wheatbelt: Chris Lewis)Violence caught on videoThe footage showed two officers tell Mr Merry he was under arrest, and attempt to pull him up by his arms. It showed Mr Merry then repeatedly punch the male officer in the face and head, knocking him to the ground and continuing to hit him.The footage then captured the officer's female colleague attempting to pepper spray Mr Merry, who began throwing punches at her.The 29-year-old then turned his attention back to the male officer, punching him several times in the head while the police officer remained on the ground.Ronald Merry faced the Geraldton Magistrates Court on Wednesday. (ABC News)The female officer then attempted to taser Mr Merry, who fled the scene and ran out of the house.Police located him several hours after the incident, charging him with a string of offences, including aggravated assault, escaping lawful custody and assaulting a public officer.The female officer was treated at the Mullewa Nursing Post, and the male officer was flown to Sir Charles Gairdner Hospital in Perth.Man allegedly drinking, using methamphetamineMagistrate Matthew Walton noted the male officer's injuries showed bruising and an apparently closed-over eye. Police alleged Mr Merry had been drinking and using methamphetamine the previous night.Defence counsel Matt Reen requested Mr Merry be released on bail, although he noted the prosecution's case was strong.Magistrate Walton denied bail, remarking the body-worn footage was clear and stark in supporting the alleged facts of the matter. He noted Mr Merry's history of breaching court orders, and the inevitability of an immediate term of imprisonment following a conviction. Mr Merry was remanded in custody and will return to court in October.ABC Midwest & Wheatbelt — local news in your inboxGet our local newsletter, delivered free each ThursdayEmail addressSubscribeYour information is being handled in accordance with the ABC Privacy Collection Statement.Posted Wed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amWednesday 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amWed 20 Aug 2025 at 7:31amShare optionsCopy linkFacebookX (formerly Twitter)Top StoriesMushroom murders 'robbed' Erin Patterson's children, estranged husband saysLIVEPhoto shows Erin Patterson Supreme CourtA thousand new homes sit empty across the country. who: Michael Woods; Dennis RomeroDennis Romero; Michael Kosnar; Alexandra Hess; Tangni Noriega; Jean Lee; Colin Sheeley

full_text: Colleges across the country deal with shooting hoaxes as classes resume U.S. newsColleges across the country deal with shooting hoaxes as classes resume From Kansas State University to Northern Arizona, students back on campus received alerts about violence in their midst that turned out to be fake threats. University of Arkansas students and employees evacuate and take shelter on Monday in Fayetteville, Ark., as police respond to reports of a shooting.Michael Woods / APAug. 25, 2025, 9:28 PM EDTBy Dennis RomeroAt least a half-dozen universities across the nation on Monday welcomed students to first-day-of-fall classes with run-and-hide warnings about possible gunmen on campus.In almost all the cases, police and administrators said the reports were hoaxes or swatting calls, which is when someone uses temporary cellphone numbers and voice-cloaking apps to create havoc. A few campuses said simply that no evidence of a gunman or violence was found.The reports were sent to students at the University of Arkansas, Colorado State University Boulder, Iowa State University, Kansas State University, University of New Hampshire and Northern Arizona University, according to student alerts and school statements.Additionally, according to campus officials, the University of South Carolina received two reports of an active shooter at Thomas Cooper Library in Columbia on Sunday night; the University of Tennessee-Chattanooga received a hoax active shooter call on Aug. 21; and Villanova University received two false active shooter reports during freshman orientation last week.Students at Villanova University were alerted to an active shooter situation on campus on Aug. 21 in Villanova, Pa.NBC PhiladelphiaThe University of Arkansas canceled classes Monday after determining reports of active threats could not be confirmed. Students are free to leave campus at this time if desired, university police said.Kansas State University described a false report Monday at its Manhattan campus as similar to other swatting reports happening at universities across the country. University of South Carolina police said in a statement Monday that both false reports from Sunday night appeared to be carried out by the same male and triggered a massive response that included mutual aid, or officers from surrounding communities. Both calls were initiated by an unknown male and included background noise that mimicked gunfire, police said.Northern Arizona University said in a statement that a caller reported a gunman Monday at Cline Library on its Flagstaff Mountain Campus, triggering a response that included Flagstaff police, Coconino County Sheriff's Office deputies and state and federal agents. The report was determined to be a hoax, and at no time was there an active threat to the NAU community, the university said in a statement. An investigation is underway into the false report, with assistance from the Federal Bureau of Investigation. An FBI spokesperson said the bureau was aware of many of the reported incidents and was helping with investigations. The FBI continues to work with state and local partners to investigate the swatting hoaxes but cannot say at this stage whether or not the incidents are connected, the bureau said.Some of the earliest swatting incidents from the 2010s involved false shooting reports at the homes of celebrities, and in recent years, they've expanded to include politicians and institutions. The FBI created a national database to track such fake calls.Last year, authorities alleged a California teenager carried out hundreds of swatting calls that targeted historically Black colleges, high schools, the homes of FBI agents, and a Florida mosque in a spree he ultimately admitted carrying out.Dennis RomeroDennis Romero is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.Michael Kosnar, Alexandra Hess, Tangni Noriega, Jean Lee and Colin Sheeley contributed.

full_text: Lil Nas X charged with 4 felonies after allegedly assaulting officers on L.A. street U.S. newsLil Nas X charged with 4 felonies after he's accused of assaulting officers while wandering naked on L.A. streetThe “Old Town Road” rapper, whose legal name is Montero Lamar Hill, charged at officers when they approached him early Thursday, authorities allege.Get more newsLiveonAug. 25, 2025, 1:49 PM EDT / Updated Aug. 25, 2025, 6:00 PM EDTBy Doha Madani and Lindsay GoodLil Nas X was charged with four felonies accusing him of injuring officers when he was found naked on Ventura Boulevard in Los Angeles last week, charges he pleaded not guilty to. Los Angeles police had said Lil Nas X, the “Old Town Road” rapper whose legal name is Montero Lamar Hill, charged at officers when they approached him early Thursday. Officers said they received reports of a nude man in the area.A law enforcement source alleged to NBC News last week that Hill punched an officer in the face twice and that it was unclear whether he was in mental distress or experiencing an overdose. Hill was taken to the hospital and accused of battery on a police officer.Court documents filed Monday in Los Angeles County Superior Court show Hill faces three counts of battery on a police officer and one count of resisting arrest. More details on the incident were not immediately available. TMZ first reported Thursday that Hill was hospitalized and obtained exclusive video of him walking the street in a pair of white briefs and cowboy boots. It later obtained video in which Hill was naked and barefoot.Hill was held in custody over the weekend and released on a conditional $75,000 bail after he appeared before a judge Monday morning. Attorney Christine O’Connor told the court that Hill has strong community ties and no criminal history and that he does not present a flight risk. There has been no evidence that any drugs were involved, O’Connor said. She said that test results may be pending but that nothing has been submitted into the record.Hill has led a remarkable life, O'Connor told the court. She cited his two Grammy awards in her address to the judge. Assuming the allegations here are true, this is an absolute aberration in this person's life, O’Connor said. Nothing like this has ever happened to him. A plea of not guilty was entered into the court record Monday, and a hearing was scheduled for Sept. 15. Hill is expected to attend four Narcotics Anonymous meetings a week or enroll in an outpatient narcotics program as a condition of his release. His father, Robert Stafford, said Hill is very remorseful for what happened. He’s going to get the help that he needs, and just keep him in your prayers, Stafford said. full_text: Miami-Dade deputy charged in UPS driver’s death claims Stand Your Ground Crime Miami-Dade deputy charged in UPS driver’s death claims Stand Your Ground By Charles Rabin Updated August 23, 2025 11:02 AM Defendant Jose Mateo with his lawyer Carlos Salazar argues Florida’s Stand-Your-Ground statute before Judge Ernest A. Kollra on Friday, Aug. 22, 2025. Mateo is one of four Miami-Dade police officers charged with manslaughter in the case stemming from the death of UPS driver Frank Ordonez, who was shot by police during a shootout with his kidnappers in Broward in 2019. (Mike Stocker/South Florida Sun Sentinel) Mike Stocker South Florida Sun Sentinel A police officer charged in the gunfire deaths of two innocent bystanders during a shootout at a busy intersection six years ago is taking a novel approach in a last-ditch effort to avoid trial: He wants the charges dropped based on Florida’s Stand Your Ground statute — even though he’s not charged with killing the suspected gunmen.Suspended Miami-Dade Sheriff’s deputy Jose Mateo, 33, who pleaded not guilty to manslaughter along with three other officers last year in the shooting death of a UPS truck driver and a man stuck in traffic, argued in Broward County Circuit Court Friday that he is protected by the state’s Stand Your Ground and fleeing felon laws and that the charges against him should be dismissed. His trial is scheduled to begin next week.The Stand Your Ground statute allows a person — and police officers — in Florida to take up to deadly action if they feel their life is threatened. The fleeing felon law allows police to shoot at a suspect if they believe that person is a danger to society while trying to avoid custody.The roughly 90-minute argument before Broward Circuit Court Judge Ernest Krolla Jr. came down to whether an officer should receive immunity under those statutes for the accidental killing of an innocent bystander. State prosecutor Chuck Morton, using an example of a civilian shooting at a would-be robber and accidentally killing someone taking a walk, said it should not. Morton said the self-defense argument only holds water if Mateo were charged in the shooting death of the two men accused of committing the crimes.“You need to be prudent when shooting into crowds,” said Morton, a Broward County assistant state attorney.Mateo’s attorney Richard Diaz argued the killing of an innocent bystander while police are shooting at someone firing in a crowd should get the same consideration of “transfer of intent” as a criminal being charged for the shooting death of someone by accident. He also told the judge, either way, his decision Monday would be “groundbreaking law.”“The Legislature never wrote into the statute whether it does apply, or doesn’t apply,” Diaz said. Richard Diaz, attorney for Jose Mateo, argues Florida’s Stand-Your-Ground statute before Judge Ernest A. Kollra on Friday, Aug. 22, 2025. Mateo is one of four Miami-Dade officers charged with manslaughter in the case stemming from the death of UPS driver Frank Ordonez, who was shot by police during a shootout with his kidnappers in Broward in December 2019. Mike Stocker South Florida Sun Sentinel Krolla didn’t appear to be leaning in any direction, but did question Morton repeatedly on whether an officer should shoot into a crowded situation — like a football game — to subdue an active shooter. He said he’d have a decision by Monday.A Florida Department of Law Enforcement investigation completed last year found that the six bullets that killed carjacked UPS truck driver Frank Ordonez, 27, and and Rick Cutshaw, 70, the bystander and former union organizer who was stuck in traffic that day, came from the guns of four Miami-Dade police officers.Mateo and three other Miami-Dade Sheriff’s deputies, Richard Santiesteban, 40, Leslie Lee, 58 and Rodolfo Mirabal, 39, were indicted of manslaughter in Broward County in June 2024. All pleaded not guilty and all have been suspended without pay.More than 90 bullets fired during shootoutOrdóñez and Cutshaw lost their lives in a hail of gunfire in the packed intersection of Miramar Parkway and Flamingo Road during the 5 p.m. rush hour in December 2019.Nearly 90 bullets were fired during the raging gun battle that involved more than a dozen officers from four agencies — and which was filmed live by television choppers flying overhead.An investigation by the FDLE last August determined five bullets from Miami-Dade police officers were uncovered during Ordóñez’s autopsy. Two linked to back to Santiesteban, and the rest to Mateo, Lee and Mirabal. A single bullet was recovered during Cutshaw’s autopsy. That one was tied to Mirabal, the report states.Also killed that day were Lamar Alexander and Ronnie Jerome Hill, two ex-cons whose exploits that day began with a bungled attempt to rob a Coral Gables jewelry store.The investigation found Santiesteban fired at least 44 times; Mirabal 19; Mateo 18 and Lee, six. In all, 20 Miami-Dade officers, three Miramar officers, one Pembroke Pines officer and one Florida Highway Patrol trooper were involved in the shootout that began earlier that day when a robbery at a Coral Gables jewelry store went awry.Botched jewelry heist led to tragedyThe unlikely course of events that led to the four deaths on Dec. 19, 2024, began in the late afternoon at Regent Jewelers on Miracle Mile in Coral Gables. When the robbery soured, Hill and Alexander raced from the store and hijacked the UPS truck driven by Ordóñez - with the driver still in it. Yellow tape blocks the access to the sidewalk after a robbery at Regent Jewelers at 386 Miracle Mile in Coral Gables on Dec. 5, 2019. The shootout in Broward County - that left a UPS driver and bystander dead - began with a bungled robbery attempt at Regent Jewelers. The robbers carjacked the UPS truck in the Gables - with the driver in it - and fled into Broward, where multiple police agencies engaged in a shootout amid rush-hour traffic. Pedro Portal pportal@miamiherald.com That ignited a high-speed chase up the Florida Turnpike, on Okeechobee Road and Interstate 75 — with gunfire being exchanged — and to the busy rush-hour streets of Pembroke Pines. There, the UPS truck and police cars from several agencies got stuck in a traffic jam and officers and the kidnappers began a blistering gun battle caught live on television station cameras hovering overhead.Bullets from police weapons struck several unintended targets, the FDLE report found. Some fired by Mirabal struck two vehicles, hitting a dashboard and a car seat. Four from Mateo’s weapon hit the rear bumper of another vehicle. Body camera footage also showed Mirabal stopping his cruiser behind the passenger side of the UPS truck and firing his weapon.The report said Mateo got out of his patrol vehicle and walked toward the passenger side of the UPS truck, shooting. On police radio, Santiesteban reported that shots were fired at the officers from the driver’s side of the truck.Judge Krolla said he expects to deal with a few other pre-trial motions Monday and Tuesday and that he expects attorneys to begin choosing jurors for Mateo’s trial some time on Wednesday. Supporters for Jose Mateo listen in court as lawyers argue Florida’s Stand-Your-Ground statute before Judge Ernest A. Kollra on Friday, Aug. 22, 2025. Mateo is one of four Miami-Dade officers charged with manslaughter in the case stemming from the death of UPS driver Frank Ordonez, who was shot by police during a shootout with his kidnappers. full_text: Judge says state can’t stop plea deal. Key Biscayne coach gets 12 years for sex crimes Crime Judge says state can’t stop plea deal. Key Biscayne coach gets 12 years for sex crimes By Charles Rabin and Clara-Sophia Daly Updated August 21, 2025 6:10 PM Miami-Dade Judge Alberto Milian ruled Thursday, Aug. 21, 2025, there would be no trial for Oscar Olea, above, the Key Biscayne gymnastics coach who as a result of a plea deal, will spend 12 years in prison on his sex crime convictions. He was accused of sexually assaulting girls who were students in his program. Carl Juste cjuste@miamiherald.com Despite detailed statements and objections from two sexual assault victims, Miami-Dade Circuit Court Judge Alberto Milian said Thursday there would be no trial for former Key Biscayne gymnastics instructor Oscar Olea, who last week reached a deal with prosecutors to avoid what was likely to be a lengthy and gut-wrenching trial.The judge reached his decision after nearly two hours of discussion and despite state prosecutors asking that the deal be reneged after two of Olea’s three victims said they were dissatisfied with the terms. One victim said she didn’t agree with the plea deal, but despite her disagreement, she deferred to whatever decision the state made, her attorney said.Olea, 40, will spend the next 12 years in prison, followed by a decade of probation. He will also be listed as a registered sex offender, a scar for life that keeps him away from minors and specific distances from gathering spots like parks and schools.“I didn’t take this job because I thought it would be easy,” Milian said just before Olea agreed to the terms of the agreement. “But I conclude this was in fact a meeting of the minds. My heart goes out to the victims. Justice is very imperfect.” Oscar Olea, right, listens as Miami-Dade Judge Alberto Milian explains his plea deal while standing next to his attorneys -- Charlton Stoner, left, and Matthew Ladd, center, inside Courtroom 7-2 at the Richard E. Gerstein Justice Building on Thursday, Aug. 21, 2025, in Miami, Florida. Carl Juste cjuste@miamiherald.com One of Olea’s victims said the former gymnastics instructor stole more than just her virginity and made her a victim - something she never asked for.“That identity was forced on me by someone else’s action, actions that stole something sacred, my virginity, my purity, my innocence,” said 28-year-old A.E., who was 12 when she was assaulted by Olea. “Things I can never get back.”READ MORE: Key Biscayne’s Dark SecretOlea, seated handcuffed in the jury box in an orange jumpsuit, sat silently, often jittery and shaking his legs, as his victims shared horrific stories. He answered Milian’s questions with simple “yes sir” and “no sir” responses. With the plea deal, Olea is now convicted of two counts of lewd and lascivious battery and two counts of unlawful sexual activity with a minor.The agreement stipulates that when Olea leaves prison he will not have access to electronic devices, he won’t be permitted to contact victims or family members and he must stay away from the Village of Key Biscayne until his probation concludes. Though each of the four charges carry a 15-year sentence, state prosecutors said a scoring system they use to determine prison stays would have landed Olea behind bars for 19 years.Before formally accepting the plea, Milian told Olea’s victims they were courageous and created a path forward for future victims of similar crimes. Still, in urging them to accept the plea, he warned them of just how imperfect the legal system can be.“Twelve years is not enough,” he said. “But, sometimes, there is not justice” at all.‘I obeyed out of fear’Olea’s three victims all spoke during the hearing. A.E. told the judge that Olea deserved more than 12 years behind bars. She said he assaulted her when she was 12 and that he stole her virginity and “purity.”“It lives with me. It has touched every single part of who I am,” she said. “I hated myself. I obeyed out of fear.” Oscar Olea, left, is fingerprinted inside Courtroom 7-2 at the Richard E. Gerstein Justice Building on Thursday, Aug. 21, 2025, in Miami, Florida. Miami-Dade Judge Alberto Milian ruled state prosecutors could not renege on Olea’s plea deal of 12 years in prison. Olea’s victims were dissatisfied with the deal. Carl Juste cjuste@miamiherald.com Another of Olea’s victims said, “This man took everything from me... it took me time to realize he brainwashed me.” The victim, who went by the initials E.M., says she wished she’d have spoken out sooner, but she was “completely terrified.”The woman, who is now in her 30s and said she was raped when she was 16, struck a defiant tone after the sentencing: “He has no power on me. I was a victim and now I am a survivor.”READ MORE: ‘Direct insult’: Victim in Key Biscayne gymnastics case demands trialHerald investigation gets police attentionOlea’s sordid history played out mostly in the dark for more than a decade as law enforcement investigations were bungled and parents grappled with how to respond to the belief that their young child had been sexually assaulted.It wasn’t until a 2024 Miami Herald investigation uncovered long-dormant allegations of sexual abuse from three former students, that the story grabbed the public and Key Biscayne Police Department’s attention. The three women, all in their 20s and 30s now, said they were sexually abused by Olea when they were 12, 16 and 16.Charges were never brought in the case involving one woman who spoke Thursday because the statute of limitations had passed. She was a colleague of Olea’s at the Key Biscayne Community Center.One victim said she was sexually assaulted more than 10 times between 2011 and 2012, during private lessons with Olea. Another woman’s mother told the Herald that Olea raped her daughter when she was 17. And a third woman told investigators she was underage and working with Olea at the Key Biscayne Community Center, known as “The Rec,” when they began a sexual relationship that often involved liquor.The Herald investigation also found that more recently, police and the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office investigated cases against two young girls ages 4 and 7. But charges were never brought, state prosecutors said, because of inconsistent statements from victims, statements from witnesses that contradicted each other and Olea’s denial of the allegations. In the end, the state said it did not have enough evidence to try the cases despite the police reports.Key Biscayne Police failed to fully investigateThe cases essentially sat stale for over a decade - in part - because the Key Biscayne Police Department failed to act on multiple complaints, including one in 2012 in which a child’s mother brought police love letters between her 14-year-old daughter and Olea. In one letter from Olea to the young girl, he mentions “kissing her lips.”Olea was never brought in for questioning and continued coaching at the Village Green in Key Biscayne and for the gymnastics company American Gymsters. Yet even after Olea was dismissed from the Key Biscayne Parks and Recreation Department in 2011 for inappropriately carrying a young girl whose legs were seen wrapped around his waist, he was able to get a permit that allowed him to practice in the park outside the center.Key Biscayne Police said they were hindered from filing charges because families of the victims never filed charges. Police Chief Charles Press said the department knew Olea was a “bad seed,” and that in hindsight he may have issued a watch order to send undercover detectives to watch Olea’s interaction with the children at the park.Prosecuting sex cases difficultDespite courthouse optics that are likely to weigh heavily in the accuser’s favor, prosecuting rape and sex cases can be tricky. Two recent decisions in recent high-profile cases show exactly how difficult it can be to convince a jury of the crime.After a seven-week trial in July that included a panalopy of testimony, megastar rapper and producer Sean “Diddy” Combs was exonerated of racketeering and sex trafficking charges at trial in New York.Locally, the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office dropped sexual battery charges against the Alexander brothers’ friend Ohad Fisherman after prosecutors admitted they weren’t even certain he was at the scene when a woman said she was raped.Milian explained that to the victims Thursday before his ruling. Still, another of Olea’s victims, A.R., said she was taken advantage of by the gymnastics teacher because she was young and impressionable.To this day, she said, “I struggle with trust, confidence and relationships. Twelve years is not enough.”Miami Herald Staff Writer Ana Claudia Chacin contributed to this report.This story was originally published August 21, 2025 at 1:47 PM. The driver faces vehicular homicide charges. An arrest warrant for Harjinder was issued on Friday. He was arrested in Stockton, California, without incident on Saturday.“This priority effort was a cross country, multi-state and multi-agency success,” said USMS Director Gadyaces S. Serralta in a statement.The Aug. 12 crash occurred when Singh attempted to make a U-turn in his 18-wheeler at an “official use only” area of the Turnpike, 19 miles north of Fort Pierce in St. Lucie County.Singh was blocking all the northbound lanes as a 2015 black Chrysler Town & Country minivan approached in the middle lane, FHP said. full_text: US court throws out massive fraud penalty against Trump Law and JusticeUnited States of AmericaUS court throws out massive fraud penalty against TrumpRoshni Majumdar with AP, Reuters08/21/2025August 21, 2025A New York appeals court has ruled that US President Donald Trump will not be required to pay a $515 million (around €443 million) civil fraud penalty, eliminating one of his biggest financial liabilities.https://p.dw.com/p/4zKrVThe latest ruling only applies to financial penalties levied against Trump and his executivesImage: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFPAdvertisementA US court on Thursday threw out the half-billion-dollar penalty in the civil fraudcase against President Donald Trump and his company. But a panel of five judges upheld other punishments, including a lower court's finding that Trump and Trump Organization executives engaged in fraud. New York Attorney General Letitia James had sued Trump in 2022, alleging he falsely altered his net worth on key financial statements to receive tax and insurance benefits. The lawsuit made James one of Trump's most prominent adversaries. A New York judge Arthur Engoron last year ordered Trump to pay nearly $355 million in penalties after holding him liable for fraud. With interest, that sum topped $515 million. If including additional penalties levied on Trump's eldest sons, Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, the total balloons to more than $527 million as of Thursday. Judges say penalty 'excessive' but disagree over merits of lawsuit The court agreed to eliminate the penalty that came with the verdict, writing that the order which directs that defendants pay nearly half a billion dollars to the State of New York, is an excessive fine that violates the Eighth Amendment of the United States Constitution. But the panel remained sharply divided on the merits of the lawsuit and Engoron's fraud finding. Two judges wrote that they felt New York Attorney General Letitia James' lawsuit against Trump and his companies was justifiable and that she had proven her case, even with the penalty being too severe. Another judge wrote that James exceeded her legal authority in bringing the suit, saying that if any of Trump's lenders felt cheated, they could have sued him themselves, and none did. One judge wrote that Engoron was wrong to rule, before the trial began, that the attorney general had proved Trump engaged in fraud. Trump claims 'total victory' after NY appeals court decision Trump and his sons painted the ruling as a win, with Trump posting to Truth Social that: TOTAL VICTORY in the FAKE New York State Attorney General Letitia James Case! I greatly respect the fact that the Court had the Courage to throw out this unlawful and disgraceful Decision that was hurting Business all throughout New York State. Eric Trump, the president's son, wrote to X: Total victory in the sham NY Attorney General case!!! After 5 years of hell, justice prevailed! Court ruling upholds other punishments The court in the same ruling said that other non-monetary sanctions imposed by Arthur Engoron on Trump, the Trump Organization, and other defendants were well crafted to curb defendants’ business culture. Judges Peter Moulten and Dianne Renwick, who wrote the principal opinion, said that the trial record supports the lower court’s finding that Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, possessed the requisite intent to defraud, in addition to top executives Allen Weisselberg and Jeffrey McConney, according to The Hill.
